National Fraud Enforcement Division and the Department of Health and Human Services Announce Self-Disclosure Protocol for Criminal Health Care Fraud
The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division) and the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG) today issued a policy that clarifies that companies seeking to voluntarily self-disclose potential criminal conduct related to health care need only to disclose to the Fraud Division to receive the benefit of both the Department’s Corporate Enforcement Policy and HHS-OIG’s Health Care Fraud Self-Disclosure Protocol (SDP). HHS-OIG separately updated the SDP to clarify that criminal health care matters should be disclosed to the Department of Justice.
“Companies that discover fraud within their own operations should not have to navigate a maze of agencies before reporting it,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “Today, together with our partners at HHS-OIG, we are eliminating unnecessary bureaucratic barriers that have caused confusion about whether companies must make multiple disclosures of potentially criminal conduct. There is now one clear point of contact: DOJ’s Fraud Division. If a company comes forward, cooperates fully, and remedies the misconduct, the benefits are clear and predictable. If a company conceals what it knows, it should expect a very different conversation.”
“We encourage companies to come forward and disclose criminal conduct to the Justice Department, and we are committed to extending the benefits of the HHS-OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol to those who do.” said Department of Health and Human Services Inspector General T. March Bell. “The OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol is a critical tool for promoting accountability, transparency, and integrity across the health care system, providing organizations with a clear pathway to voluntarily report potential misconduct and address compliance concerns. This process helps strengthen trust in federally funded health care programs by encouraging timely corrective action, reducing future risk, and demonstrating a commitment to ethical conduct.”
The Policy announced today is designed to eliminate obstacles that may slow disclosures. A single arrangement - an illegal kickback, a scheme to bill Medicare for medically unnecessary services, a scheme concealing an excluded provider - routinely may result in potential criminal, civil, or administrative consequences. Companies facing that overlap have had to decide not only whether to come forward, but also where to make that disclosure. Under the Policy announced today, a company that voluntarily self-discloses criminal conduct affecting a federal health care program to the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section will receive the benefits of HHS-OIG’s SDP - automatically, with no additional direct submission necessary through the HHS-OIG portal.
HHS-OIG separately updated the SDP today to settle the reverse question. The SDP covers conduct that may violate civil or administrative law, and the SDP was updated today to clarify that criminal conduct should be disclosed to the Department of Justice. A company that discloses only to HHS-OIG generally will not have made a voluntary self-disclosure to the Department and generally will not qualify for a declination on that basis. Companies seeking the benefits of both programs should bring potentially criminal conduct to the Fraud Division first.
The policy announced today may be found here. HHS-OIG’s updated protocol may be found here. Self-disclosures may be reported to the Fraud Division at: corporate.enforcement@usdoj.gov.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
title: National Fraud Enforcement Division and the Department of Health and Human Services Announce Self-Disclosure Protocol for Criminal Health Care Fraud

text:
Press Statement

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

October 15, 2026

President Trump has been absolutely clear: under his administration, the United States will not tolerate terrorism, organized crime or extra-hemispheric forces spreading anti-American influence in our region. For too long, Communist Cuba has been allowed to operate as an outpost for malign actors and terror groups – including the Islamic Republic of Iran, the world’s number one state sponsor of terrorism – to target the United States.

Cuba’s BANCO INTERNACIONAL DE COMERCIO S.A. (BICSA) has provided services to the designated Iran’s Karafarin Bank since at least 2022. The Department of the Treasury sanctioned Karafarin Bank pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902 in 2020. Today, in concert with a Department of the Treasury action on Iranian financial actors, I am sanctioning the Cuban state-owned BICSA pursuant to Section 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the financial services sector of the Cuban economy.

Let me be clear: the Trump Administration will not tolerate a rogue state hosting hostile foreign military, intelligence and terror operations less than a hundred miles from the American homeland. We will continue to aggressively identify and eliminate the Cuban regime’s financial and security interconnections with Iran and other dangerous and hostile states and actors.

The Department’s actions are being taken pursuant to E.O. 14404, which authorizes sweeping sanctions on Cuba, including against persons who support the Cuban regime’s security apparatus and those responsible for repression in Cuba and other threats to U.S. national security. These actions also further both E.O. 14380, “ Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of Cuba ” and National Security Presidential Memorandum 5 , which directs the Executive Branch to improve human rights, encourage the rule of law, foster free markets and free enterprise, and promote democracy in Cuba.

Sanctions Implications

As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 14404 of May 1, 2026, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to U.S. National Security and Foreign Policy,” all property and interests in property of the designated person described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). Additionally, all entities that are owned individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.

Any transaction or dealing by U.S. persons or persons subject to the jurisdiction of the United States in property or interests of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized or exempt. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Foreign persons that engage in transactions with persons designated pursuant to E.O. 14404—or that operate or have operated in the energy, defense and related materiel, metals and mining, financial services, or security sector of the Cuban economy, as identified in E.O. 14404—are themselves at risk of sanctions. Non-U.S. persons, including foreign financial institutions, should proceed with caution in any dealings with a party sanctioned under this authority. Actions to return assets to a sanctioned party or transfer them to another jurisdiction for potential use by the target expose non-U.S. persons to significant sanctions risk. All property and interests in property of persons that are blocked pursuant to the Cuban Assets Control Regulations (CACR) are blocked. The CACR prohibits persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction from dealing in property in which Cuba or a Cuban national has an interest, unless authorized or exempt.

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be routed through OFAC’s Reconsiderations Portal . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

MATSUI ACTS TO PROTECT AMERICANS FROM HIGH COSTS AT THE GAS PUMP
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) introduced legislation to require the Department of Transportation (DOT) to examine whether it can strengthen fuel efficiency requirements to counter high gas prices and reinstate penalties for automakers that fail to produce fuel-efficient vehicles.
“Across the country, Americans are being squeezed by high gas prices, rising grocery bills, and everyday costs that keep stretching family budgets thinner,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The Gas Money Saved Act meets people where they are by strengthening fuel efficiency standards that help drivers spend less on gas for years to come. This is a practical step to lower everyday costs, give families more breathing room, and build a cleaner, more efficient transportation future.”
“With gas prices skyrocketing because of President Trump’s prolonged and illegal war, we must take immediate steps to give American consumers some relief,” said Congresswoman Titus. “In May 2026, gas prices rose at a rate ten times higher than the rate of inflation. In Nevada, they now average $5.45 per gallon. Coupled with higher prices on groceries and other goods because of the Trump tariffs, families are struggling to make ends meet.”
Congresswoman Matsui, a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and Rep. Dina Titus (NV-01), a member of the House Transportation Committee, introduced the Gas Money Saved Act to review Corporate Fuel Economy (CAFE) standards and reinstate fuel-efficiency requirements that were stripped away by Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill in 2025. Companion legislation has been introduced in the Senate by Senator Ed Markey (D-MA).
“Fuel economy standards help American drivers get around without breaking the bank while gas prices are high, but Trump and the Republicans gutted these standards as part of their crusade to put Big Oil above American families,” said Senator Markey. “Auto innovation should give consumers better choices, not cut corners at their expense. The Gas Money Saved Act would make sure American drivers have fuel-efficient vehicle options that are cheaper to fill up and hold automakers to account—a cost-saving measure that is especially critical as the Trump Administration would rather spend billions on an illegal war than keep costs low for Americans.
The Gas Money Saved Act would:
- Require DOT to reevaluate CAFE standards if gas prices rise at a rate five times faster than inflation over a six-month period, and;
- Restore and increase financial penalties on automakers if their car and truck fleet does not meet fuel efficiency standards.
title: MATSUI ACTS TO PROTECT AMERICANS FROM HIGH COSTS AT THE GAS PUMP

Illegal Alien from Mexico Sentenced for International Conspiracy to Smuggle Aliens from Canada into United States
Edgar Sanchez-Solis, 27, an illegal alien from Mexico, was sentenced today to five years in prison for his role in an international human smuggling conspiracy that illegally brought aliens from Mexico and Central and South America across the northern border with Canada into the United States.
“Mr. Sanchez-Solis profited off of a scheme that undermined the security of our northern border and placed law enforcement officers and aliens in harm’s way when fleeing law enforcement,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Thanks to Operation Take Back America and the Justice Department’s commitment to enforcing the rule of law, yet another human smuggler has been held accountable for endangering human life.”
“HSI remains relentless in our pursuit to dismantle criminal networks that profit from human smuggling along the northern border,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony J. Patrone of HSI Buffalo. “These organizations exploit vulnerable individuals, endanger lives, and threaten the safety of our communities. Working closely with U.S. Border Patrol and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, HSI Rouses Point is committed to disrupting illegal entry and transnational criminal activity throughout Northern New York.”
According to court documents, Sanchez-Solis was a leader of an alien smuggling organization (ASO) that operated between December 2022 and April 2025 and smuggled hundreds of aliens from Mexico and Central and South America into the United States. Once the aliens were inside the United States, the ASO employed drivers to pick them up and drive them further into the country. The defendant personally participated in and coordinated smuggling events with other leaders of the ASO. During one smuggling event in May 2023, a van carrying aliens became involved in a vehicle chase with U.S. Border Patrol. Border Patrol had to stop their pursuit due to risk to the public, and law enforcement had to use a tire deflation device to stop the vehicle after it failed to yield. The smuggled aliens paid the ASO thousands of dollars to be smuggled into the United States, and some then worked for the ASO smuggling other aliens to pay off their own smuggling debts.
Sanchez-Solis pleaded guilty on May 7 to one count of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and five counts of alien smuggling for commercial advantage and private financial gain. Three other illegal aliens from Mexico were charged for their roles in the conspiracy. Ignacio Diaz-Perez, 37, and Samuel Diaz-Perez, 27, each pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and six counts of aliens smuggling for financial gain. Salvador Diaz-Diaz, 34, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and five counts of aliens smuggling for financial gain. They are expected to be sentenced on Nov. 23.
HSI Rouses Point and U.S. Border Patrol Burke Station investigated the case, with substantial assistance from HSI’s Human Smuggling Unit in Washington, D.C., and U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s National Targeting Center International Interdiction Task Force.
Trial Attorney Spencer M. Perry of the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Carling Dunham for the Northern District of New York is prosecuting the case.
This case was supported and prosecuted by Joint Task Force Alpha (JTFA), the U.S. Department of Justice’s lead effort in combating human smuggling and trafficking committed by cartels and Transnational Criminal Organizations throughout the Americas. In partnership with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), JTFA investigates and prosecutes the most prolific and dangerous human smuggling and trafficking networks that impact public safety and border security. Led by the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section and supported by other Criminal Division components, JTFA has dedicated prosecutors from U.S. Attorneys’ Offices along the Southwest border, Southern Florida, Northern New York, and Vermont. JTFA partners with U.S. Attorneys’ Offices throughout the country and supports high-priority cases in any district. All JTFA cases rely on substantial law enforcement resources from DHS components, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, and the Office of Field Operations. JTFA also partners with FBI and other law enforcement agencies. To date, JTFA’s work has resulted in more than 486 domestic and international arrests of leaders, organizers, and significant facilitators of alien smuggling and trafficking; more than 486 U.S. convictions; and more than 374 significant jail sentences imposed and forfeitures of substantial assets.
This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and other transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Project Safe Neighborhood.

Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works (EPW), last month launched a bicameral investigation into the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) guidance exempting data center power plants from the Acid Rain Program (ARP).
By EPA’s own admission, the decision to issue new guidance came at the behest of data center companies. And according to the EPA press release issuing the new guidance, the agency took this action to “further President Trump’s agenda promoting data centers.”
“EPA’s new ARP guidance is a handout to the richest and most powerful companies in the world. And this handout comes at the expense of Americans’ health and the safety of our ecosystems and communities that were, prior to the inception of the ARP, regularly drenched in dangerous acidic rainfall,” the lawmakers wrote in their letter to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin.
The ARP regulates the emission of sulfur dioxide (SO2) and nitrogen oxides (NOx) from power plants. SO2 and NOx are both harmful to human health, damaging the respiratory system and worsening heart disease. They are also linked to adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes, kidney damage, autoimmune disorders, and cancer.
The pollutants are also the primary causes of acid rain. Prior to the ARP, acid rain poisoned rivers, lakes, and streams; damaged forests; killed and sickened aquatic animals; and corroded buildings, monuments, and statues.
“EPA explicitly bills its new guidance as a means to facilitate data center development. In so doing, EPA misapprehends its own mission, which is to ‘protect human health and the environment,’ as stated in black and white on the agency’s own website,” continued the lawmakers.
“Bizarrely, under EPA’s new guidance, massive new gas-fired power plants large enough to power cities would be exempt from NOx and SO2 caps under the ARP only as long as they do not serve the public electricity grid and instead exclusively power a privately-owned data center. This is a perverse outcome, and it is contrary to Congress’s design for the Clean Air Act, which creates specific and comprehensive regulatory requirements for significant pollution sources like these,” added the lawmakers.
The lawmakers, together with Senators Ed Markey (D-MA) and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), requested answers from EPA by October 7th about the agency’s decision-making process while crafting this new guidance, as well as any information regarding the agency’s communications with data center companies. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Cory Booker (D-NJ), and 24 Members of the House of Representatives also signed the letter. EPA has not yet responded to the lawmakers’ letter.
The letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin is available here.
title: McClellan, Whitehouse Investigate EPA’s Decision to Exempt Data Center Power Plants from Acid Rain Protections

Members of Congress Hold Hearing in Austin to Investigate ICE Shootings Across Texas
Casar, Thompson, Jayapal, Democratic Members of Congress demand accountability and change with ICE
AUSTIN, TEXAS – On Thursday, October 15th, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas), alongside Representatives Bennie G. Thompson (D-Miss.), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, and five other members of Congress held a field hearing to investigate the numerous ICE shootings across Texas, including the recent shooting of Wilber Garcés-Pérez.
Representatives Greg Casar, Bennie G. Thompson, and Pramila Jayapal were joined by Representatives Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02), Lou Correa (CA-46), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), and Al Green (TX-09).
The Members of Congress were joined by witnesses Ms. Rachel Reyes, mother of Ruben Ray Martinez, Kristin Etter, Director of Policy & Legal Services at the Texas Immigration Law Council, Carolina Rivera Nelson, Attorney at the ACLU of Texas, and Danny Woodward, Policy Attorney with Texas Civil Rights Project.
“Texas has become the epicenter of Trump’s deadly deportation machine, so we brought Members of Congress from across the country to Austin to see it firsthand,” said Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas). “ICE shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez, a DoorDash driver and a father, in the back then denied him medical care. They even tried to deport him so he could never speak the truth. Donald Trump's ICE isn't going after the worst of the worst — it's gone after people like Wilber, who have no criminal record. We will fight to hold the perpetrators in this administration accountable, and not provide another dime in funding to this rogue agency."
“Democrats came to Austin today to demand justice and accountability for Wilber Garcés-Pérez and the others that have been shot by immigration agents in Texas. If Republicans refuse to conduct any oversight of the Trump administration, we must do so in their place,” added Congressman Bennie G. Thompson. “What we heard today was powerful and informative. Make no mistake: we will do everything possible to hold this administration accountable for what it is doing. This violence, lawlessness, and chaos in our communities must end.”
“Twenty-five days ago, ICE agents in Austin, Texas shot Wilber Garcés-Pérez in the back. Instead of taking him to the hospital, they locked him up in a detention center and did not allow him to have surgery for 11 days. This is not the most recent shooting by ICE, and is one of nearly a dozen that we know of since Trump returned to office,” said Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal. “ICE is a lawless, rogue agency that is causing generational trauma in communities across the country. House Democrats today are doing the oversight work that Republicans refuse to do — and we will continue to do everything possible to protect our communities from Trump’s mass deportation agenda.”
"The shooting and medical neglect of Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez follows the many other cases that have become synonymous with cities being swarmed with masked, armed federal agents and the nation’s dangerous descent into tyranny: Renée Nicole Good, Alex Pretti, Johan Sebastian Guerrero, and too many others. No life is meaningless, and each individual assaulted or killed by our immigration system is someone's child, someone's sibling, someone's parent, and they all still belong here with us,” said Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. “Unless you’re Native American, we all come from somewhere else. The Trump immigration system is structured and staffed as a deportation machine that violates individuals' constitutional rights. Democrats will fight for an immigration system that honors our history and sets forth a reasonable, compassionate path to citizenship." 
“President Trump got elected on the promise to go after the “worst of the worst.” Instead, since January, federal immigration agents have detained over 500 U.S. citizens and killed at least three. ICE is arresting people with no criminal record to hit political quotas while cutting training and lowering hiring standards,” said Congressman Lou Correa. “There is an urgent need for major reforms to keep our communities safe from violence. DHS was created to defend Americans against foreign terrorists. Instead, we have permanent residents and American citizens being shot by ICE agents in our streets.”
"In Texas, we have witnessed at least three ICE shootings since this administration began its aggressive, unprecedented enforcement actions,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher.  “People across our community in Houston are still reeling from the shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo.  Just last weekend, ICE agents ran over and gravely injured Miguel Parra Hernandez while pursuing someone else. ICE's reckless and brutal actions are not only unprecedented, they're unconstitutional.  They are making us less safe, creating fear and danger for immigrants and citizens alike.  This Republican-led Congress that has enabled this lawlessness has utterly failed Wilber Garcés-Pérez, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Ruben Ray Martinez, and so many others.  All Americans deserve better from our government, and that is why I joined Congressman Casar, Ranking Member Thompson, Congresswoman Jayapal, and my Democratic colleagues in Austin today to hear from some of the many people impacted, learn more, and demonstrate our commitment to bringing justice, accountability, and change.” 
“Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst. But judging by what we’re seeing across Texas and the country, that sounds more like ICE’s recruitment strategy. People are being shot, injured, and killed by federal agents operating without basic law enforcement standards or accountability,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “In Houston, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work. One hundred days later, his family still has no answers. Instead they’ve been met with stonewalling and excuses. These families deserve the truth and justice, and we will not stop fighting until they get both. 
“No President is above the law, and no federal agency should be allowed to serve as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner while operating with impunity,” said Congressman Al Green. “Under President Trump, ICE has been emboldened to use deadly force against people in our communities while the administration evades transparency and accountability, engaging in a cover-up. These shootings are not isolated incidents. They are part of a deeply troubling pattern of conduct that threatens the constitutional rights and lives of people in this country.”
The Members of Congress’ full remarks can be found here.
###
Congressman Greg Casar represents Texas’s 35th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, which runs down I-35 from East Austin to Hays County to the West Side of San Antonio. A labor organizer and son of Mexican immigrants, Casar serves as the Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus for the 119th Congress. He also serves on the Committee on Education and Labor and the Committee on Oversight and Accountability.
title: Members of Congress Hold Hearing in Austin to Investigate ICE Shootings Across Texas

Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell provided the following readout:
On October 15, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth met with his United Kingdom counterpart, Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting, at the Pentagon. Secretary Streeting highlighted the United Kingdom's recently released Defence Investment Plan, which outlines increased British defense spending. Secretary Hegseth encouraged the United Kingdom to continue increasing defense spending further and faster to advance a fairer, stronger, and more sustainable NATO 3.0. Secretary Hegseth and Secretary Streeting discussed the Review of U.S. Force Posture and Basing in Europe and the opportunity it presents to ensure U.S. posture is aligned with the alliance we need—not the alliance of the past. Secretary Hegseth urged Secretary Streeting to continue supporting President Trump's objective of a durable peace in Ukraine and global security in the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Readout of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's Meeting With the United Kingdom's Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting

text:
Remarks

Christopher Landau, Deputy Secretary of State

Philip J. Pierre, Saint Lucia Prime Minister

Susan Walke, State Department Director for Caribbean Affairs

Juan Pablo Segura, Assistant Secretary for Western Hemisphere Affairs

Loy Henderson Conference Room

Washington, DC

October 15, 2026

MS WALKE: Good morning, everyone, and welcome. My name is Susan Walke I’m the director for Caribbean affairs here at the State Department, and I will be your emcee for today’s dialogue. We are looking forward to a day of in-depth discussions on a number of key issues of importance to all of our countries.

I am delighted to introduce you to Assistant Secretary for Western Hemisphere Affairs, Juan Pablo Segura. Assistant Secretary Segura was sworn in as assistant secretary of state on August 14th. Before joining the State Department, he was the secretary of commerce and trade for the Commonwealth of Virginia for Governor Glenn Youngkin. As secretary, he was responsible for growing Virginia’s more than $710 billion a year in GDP economy, and managed the state’s international trade portfolio. Assistant Secretary Segura, I’m pleased to welcome you up to the dais. (Applause.)

ASSISTANT SECRETARY SEGURA: Thank you, Susan, for that great introduction. It’s a true honor to be here with all of you this morning, this incredible group of distinguished leaders across the Caribbean.

I’d like to start with just a reminder that Secretary Rubio made a promise earlier this year at Saint Kitts and Nevis. He promised that the U.S. would step up in the Caribbean, and this is a manifestation of that promise. This dialogue is the U.S. making good on its promise, which is incredibly exciting for all of us at the United States.

As you review the agenda, as we have the conversation that – the conversations that will happen over the next two years, you’ll see that the agenda mirrors the objectives of the Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs. Our objectives are very simple. The first is we want to uplift the region through economic investment. The second is we want to end the scourge of narcoterrorist threat across the hemisphere. And the third is we want to end illegal immigration. We want countries to have sovereignty, true sovereignty, across the hemisphere.

Now, as I introduce my boss, Deputy Secretary Landau, I do want to just highlight that this conversation really touches the why of why this conversation is so important. And I was recently speaking to one of you a week ago or a week and a half ago at the OAS, and it was very encouraging to see how everyone was leaning into the dialogue with the United States, but there was also a part of conversation where folks didn’t know the tools that are available in this economic conversation, this security conversation. A lot of folks don’t know that the President has prioritized 20 percent of our foreign assistance to the hemisphere. A lot of people don’t know that the DFC, the Development Finance Corporation, the mandate has changed.

The tools, the investment opportunities have changed. The (inaudible) has changed in how we can help countries grow economically and so I feel like there’s no better person to be the keynote speaker for today than the chair of the board of the DFC, a former ambassador, someone that knows the conversations, the real conversations that are happening at posts with your countries. And so it is an honor for me to introduce our incredible deputy secretary of state for the United States of America, Deputy Secretary Landau. (Applause.)

DEPUTY SECRETARY LANDAU: Thank you, Assistant Secretary. Welcome to our friends from the Caribbean. It’s really a pleasure to have such a distinguished group of leaders here today. I think this kind of dialogue is, frankly, overdue.

And I want to just start with what to me is the central reality underlying all of this, which is the United States is a Caribbean nation. You all know that. That is true as a matter of geography. We have – Puerto Rico is in the Caribbean. It’s true of our history. I was just discussing with several of you how Alexander Hamilton is from Nevis and, frankly, a huge part of our economy was the triangular trade between Europe, the eastern shore of the United States, the Caribbean. The relationships between the United States and this part of the world have been crucial throughout our history and throughout your history. And so we’re not writing on a blank slate as we gather here.

I think you all know this far better than I do, that the ties between our countries are not only historical; they involve people. When I was in Antigua last year, I was talking to somebody and I think of his siblings, two of them were in the States, and the cousins were in the States. The personal bonds between our countries are amazing. So many successful people in the United States, in this generation and previous generations, have come from your region. I’m going all the way back to Alexander Hamilton, but people like Colin Powell, who ran this building 25 years ago. I mean, our country has benefitted enormously from the ties with your region.

And frankly, it has been a source of pain for many of us as Americans to see the United States not giving the Western Hemisphere generally the attention it deserved, and specifically the Caribbean. The Caribbean is very much part of the Western Hemisphere. So I’m sure you’ve all seen the stories about how the United States is, under President Trump and Secretary Rubio – we are making the Western Hemisphere a – we’re not – we are restoring – I think that’s the better word – the Western Hemisphere to its position of preeminence and priority in American foreign policy. For far too long, we have been looking at things that are happening halfway across the world, and we have been ignoring things that are happening right in our own neighborhood.

And so I just want to – I think it’s very important that we recognize some of the flaws of recent years in our policies and we talk together to commit to ways that we can build institutional relationships. Because all of us in this room – I mean, we all have government positions, and it’s great, it lasts for a while. But then all of us will be gone in a matter of years, right? And I think the challenge for us is to create a lasting foundation that doesn’t just depend on so-and-so being friends with so-and-so. I mean, it’s wonderful and it’s great. One of the great things about these kinds of gatherings is that we can establish personal relationships, right? It’s great if I can have you on WhatsApp or that kind of thing. But that is not the basis for a lasting institutional structure of a relationship that’s going to survive over decades.

And I think – that’s what I’m hoping that a conference like today can establish – really both those things. I mean, again, personal ties are important in diplomacy. But again, I think I’m looking to strengthen the structural ties, again, many of which are there. I mean, we’re not building this from scratch, and I think we have a lot of historical precedent. But I also want to make clear that we in the United States do not have all the answers, right? I think I entered this job with a fair dose of humility that – I grew up in Latin America myself. My father was a diplomat and – including in Venezuela, where actually when – during the years in the early 80s when he lived in – when we lived in Venezuela, I actually had the opportunity to visit many of your countries for the first time. That’s when I first got the chance to go to Haiti, to Barbados, to Grenada, way back more than 40 years ago now. And again, that only underscored for me obviously the great diversity in the Caribbean but also the importance in so many areas of the United States with these relationships in the Caribbean.

So bringing together the leaders has been a real – your leaders – all of you has been something that’s been very important both for Secretary Rubio and for me. I think he was delighted to go to CARICOM. I think it was in – was it in Saint Nevis or in Saint Kitts and Nevis? He was at a meeting or – he went recently. And so I think he very much – again, as somebody from Florida – understands better than anybody the importance of this Caribbean region to the United States, across all dynamics, again, on a human level, on a economic level, on a security level.

And so, again, I just want to underscore that I think this dialogue is overdue, and I just want to underscore that – I want to underscore the word “dialogue,” right? A dialogue doesn’t mean that you have come here to have me or anybody else in the United States just give lectures, right? I mean, I just think it’s very important that we, the United States, listen to you from the Caribbean what your vision is. I mean, you obviously are – you all are sovereign countries; you are going to decide your fate. And – but I think – honestly, I truly believe we wouldn’t be having this meeting if the Secretary and I didn’t believe that what is in your interests is also in our interests; that there are many, many areas where we should be deepening cooperation where there are great solutions.

So again, I will talk today in part about further commitments the United States is going to make, and that’s fine. I was reading through the remarks that they prepared for me here; it’s like, well, we’ll give millions of dollars for this and millions of dollars for that. Ultimately, I’m more interested – and I think you should be more interested, or I would hope that you would be more interested – in, like, where do we get the businesses that are going to be there for the long term, that are investing in real economic opportunities that are creating a lasting foundation for the relationships? Because ultimately, a particular grant can be fine to fill a particular need, but for a long-term growth strategy, a particular grant isn’t going to fix that. Now, there may be particular grants that are useful insofar as they create a framework or a foundation for private-sector-led economic development. But ultimately, I think that’s what’s going to, frankly, be the main driver here.

So again, I just was talking to the representative of Suriname before we walked in here, and they said they had a great meeting, I think yesterday, with a private American security company that offered some services that could help them really improve their own security for their country. I said to me, that is great. And I feel my job, our job here at the Department of State, is to be the connective tissue between you, the leaders from your region, and the dynamic American private sector. The American private sector is going to have more creative, cost-effective solutions for the problems you’re looking at than the U.S. Government will. I’ll just tell you that. I say that as somebody who works for the government right now.

But ultimately, the greatness of the United States is not driven by the government; it’s driven by our private sector. And so our job – or what I see our job as being is just to be an interlocutor so that our private sector is aware of the opportunities in the Caribbean, and that the Caribbean is aware of what the private sector might be interested in here. I mean, it’s a conversation that has to go both ways.

So let’s actually start talking a little bit about economics. One of the things that makes me very happy is that we’re launching an investment dialogue next year precisely to bring together all of your countries with the American private sector. And so I think – this is an issue that I also fostered out in the Pacific region. That’s another area I’ve been very focused on, some of the island states, some of which have some similarities to some of the islands – nations of the Caribbean – not that big in terms of land mass of the country or even the population. So they present kind of interesting economic models, where there can be opportunities for economic development, but it’s not necessarily the most obvious target as a mass export market for American companies, let’s say, but where there might be investment opportunities that you all are interested in.

But I think for this kind of an investment conference to work, it needs a lot of advanced thought from both sides. I think I really would urge all of your countries to think about what kind of American private sector investment you are particularly interested in in your country. If you have an infrastructure project, a port, or a digital infrastructure project, an energy infrastructure project that you’re interested in; you want to talk to people in the telecommunications area – I mean, if you all – again, it’d be most helpful if you all let us know in advance. If you want to see a specific company, you say, I would like to see Google, I would like to see Bechtel, I would like to see a shipping company, I’d like to see American Airlines – whatever it is, that will make this kind of a conference more helpful. Because we don’t want to just have a conference for the sake of bringing people together to meet; we want to actually be able to have people who are actually interested in pursuing deals. And again, we will also reach out to the private sector and say, who is interested in opportunities in the Caribbean? And again, we will try to work it both ways.

But again, I encourage you to really give some thought. I don’t really have the details about what month this is yet next year, but I know it is next year. We will keep in touch on that. Again, that just makes me very, very happy, because ultimately, again, it’s this kind of investments that will create growth and jobs in your country and build skills.

We also recognize that economic development entails health. And we understand some of the health needs in your region.

And on health, this is when I start – this is what – I’m starting to tell some of the goodies that I’m here to talk about. I’m happy to announce we have 61 – set aside $61.5 million to launch ASPIRE, the America Strategic Partnership for Independent Regional Healthcare Excellence – that’s a long one – in order to allow the region to build its own strong, self-reliant health care workforce capacity. So again, I think we can get more details on that, but that’s one of the deliverables that I wanted to announce to you all today.

Second, I wanted to talk a little bit about security, and I think the assistant secretary alluded to this. I think we have seen an uptick in recent years of drugs coming through the Caribbean from South America towards the United States. I don’t need to tell you what a danger this is for all of us. And frankly, as you’ve all seen if you read the news, the United States is not going to just sit by with business as usual where we have more than 100,000 Americans dying of overdose from some of these drugs just in perpetuity. I think we’re – we have followed a approach of using the judicial system, asking for arrests, extraditions, trying people. And I think, as you’ve seen, we now recognize that this is actually also a national security threat to our people. We’re taking actions accordingly. And we’d like to work with your countries to make sure that we’re all on the same page, at least in recognizing the common danger of this and seeing how we can try to address this scourge together.

So we already have a Caribbean Basin Security Initiative, and that’s the foundation of our security partnership with 13 of the countries. And today we are – again, my next deliverable that I’m announcing is that we’re increasing our support through CBSI, and I’m pleased to announce $37 million in new programming to protect critical digital infrastructure and strengthen port security. Obviously, strong ports are the first line of defense. If drugs are coming into your ports – or it’s not just drugs also; it’s also weapons and other illegal goods. I mean, and I think in my first week in the job, the Secretary called me down to his office and handed me an article about guns going to Haiti from the Miami River and said, “Could you please deal with this?” And that was the beginning of what has been a pretty intense involvement, as the prime minister of Haiti here, my friend, Prime Minister Fils-Aimé, knows. I’ve been very involved in Haiti, but it really stemmed out of trying to stop the flow of guns that are going from our country into Haiti and destabilizing it.

And I will say on this note, I am working closely with our U.S. attorney in the Southern District of Florida to make sure that our law enforcement capabilities are fully mobilized and that we are coordinating with them, so if there are issues where you think the American judicial system can actually be helpful to you as leaders in your countries who are trying to solve particular problems – if there are criminal networks that are exporting drugs from your country and you think your country may not have all the infrastructure or the legal infrastructure to address this problem, let’s work together on some of these security challenges, because our U.S. Attorney’s Office in Miami is very eager to work with you on that.

Another big priority is illegal fishing, and I’d like to – that’s been a priority of mine worldwide. If there are people fishing illegally in your waters, we want to work with you to address that, because obviously fish is a important resource for all of our peoples. And I’m also – on this issue, I’m announcing an additional $55.5 million to strengthen law enforcement – I told you I had a lot of millions here to talk about – 55.5 million to strengthen law enforcement and $11 million in Foreign Military Financing to build the capabilities of your security forces. So again, I think let’s talk about how we can work together with the security ministers, with CARICOM IMPACS, to convene the next Caribbean Basin Security Initiative security ministerial in spring 2027, next spring.

Third – and I see I’m running low on time, but I just want to cover a range of issues that – I’m sure that all of you can flesh out what’s on your mind – trusted infrastructure is really important, and particularly secure communications networks. Ultimately, a modern economy cannot exist without a secure network. We all have seen vulnerabilities. Every day you read about it in the news. And – but without a good digital footprint, you can’t have a solid banking system, tourism system, energy grid, or government services. And who builds those networks matters, and we would like to work with you on that. In fact, on this – in this connection, I’m announcing $175.8 million in U.S. investment in secure infrastructure through our Caribbean and Central America underseas cables program. This will provide trusted, high-speed connectivity across the region to build resilient, secure networks that serve your people and not outside interests.

So together, the numbers that I have mentioned really total hundreds of millions of dollars in new commitments, but it’s not just about a certain dollar amount. It’s about just the long term, the United States reaffirming its interest and commitment to this critical region.

So I just want to end by underscoring the values that I think that we all share: respect for national sovereignty, the rule of law, open markets. These are some of the central tenets that underlie our relationships. And these are – by focusing on these core issues, that’s how we’re going to stimulate economic growth, attract investment, and allow you and us to provide prosperity and security for our – your citizens and our citizens. So again, as somebody who is very, very committed to your region, I just say that there are few events that I have attended during my time as Deputy Secretary of State that I’m as excited to be part of as this one.

I will close by just saying my last class in college, at Harvard College, was Sociology 113 that was taught by Orlando Patterson. He was visiting at Harvard that year. And it was on the sociology of the Caribbean, just all the many fascinating aspects of culture that emerged in your region. I mean, you have such an interesting mixture, just looking at the backgrounds of your countries. And I remember my last exam in college was comparing Rastafarianism in Jamaica with Vodou in Haiti and how some of those ancestral beliefs affected the modern development of those countries.

And I just want to say that, at least in me, I want you to know that you have a true friend of the Caribbean, someone who, again, is very cognizant of the critical role that your region has always played in the development of our country, and I think it is – you’re part of our past, you’re part of our present, and part of our future, and vice versa, I think. And I just want to, on that note, say how pleased and excited I am to welcome all of you here. And I hope this is a very enriching experience for all of you, as I’m sure it will be for us. Thank you very much. (Applause.)

MS WALKE: Thank you. And may I now ask Prime Minister Pierre of Saint Lucia, our CARICOM chair, to please come to the podium to deliver your remarks? Thank you. (Applause.)

PRIME MINISTER PIERRE: Thank you very much. Good morning, everyone. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, Assistant Secretary Juan Pablo, fellow heads of government, heads of delegation, ladies and gentlemen, I’ve been told I have three minutes. (Laughter.)

DEPUTY SECRETARY LANDAU: I’m sorry. I went way over on mine, so —

PRIME MINISTER PIERRE: I shall remain within my three minutes. Good morning, everyone. I speak as Prime Minister of Saint Lucia and chairman of the Caribbean Community. I thank the Government of the United States for convening this dialogue and for its hospitality. This meeting responds to the call by CARICOM leaders for political-level consultations following our constructive engagement with Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Saint Kitts and Nevis in February.

We value this relationship. Our countries are connected by geography, commerce, tourism, family, and friendship. The Caribbean community is a close neighbor, a stable democratic partner, and a region open to investment. We seek a more strategic partnership sustained by regular dialogue and measured by improvements in the daily lives of our people.

For Caribbean families, energy security means affordable electricity. Economic cooperation means jobs, investment, and opportunity. Security cooperation means safer communities. Disaster preparedness means knowing that help will arrive when it is needed and will arrive promptly. These are shared interests.

Our discussions today should translate into practical commitments financing for resilient energy systems, predictable trade and stronger commercial partnerships, secure infrastructure, stronger health systems and disaster response, and coordinated action against organized crime and illicit firearms trafficking. Haiti must remain central to our attention. We appreciate the U.S.’s role and welcome the extension of the United Nations mandate for the Gang Suppression Force. CARICOM continues – continues its work through the Eminent Persons Group. Sustained international assistance and credible elections with the widest possible participation are essential to restoring confidence and supporting Haiti’s return to stability.

Our dialogue must also make room for immigration and migration matters, with profound implications for our communities and our people-to-people ties. The strength of today’s meeting will be demonstrated by what follows it. Let us connect political dialogue with sustained technical engagements, identify priorities, and establish clear arrangements for follow-up between governments and the private sector. The CARICOM Secretariat will help coordinate the community’s technical work alongside our national authorities and regional institutions. CARICOM comes to this table ready to listen, ready to engage, and ready to build a partnership that delivers mutual benefit, with respect for our sovereignty and our shared aspirations.

I look forward to these discussions and the (inaudible) development of the people of the region. I thank you. (Applause.)

Tags
title: Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau With Saint Lucia Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre at the Opening Remarks of the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue

Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland
WASHINGTON – Today, Representatives April McClain Delaney, Glenn Ivey, Steny Hoyer, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Sarah Elfreth, and Johnny Olszewski and U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) released the following statement regarding last night’s ruling by a federal judge, temporarily halting the Trump Administration’s efforts to close the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center (BARC) in Beltsville, Maryland.
“As we’ve said time and again, this Administration’s attempts to shutter BARC are not only unwise – they’re illegal. BARC conducts critical research that helps farmers across our nation put food on the table for American families – including combatting serious threats to our agriculture, like cyclospora and avian flu. Last night’s ruling from a federal judge made plain: the Administration’s efforts are in clear violation of Congressional intent. We will continue fighting back against the Trump Administration’s lawless attempts to close this facility, undermining its crucial research on behalf of American farmers and families.”
The lawmakers have repeatedly stressed the importance of maintaining BARC, including, most recently pushing Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins on this matter in April. Additionally, they have raised this issue in Committee hearings with Administration officials and fought for language in Congressional Appropriations and the most recent Continuing Resolution.
title: Maryland Delegation Members Release Statement on Judge Ruling Halting Trump Administration Efforts to Close BARC in Beltsville, Maryland

text:
DOJ, ATF, Law Enforcement Partners Conclude Operation Show Me Justice
The Department of Justice, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri, and others today announced the conclusion of Operation Show Me Justice, an ATF-led high‑impact violent crime enforcement surge in St. Louis.
The DOJ‑sponsored operation was a whole‑of‑government initiative led by ATF and carried out in close coordination with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Missouri and in partnership with the St. Louis Metropolitan Police Department, USMS, Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), FBI, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), and other federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies.
“Operation Show Me Justice demonstrates exactly what happens when federal, state, and local partners unite behind a single mission: protecting communities from violent criminals,” said Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter. “The results speak for themselves. Dangerous criminals are off the streets, their weapons are out of circulation, and families in St. Louis are safer today than they were before.”
“Operation Show Me Justice delivered the kind of decisive action the public should expect from ATF,” said ATF Director Rob Cekada. “We removed violent offenders from the street, cut off their access to firearms, and dealt a significant blow to the criminal networks endangering this community.”
“By removing these dangerous firearms from St Louis, together, we have achieved unprecedented results, not just for the partners who participated in Operation Show Me Justice, but for all the residents, commuters, students, and visitors to the Gateway City,” said Director Gadyaces S. Serralta of the U.S. Marshals Service.
“We in St. Louis are very grateful for the women and men of ATF who left home, came to our community, and faced daily danger to assist in this enforcement effort,” said U.S. Attorney Thomas C. Albus for the Eastern District of Missouri. “Just as important, we are grateful to all local, state, and federal law enforcement and prosecutors who fight violent crime every day and who will remain. We are in this for the long haul and want so much to help continue to drive down violence for the health and safety of our city that we love.”
“Driving down violent crime takes relentless follow-through, and our partnership with ATF and our other law enforcement partners helps us turn local intelligence into cases that hold violent offenders accountable,” said St. Louis Metropolitan Police Chief Robert J. Tracy. “Operation Show Me Justice builds on that daily collaboration and our commitment to lasting progress—so every neighborhood can experience a safer St. Louis.”
The operation focused on violent criminal conduct and the illegal supply of firearms to violent offenders. During the operation, ATF and its partners arrested more than 435 violent offenders, including individuals with histories of possessing machine guns illegally, carrying stolen firearms, resisting arrest, violating felon‑in‑possession laws, engaging in straw purchasing, and committing other serious weapons-related offenses.
Agents, officers, analysts, and prosecutors combined local intelligence with ballistic leads from the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network (NIBIN) and insights from crime‑gun tracing to drive investigations forward. This coordinated approach enabled investigators to connect shootings, link firearms to multiple crime scenes, identify gun and drug trafficking patterns, and develop leads that otherwise would remain isolated across jurisdictions.
NIBIN compares ballistic evidence from crime scenes with test‑fired shell casings from recovered firearms, generating actionable leads. Crime‑gun tracing tracks a firearm’s commercial history, from the manufacturer or importer to its first retail sale. When paired with traditional investigative work, these tools help investigators identify shooters, associates, firearms traffickers, and sources of crime guns fueling violence.
Operation Show Me Justice has delivered significant enforcement results in St. Louis, with 435 criminal arrests and 166 firearms seized to date. Participating agencies have cleared 412 warrants, including the execution of 32 search warrants, and seized 81 kilograms of drugs, six machine gun conversion devices, and more than $1.25 million in currency related to suspected illegal firearms and drug transactions.
title: DOJ, ATF, Law Enforcement Partners Conclude Operation Show Me Justice

WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) announced that its Million Dollar Pitch Competition will stream starting October 20 on Prime Video and YouTube. The high-stakes contest, hosted by Dean Cain and judged by celebrity entrepreneurs Nicki Minaj, Grant Cardone, and Joe Gebbia, was taped before a live audience in Washington, D.C., where five finalists pitched their small businesses for a chance to win a portion of a $1 million cash prize pool funded by Clover Network, Inc. (Clover). The show includes a special appearance by President Donald J. Trump and recalls the vision he shared with the nation during The Apprentice, an award-winning show that celebrated the tenacity and vision required to compete and win in business.
“The Trump SBA is thrilled to announce that the Million Dollar Pitch Competition will stream on Prime Video and YouTube reaching audiences across our country and around the world, celebrating 250 years of free enterprise, American exceptionalism, and the hardworking small businesses that make it possible,” said SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “Competing nationally to reach the stage, five exceptional entrepreneurs put everything on the line to earn a share of a $1 million cash prize pool – showcasing the grit, vision, and sacrifice of Main Street leaders who believe in the American Dream. The SBA is proud to highlight the importance and contributions of our nation’s small businesses, while inspiring the next generation of entrepreneurs, risk-takers, and innovators to build their future.”
Launched as part of the SBA's Freedom 250 celebration, the Million Dollar Pitch Competition marks the culmination of a nationwide entrepreneurship contest created to honor the innovation, grit, and economic impact of America’s Main Street businesses. The five finalists put their business acumen, growth strategies, and vision to the test – while sharing the personal stories of resilience and sacrifice that brought them to the national stage. The special gives audiences across America and around the world a window into the families, workers, and communities that power our nation’s economy from jobs to innovation and growth in every state.
The following national finalists are featured in the Million Dollar Pitch Competition finale:
- Paul Melrose, Compotech, Inc. (Brewer, Maine)
- Lisa and George Winton, Winton Machine (Suwanee, Georgia)

Washington, D.C. — Today, Rep. Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), together with Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Ron Wyden (D-OR), with all Oversight Democratic Members and Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY), introduced the Epstein Wall Street Records Act. This bill seeks accountability for the financial institutions and bank executives that enabled disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation.
“Jeffrey Epstein used his immense wealth to abuse women and girls for decades. Meanwhile, banks and financial institutions enriched him and themselves by servicing his accounts and helping him move money around. We need to know what financial institutions and their executives knew about Epstein, whether they complied with relevant law, and what regulatory agencies learned,” said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.
“I have spent the last year calling on Donald Trump’s financial regulators to launch investigations into the big banks and executives who may have enabled Jeffrey Epstein’s horrific crimes,” said Senator Elizabeth Warren. “Since they have failed to act, Congress must. The bipartisan Epstein Wall Street Records Act will ensure overdue accountability for the wealthy and well-connected on Wall Street who put profits over people.”
“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act is about transparency and releasing financial records that are critical to holding the Epstein Class accountable and fighting to get justice for the survivors. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan bill,” said Congressman Ro Khanna.
“The Epstein Wall Street Records Act requires the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, the Comptroller of the Currency, and the SEC to release their files on Jeffrey Epstein’s money,” said Congressman Thomas Massie. “The Epstein Files Transparency Act forced the Attorney General to release DOJ, FBI, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices’ files. This bill does the same for bank regulators. Justice for the survivors means following the money.”
“Jeffrey Epstein’s sex trafficking operation left a money trail, and Wall Street has serious questions to answer. Our legislation will force federal regulators to release their records, investigate the banks and executives who may have enabled his crimes, and hold lawbreakers accountable,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Epstein’s survivors deserve the full truth, no matter how powerful or well-connected those responsible may be.”
“For far too long, financial institutions have leveraged their power, influence, and privilege to evade accountability. Their role in enabling Jeffrey Epstein’s decades of sexual exploitation and abuse demands serious scrutiny. That is why World Without Exploitation is proud to support the Epstein Wall Street Records Act of 2026,” said Becca Zipkin, Vice President of Policy and Programs, World Without Exploitation. “We must follow the money to uncover the truth and ensure that the financial institutions that enabled this abuse are held accountable. Survivors deserve transparency, accountability, and the justice they have long been denied.”
The Epstein Wall Street Record Act would require federal financial regulators to disclose supervisory records related to Epstein and his associates to Members of Congress and the American people, force the financial regulators to investigate Epstein-connected banks and executives for possible banking, securities, or illicit financing violations, and mandate industry bars and civil penalties for executives who assisted Epstein’s financial operations, as well as potential referrals of criminal violations to the Department of Justice if necessary.
###
title: Ranking Member Robert Garcia and Senator Elizabeth Warren Lead Bipartisan Bill to Hold Epstein’s Bankers Accountable

Staunch opposition to Donald Trump’s proposed vanity arch grew sharpy in early October, as veterans, residents, and workers expressed hostility to the project, and the Northern Virginia county that surrounds the site filed suit against it.
On October 1st, as NPR reported: “Veterans, retirees and lawmakers spoke out — against its scale, its cost, its lack of Congressional approval, its gaudiness, its intrusion on nearby Arlington National Cemetery and more.”
On October 7th, per the Associated Press: “The union representing thousands of flight attendants said Wednesday it has safety concerns about President Donald Trump’s proposed triumphal arch that will be on final approach to Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.”
On October 8th, the Washington Post reported: “Arlington County’s local elected body sued to block construction of President Donald Trump’s planned triumphal arch on Thursday, arguing that administration officials bypassed a key review process in their push to begin work on the structure.”
Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who represents a Northern Virginia district in the U.S. House that includes Arlington County, Arlington National Cemetery, and Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA), today issued the following statement:
“The Administration’s pursuit of Donald Trump’s deeply disrespectful arch has broken the law repeatedly, and now people from many backgrounds are banding together to fight it. I applaud Arlington County’s legal challenge, which rightly confronts the Administration’s illegal attempts to bypass legally required processes to assess the project’s impacts on the local community. Trump wants to avoid these assessments because everyone knows what an honest study would say: this arch is a costly boondoggle that would increase traffic and decrease air safety for the local community. The latter point has also been echoed by workers on the planes that fly in and out of DCA, and the safety concerns would be multiplied many times over if the structure were used as a base for military drones. The bottom line is that Trump’s arch is morally repugnant, and as his pursuit of it gets more corrupt the opposition will continue to grow.”
Rep. Don Beyer is leading congressional efforts to block construction of Trump’s arch. His Northern Virginia district includes the Arlington National Cemetery, where his parents, grandparents, and sister are buried. He is the author of the Arlington National Cemetery Viewshed Protection Act, which would explicitly prohibit construction of the arch. He previously raised concerns about the projects impacts on traffic in the region, which the Trump Administration has yet to address. The arch has been a consistent source of anger and concern to Beyer’s constituents, who like much of the country, vociferously oppose the project.
The National Park Service’s “Assessment of Effect” on President Trump’s proposed 250-foot “triumphal arch” found that the arch would “adversely affect” dozens of nearby historic sites and monuments, including Arlington National Cemetery, Arlington Memorial Bridge, the Lincoln Memorial, the Washington Monument, the National Cathedral, George Washington Memorial Parkway, and many others. The proposal currently faces legal challenges, which allege that it violates the National Historic Preservation Act.
title: Opposition To Trump’s Vanity Arch Grows

Rep. McDonald Rivet Launches Portal to Amplify Voices of Michiganders Facing Skyrocketing Health Care Costs
FLINT— Today, Congresswoman Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08) announced a new portal where constituents can share the impact of rising health care costs on them and their families. In the coming weeks, insurance companies will be posting their 2027 rate notices, and costs are expected to rise significantly, due in part to Congress’ failure to extend the Affordable Care Act’s (ACA) enhanced premium tax credits and the One Big Beautiful Bill’s massive cuts to Medicaid.
“Working families and seniors have been paying the price all year after out-of-touch Washington policies gutted our healthcare. Now, premiums are about to go even higher in 2027,” said Congresswoman McDonald Rivet. “Higher costs will force more people to drop their coverage, make it harder to see a doctor, and stretch more families’ budgets to the breaking point. Until Congress stops the political games, we will keep bringing mid-Michigan’s stories to Washington to show how devastating these cuts are.”
Residents of Genesee, Saginaw, Bay, and Midland Counties are encouraged to share their health care story at McDonaldRivet.house.gov/ShareYourStory.
In January 2026, Congress refused to extend the ACA tax credits, which reduce out-of-pocket health care insurance premium costs for hard working Americans. The tax credits’ expiration contributed to Michigan having the sixth-biggest decline in ACA enrollment in the nation in 2026. In 2027, nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts will take effect as a result of Republicans' so-called “Big Beautiful Bill.” Employer-sponsored health plans are expected to raise premiums by at least 8.2% nationally, the largest rate hike since 2003. In Michigan, rates for Individual Marketplace plans are expected to increase by an average of 14.2% in 2027.
Throughout her first term in office, Congresswoman McDonald Rivet has been working to prevent these hikes and fix our healthcare system. For example:
- In July 2025, the Congresswoman voted against Republicans’ trillion-dollar Medicaid cuts, and spoke about the local consequences alongside health care workers and a Flint family that relies on Medicaid for cancer treatments.
- Later that month, she called on Republican colleagues to join her in supporting the Health Care Affordability Act of 2025, which would make the ACA tax credits permanent.
- In September 2025, the Congresswoman led three dozen of her colleagues in demanding Congressional Leadership support efforts to extend the ACA tax credits.
- In the months leading up to the tax credits’ expiration, the Congresswoman elevated the voices of constituents from across the district. 
  - In October 2025, she stood with a mother from Midland whose insurance premiums were expected to jump by 18% to call on Congress to renew the ACA tax credits and lower costs in Saginaw.
  - In November 2025, she hosted a roundtable discussion in Flint with local health care administrators and community members who rely on the ACA tax credits.
- In November, the Congresswoman voted against the government funding package that failed to lower health care costs.
- In January 2026, the Congresswoman helped pass an extension of the ACA tax credits through the House of Representatives. The Senate refused to vote on that bill.
title: Rep. McDonald Rivet Launches Portal to Amplify Voices of Michiganders Facing Skyrocketing Health Care Costs

text:
Davids Demands Accountability Following ICE Sweeps in Southwest Kansas, Citing Threats to Ag Economy and Grocery Prices
Today, Representative Sharice Davids called on Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to answer for the economic fallout of recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) enforcement sweeps in southwest Kansas. Davids highlighted the severe disruption to Kansas’ agricultural economy, local small businesses, and food supply chains following sudden enforcement sweeps, which could raise beef and grocery prices.
"I write to raise grave concerns regarding recent... ICE operations in western Kansas... where sudden enforcement sweeps... immediately paralyzed local agricultural economies, threatened to push grocery prices even higher, and left small businesses shuttered across the region,” wrote Davids. “While I continue pushing both parties for common-sense immigration reform... we need immediate accountability. I urge you to commit to immigration enforcement that coordinates with local law enforcement, respects legal workers, and does not rely on racial profiling or significant economic disruptions for the sake of headlines or mass panic."
Recent federal enforcement operations in Dodge City, Garden City, and Liberal resulted in 104 arrests, sparking widespread panic across southwest Kansas — a crucial hub responsible for more than 20 percent of the nation’s daily cattle slaughter.
The abrupt operations severely disrupted local meatpacking plants, causing a nearly 16 percent single-day drop in fed-cattle slaughter and an overall 8.5 percent week-to-week decline, according to USDA reports. Local businesses were forced to temporarily close their doors, while union representatives and economists warned that halting plant operations will drive beef prices far beyond ground beef's already elevated $7.16-per-pound average.
Major Kansas agricultural organizations have voiced sharp criticisms of the uncoordinated federal actions:
"These ICE operations are having a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving. Additionally, these types of disruptions will lead to higher beef prices for consumers… These disruptions come at a time of enhanced focus and pressure on the cattle and beef supply chain. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain. Frustratingly, the harm these actions cause to cattle producers last for days and weeks after such operations conclude.” — Kansas Livestock Association
“Kansas dairy farms depend on a reliable workforce to provide consistent, around-the-clock care for animals. Recent [ICE] enforcement activity has created significant uncertainty and concern among workers, including those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. We urge federal officials to carry out enforcement actions in a lawful, orderly, and transparent manner that respects due process and provides clear, timely communication to affected employers, workers, local law enforcement, and communities.” — Kansas Dairy Association
Read Davids’ full letter here or below
Dear Secretary Mullin,
I write to raise grave concerns regarding recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations in western Kansas, where sudden enforcement sweeps in Dodge City, Garden City, and Liberal resulted in 104 arrests, and immediately paralyzed local agricultural economies, threatened to push grocery prices even higher, and left small businesses shuttered across the region.
I believe in the importance of enforcing federal immigration laws and protecting Kansas families from crime. In this instance, however, I have heard concerns from agriculture and business stakeholders about how these activities were conducted and their impact on communities across the state. Kansans have shared with me several instances of citizens and documented persons being targeted on their way to work or going about their day, and in many cases, local law enforcement was not consulted.
Southwest Kansas is a crucial hub for American agriculture – home to more than 20 percent of the country’s daily cattle slaughter. ICE’s activities corresponded with an 8.5 percent drop in cattle slaughter week-to-week according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture as meatpacking capacity was significantly disrupted. The Kansas Livestock Association stated last month that these operations, “[had] a massive chilling effect on the legal, documented, skilled workers that put beef on the table and keep the cattle supply chain moving…. They are a costly and unnecessary impact to cattle producers already suffering from unwelcome political interference to both the markets as well as the physical supply chain.”
This comes as Americans are struggling with staggeringly high grocery prices – including the price of ground beef jumping 7.9 percent year-to-year – and the smallest cattle herd in decades.
The immigration enforcement efforts also delivered a notable hit to Kansas’ dairy industry, which accounts for more than $3 billion in economic impact and 11,000 jobs statewide. The Kansas Dairy Association shared that ICE’s activities, “created significant uncertainty and concern among workers, including those who are legally authorized to work in the United States.”
While your agency frames these multi-day September 2026 operations as targeted at individuals with criminal histories, the immediate fallout has inflicted severe collateral damage on southwest Kansas’s economy, national food supply chains, and working families already struggling at the checkout counter. In addition to notable impacts on the agriculture sector, ICE’s activities led to local business closures and school absences.
These extreme actions leave Kansans feeling less safe, strain local economies, and disrupt national supply chains. While I continue pushing both parties for common-sense immigration reform – securing our border against violent crime and drug trafficking while supporting our agricultural sector – we need immediate accountability.
I urge you to commit to immigration enforcement that coordinates with local law enforcement, respects legal workers, and does not rely on racial profiling or significant economic disruptions for the sake of headlines or mass panic.
Sincerely,
title: Davids Demands Accountability Following ICE Sweeps in Southwest Kansas, Citing Threats to Ag Economy and Grocery Prices
