EPA Regional Administrators Visit Farms in Maryland and Kentucky to Highlight Soil Health, Water Quality, and Agricultural Partnership
PHILADELPHIA, PA / ATLANTA, GA (October 15, 2026) - U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Regional Administrators from the Mid-Atlantic (Region 3) and Southeast (EPA Region 4) recently toured farms in both Maryland and Kentucky to highlight the importance of regenerative agriculture practices that support healthy soils, cleaner water, and long-term farm resilience.
In support of President Trump’s recent executive order, “Advancing regenerative agriculture and strengthening American farm resilience,” these visits underscored the value of voluntary, locally informed conservation practices such as cover crops, reduced tillage, nutrient management, rotational grazing, buffer plantings, and other approaches that can improve soil structure, retain moisture, reduce erosion, and limit nutrient loss to nearby waterways.
Hosted by Regenified, a regenerative verification program, the visits provided the Regional Administrators an opportunity to meet directly with farmers and have discussions focused on practical approaches that can improve land management, reduce runoff, strengthen watershed protection, support supply chain resilience and advance the continued success of American agriculture.
“Farmers are at the heart of America’s food supply, our rural economy, and our environmental progress,” said EPA Mid-Atlantic Regional Administrator Amy Van Blarcom-Lackey. “These visits are about listening, learning, and recognizing the innovation farmers are already putting to work—from improving soil health and protecting water quality to adopting practices that keep their operations productive, resilient, and profitable for future generations.”
“Across the Southeast, we see every day how conservation-minded farming practices can strengthen both the land and the local economy,” said Southeast Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber. “EPA’s role is to support that work by partnering with states, farmers and local organizations to share information, reduce barriers, and help communities put practical solutions to work.”
About Regenified
Regenified is a practice and outcome-based land verification and product certification program that champions regenerative agriculture. Founded by a team of regenerative farming pioneers, experts, and innovators, Regenified promotes practices that enhance biodiversity, soil health, water quality, and nutrient density while aligning with nature. Regenified verifies and certifies farms, ranches, and products that restore ecosystems and regenerate soil, ensuring a legacy for future generations. Committed to cultivating a regenerative world, Regenified guides farms and brands toward practices that rejuvenate the Earth, support thriving ecosystems, and transform agriculture into a healing force for our planet.
About Harborview
Harborview Farms produces corn, wheat, and soybeans for the Mid-Atlantic region focusing on sustainable agriculture and environmental stewardship. The Hill family has been farming in Rock Hall, MD since the early 1900s. Today, Harborview Farms is owned and managed by Trey and Cheryl Hill and his father Herman Hill, and they are both committed to producing grain in a responsible and environmentally friendly manner.
title: EPA Regional Administrators Visit Farms in Maryland and Kentucky to Highlight Soil Health, Water Quality, and Agricultural Partnership

text:
Owner of Health Care Software Company Sentenced to 19 Years in Prison for $1B Medicare Fraud
A Kansas CEO and owner of an internet platform was sentenced yesterday to 19 years in prison for his role in operating a platform that generated false doctors’ orders and prescriptions to defraud Medicare and other federal health care benefit programs out of more than $1 billion.
“The Department of Justice and our agency partners dismantled one of the largest telemedicine fraud schemes ever, and yesterday’s lengthy prison sentence holds the orchestrator of that scheme accountable,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “The defendant’s fraud scheme lured hundreds of thousands of elderly and disabled Americans into a sophisticated international telemarketing system with one goal: stealing as much as possible from the Medicare trust fund. The Fraud Division will continue to leverage its resources to take down complex fraud operations like Blackman’s DMERx.”
“This sentence delivers a decisive warning: anyone who exploits VA programs and services for personal profit will be found and held fully accountable,” said Inspector General Cheryl L. Mason of the Department of Veterans Affairs. “The VA OIG remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to uncover complex fraud schemes and protect our nation’s veterans.”
“This 19-year sentence sends an unmistakable message: those who exploit federal health care programs for personal enrichment will face serious consequences,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HH-OIG). “Schemes that corrupt medical decision-making and siphon taxpayer dollars from programs serving vulnerable Americans undermine trust in our health care system. HHS-OIG and its law enforcement partners will continue to pursue those responsible and hold them accountable.”
“This sentencing sends a clear message that those who exploit federal health care programs for personal gain will be held accountable,” said Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office. “This scheme undermined the integrity of our health care system and defrauded taxpayer-funded programs designed to serve those in need. The FBI remains committed to working alongside our law enforcement partners to investigate complex health care fraud schemes, protect taxpayer dollars, and hold those responsible accountable. Through these efforts, we remain focused on defending the homeland and protecting the American people from those who seek to exploit our nation’s systems for personal gain.”
“This investigation reinforces DCIS’s steadfast commitment to protecting the integrity of the TRICARE program and ensuring that taxpayer-funded military health benefits are used appropriately,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Nakia Martin Alexander of the DCIS Southeast Field Office. “Fraud schemes that divert TRICARE resources erode the support promised to our service members and their families. As the criminal investigative arm of the DoD Office of Inspector General, DCIS remains focused on identifying these schemes and holding those responsible fully accountable.”
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Brett Blackman, 43, of Johnson County, Kansas, and his co-conspirators aggressively targeted hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries across the United States to get them to accept medically unnecessary orthotic braces and other items. They then arranged for purported telemedicine doctors to sign bogus prescription orders for these items so that their co-conspirators could bill Medicare for them. All told, Blackman and his co-conspirators billed Medicare and other federal health care benefit programs over $1 billion for this unnecessary equipment.
Blackman owned, controlled, and was the CEO of HealthSplash, which acquired Power Mobility Doctor Rx, LLC (DMERx) in Sept. 2017. DMERx was an internet-based platform that generated false and fraudulent doctors’ orders for durable medical equipment (DME) and prescriptions for other items. As part of the scheme, Blackman and his co-conspirators connected pharmacies, DME suppliers, and marketers with telemedicine companies that would accept illegal kickbacks and bribes in exchange for signed doctors’ orders created using the DMERx platform. Blackman and his co-conspirators took a cut for themselves in exchange for the referrals.
The fraudulent doctors’ orders and prescriptions generated by DMERx falsely represented that a doctor had actually examined and treated the Medicare beneficiaries when, in fact, the doctors were simply paid to sign orders and prescriptions without any meaningful interaction with the beneficiary, and in some cases, no interaction at all. Testimony and evidence presented at trial from an undercover agent who posed as a Medicare beneficiary showed the scheme in action — starting with a foreign call center that pushed the undercover agent to agree to multiple braces to a doctor signing bogus orders for the braces using Blackman’s DMERx platform. The doctor’s order for one of these undercover agent beneficiaries claimed that the doctor conducted various tests that can only be performed in person even though the doctor never even spoke with the undercover agent “patient.”
The DME suppliers and pharmacies that were paying illegal kickbacks for these orders billed Medicare and other insurers more than $1 billion. Medicare and the other insurers paid more than $450 million based on these claims. According to evidence presented at trial, Blackman and his co-conspirators concealed the scheme through sham contracts and by manipulating the doctors’ orders to avoid Medicare audits, including by removing references to telemedicine in the doctors’ orders.
As a result of Blackman’s scheme, Medicare was fraudulently billed for orthotic braces for more than 346,000 Medicare beneficiaries. On average, Medicare was billed for four braces per beneficiary, with Medicare being billed for at least 21 orthotics prescribed through Blackman’s DMERx platform to over 1,200 beneficiaries.
Exhibit from Trial Summarizing the Number of Orthotics Billed per Medicare Beneficiary as a Result of Blackman’s Fraud Scheme
After a 23-day jury trial ending in Apr. 2026, Blackman was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud, conspiracy to pay and receive kickbacks, and conspiracy to defraud the United States and to make false statements in connection with health care matters. Blackman’s restitution and forfeiture obligations will be determined by the Court at a later date.
In Dec. 2025, Blackman’s co-defendant, Gary Cox, was sentenced to 15 years in prison.
HHS-OIG, FBI, VA-OIG, and DCIS investigated the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief Darren C. Halverson and Trial Attorney Reginald Cuyler Jr. of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
title: Owner of Health Care Software Company Sentenced to 19 Years in Prison for $1B Medicare Fraud

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an Alert asking financial institutions to report potential Iranian regime abuse of religious charity networks, including diversion of religious tithes, or khums.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury will not allow the Iranian regime to continue its long history of abusing religious institutions to line the pockets of its elites and fund terrorism,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “By identifying and reporting this potential abuse, financial institutions can provide law enforcement with critical information to isolate the Iranian regime and its financial enablers.”
The Iranian regime has been known to abuse ostensibly religious organizations in Iran and neighboring countries to enrich its elites, fund the repression of the Iranian people, and support terrorism abroad. In addition, the regime co-opts khums payments from the global Shi’a community to further its destabilizing activities*.* In some cases, organizations that collect these payments do so on behalf of prominent Iranian ayatollahs with ties to the regime. These entities may use informal financial channels like hawalas and cash couriers to remit the funds to Iran or to Iran-linked actors. FinCEN’s Alert includes red flag indicators to aid financial institutions in detecting, preventing, and reporting this illicit activity.
Indicators of Potential Iranian Abuse of Religious Charities
- A charitable organization or nonprofit organization (NPO) solicits donations but does not appear to provide any charitable services, or openly supports the Iranian regime or its terrorist proxies, such as in fundraising appeals or on social media.
- A charitable organization or NPO receives large donations from an unknown source over a short period of time and then sends significant wire transfers or checks to other charitable organizations or NPOs.
- A charitable organization or NPO, or the customer’s employee, engages in behavior suggesting efforts to evade certain reporting or recordkeeping requirements.
- A customer receives transfers from a charitable organization or NPO with which the customer has no clear business relationship, and then the customer proceeds to withdraw the funds in cash or remit them onward.
FinCEN recognizes that legitimate charities should have access to financial services and can transmit funds through transparent channels. FinCEN reminds banks to apply a risk-based approach to customer due diligence requirements when developing the risk profiles of charities and other non-profit customers, as discussed in the Joint Fact Sheet on Bank Secrecy Act Due Diligence Requirements for Charities and Non-Profit Organizations.
###
title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iranian Regime’s Abuse of Religious Charity Networks

Krishnamoorthi Responds to Attempted Mass Shooting at His Family’s Hindu Temple in Aurora, Warns of Surging Anti-Indian Hate
SCHAUMBURG — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) issued the following statement after authorities arrested a 19-year-old man accused of attempting to carry out a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. According to prosecutors, the suspect, who espoused white supremacist and neo-Nazi beliefs, allegedly attempted to open fire Sunday before his rifle jammed. After he told coworkers what happened and shared plans to try again, they alerted police, who arrested him before he could return.
“I am horrified that a white supremacist attempted to carry out a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans at the Hindu temple in Aurora where my family worships. My family and I were there when the attack was attempted last Sunday. The threat of such violence shows how dangerous anti-Indian hatred and white supremacy have become, and we cannot wait until innocent people are killed to take these threats seriously. I am grateful to the suspect’s coworkers who alerted police and commend the law enforcement officers who intervened. Every American deserves to live and worship without fear, and we must stand together against hatred in all its forms.”
title: Krishnamoorthi Responds to Attempted Mass Shooting at His Family’s Hindu Temple in Aurora, Warns of Surging Anti-Indian Hate

Pappas Leads Bipartisan Call to Increase Home Heating Assistance Funding
Today Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) led a bipartisan group of 73 members in calling on the House Appropriations Committee to provide an additional $3 billion in emergency supplemental appropriations for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27).
In the letter, the members wrote, “As the war with Iran remains unresolved, energy prices are expected to keep rising, with heating oil up 60% since February. LIHEAP’s $4 billion in funding for the last fiscal year would fall significantly short in meeting the needs of American families this fiscal year.”
“LIHEAP is a critical lifeline for low- and moderate-income individuals, but even if your household qualifies, LIHEAP does not provide guaranteed security. Five out of six families who qualify for LIHEAP receive no financial assistance due to the program’s woefully underfunded status. When adjusting for inflation, LIHEAP funding is lower now than it was in 1981 when the program was first created. If LIHEAP was funded at the same level as it was 45 years ago, the program would have received nearly $7 billion in FY27,” they continued.
“Emergency LIHEAP assistance is urgently needed as winter weather approaches and colder temperatures have already begun. Families should not have to choose between staying warm and purchasing other essential items like food, medication, or rent. Congress must act and not leave families in the cold,” they concluded.
LIHEAP helps low-income individuals and families pay for heating and cooling and mitigates the impacts of rising energy costs and extreme weather events. Across the nation, LIHEAP helps nearly 6 million households afford their energy bills, including nearly 30,000 households in New Hampshire, but Secretary Kennedy’s decision last year to fire all LIHEAP staff last year and President Trump’s repeated demand to cut all funding for the program has put this assistance at risk. In response, Pappas led 89 of his Congressional colleagues in calling for the protection of LIHEAP and the rehiring of all HHS staff who manage the LIHEAP program that were fired in April 2025. Pappas also led a bipartisan letter in November 2025 calling for immediate distribution of funds following delays in LIHEAP allocations to states. In April of this year, Pappas again led his colleagues in a bipartisan letter following additional LIHEAP delays from HHS.
Last month Pappas led a group of 116 bipartisan members in calling on HHS to take all necessary steps to ensure that LIHEAP funds are distributed to the states as soon as possible and no later than November 1, 2026. Pappas also recently introduced the American Homes First Act which would redirect $1 billion from President Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ slush to LIHEAP.
title: Pappas Leads Bipartisan Call to Increase Home Heating Assistance Funding

Justice Department Files Complaints Against the Cities of St. Paul and Portland Challenging Mask Ban and Identification Requirements for Federal Officers
Today, the Department of Justice filed two lawsuits against the Cities of St. Paul, Minnesota and Portland, Oregon, challenging their unconstitutional attempts to regulate federal law enforcement officers by prohibiting federal officers from wearing masks and requiring them to provide identification in the manner prescribed by Code of Ordinances of the City of Saint Paul, Minnesota §§ 268A–268B and P.C.C. §§ 23.30.030, 23.30.100.
Not only are these laws illegal attempts to regulate the Federal Government, but, as alleged in the complaints, the laws threaten the safety of federal officers who have faced an unprecedent wave of harassment, doxxing, and even violence. Threatening officers with prosecution for simply protecting their identities and their families also chills the enforcement of federal law and compromises sensitive law enforcement operations.
“Under the Supremacy Clause of our Nation’s Constitution, states and localities cannot regulate the Federal Government and its law enforcement officers,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. “And they certainly cannot enact laws that place the safety of federal law enforcement at risk and undermine federal operations authorized by Congress. This Department of Justice will never tolerate the doxxing or harassment of federal officers, or any law like those in St. Paul and Portland that enables violent behavior against federal law enforcement officers and their families.”
“These St. Paul and Portland local laws are a direct regulation of federal law enforcement operations and threaten severe consequences for officers and public safety alike,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The Federal Government, not state and local governments, gets to decide which equipment federal officers may or may not wear when performing their official duties.”
“Aside from being unconstitutional, laws like these impede federal law enforcement’s ability to keep Oregonians safe and endanger the brave men and women of federal law enforcement,” said U.S. Attorney Scott Bradford for the District of Oregon. “They live in our communities. Their kids go to school in our communities. They care about our communities. They are part of our communities. It is unfair and improper to vilify them for political purposes.”
Attorney General Blanche has instructed the Department’s Civil Division to identify state and local laws, policies, and practices that facilitate violations of federal laws or impede lawful federal operations. Today’s lawsuits are the latest in a series of lawsuits brought by the Civil Division targeting illegal policies designed to thwart federal law enforcement across the country, including in New York, Virginia, Connecticut, New Jersey, California, Maryland, Philadelphia, Denver, and Milwaukee. Through these filings, the Department reaffirms that federal law enforcement operations cannot be compromised by state or local measures that violate federal law.
Note: Read the lawsuit against St. Paul here and Portland here.
Press Release Number: 26-1209
title: Justice Department Files Complaints Against the Cities of St. Paul and Portland Challenging Mask Ban and Identification Requirements for Federal Officers

text:
Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Target Scammers who Prey on Older Americans
WASHINGTON, DC — This week, Reps. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and Tom Barrett (MI-07) introduced the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act, a piece of legislation designed to streamline the reporting process for elder fraud. This bill will create an inter-agency framework to give law enforcement and prosecutors better information to fight fraud.
Reporting fraud is the first step to recovering stolen funds or preventing other would-be victims from falling prey to the same scam. Right now, there are ten federal agencies, most with their own separate intake channels, and a poorly coordinated set of federal reporting sites, plus 50+ state portals, with no single number to call and no designated first-click destination. As a result, fraud reporting is an overly complicated process that handicaps law enforcement efforts to quickly respond and, in some cases, recover stolen funds. This legislation will address these barriers.
Specifically, this legislation would:
- Designate a single front door for elder-fraud reporting, reachable two ways, by phone and on the web, to route each request to the federal agency whose mandate fits.
- The hotline should answer 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
- The website should also include digital resources for combatting the most common types of scams.
The new reporting framework would be similar to VSAFE, introduced by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs in 2024 to create a single number and website specifically for veterans to report fraud, scams, and predatory practices.
“People who steal from seniors and retirees are the lowest of the low. No one should have to navigate impenetrable government websites or spend hours stuck on hold trying to report these scams,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez. “ My bill makes it simple, you call one number or go to one site and your report goes directly to the investigator you need. When we give law enforcement the tools to fight back, they can respond immediately and take on these predatory scammers.”
“Fraudsters are constantly targeting seniors to cheat them out of their hard-earned retirement. These sophisticated scammers pose as federal agencies, banks, and even loved ones, while artificial intelligence is making impersonation easier than ever,” said Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07). “Families need resources to recognize and quickly report suspected fraud. By establishing a 24/7, one-stop shop for addressing elder fraud, this bipartisan bill will protect vulnerable seniors and empower law enforcement to crack down on these criminals.”
“When an older American falls victim to fraud, every minute counts. Yet victims and families are often left navigating a fragmented reporting system when they need help the most. No one should have to figure out which government agency to call while their life savings are at risk. By establishing a single national entry point, available around the clock, the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act of 2026 represents an important step toward protecting older Americans.”
- Yuksel Aydin, Director of the anti-scam website seniors.hcsk.org
“Reporting a scam should be as simple as one click or one call. But today, older adults who’ve been scammed face a maze of reporting options, leaving them unsure where to turn and often not reporting at all. Combating fraud requires a system that makes it easy for people to report scams and for authorities to track them. By creating one front door, a single website, and hotline, the One Front Door for Elder Fraud Act would give the growing number of older adults targeted by scammers the help they deserve.”
- Ramsey Alwin, President and CEO, National Council on Aging
During the appropriations process this year, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez advanced multiple provisions targeting scammers and helping working families keep their hard-earned money. This included encouraging the Department of Justice to pursue further action against crypto scams targeting older Americans and instructing law enforcement to work across jurisdictions to combat fraud and scams.
The legislation is supported by the National Council on Aging and seniors.hsck.org.
####
title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Introduces Legislation to Target Scammers who Prey on Older Americans

CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE HONORS ROCHESTER STUDENT AZALEA DIETZ WITH CONGRESSIONAL AWARD GOLD MEDAL
Dietz receives Congress' highest honor for young civilians in recognition of her commitment to community service, personal growth, and achievement
(Rochester, N.Y.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle recognized Rochester student Azalea Dietz with the Congressional Award Gold Medal, the highest honor bestowed by the United States Congress upon young civilians. The prestigious award recognizes Dietz's exceptional dedication to community service, personal development, physical fitness, and exploration.
“Azalea represents the very best of the next generation of leaders in our community,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “I am proud to recognize her achievements with this prestigious honor, and I hope her example inspires other young people across our community to get involved, pursue their passions, and discover the difference they can make.”
A student at Rochester's School of the Arts, Dietz has demonstrated a wide-ranging commitment to service and personal achievement. She volunteered at a local music and arts center, where she worked with children, assisted with summer camp activities, and supported the center's operations and photography needs. Her service also extended internationally to Portugal, where she volunteered at an animal rescue center caring for puppies and at a food bank packaging essential supplies for families in need. As part of her Congressional Award journey, Dietz planned and completed a five-day hiking expedition through the Adirondack Mountains alongside her mother and brother, tackling trails on Whiteface Mountain, Mount Jo, and Ampersand Mountain.
Established by Congress in 1979, the Congressional Award is a nonpartisan, voluntary, and noncompetitive program designed to encourage young Americans to set goals, challenge themselves, and make meaningful contributions to their communities. The program recognizes achievement in four areas: Voluntary Public Service, Personal Development, Physical Fitness, and Expedition/Exploration.
Young people interested in participating in the Congressional Award program are encouraged to contact Congressman Morelle's office to learn more about the program, eligibility requirements, and how to get started.

WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, joined Co-Chairs of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Representatives Mike Quigley (IL-05), Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), and Joe Wilson (SC-02) in leading a bipartisan letter urging President Trump to fully implement the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
“As Russia prepares to wage a fifth winter campaign against Ukraine, the United States has an opportunity to reinvigorate peace efforts by placing maximum pressure on Vladimir Putin and the governments and networks that finance his war,” the lawmakers wrote. “Utilizing the tools for economic pressure in this law will be decisive in forcing Putin to take peace talks seriously.”
In the letter, the lawmakers urged the Administration to:
- Fully enforce mandatory sanctions against Russian officials, oligarchs, banks, state enterprises, and foreign entities helping Russia evade existing restrictions.
- Impose secondary tariffs on major purchasers of Russian energy, targeting revenue from oil and gas sales that continues to finance Russia’s war.
- Crack down on sanctions evasion, including foreign financial institutions, shadow fleet operators, and intermediaries facilitating Russian energy transactions.
- Protect U.S. allies by applying exceptions and tariff adjustments for countries actively reducing their dependence on Russian energy.
- Strengthen congressional oversight by providing implementation details, tariff justifications, and measurable benchmarks to assess the effectiveness of sanctions.
The lawmakers emphasized that Russia continues to rely heavily on oil and gas exports to finance its military operations, while intensifying attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure and commercial shipping in the Black Sea, threatening global food security. The letter also calls on the Administration to reverse course in issuing general licenses that could reopen Russian energy transactions and restore revenue to the Kremlin. The lawmakers requested answers ahead of the October 18 deadline on which sanctions and tariffs will be implemented, whether any provisions will be delayed or waived, and how the Administration will measure their effectiveness.

text:
MATSUI, LEADER SCHUMER, MARKEY, MENENDEZ, MENG LEAD COLLEAGES IN DEMANDING TRUMP FCC WITHDRAW PROPOSAL TO UNDERMINE E-RATE PROGRAM
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), and Representatives Rob Menendez (D-NJ) and Grace Meng (D-NY), led nearly the entire Senate Democratic Caucus and more than 60 members of the House Democratic Caucus in urging Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to withdraw the Commission’s damaging proposal to eliminate or limit the E-Rate program. In June, the Carr FCC voted to open a rulemaking examining E-Rate, which helps schools and libraries across the country afford reliable internet access.
For nearly 30 years, E-Rate has helped close the digital divide by ensuring that students and library patrons can access the internet regardless of their income or ZIP code. In 2025, E-Rate helped more than 158,000 schools and libraries pay recurring broadband bills, increase bandwidth, maintain secure internal Wi-Fi networks, and replace aging infrastructure. Ending or sharply curtailing E-Rate would impose severe costs on schools and libraries while weakening economic growth, undermining American technological leadership, and jeopardizing national security.
The E-Rate program has invested more than $69 billion to connect schools and libraries to the internet across the country. Massachusetts schools and libraries have received more than $950 million from the E-Rate program and another $97 million from the Emergency Connectivity Fund, a $7 billion program that Senator Markey created within the American Rescue Plan to provide devices and connectivity for students and educators at home.
In the letter, the lawmakers wrote, “Schools and libraries help develop the next generation of engineers, scientists, and cybersecurity professionals, including in communities that have historically lacked access to those opportunities. Cutting E-Rate would narrow that talent pipeline. Maintaining connectivity in every school and library is therefore an investment in America’s technological leadership, economic competitiveness, and national security.
The lawmakers continued, “We strongly support measures to protect children online and address concerns around excessive screen time. But cutting E-Rate is not a child-safety measure. E-Rate funds broadband connectivity — not laptops, tablets, applications, or online content — and recipients must already comply with the Children’s Internet Protection Act, including by using filtering and blocking tools, adopting internet-safety policies, and educating students about appropriate online behavior. States and local communities, meanwhile, are developing targeted policies governing when and how students use devices in schools — an appropriate way to address screen-time concerns, rather than cutting broadband support. The Commission should not use child safety as a pretext to dismantle the secure, managed broadband infrastructure that schools and libraries need to educate students and help them navigate the digital world safely.”

WASHINGTON — Today, Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Claudia Tenney (NY-24) introduced the bipartisan Internet Reach and Access Now (IRAN) Act to strengthen U.S. efforts to help the Iranian people access the open internet, communicate securely, and overcome the Iranian regime’s censorship, surveillance, and internet shutdowns.
“Freedom of expression and access to unrestricted information are fundamental human rights. The Islamic Republic regularly shuts down or restricts internet access while committing mass atrocities,” said Congresswoman Ansari. “President Trump has said 'help is on the way' for the Iranian people. Ensuring unrestricted internet access would actually help people immediately. I’m proud to introduce the IRAN Act, a bipartisan, noncontroversial, and not militarily invasive bill that would do just that.”
Iran remains one of the world’s most restrictive digital environments, with the regime routinely restricting internet access to suppress dissent, conceal human rights abuses, and isolate the Iranian people. The IRAN Act strengthens the U.S. internet freedom strategy for Iran by requiring regular reviews, implementation assessments, and congressional reporting, while evaluating emerging technologies such as VPNs, decentralized and peer to peer networks, and direct to cell satellite communications. The legislation also seeks to expand cybersecurity training and secure digital tools for journalists, human rights defenders, and other civil society actors, and directs greater coordination among federal agencies to help ensure U.S. sanctions and export controls do not unintentionally hinder access to open internet technologies.
“The Iranian regime knows that access to information is a threat to its grip on power, which is why it relies on censorship, surveillance, and internet blackouts to silence the Iranian people,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “The United States should stand with the courageous Iranians demanding basic freedoms by helping them stay connected to one another and the outside world. The bipartisan IRAN Act strengthens our internet freedom strategy, supports secure technologies that can overcome the regime’s censorship, and improves coordination across our government so these efforts deliver real results. The Iranian people deserve the ability to communicate freely, access independent information, and expose the regime’s brutality to the world.”

text:
Rep. Panetta Leads Bipartisan Letter Raising Concerns About Meta’s Use of Research Tax Credit for Data Centers
Monterey, CA – United States Representatives Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) and Greg Steube (FL-17) wrote a bipartisan letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressing concerns about reports that Meta is seeking to use the federal research tax credit for its data center buildout. The bipartisan letter, co-led by Reps. Mike Thompson (CA-04) and Suzan DelBene (WA-01), emphasized that any claims by Meta for the federal tax credit must meet the clearly defined requirements for qualified research and experimentation.
Congress established the research tax credit in 1981 amid concerns about declining private-sector research investment and U.S. technological competitiveness. By reducing the cost of qualifying research, the credit is meant to encourage businesses to pursue projects involving technical uncertainty and experimentation, rather than simply purchasing and deploying proven technology.
“We are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit,” wrote the lawmakers. “The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.”
To qualify for the credit, research must meet a four-part test, including being technological in nature, addressing technical uncertainty, seeking to develop or improve a product or process, and involving a process of experimentation. Certain activities, including research conducted after commercial production begins and duplication of an existing product or process, are excluded. The lawmakers emphasized that the scale or configuration of a data center does not, by itself, establish that its construction and equipment costs qualify.
“Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business,” continued the lawmakers.
“The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment,” concluded the lawmakers.
In addition to Reps. Panetta, Steube, Thompson, and DelBene, the letter was also signed by Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Donald Beyer (VA-08), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Sharice Davids (KS-03), Danny Davis (IL-07), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), John James (MI-10), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Hillary Scholten (MI-03), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Victoria Spartz (IN-05), Lori Trahan (MA-03), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).
The full text of the letter is available here and below:
Dear Secretary Bessent:
In light of concerning reports that Meta Platforms, Inc. is seeking to claim the research credit under 26 U.S.C. § 41 for substantial expenditures associated with its data center buildout, we write as Members of Congress to reaffirm that the credit is intended to incentivize qualified research and experimentation, not subsidize the routine deployment of existing technology. We believe that the credit remains a critical support for American innovation, but that an overly expansive interpretation of qualifying expenditures risks undermining its purpose by subsidizing ordinary capital investment rather than encouraging genuinely novel research.
Congress created the research credit as part of the Economic Recovery Tax Act of 1981 in response to declining private-sector research and development investment and concerns about U.S. technological competitiveness. The credit was designed to encourage companies to undertake additional research and experimentation, not to subsidize ordinary capital investment or the deployment of established technology.
Internal Revenue Code Section 41 and Treasury Regulation 1.41-4 establish specific requirements for activities to constitute qualified research. Research must satisfy the IRS four-part test, which mandates the research must aim to develop or improve a product, process or technique, be technological in nature, eliminate uncertainty about capability, design, or methodology and importantly belong to a process of experimentation. A company must pinpoint the specific components of a project that are technically uncertain and prove it used scientific experiments to overcome that uncertainty.
These limitations are particularly important in distinguishing genuine research and experimentation from ordinary commercial activity. IRS guidance makes clear that research conducted after the beginning of commercial production and the duplication of an existing product or process do not qualify. Likewise, uncertainty about how best to configure or implement existing technology does not, alone, establish that a taxpayer has undertaken the process of experimentation required by Section 41. The IRS has repeatedly found that proven and commercially available equipment and technology is not eligible for the credit.
As a result, we are concerned by Meta’s apparent position that expenditures associated with its massive data-center buildout qualify for the research credit. The purchase and deployment of commercially available servers, networking equipment, electrical infrastructure, cooling equipment, and other proven technologies cannot be transformed into qualified research merely because they are installed at unprecedented scale or in new configurations.
Allowing ordinary data-center construction and deployment costs to qualify would significantly expand the research credit beyond its intended purpose and risk converting an incentive for technological experimentation into a subsidy for capital expenditures that companies would undertake in the ordinary course of business.
The research credit is an important tool for promoting American innovation. Protecting its integrity requires ensuring that it rewards genuine research and experimentation rather than subsidizing routine capital investment.
We appreciate your attention to this matter and look forward to your response.
###
title: Rep. Panetta Leads Bipartisan Letter Raising Concerns About Meta’s Use of Research Tax Credit for Data Centers

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs processed a record-high 3.11 million disability compensation claims in fiscal year 2026, a testament to the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensuring Veterans can more quickly and conveniently access the benefits they’ve earned.
The 3,111,399 compensation claims VA processed in FY 2026 tops the prior record of 3,001,734 claims set in FY 2025. Until the second Trump Administration, VA had never processed more than 3 million claims per year.
VA’s focus on the timely processing of compensation claims has led to a dramatic reduction in the backlog of Veterans waiting for VA benefits. That backlog has been reduced by more than 70%, after it increased 24% under the Biden Administration.
Claims processing accuracy has improved despite an increased workload and is currently at 94% — the highest rate in two years. Additionally, VBA continues to grant more than 60% of the claims submitted by Veterans, and only about 3% of VBA’s decisions are appealed to the Board of Veterans’ Appeals.
“Under the leadership of President Trump, VA is making historic progress to better serve Veterans, and these record-breaking claims processing numbers prove it,” said VA Secretary Doug Collins. “Whether we’re lowering wait times, improving healthcare, or opening new VA facilities, we will continue to put Veterans first.”
These record-breaking claims processing numbers are one of many ways the Trump Administration is making VA work better for Veterans. Since Jan. 20, 2025, VA has:
- Reduced VA’s average disability claims processing time by 46% since Jan. 20, 2025.
- Eliminated the backlog of Veteran families waiting for VA healthcare.
- VA reduced paperwork by nearly two thirds for Veterans and survivors applying for VA benefits.
- Enrolled more than 300,000 new Veterans in VA healthcare in 2026.
- Opened 43 new VA healthcare facilities since Jan. 20, 2025, expanding healthcare access for Veterans around the country.
- Offered Veterans more than 3.4 million appointments outside of normal operating hours since Jan. 20, 2025, giving Veterans more timely and convenient options for care.
title: VA in FY 2026 processes the most claims ever

In the last year, TSA officers have been forced to work 88 days without on-time payment. Now, leadership has taken away their chairs.
Atlanta, GA – Today, Representative Lucy McBath (GA-06), is leading 37 of her House colleagues in urging TSA Administrator David P. Cummins support the well-being of TSA agents and the safety of the nation by reversing his decision to remove their chairs at document check stations in airports around the country. This letter is officially endorsed by AFGE, AFGE TSA Council 100, and AFGE TSA Local 554 in Atlanta. McBath, who was a flight attendant for 30 years before she came to Congress, represents many of the employees of Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International—America’s busiest airport.
“Transportation Security Officers, or TSOs, have an incredibly important job. They are the first line of defense in keeping Americans and their families safe during air travel,” the members write. “Since October of last year, officers at TSA have been forced to work 88 days without being paid on time. They have had to fight in court to protect their collective bargaining agreement from being unilaterally canceled and are now being told that they are not allowed to sit down while they perform their duties at checker stations. It is abundantly clear that these changes are intended to try to push officers out of their jobs with TSA, not to keep the American people safe or improve service.”
“This is about more than chairs,” the members continue. “This is about the respect that every person in the United States deserves at work and on the job. American workers are tired of being treated as expendable.”
“TSA officers have continued to show up and protect the traveling public through government shutdowns, delayed pay, and attacks on their collective bargaining rights. Removing chairs from document checker stations is yet another unnecessary hardship placed on an already strained workforce, and I commend Congresswoman McBath and her congressional colleagues for standing with our officers and demanding the dignity, respect, and working conditions they deserve,” said Aaron Barker Jr., President of AFGE Local 554.
In addition to Representative Lucy McBath, the letter is signed by Representatives Nanette Barragán, Salud Carbajal, André Carson, Troy Carter, Kathy Castor, Jasmine Crockett, Danny Davis, Mark DeSaulnier, Lois Frankel, Maxwell Frost, Robert Garcia, Sylvia Garcia, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Pablo Hernández, Val Hoyle, Glenn Ivey, Jonathan Jackson, Hank Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Tim Kennedy, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Betty McCollum, Christian Menefee, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Holmes Norton, Emily Randall, Mary Gay Scanlon, Greg Stanton, Mark Takano, Bennie Thompson, Gabe Vasquez, Marc Veasey, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Bonnie Watson Coleman, Nikema Williams, and Frederica Wilson.
The full text of the letter is available here.
title: McBath Leads Colleagues in Urging TSA Administrator to Respect the Dignity of Hard-Working Agents

MANCHESTER, NH – Today, U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon visited New Hampshire as part of her Returning Education to the States Tour.
Alongside New Hampshire Commissioner of Education Caitlin Davis, Secretary McMahon began her visit at the Manchester School of Technology, where she toured the specialized woodworking, cosmetology, and aviation programs to observe how the school equips students with high-demand technical skills. Then, she visited Southside Middle School, a public school serving students in grades 5 through 8, followed by a combined tour of the campuses at St. Joseph Regional Junior High School and Trinity High School. During her time in these classrooms, Secretary McMahon observed instruction across diverse subject areas, including fine arts, English, Spanish, pre-calculus, and early college personal finance.
To conclude her visit, Secretary McMahon hosted a roundtable with parents and students to discuss how state and federal education freedom initiatives impact families. The discussion also focused on how the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit – which New Hampshire has joined – will further multiply these opportunities in the Granite State.
“At every stop on the Returning Education to the States Tour, we are seeing firsthand the impactful work happening in classrooms and communities across the country,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “New Hampshire is demonstrating how states can build a more responsive education system by integrating rigorous academics, technical training, and flexible learning choices. By coupling local innovations with new federal tools like the Education Freedom Tax Credit, we are empowering families to bridge the gap between traditional instruction and personalized models, ensuring more students have the resources to meet their full potential.”
Background:
On her Returning Education to the States Tour, Secretary McMahon is traveling to all 50 states to hear directly from teachers, parents, students, and community leaders about what is working in their communities and to compile a toolkit of best practices to share with states across the nation. Learn more about Secretary McMahon’s Returning Education to the States Tour here.
title: U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon Visits New Hampshire on Returning Education to the States Tour

Ahead of Elections, Ramirez, Immigration Advocates Introduce a People-Centered Vision for Immigration Reform
Congress last acted on immigration reform 40 years ago, when President Ronald Reagan signed the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, which created pathways to citizenship for approximately 2.7 million immigrants.
Chicago, IL – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Committee on Homeland Security Subcommittee, immigration advocates, and community members unveiled the People’s Vision for Immigration Reform, a resolution outlining policy priorities to preserve and expand pathways to citizenship. As the elections approaches and the House of Representatives prepares for the 120th Congress, the resolution calls on the House of Representatives to pass real protections for immigrant communities.
The resolution calls on Congress to transform our immigration system and advance humane immigration reform with:
- Pathways to citizenship for the millions of undocumented, long-term residents of the United States who are our family members, friends and neighbors;
- Humanitarian protections that welcome with dignity those who are seeking safety and asylum in the United States, upholding our domestic and international legal obligations to provide refuge to those in need; and
- Expanded legal pathways for family and employment immigration, recognizing that family unity and strengthened protections for all workers in the United States are foundations of thriving communities for all.
“For years, administration after administration, Congress after Congress, has promised relief and has asked our communities to wait for the ‘right time,’ for the ‘politically convenient time,’” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “So today, we announced the People’s Vision for Immigration Reform – a resolution that reaffirms the commitment of Members of Congress to act in defense of our immigrant communities and preserve and expand pathways to citizenship. Now is the time to build a system that honors the contributions of our immigrant neighbors. No more excuses or peros.”
The resolution’s original cosponsors include Representatives Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (IL-04), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Federica S. Wilson (FL-24), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), and Al Green (TX-09).
“Immigrants have bound our communities together, continue to contribute to our economy, and embody everything that Americans are made of and striving to be. All of which they do while asking nothing in return but the opportunity to reach for and obtain the American Dream,” said Congresswoman Yvette Clarke. “The 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States must not be only the opportunity to reflect on how far we have come; it must be an obligation to remember the terrible price that we pay to reach here. The People’s Vision for Immigration Reform is in large part the only future for this nation worth fighting for.”
“It’s time to send out a strong vision of where we need to be. We have spent an awful lot of time in Washington talking about immigration enforcement this year, but not nearly enough time talking about how we fix the system that has been broken for decades,” said Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia. “We need an immigration system that gives people a fair chance. We can start by making progress now. That’s why I’m leading the discharge petition of the American Dream and Promise Act; we are just one signature away from getting a forced vote. We need to get serious about real reform, not another round of empty promises.”
The bill is endorsed by a coalition of more than 60 national and and local organizations, including Immigration Law Center (NILC), Fair Immigration Reform Movement (FIRM) and FIRM Action, National Immigrant Justice Center (NIJC), League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), Haitian Bridge Alliance, United We Dream (UWD), Refugees International, National Partnership for New Americans (NPNA), Immigrant Legal Resource Center (ILRC), Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), Human Rights First, Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, Justice in Motion, Indivisible, Service Employees International Union (SEIU), National Health Care for the Homeless Council, United Parent Leaders Action Network (UPLAN), Children's Rights, Unitarian Universalists for Social Justice, Community Change Action, Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR) and ICIRR Action, CAIR Chicago, Grassroots Collaborative, Warehouse Workers for Justice, National Korean American Service and Education Consortium (NAKASEC), Indivisible Chicago Alliance, Hana Center, Here to Stay Community Land Trust, Illinois Unidos, PASO, Organized Communities Against Deportation (OCAD), Massachusetts Immigrant and Refugee Advocacy Coalition, Jewish Council on Urban Affairs (JCUA), Colorado Immigrant Rights Coalition (CIRC), Popular Democracy, Florida Immigrant Coalition (FLIC), SIREN, Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice, Maine People's Alliance, We are CASA, Workers Defense Action Fund, Make the Road States, Voces de la Frontera, Make the Road New York, Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA), Council of Mexican Federations in North America (COFEM), Sunflower Community Action, East Bay Sanctuary Covenant (EBSC), Federación de Clubes Michoacanos en Illinois (FEDECMI), Nebraska Appleseed, and Pineros Y Campesinos Unidos Del Noroeste (PCUN).
“Over the last 40 years we’ve seen the consequences, not only the inability of Congress to prioritize legislation, but of the overreach of the Trump administration that has taken a sledgehammer to refugee admissions, temporary protected status, health care and food access and the basic simple notion that all people in this country deserve due process under the law,” said Lawrence Benito, ICIRR Executive Director. “We know we need permanent solutions, not chaos and fear. We’re here today to recommit to dignity and respect for all through legalization and keeping families together.”
“Let me be clear: Our economy works because of workers, and for generations, immigrant workers have poured their sweat, their strength, and their labor into building this country. Working families deserve to go to work, provide for their families, and return home safely without fear of being detained or disappeared,” Laura Garza, Executive Director at Arise Chicago. “Now is the time to demand real protections for communities. It’s time to expand pathways to citizenship and ensure all working families can live and work with dignity and safety. As communities mobilize across the country, we stand together in our power to change our country’s direction.”
“Immigrants deserve a system that provides dignity, fairness, and a real opportunity for a life in this country. Congress must do its job to defend our neighbors by creating viable pathways. Otherwise, the executive branch will be able to continue to sow chaos in our communities, return refugees to danger, and trample our Constitution,” said Keren Zwick, Executive Director at the National Immigrant Justice Center (NIJC). “NIJC stands ready to advance lasting solutions, even as we continue to fight the problems this administration created.”
“At PASO, we see the resilience of our communities, but resilience should never mean having to live in fear. Instead of being supported, our communities are increasingly being targeted because of their immigration status. But we have resisted, organized, advocated, and continue doing the work to prepare families for citizenship and help them navigate the immigration system. We have done our part, and now the federal government must do theirs. Because the truth is, no matter how much we prepare our communities, if the federal government fails to create real pathways to citizenship, our families will continue to face barriers,” Marien Casillas Pabellon, PASO Executive Director.
“While ICE and DHS terrorize our communities and attack and deport our neighbors, Congress has not acted. While most Americans support creating and ensuring legal pathways to citizenship for immigrants, Congress has done nothing. Their silence enables this administration's campaign of terror against immigrants and their families. Today, as voters, we must demand that our elected representatives take action to create pathways to citizenship and legal status and protect immigrants and their families from abuse by our government,” said Kathy Tholin with Indivisible Chicago.
“Asians are the fastest-growing racial group in the US, and 1 out of 7 undocumented immigrants is Asian. We are longstanding generations, mixed-status families, and new Americans who call this country home. We are all affected by the militarized violence, immigration backlogs, unaffordable costs, and attacks by this President and some Congress members against anyone they think doesn’t belong,” said Danae Kovac, HANA Center Executive Director. “Immigration affects all of us, and let me be clear: our country needs pathways to citizenship. HANA Center will continue to fight alongside Congresswoman Ramirez for Citizenship for All, not only for a pathway to citizenship, but also for the healthcare, education, climate justice, and more that we all need and deserve. Together, we, the people, can create an America where every person belongs and thrives.”
“It is long past time to lift up families and embrace the worth of each of our neighbors. It is time to reject the politics of fear and division that have marked too much of the discussion around immigration in recent years,” said Ed Yohnka, ACLU Illinois Director of Communications and Public Policy. “In recent months, we have seen how years of rhetoric meant to stall meaningful immigration reform can be turned to justify a military-style invasion of our communities and cause too many hard-working people to live in fear and isolation. Immigration policy does not have to be this way. Immigration policy can be based on a commitment to family unification, a commitment to fairness and due process, and a recognition of the dignity and worth that people from other countries and other cultures bring to the United States. 
“As a recently naturalized citizen, I have a message to those like me who can now exercise that power. The power of our vote. Let’s show our humanity in how we treat our neighbors, but also let’s show solidarity at the ballot box,” Fasika Alem, United African Organization (UAO) Programs Director. “Elections matter. Make a plan and vote.”
“Our church is home to Indigenous people and to immigrants, old and new. People without documents worship in our assemblies and lead our ministries. Scripture commands: ‘Love the stranger as yourself, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.’ For decades, our church has urged compassionate ways for longtime undocumented neighbors to gain legal status,” said Bishop Erik Christensen of the Metropolitan Chicago Synod of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America. “Forty years ago, Congress opened a path to citizenship and those who received status in time became citizens, homeowners, and neighbors. Now is the time to finish that work.
"As a Haitian immigrant, experiencing the agonizing pain and fear of the Haitian community every day who have lost TPS, I particularly welcome the resolution, because it brings to light all the changes needed in our immigration system to ensure the safety of our immigrant friends and family members who are here and deserve justice and dignity,” said Tessa Petit, Florida Immigrant Coalition Executive Director and Co-Chair of FIRM. “It is time for immigrants to no longer be treated as political pawns and sub-creatures, and this resolution will engage Congress to put an end to the abuse of our communities.”
“1 of every 4 ICE arrests happen in Texas. In just over three months, ICE shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, shot Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in Austin, hospitalized Miguel Parra-Hernandez after striking him with an ICE vehicle in Houston, and has separated countless of families,” said Lizeth Chacon, Workers Defense Executive Director. “Immigrant workers and their families strengthen and build our state – Texas is their home, and for many it has been for more than 30 years. It's time for Congress to act, for there to be an end to ICE violence and a real pathway to citizenship for all immigrant workers and their families.”
“For 25 years, my mother and I were both undocumented. We were able to adjust to legal permanent residency because we qualified for a U visa, something that only undocumented immigrants who are victims of a violent crime could apply for. There are over 12 million undocumented immigrants in the United States who have no pathway to citizenship and I sure wish not a single one ever needs to apply to a U visa,” said Jose-Arnulfo Cabrera, National Campaigns and Congressional Affairs Deputy Director, Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA). “But that is how broken our immigration system is and why Congresswoman Ramirez’s resolution is quite important today.”
The violence of the Department of Homeland Security under the Trump administration has only served to underscore citizenship's importance. Last week, a five year old child had to watch his father get shot by agents of our government. He is only the latest child to be failed by the unimaginable cruelty of the DHS's at-all-costs approach to mass deportations,” said Ben D’Avanzo, National Immigration Law Center. “But he was also failed by our completely broken immigration system that has allowed families to go without health care, be abused by their employers, and stripped of longtime protections. This resolution represents the right pathway, one that upholds our core values and refuses to pit immigrant communities against each other.”
“LULAC is proud to support Congresswoman Ramirez’s resolution to protect immigrant families, defend workers, and create pathways to citizenship. As America celebrates 250 years of independence, we should remember who helped build this country,” said Dr. Ray Serrano, National Director of Research & Policy, League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC). “Congress needs to act. Keep families together. Protect workers. Give people a fair chance at citizenship. Our families helped build this country. We deserve a place in its future.”
For the full text of the resolution, CLICK HERE.
To watch the full press conferences, CLICK HERE.
For photos of the event, CLICK HERE.

40 years ago, Congress passed the Immigration Reform and Control Act, creating a pathway to citizenship for approximately 2.7 million immigrants. Today, the American people are overwhelmingly in support of a pathway to citizenship, the popularity of which has grown because of the brutality we have witnessed over the last 2 years.
For more than a year, IL-03 has been targeted, terrorized, and attacked by DHS with zero accountability. Congresswoman Ramirez has led the call for a pathway to citizenship for all and accountability from DHS.

Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $550 Million Investment to Build New Amtrak Service in the Tar Heel State
Funds will be used to increase safety and decrease travel time between Raleigh and Richmond
RALEIGH, NC – The U.S. Transportation Department’s Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) today joined the North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) to celebrate obligating $550 million in federal funding to develop the new S-Line passenger rail route between Raleigh, North Carolina, and Richmond, Virginia. The long-awaited line will reduce travel time by up to 90 minutes, increase the number of trips, and improve reliability.
The S-Line announcement comes on the heels of Secretary Duffy’s $5.3 billion “Golden Age of Rail” nationwide grant package, which included an additional $300 million in funding to fix rail crossings as part of the NCDOT’s Piedmont Corridor Safety Program between Raleigh and Charlotte.
Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.
The federal investments into North Carolina rail include:
- $550 million for the future S-Line to make critical track repairs and upgrades on existing track with plans for additional funds to follow pending project success.
- $300 million for the existing Piedmont Corridor to close 9 at-grade rail crossings, construct 5 grade separations, and improve trespassing prevention infrastructure along the entire corridor.
“From launching the new Acela and Airo trains to overhauling New York Penn Station to today’s announcement in Raleigh, the Trump Administration is committed to investing in Amtrak to make passenger rail in America great again,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “Our additional rail safety investments are also an important reminder of the tangible difference we can make when we defund boondoggles like California’s train to nowhere and instead direct the funds to protect pedestrians, drivers, and riders in the Tar Heel State."
“This milestone is a testament to the strong partnership between the FRA, Amtrak, and NCDOT in advancing the S-Line and the earlier announced Piedmont Line corridors,” said FRA Administrator David Fink. “Through close collaboration, we are delivering vital investments that will modernize passenger rail and create a new Golden Age of Rail for the people of North Carolina.”
Additional Information:
When complete, the Raleigh-to-Richmond Passenger Rail Line is anticipated to save rail travelers 90 minutes when traveling between the two cities and will increase corridor bandwidth, allowing for more passenger and freight trips each day.
FRA’s $300 million investment in the Piedmont Corridor Safety Program is a key pillar of Secretary Duffy’s “Golden Age of Rail” package announced in August. Roughly $2 billion of this grant package is funding Secretary Duffy saved the American people by canceling Gavin Newsom’s disastrous high-speed train to nowhere.
title: Trump’s Transportation Department Celebrates $550 Million Investment to Build New Amtrak Service in the Tar Heel State

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05) joined Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06) to introduce the Title IX Take Responsibility Act, legislation that would hold schools accountable for mishandling reports of sexual assault and provide survivors a stronger path towards justice.
The legislation amends Title IX; a U.S. federal civil rights law passed as part of the Education Amendments of 1972 that bans sex-based discrimination in any education program or activity receiving federal money. The bill would reform how schools handle sexual assault and harassment by replacing outdated legal loopholes with clear accountability.
"One incident of sexual violence is one too many," said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes. "I am committed to protecting students, supporting survivors, and ensuring college campuses are safe learning environments for all. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act will put the responsibility on educational institutions for any mishandling of sexual assault reporting and failure to prevent further assaults. This legislation should be considered immediately, and I thank Congresswoman Dingell for partnering on this effort."
"For far too long, outdated legal loopholes have allowed educational institutions to turn a blind eye to reports of sexual assault, leaving survivors without justice or support," said Congresswoman Dingell. "Title IX was enacted to protect students, not to shield institutions from accountability when they fail to keep campuses safe. This bill closes these gaps and ensures that every student has access to a safe learning environment free from abuse."
Under current Supreme Court precedents, schools can only be held liable if high-level officials had "actual notice" and reacted with "deliberate indifference," creating an incentive for institutions to turn a blind eye. This bill eliminates that defense by holding schools legally responsible if they knew or reasonably should have known about the abuse and failed to take effective action. It also expands access to justice by allowing survivors to hold schools accountable in federal court for monetary damages and legal fees.
The legislation is endorsed by End Rape on Campus, Just Solutions, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence (NAESV), National Organization for Victim Advocacy (NOVA), Ujima, Volare, YWCA,
Survivors should never have to choose between their safety and their education. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act affirms survivors’ rights to support, to make their own choices about reporting, and to seek justice when their access to education is harmed. It also gives schools clear standards that reflect what effective, survivor-centered response looks like. NOVA strongly supports this bill,” said Claire Ponder Selib, Executive Director, National Organization for Victim Advocacy.
"Schools must take sexual misconduct more seriously. We're abandoning survivors and ignoring the enormous impact of sexual violence on their educational attainment, health, and quality of life. This is unacceptable. The National Alliance to End Sexual Violence applauds Representatives Dingell and Hayes for re-introducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. We must have more accountability," said Monika Johnson-Hostler, President & CEO, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence.
“YWCA USA is unwavering in our pursuit of a world where all women and girls can thrive. To meet that mission, it is essential that every student can learn in an environment free from sexual violence. Sadly, we know that violence does occur. The deeply disturbing reports from Cornell University underscore that passing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act is an essential and overdue step that would hold our educational institutions more responsible for protecting students from the start and accessing swift, meaningful pathways to justice and healing,” said Kate Kasper, VP of Public Policy and Advocacy, YWCA USA.
“I’m grateful to Reps. Dingell and Hayes for reintroducing the Title IX Take Responsibility Act. At moment when the Dept of Education is rolling back protections under Title IX and leaving survivors of sexual violence vulnerable, this bill would strengthen protections and where appropriate, hold institutions accountable,” said Lisalyn Jacobs, CEO of Just Solutions.
“Survivors should not have to sacrifice their education because an institution failed to respond meaningfully to sexual harassment or violence. The Title IX Take Responsibility Act strengthens survivors’ ability to enforce their rights and recognizes that students should be able to access meaningful support without being required to pursue an investigation. Survivors deserve options that protect their safety, well-being, and ability to continue their education,” said Volare CEO Bridgette Stumpf.
Text of the Title IX Take Responsibility Act is available here.
title: Hayes, Dingell Introduce Bill to Hold Schools Accountable for Mishandling Reports of Sexual Assault

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11) introduced the Heat Island Reduction Act, which would require federal agencies to plan cost-effective upgrades that cool their properties, improve air quality, and lower energy costs.
Parking lots and dark rooftops soak up heat and hold it, which warms nearby communities, raises cooling bills, and speeds the formation of smog. The bill targets federal properties in areas that already fail federal smog standards.
Northern Virginia is already working on the problem. This summer, more than 80 volunteers teamed up with the Faith Alliance for Climate Solutions and George Mason University’s Virginia Climate Center to map where heat hits hardest across Fairfax County, Arlington, and Alexandria. What they found points to simple fixes: more trees, more shade, and cooler surfaces. Walkinshaw’s bill would apply the same approach to federal properties nationwide.
“Extreme heat endangers workers, worsens the air our families breathe, and drives up cooling costs,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Volunteers here in Northern Virginia are working to pinpoint where heat hits hardest. The federal government should take the same hard look at its own properties and start with the fixes that deliver the most. Shade trees and cooler roofs protect federal workers and visitors and lower the cooling bills taxpayers pay.”
The Heat Island Reduction Act would:
    - Within six months: Require agencies to plan cooling fixes, such as trees, shade, cool roofs, and cooler pavement, for their properties in areas that fail federal smog standards.
- Six months later: Require agencies to set out each project’s cost, funding source, and timeline, and to update these plans every two years.
- Every year: Require the General Services Administration to report to Congress on progress, spending, and changes in temperature and energy use.
- At every step: Prioritize cost-effective fixes and build them into routine repairs and construction.
Congressman Paul Tonko (NY-20) and Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC) are original cosponsors.
Read the full bill text here.
