WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced the American Integrity Act to prohibit the live-streaming of executions under the Uniformed Code of Military Justice following President Donald Trump’s decision to cancel Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s plans to broadcast the execution of Nidal Hasan, the perpetrator of the horrific 2009 Fort Hood shooting.
The bill would establish a federal prohibition on live-streaming military executions, ensuring that such broadcasts cannot be authorized by future administrations.
The legislation comes after widespread opposition to the proposal, including from Vindman, who publicly called on Hegseth to reverse course and abandon plans to turn Hasan’s execution into a public spectacle.
“Having overseen the post-trial legal proceedings in Nidal Hasan’s case, I know firsthand the gravity of his horrific crimes. I believed then, and I believe now, that he should face the fullest consequences of the law,” said Vindman. “But there is a fundamental difference between carrying out justice and turning an execution into a public spectacle. Live-streaming executions is what terrorists and authoritarian regimes do. I’m glad the president ultimately reversed course, but we should never have reached this point in the first place. The American justice system must uphold the rule of law and the dignity of our institutions. My legislation will ensure that no future administration can turn an execution into a televised spectacle.”
The bill is sponsored by U.S. Representatives Reps. Ro Khanna (Calif.-17), Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-02), and George Whitesides (Calif.-27).
Click here to read the full bill text.
BACKGROUND
As an Army Judge Advocate General (JAG) officer, Vindman oversaw the post-trial legal proceedings following Hasan’s attack at Fort Hood. His direct involvement in the case gave him firsthand experience with the gravity of Hasan’s crimes and the importance of ensuring justice is carried out.
###
title: Vindman Leads Effort in U.S. House to Ban Live-Streaming of Military Executions in the United States

text:
Lofgren Demands Answers to Outstanding Oversight Requests, Warns EPA that Lack of Cooperation is Unacceptable
(Washington, DC) - On Tuesday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) sent a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin demanding that he comply with outstanding congressional oversight requests from the Committee.
“Since January 2025, I have sent a number of formal oversight letters to EPA requesting agency records, documents, and communications regarding various policies and activities,” writes Ranking Member Lofgren in her letter. “However, rather than providing the requested information in a comprehensive and timely manner, EPA has failed to produce a single responsive document, communication, or record.”
In closing, she writes: “EPA’s non-responsiveness to Committee oversight during the 119th Congress has been unacceptable. The agency must respect congressional prerogatives. We remain determined to obtain the information we need to perform our duties on behalf of the American people. EPA should understand that a lack of cooperation will not frustrate the Committee’s oversight permanently. It will merely strengthen our commitment to employing all the tools at our disposal to hold the agency accountable.”
In her letter, Ranking Member Lofgren requires a response from EPA to the Committee’s outstanding oversight requests by no later than 5:00 pm Friday, November 6th, 2026.
Access the letter here and below.
Dear Administrator Zeldin,
Agencies are required to comply with congressional oversight. It is an obligation, not a choice. But under your leadership, the EPA appears to have forgotten that basic principle. Since President Trump took office in January 2025, I have made multiple requests to the agency for internal records, documents, and communications related to various topics. These oversight requests are crucial to my ability to properly carry out my oversight duties as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, which possesses jurisdiction over environmental research and development programs at EPA. However, rather than providing the requested information in a comprehensive and timely manner, EPA has failed to produce a single responsive document, communication, or record. Instead, the agency has merely responded with letters that deflect questions rather than answering them. That was never acceptable. It becomes less tolerable with each passing month. I am writing to you to reaffirm my prior oversight requests from the 119th Congress, and to formally notify the agency that they remain outstanding. I expect EPA to promptly comply.
Since your confirmation as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) on January 29th, 2025, roughly 20% of the agency’s workforce has quit, retired, or been fired. Irreplaceable laboratory facilities have been shut down. The independent Office of Research and Development (ORD) has been wiped out. Scientific capacity has been gutted, scientific integrity is compromised, industry capture is widespread, and climate denialism is ascendant. In short, EPA’s basic mission to use the best available science to protect human health and the environment has been damaged under your leadership.
To take just one of countless examples, I have learned that the Office of Air and Radiation (OAR), acting under direct orders from former Assistant Administrator Aaron Szabo, has refused to grant the Office of Applied Sciences and Environmental Solutions (OASES) permission to conduct or publish virtually any air pollution research without prior approval from OAR political leadership. OASES is the ostensible successor to ORD, which was a global scientific leader in air quality and air pollution research. It is my understanding that OAR has categorically denied OASES the authority to conduct and publish its own air-related research without OAR political approval, except for narrow circumstances in which technical support from OASES cannot be avoided for OAR to meet certain statutory obligations. Indeed, OASES cannot even independently initiate air-related research without approval from OAR political appointees. OAR can only assert this control because of the agency’s new “no surprises” policy for OASES, which appallingly requires that OASES research “must be supported by appropriate political leadership” before it can proceed. The policy is a clear violation of scientific integrity, and the notion that EPA’s primary science office cannot even study air pollution without getting permission from the political appointees of a different office would be laughable if it was not so dangerous.
In my role as the Ranking Member of the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (“the Committee”), I have attempted to conduct oversight of these types of actions. There are many reasons for this oversight: to document the damage done to the agency and its workforce; to understand the scientific capabilities that have been lost and the implications of those losses for human health and the American people; to identify violations of scientific integrity and administrative procedure; and to comprehend why all of this happened in order to inform legislative efforts to reverse it and prevent it from ever happening again. Since January 2025, I have sent a number of formal oversight letters to EPA requesting agency records, documents, and communications regarding various policies and activities. The agency has been non-responsive to my requests and has utterly failed to comply. I am now reaffirming these oversight requests to provide the agency with a second opportunity to demonstrate the appropriate degree of deference and respect for congressional prerogatives. I expect EPA’s full and prompt responsiveness to each of the requests detailed below, which are long overdue:
1. Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans (ARRPs)
On March 26th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with several other Democratic Committee Members requesting that the agency “provide the Committee with your Agency RIF and Reorganization Plan immediately upon transmitting it to OMB and the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).” The context for this request was the revelation that EPA’s ARRP proposed to “eliminate the Office of Research and Development as an EPA National Program Office” while pushing “a majority (50-75%)” of ORD’s employees out of the agency. Of course, that is exactly what happened. But EPA never provided its Phase One and Phase Two ARRPs to the Committee, which has hindered the Committee’s ability to understand the motivations and decisions that led to the elimination of ORD. For instance, information revealed last year in a lawsuit related to agency ARRPs appeared to suggest that disagreements may have existed between EPA and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regarding the elimination of ORD. Without reviewing the ARRPs themselves, the Committee cannot properly assess the agency’s position towards ORD and the bureaucratic actions that contributed to its demise.
2. Laboratory Budget and Staffing Levels
On May 27th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Gabe Amo requesting that the agency “share the projected post-reorganization budget and staffing levels for each of the facilities that will remain open.” The “facilities” in this case referred specifically to the ten field laboratory and research facilities managed by ORD. These research laboratories are a crown jewel of EPA science, and the agency’s intention to eliminate ORD had raised the alarming prospect that the laboratories might be shut down as well. EPA has not subsequently acted to do so, and the laboratories appear to be continuing under the management of different program offices. But while I am relieved that they continue to operate, I remain concerned that staffing shortages and reduced scientific capabilities at the former ORD laboratories could undermine their ability to appropriately study environmental hazards. EPA’s unwillingness to provide basic budgetary and personnel information for its research laboratories impedes the Committee’s ability to evaluate whether they remain capable of supporting core agency activities.
3. Endangerment Finding Repeal Documents and Communications
On August 18th, 2025, I sent a letter to EPA along with Environment Subcommittee Ranking Member Amo requesting that the agency provide “all documents and communications” exchanged between EPA and OMB, the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Trump Vance 2025 Transition Team, regarding “the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.” I also requested “all documents and communications” exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the report developed by DOE’s Climate Working Group, and “all documents and communications” within EPA regarding “the agency’s review of the scientific basis for the proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding.” These oversight requests relate to the repeal of the 2009 Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding, which the agency proposed in July 2025 and finalized in February 2026. I continue to have concerns about potential violations of administrative law in the agency’s rulemaking process to repeal the Endangerment Finding. The documents and communications that I requested are central to the Committee’s ability to conduct oversight of the agency’s actions. EPA’s refusal to provide them only strengthens my belief that these records remain highly material to my review and must be disclosed without delay.
4. Status of PFNA IRIS Assessment
Dr. Maureen Gwinn, the EPA Deputy Associate Administrator for Science, testified before the Science Committee’s Subcommittee on Environment on June 4th, 2026. The subject of her testimony was OASES and the general status of environmental research and development at the agency after the elimination of ORD. During that hearing, I questioned Dr. Gwinn about the agency’s decision earlier in 2026 to disavow chemical assessments conducted by the Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS). In particular, I asked about the status of the IRIS assessment for PFNA, which press reports indicate has been fully completed for more than a year but which the agency refuses to finalize and publish. In response, Dr. Gwinn told me that she was “not sure of the details on that” and said that she would “have to get back to you.” She also stated that she would “go back and confirm” the status of the PFNA assessment. While that hearing took place over four months ago, the agency has not provided any subsequent information regarding the PFNA assessment and whether it ever intends to finalize and publish the assessment, nor has it offered any scientific justification for refusing to do so. I continue to seek clarity on whether the IRIS assessment for PFNA, a dangerous and highly toxic PFAS chemical, will ever see the light of day under this administration.
5. Administration Delays of Environmental Research
At the same June 4th Environment Subcommittee hearing with Dr. Gwinn, one of my colleagues, Representative Suzanne Bonamici, questioned Dr. Gwinn about whether the agency under its current leadership had sought to delay or suppress any environmental research due to its perceived lack of alignment with administration priorities. Specifically, Representative Bonamici asked whether “any proposed research products, even one, [had] been delayed, modified, or declined because they did not align with the priorities set by political appointees?” In response, Dr. Gwinn acknowledged that “there have been delays” due to the agency’s review of whether certain research products complied with President Trump’s various Executive Orders. But when Representative Bonamici followed up and directly asked “what was the topic of the research,” pertaining to research that had been halted, Dr. Gwinn could only respond that she would “have to get back to you on that.” The agency has not provided any further information regarding which specific research topics were “delayed, modified, or declined” due to the political directives of agency leadership. This information is highly material to the Committee’s ability to understand the current state of scientific integrity at EPA, as well as the role played by political appointees in influencing the environmental research being conducted by the agency.
In summary, the following oversight requests remain outstanding and require compliance on the part of the agency. Please produce the requested records no later than 5:00 PM on Friday, November 6th, 2026:
1. Please provide to the Committee the EPA’s Agency RIF and Reorganization Plans (ARRPs) transmitted to OMB and OPM pursuant to OMB Director Russ Vought’s February 2025 memo.
2. Please provide to the Committee the post-reorganization budget and staffing levels for each of the agency’s field laboratory and research facilities that remain open.
3. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and OMB regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.
4. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.
5. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and the Trump Vance 2025 Transition Team regarding the repeal of the Endangerment Finding.
6. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) exchanged between EPA and DOE regarding the report titled, “A Critical Review of Impacts of Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the U.S. Climate.”
7. Please provide to the Committee all documents and communications (including, but not limited to, emails, text messages, instant messages, comments, notes, analyses, legal and other memoranda, letters, telephone logs, Signal messages, meeting minutes, calendar entries, PowerPoint slides, and presentation materials) within EPA regarding the agency’s review of the scientific basis for the proposal to repeal the Endangerment Finding.
8. Please provide to the Committee a written update regarding the status of the IRIS assessment for PFNA, including whether any scientific work remains ongoing for the assessment and the date by which the agency intends to finalize and publish the assessment.
9. Please provide to the Committee a list of all research products that have been delayed, modified, or declined since January 20th, 2025, due to the agency’s review or conclusions regarding the alignment of scientific research with administration priorities, including the topics of the research products.
EPA’s non-responsiveness to Committee oversight during the 119th Congress has been unacceptable. The agency must respect congressional prerogatives. We remain determined to obtain the information we need to perform our duties on behalf of the American people. EPA should understand that a lack of cooperation will not frustrate the Committee’s oversight permanently. It will merely strengthen our commitment to employing all the tools at our disposal to hold the agency accountable.
Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” The Committee possesses jurisdiction over environmental research and development.

Representatives Torres and Fleischmann Lead Bipartisan Bill to Build America’s Advanced Manufacturing Workforce
Legislation expands workforce training and connects workers with good paying careers in growing manufacturing industries
Washington, D.C. – Today, during National Manufacturing Month, Representatives Norma Torres (CA-35) and Chuck Fleischmann (TN-03) introduced the bipartisan Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act of 2026, legislation to help workers train for and connect with advanced manufacturing careers. The legislation, which was inspired by the successful public-private partnership that created the InTech Center at Chaffey College in Fontana, would direct the Department of Labor to initiate pilot projects between local community colleges, state and tribal colleges, local boards, advanced manufacturers, and Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) centers that are focused on education, training, and apprenticeship programs for advanced manufacturing jobs.
“Manufacturing is a cornerstone of the Inland Empire’s economy, and we need to make sure our workforce is prepared for the jobs of tomorrow,” said Congresswoman Torres. “The Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act will bring manufacturers, community colleges, and workforce partners together to give workers the skills they need to secure good-paying careers while helping American manufacturers find the talent they need to grow. Investing in American manufacturing means investing in American workers, and I am proud to partner with Congressman Fleischmann on this bipartisan effort.”
“Manufacturing is the backbone of America, driving our economy, creating jobs, and building the foundation of our nation’s prosperity. East Tennessee is leading the way in America’s reindustrialization, showing how innovation and hard work can revitalize our manufacturing sector. This legislation is vital to keeping America competitive and strong. I am honored to champion this effort in Congress and remain committed to supporting American manufacturing and the dedicated people who power it,” said Congressman Fleischmann.
The Advanced Manufacturing Jobs in America Act would amend the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act to establish pilot projects focused on advanced manufacturing education and training. The bill would support partnerships between advanced manufacturers and community colleges, workforce development boards, Manufacturing Extension Partnership centers, local educational agencies, and other eligible organizations. Programs could include classroom and hands on learning, on-the-job training, and registered apprenticeships and pre-apprenticeships.
The legislation would prioritize dislocated and unemployed workers. Eligible recipients must demonstrate their capacity to teach the skills needed for advanced manufacturing jobs and provide workers with a recognized postsecondary credential.
The bill is inspired by the public-private partnership at the InTech Center at Chaffey College, a regional training center that trains and upskills students and employed workers for in-demand technical careers at no cost. In 2014, the Chaffey College and the Inland Empire Regional Training Consortium (IERTC) received a $15 million grant from the Department of Labor, which resulted in the 2016 opening of the InTech Center, a partnership between Chaffey College and California Steel Industries (now Nucor-CSI). The center was California's first public-private workforce training partnership in advanced manufacturing. Located in Fontana, CA, the center now works with more than 70 employers in the region and is an example of how federal funding can jumpstart successful public-private workforce development programs in advanced manufacturing.
Earlier this month, Reps. Torres and Fleischmann led a bipartisan resolution recognizing National Manufacturing Day and the contributions of manufacturers and workers across the country. In 2022, Reps. Torres & Fleischmann also secured the inclusion of their bicameral, bipartisan National MEP Supply Chain Database Act in the CHIPS and Science Act (Public Law 117-167) to help manufacturers prepare for future supply chain challenges.
###
title: Representatives Torres and Fleischmann Lead Bipartisan Bill to Build America’s Advanced Manufacturing Workforce

Justice Department Files Complaint Against California Ticket Broker for Using Unlawful Tactics to Purchase Millions of Tickets to Popular Live Events
Today, the Department of Justice, together with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), announced the filing of a complaint against REPS & Company Inc. (REPS), a California corporation, along with three of its executives — Ryan Pancheri, Brian Archibald, and Nicholas Totagrande — for violations of the FTC Act and the Better Online Ticket Sales (BOTS) Act, which prohibits circumventing the measures Internet ticket sellers use to ensure equitable consumer access to event tickets.
“The Justice Department is committed to holding accountable individuals and businesses that drive up the cost of event tickets by illegally exceeding ticket purchase limits and reselling those unlawfully obtained tickets with exorbitant markups,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “Working alongside the FTC, we will continue to enforce the BOTS Act to protect consumers from such conduct.”
The complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, alleges that since 2022, the defendants have routinely circumvented ticket issuers’ controls to purchase tickets in excess of purchase limits for thousands of events. The defendants then resold tickets to these events on the secondary market. Defendants spent more than $1.3 billion to amass over 18.5 million tickets for these events and generated at least $120.8 million in profit.
The United States is represented by Assistant Director Marcus P. Smith and Trial Attorneys Meredith L. Reiter and Austin T. Mendes of the Civil Division’s Enforcement and Affirmative Litigation Branch in coordination with the Federal Trade Commission.
The claims made in the complaint are allegations only, and there has been no determination of liability.
Press Release Number: 26-1210
title: Justice Department Files Complaint Against California Ticket Broker for Using Unlawful Tactics to Purchase Millions of Tickets to Popular Live Events

Sherman & Lawmakers Challenge Trump Administration’s Effort to Restart California Oil Pipeline
SHERMAN OAKS, CA — Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32) joined Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Congressman Salud Carbajal (D-CA), and a coalition of Democratic lawmakers in challenging the Trump Administration’s efforts to restart the Sable Offshore oil pipeline in California, arguing that the Administration is unlawfully invoking national defense powers to benefit the fossil fuel industry.
In an amicus brief filed with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, Sherman and his colleagues urged the court to reverse a lower court ruling that allowed the pipeline to continue operating despite questions surrounding the Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA).
The lawmakers argue that the Trump Administration has failed to demonstrate any legitimate national defense necessity for restarting the pipeline, which had remained idle for nearly 11 years. Instead, they contend that the Administration is misusing extraordinary federal authority to circumvent California law and financially benefit a politically connected oil company.
The brief also raises concerns about potential pay-to-play politics, noting that the project was headed by a Trump donor and questioning whether the Administration's intervention was motivated by national security considerations or political favoritism.
Sherman and his colleagues emphasized that the Defense Production Act was intended to address genuine national defense needs, not provide the federal government with unchecked authority to intervene on behalf of private companies.
The lawmakers urged the Ninth Circuit to reverse the district court's denial of a preliminary injunction, arguing that the lower court failed to adequately scrutinize the Administration's national defense justification.
The effort was led by Senators Whitehouse, Padilla, and Schiff, along with Congressman Carbajal. Sherman joined Senator Tammy Duckworth and ten other House Democrats in signing the brief.
Read the full announcement and brief here.
###
title: Sherman & Lawmakers Challenge Trump Administration’s Effort to Restart California Oil Pipeline

Rep. Summer Lee Celebrates $850,000 in Federal Funding for New West Mifflin Community Recreation and Wellness Center
PITTSBURGH, PA – OCTOBER 15, 2026 — Yesterday, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined West Mifflin Borough officials and community leaders for a ceremonial groundbreaking and check presentation celebrating $850,000 in federal funding she secured for the planned West Mifflin Community Recreation and Wellness Center.
The funding, secured through the federal Community Project Funding process, will support the development of a new community facility at 371 Camp Hollow Road, creating a dedicated space for recreation, wellness, youth activities, senior programming, and community gatherings.
“I’m proud to have secured $850,000 in federal funding to help make the new West Mifflin Community Recreation and Wellness Center a reality,” said Rep. Lee. “Folks in West Mifflin deserve a space where kids can grow, seniors can stay active, and families have somewhere to come together—right in their own backyards. I'm grateful to our borough leaders and state partners for helping bring us this far and look forward to seeing how this space transforms generations to come.”
"The Borough of West Mifflin extends its sincere thanks to Congresswoman Summer Lee for helping secure this funding. This project represents an important investment in West Mifflin’s future, creating opportunities for recreation, community programs, senior services, and activities for residents of all ages. We are grateful to Congresswoman Lee for her support and partnership in helping bring this vision closer to reality. This project will be a valuable asset to our community and region for generations to come,” said Michael Moses, Council President.
The project will transform an undeveloped site into a community destination designed to serve residents of all ages. Plans for the facility include indoor athletic and recreational spaces, public meeting rooms, youth activities, senior programming, and spaces for civic and community services.
Alongside the $850,000 in federal funding secured by Rep. Lee, the project has received an additional $425,000 through Pennsylvania's Statewide Local Share Account program, bringing combined federal and state funding commitments to $1.275 million.
Through her Community Project Funding efforts, Rep. Lee has secured direct investments for community-based organizations, including a $1 million CPF award to the Greater Pittsburgh Community Food Bank, $450,000 to the Trade Institute of Pittsburgh, over $1.5 million in federal support for the Tree of Life rebuilding and healing initiatives, $1 million in Community Project Funding for historic renovations at the Carnegie Library of Homestead, more than $1 million in federal funding to combat blight and revitalize housing in North Braddock, and $1 million to help turn vacant office space into affordable homes, create good-paying jobs, and bring new life to downtown Pittsburgh.
These projects are part of more than $24.9 million in Community Project Funding secured during her time in Congress. Rep. Lee’s office has consistently directed federal dollars to historically overlooked communities to ensure equitable access to opportunities and long-term regional growth and stability.
To view photos from the event, please click HERE.
Congresswoman Summer Lee serves on the House Committee on Judiciary and the Committee on Education and Workforce. Since taking office in January 2023, she has delivered historic levels of federal investment totaling over $2.7 Billion brought back to Western PA, including over $580 million for infrastructure, over $110 million for affordable transit, over $500 million to keep clean energy manufacturing at home in Pennsylvania, and over $55 million on clean energy efforts in and around schools to help keep our kids and communities safe. These investments will help improve Western Pennsylvania’s infrastructure and transit, ensure cleaner air and drinking water, lower housing costs, fund research institutions, fuel clean manufacturing, fund STEM innovation and entrepreneurship, boost workforce development, and create thousands of good paying union jobs. Lee and her team have also delivered casework and constituent services to over 4,000 constituents with issues ranging from helping our seniors and disabled community access Medicare and social security to helping folks secure housing and helping families with immigration support and passports.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE:
October 15, 2026
MEDIA CONTACT:
e: jessica.myers@mail.house.gov
c: 202.913.0126
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09) reintroduced the REAL Political Ads Act, legislation to strengthen transparency and accountability in political advertising by requiring disclosure when generative artificial intelligence (AI) is used to create images or videos in political advertisements.
A recent Quinnipiac poll found that 55 percent of Americans are concerned about the growing risks associated with artificial intelligence, and a recent Blue Rose Research poll found that 74 percent of voters believe AI-generated voices should be prohibited in political calls to protect transparency. Those concerns are compounded in the context of the Federal Communications Commission’s proposal to waive the federal ban on unsolicited AI-generated political robocalls, as well as in the widespread use of AI by the Trump Administration and across the political spectrum to attack political opponents and spread disinformation.
“As generative AI technologies continue to evolve, clear disclosure standards to preserve transparency are essential to civic engagement. Unfortunately, Congress has failed to keep up the pace with this rapidly advancing technology, leaving voters vulnerable to AI-generated misinformation and disinformation,” said Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke. “This legislation would ensure voters know when political ads use AI-generated images and videos. If AI content can manipulate and deceive people on a large scale, it can be a serious threat to our democracy and have devastating consequences for our national and election security.”
“Voters deserve to know that the election information that we read, watch, and listen to is honest. AI makes it far too easy for campaigns to create convincing content intended to mislead voters, and too often it’s at the expense of voters of color and other communities historically pushed to the margins. Congresswoman Clarke’s REAL Political Advertisements Act would help ensure that every voter can make informed decisions based on the facts,” said Alejandra Montoya-Boyer, Vice President of The Leadership Conference’s Center for Civil Rights and Technology.
This legislation is co-sponsored by: Reps. Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Jim Costa (CA-21), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).
The full bill text can be found here.
###
title: CLARKE REINTRODUCES REAL POLITICAL ADS ACT TO STRENGTHEN TRANSPARENCY IN AI-GENERATED POLITICAL ADVERTISING

PHOTO RELEASE: Gottheimer Visits Ukrainian Community in Ramsey, Slams Appeasement of Dictator Putin, Calls for TPS Extension to Keep Ukrainian Families Safe
Calls for TPS Extension and Continued U.S. Commitment to Ukraine
Above: Gottheimer Visits St. Paul Ukrainian Catholic Church in Ramsey.
RAMSEY, NJ — Today, Thursday, October 15, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) visited St. Paul Ukrainian Catholic Church in Ramsey, where he met with parishioners and faith leaders from North Jersey’s Ukrainian community. He discussed his support for Ukrainian families in the Fifth District, the urgent need to extend Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Ukrainians living in the United States, and America’s continued commitment to standing with Ukraine in its war with Russia.He also slammed the Trump Administration’s appeasement of dictator Vladimir Putin, including its new deal to import Russian diesel.
“North Jersey’s Ukrainian community has shown incredible strength, faith, and generosity, and they have my full support. We must extend TPS so Ukrainian families here are not sent back into a war zone, and we must keep standing with Ukraine as it fights for freedom against Putin’s brutal invasion. America’s commitment to Ukraine cannot waver,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).
TPS for Ukrainians is currently set to expire on Monday, October 19, 2026, which puts at risk neighbors, workers, and students who fled amid Russia’s invasion and have since built lives here. Congressman Gottheimer called on the Administration to extend TPS protections so these families are not forced to return to an active war zone.
Gottheimer also criticized the Trump Administration’s new deal with Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel. It comes just weeks after the President signed the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which Gottheimer supported, that Congress passed to choke off the energy revenues that fund Putin’s war. Gottheimer argued that the deal breaks our own laws and hands Putin’s war machine a lifeline funded by American taxpayers.
The Congressman also reaffirmed his support for Ukraine abroad. He stressed that the United States must continue to back Ukraine’s defense against Russian aggression and stand firmly with its people.
Gottheimer was joined by Maria Keniuk, Church Trustee; Irene and Victor Hurlinsky; Jed Sunden, Director of the American Ukraine Committee and the American Ukraine PAC; Jackie Colgan, American Association for Ukraine; Oleksandr Tran, President of Svitanok; Anna Move, President and Co-Founder of the Leonid Foundation; and Tanya Khapko, Mike and Oksana Dyakiv, Ivan Durbak, and Nadiya Dovhan, members of St. Paul Ukrainian Catholic Church.

Larson Statement on the 2027 Social Security COLA Announcement
Washington, D.C. - Today, House Social Security Subcommittee Ranking Member John B. Larson (CT-01) released the following statement after the Social Security Administration (SSA) announced a 3.6 percent Social Security Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) for 2027.
“Today’s announcement demonstrates just how hard President Trump’s affordability crisis has hit our seniors," said Larson. “As Americans struggle to make ends meet, a small bump in benefits is always welcome news—but for many seniors living on fixed incomes, it won’t be enough to keep pace with rising costs. With insolvency looming, we are only a few years away from automatic benefit cuts for everyone on Social Security if Congress does not act. Rather than come to the table with solutions, this administration and their allies in Congress have been laser-focused on breaking the system from within, so they can privatize Social Security. They have slashed staff and services at the Social Security Administration, making it harder for seniors to get their benefits in full and on time, and Speaker Johnson has even teased a plan to cut benefits if Republicans hold their majorities in the House and Senate. We cannot let that happen. Americans are depending on their Congress to enhance benefits—not cut them—and Democrats are ready to act. Our plan will stop these automatic cuts, boost benefits across the board, and ensure no one can retire into poverty after a lifetime of work, all by finally making the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share. It is time for a vote.”
The annual Social Security Trustees Report released this summer confirmed that Congress must act and that failed Trump policies, including the Big, Ugly Bill, mean that Social Security’s insolvency is closer than ever. Inaction will lead to the average senior losing about $500/month in Social Security benefits in 2032.
Ranking Member Larson’s Social Security 2100 Act would enhance Social Security benefits to help beneficiaries dealing with rising costs and extend the program’s solvency by eliminating the FICA cap and imposing a net investment income tax on income over $400,000.
title: Larson Statement on the 2027 Social Security COLA Announcement

Medical Spa Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Employment Tax Crimes
A Parker, Colorado man pleaded guilty on October 2, 2026, to willfully failing to pay over employment taxes on behalf of the medical spa business he owned and operated.
The following is according to court documents and statements made in court: Spencer Carrado owned and operated “Spectrum Med Spa,” also known as “SculptedMD,” a “medical spa” operating in various locations. Carrado exercised control over SculptedMD’s financial affairs. He also was responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare and income taxes from his employees’ wages and paying those funds over to the IRS, as well as filing quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS. From the third quarter of 2020 through the fourth quarter of 2024, however, Carrado withheld taxes from his employees’ wages, but did not pay over those taxes to the IRS or file all required quarterly employment tax returns. In total, Carrado caused a tax loss to the United States exceeding $600,000.
Carrado pleaded guilty to one count of willful failure to account for and pay over trust fund taxes. He is scheduled to be sentenced on December 11, 2026, and faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorney Stuart A. Wexler of the Criminal Division’s Tax Section is prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Medical Spa Business Owner Pleads Guilty to Employment Tax Crimes

The U.S. Department of Energy Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office released a pre-publication draft of a federal register notice announcing the Emissions Value Request process for the 45Z fuel production tax credit.
October 14, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Alternative Fuels and Feedstocks Office (AFFO) released a pre-publication draft of a federal register notice announcing the Emissions Value Request (EVR) process for the 45Z fuel production tax credit. Modified and extended under the Working Families Tax Cut, the Clean Fuel Production Tax Credit (Internal Revenue Code Section 45Z) provides a production incentive for certain feedstocks produced in the United States, Mexico, or Canada.
“Thanks to President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cut, we are creating new opportunities for American farmers and fuel producers to strengthen domestic energy production, reduce costs, and unleash American energy dominance,” said Assistant Secretary of Energy Audrey Robertson. “Through the Department of Energy’s new 45Z Emissions Value Request process, we are expanding opportunities for American fuel producers to access critical tax incentives, supporting rural economies, and bringing more American-made fuels to market. In short: putting American energy first.”
Transportation fuel producers seeking to claim the tax credit must obtain the life cycle greenhouse gas emissions rate of their transportation fuel using the applicable rate table for Section 45Z. If the fuel’s type, primary feedstock, or pathway is not included in the rate table, fuel producers must petition the Secretary of Treasury for a provisional emission rate (PER). The 45Z EVR process is the route through which fuel producers can obtain a rate value from DOE and petition U.S. Treasury for a PER.
To request an emissions value from DOE, stakeholders must follow the EVR Application Instructions to submit the following requested materials:
- Engineering information/analyses consistent with the specified section of the front-end engineering and design (FEED) study or similar indication of project maturity, as determined by DOE.
- A completed EVR form.
In addition to the required documents, an applicant also has the option to include additional information that may be beneficial in completing lifecycle analysis of the transportation fuel production pathway described in the EVR form and FEED study.
For more detailed information on how to apply for a PER or the EVR process, visit DOE’s 45Z EVR webpage or contact 45ZEmissionsRequest@doe.gov. Questions about the 45Z tax credit and eligibility for the tax credit should be directed to the Internal Revenue Service.
title: Energy Department Releases Emissions Value Request Process for 45Z Fuel Production Credit

Hoyer Statement on Unannounced Starlink Terminal Restrictions in Ukraine
WASHINGTON, DC –  Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after SpaceX, an American aerospace manufacturer founded by Elon Musk, imposed sudden unannounced data speed restrictions on Starlink terminals utilized by Ukraine, disrupting its defensive military drone operations:
“The people of Ukraine have had to endure twelve years of Russian military aggression, occupation, full-scale invasion, the kidnapping of its children into Russia, and air attacks against their cities. Winters have been particularly brutal, with Russia targeting Ukraine’s energy and heating infrastructure. After four years of heroic fighting, Ukraine’s forces are now making steady progress on the battlefield, aided by relentless innovation and access to Starlink satellite networks crucial to command-and-control as well as to drone and missile interception. Members of Congress who traveled to Kyiv recently heard from Ukrainian officials just how critical Starlink is to civilian defense and battlefield progress.
“The turning off of Ukraine’s Starlink access today means that fewer Russian attacks against civilians targets will be intercepted. More Ukrainian families will face a harsh and difficult winter. Ukraine’s battlefield gains may slow. If Trump Administration officials were involved in this decision, as Elon Musk claims, it would represent a heinous act of betrayal to our Ukrainian allies and to a fellow democracy under assault by a despot. It would be an inversion of the American people’s will, as expressed by Congress, that we ought to be helping Ukraine win, not tipping the scales in Putin’s favor. This shameful act must be reversed, and I call on SpaceX to ensure that Ukrainian forces have their full connection restored. I also call on our Armed Forces to condemn this act as well.
“The surest way to ensure this war comes to an end is not to help Russia prolong it. It is to help Ukraine win. Because the people of Ukraine have shown the world that they will not allow their democracy, freedom, sovereignty, or territorial integrity be taken by a foreign power. They are unbowed and unafraid. America must show the same resolve in our unwavering support.”

CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN, NEW YORK DELEGATION DEMAND TRUMP ADMINISTRATION RELEASE $87 MILLION IN COUNTERTERRORISM FUNDING STILL OWED TO NEW YORK
Congressman Pat Ryan, New York Delegation Demand Trump Administration Release $87 Million in Counterterrorism Funding Still Owed to New York
One Year After Trump Promised Full Reversal of Funding Cuts, First Responders Statewide are Still Without Millions in Federal Investments
KINGSTON, NY – Congressman Pat Ryan joined members of the New York Congressional Delegation in demanding the Trump Administration to immediately release $87 million in FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Program (HSGP) funding that is still owed to New York. Their letter, sent to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, highlights the danger of withholding this funding from one the largest states in the nation and a top target for international and domestic terrorism.
“Since the start of the second Trump Administration, the President has waged targeted political attacks on New York State. When he cut this counterterrorism funding, New Yorkers across the state fought back and won. Now, a year later, we’re demanding Trump deliver the rest of what’s rightly ours,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “As Trump’s war with Iran continues, Americans want and deserve to feel safe. Now is the absolute last time to be cutting security funding. The need is especially stark following the grim 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks – the tragedy that changed our state forever and inspired these vital preparedness programs in the first place. Trump’s DHS has an obligation to release these funds and protect New Yorkers.”
In September 2025, DHS issued HSGP award notifications that cut New York’s allocation by 86 percent, or $187 million, leaving the state with just $30 million compared to roughly $220 million in FY24. In October 2025, following bipartisan advocacy, President Trump committed to restoring full funding at approximately $220 million. After a court order in Noem v. Illinois that found Trump unlawfully cut emergency grant funding, the administration released $100 million, but $87 million is still owed to New York.
The missing funds affect every county in the state, including Dutchess, Orange, and Ulster, and represent $11 million in losses for New York City. The letter warns that without full restoration, the Trump Administration is severely limiting local law enforcement’s ability to plan, train tactical teams, procure equipment, and conduct operations. Created in the wake of the September 11th attacks, HSGP has protected New York State for decades. The delegation underscored that the funds are due 25 years after 9/11 and one year after the President’s promise.
The full text of the letter can be found here.

Bosnian National Sentenced for Violating International Sanctions Against North Korea
A Bosnian national was sentenced to 60 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to federal export and sanctions violations by conspiring and attempting to broker the sale of Man Portable Air Defense Systems, which are anti-aircraft missiles.
“U.S. sanctions mean little if those who knowingly evade them face no consequences,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison for the District of New Mexico. “This defendant helped carry out an international scheme to conduct business that U.S. law prohibited, and this sentence holds him accountable for his role. I am proud of the investigators and prosecutors whose hard work and dedication brought this case to sentencing in New Mexico. Their commitment to seeing this prosecution through is a testament to the caliber of the people who serve in this district.”
“Those who knowingly attempt to circumvent U.S. export controls and international sanctions to facilitate the illicit trafficking of military weapons pose a serious threat to our national security and global stability,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Ryan G. McRae of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) El Paso. “Their willingness to profit from prohibited weapons transactions demonstrates blatant disregard for the law. HSI aggressively pursues those who traffic in restricted military technology and hold them accountable for their actions.”
According to court documents, Sasa Micev, 43, a citizen of Bosnia, is an international arms dealer. Micev worked with a co-conspirator based in New Mexico and others to violate and evade restrictions imposed by the U.S. Department of the Treasury under the North Korea Sanctions Regulations by brokering the purchase of SA-18 Igla portable surface-to-air missiles from North Korea without the required license or approvals from the Department of Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control.
On multiple occasions in 2020, Micev and a co-conspirator discussed unlawfully acquiring the Igla missiles and Micev provided pricing information, participated in efforts to obtain the items through falsified documentation, and worked to procure the weapons from North Korea despite knowing that such transactions were prohibited under U.S. and international laws.
In late 2020, Micev and the co-conspirator traveled to Ankara, Turkey to meet and complete the sale of the Igla missiles. However, after a price dispute with the North Koreans, the sale fell through.
Micev pleaded guilty to violating the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the North Korean Sanctions Regulations.
HSI’s Albuquerque and Phoenix Field Offices investigated this case.
Assistant U.S. Attorneys Tavo Hall and Holland Kastrin for the District of New Mexico are prosecuting the case with the assistance of the Trial Attorney Maria Fedor of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section.
title: Bosnian National Sentenced for Violating International Sanctions Against North Korea

HHS Launches Health Center Healthy Lifestyle Commitment to Advance Nutrition, Prevention, and Healthy Living
CHATHAM, VA—OCTOBER 14, 2026—U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., joined by Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Administrator Tom Engels, today launched the HHS Health Center Healthy Lifestyle Commitment, a voluntary initiative that encourages health centers nationwide to put nutrition, prevention, and healthy living at the center of patient care.
Secretary Kennedy announced the initiative during a visit to Piedmont Access to Health Services (PATHS) health center in Chatham, Virginia, where he highlighted the role health centers play in preventing chronic disease and helping patients build healthier lives.
“We will not reverse chronic disease by waiting until Americans get sick,” said Secretary Kennedy. “HHS is equipping health centers to make nutrition, physical activity, healthy sleep, and prevention part of everyday care. This commitment will help doctors and families act earlier, build healthier habits, and prevent disease before it starts.”
Through the voluntary Health Center Healthy Lifestyle Commitment, HRSA-supported health centers are encouraged to advance evidence-based best practices that support:
- Prioritizing prevention and healthy lifestyles by encouraging healthy eating, physical activity, adequate sleep, limited screen time, and other behaviors that can help prevent, delay, and better manage chronic disease;
- Promoting healthy eating by helping patients and families understand and apply the new Dietary Guidelines for Americans, including choosing whole, nutrient-dense foods and limiting highly processed foods and added sugars;
- Empowering patients and families with practical, actionable information about nutrition, preventive care, and healthy behaviors that support lifelong health;
- Connecting patients to community health activities, including community gardens, fresh produce programs, nutrition education, and physical activity opportunities;
- Strengthening the prevention workforce by equipping health center staff with tools, training, and resources to integrate nutrition and healthy living into everyday patient care; and
- Building a culture of health that encourages healthy choices and empowers patients to take an active role in improving their health.
As part of the initiative, HHS is encouraging participating health centers to display the new food pyramid and use it as a resource to help patients and families understand the Dietary Guidelines for Americans, 2025–2030 and make healthier food choices.
“Health centers are trusted partners in their communities, caring for millions of Americans every year,” said HRSA Administrator Tom Engels. “They are uniquely positioned to help patients and families make healthier choices and prevent chronic disease before it starts. This commitment builds on the important work health centers are already doing by giving them additional tools and resources to make nutrition, prevention, and healthy living part of everyday patient care.”
HRSA is also making resources available on the new Health Centers and Nutrition webpage, including nutrition education materials, tools for patients and providers, and practical guidance to support conversations about healthy eating and disease prevention.
The Health Center Healthy Lifestyle Commitment builds on the Trump Administration’s Make America Healthy Again Strategy by recognizing the critical role of community-based primary care in addressing chronic disease and improving the health of American families.
Participation in the commitment is voluntary and does not establish new federal requirements or standards of care. A health center’s decision to participate will not affect its eligibility for or receipt of HRSA funding.
Learn more about the HHS Health Center Healthy Lifestyle Commitment.

Thompson, Correa, Thanedar Release Government Report on Problems with DHS Body Camera Program
Legislation to Be Introduced to Address ICE’s Refusal of Automatic Camera Activation
(WASHINGTON) – Today, Democratic Members of the House Committee on Homeland Security announced the release of a U.S. Government Accountability Office report they requested on the Department of Homeland Security’s Body-Worn Camera program for its immigration officers and agents. Recent tragic shootings have shown that not only do these cameras need to be deployed, they need to be activated with proper controls.
In the report, entitled “Federal Law Enforcement: CBP and ICE Should Improve Body-Worn Camera Program Management,” the GAO found while DHS has rushed deploying body-worn cameras, both CBP and ICE lack updated program plans, results oriented performance measures, and sufficient controls to ensure cameras are activated and used consistently. GAO concludes that these gaps limit DHS’s ability to achieve the core objectives of the program—transparency, accountability, and strengthened public trust.
GAO also found that ICE, unlike CBP, relies on manual camera activation and that the absence of automated controls – which GAO recommends – puts ICE at greater risk of missing critical recordings.
“With shootings by DHS officers on the rise, the American people – and Congress – have rightfully demanded DHS use body-worn cameras when its officers are out in the field. However, this government report shows that DHS’s body-worn camera program is deficient and needs to be revamped if DHS is going to be transparent and accountable,” said Rep. Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security. “Worse yet, ICE – which has shown time and again it thinks it is immune to accountability – is unwilling to implement automatic activation for its cameras, increasing the risk of missing critical recordings, just like what happened when Wilber Garces Perez was shot by an ICE agent in Austin last month. This is completely unacceptable and I will be introducing legislation in the coming days to close this gap and ensure all DHS body-worn cameras have the recommended automatic activation.”
"Since January, federal immigration agents have shot at least 25 people. Six are dead, three of them American citizens. These are not just numbers – they are real lives lost, and the public deserves transparency and accountability from DHS,” added Rep. Lou Correa (D-CA), Ranking Member of the Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee. “DHS has been turned into a tool for political ends, and that has to stop. This report confirms the DHS body-camera program is lacking, even though the department has had more than enough time to get it right. Transparency and accountability aren't optional."
“ICE is violently terrorizing Americans left and right. To help with transparency and accountability, they need to have body cameras that are automatically activated. This latest GAO report shows DHS's current body camera program is unacceptable, plagued with old plans and no performance goals,” added Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-MI), Ranking Member of the Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability subcommittee. “DHS must reverse course immediately and implement additional automatic activation controls for body cameras as well as issue transparent operations guidance for this program. DHS's continued attempts to avoid accountability for their horrific actions are unacceptable, and I will continue to work with my Homeland Security Committee colleagues to hold this department accountable.”

Texas Tax Preparer Sentenced to Prison as Part of False Tax Return Scheme
A Texas tax return preparer was sentenced on October 7, 2026, to 14 months in prison for her role in conspiring to file false tax returns on behalf of clients.
According to court documents and statements made in court, from approximately February 2020 to October 2022, Sivagami Chidambaram conspired with a tax return preparation business owner and several of his employees to defraud the United States by filing tax returns for clients that contained false business expenses. These false expenses artificially reduced the taxes the clients owed to the IRS, which enabled them to receive refunds to which they were not entitled. Sometimes, Chidambaram added false business expenses on client returns by asking the client about work-from-home expenses, even though Chidambaram knew such expenses could not be claimed on their returns. In some instances, Chidambaram included false business expenses on clients’ tax returns before speaking with the client. In other instances, Chidambaram added false items to appease clients who demanded higher tax refunds. Chidambaram admitted to causing a tax loss to the United States exceeding $250,000 but less than $550,000.
Three other tax return preparers – including a tax return preparation business owner and two of his employees – were sentenced to prison in July in relation to the same scheme. One tax return preparer who admitted to filing false tax returns for clients was sentenced to home confinement.
Tax preparation business owner Mathews Chacko was previously sentenced to 50 months in prison after pleading guilty to conspiracy to defraud the IRS as part of the same scheme. Chacko admitted to causing a tax loss to the United States exceeding $3.5 million but less than $9.5 million. Tax preparers Anish Pillai, Subhala Suresh, and Mou Kundu were previously sentenced to 26 months’ imprisonment, 18 months’ imprisonment, and 18 months’ home confinement, respectively, after pleading guilty to aiding and assisting the filing of a false tax return as part of the same scheme.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Justin Simmons of the Western District of Texas made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case.
Acting Assistant Deputy Chief Marissa R. Brodney and Trial Attorney Michael L. Jones of the Criminal Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Texas Tax Preparer Sentenced to Prison as Part of False Tax Return Scheme

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced legislation to protect hardworking Virginia families and small businesses from being forced to shoulder the rising electricity costs associated with the growing electricity demands of data centers.
The Make Data Centers Pay Act would amend the Federal Power Act to require large and medium-sized data centers to pay the full incremental costs associated with their electricity use, preventing those expenses from being passed on to residential customers and small businesses.
“Families in Virginia and across the country should not have to pay higher electricity bills to subsidize some of the largest and most energy-intensive data centers and computing facilities in the world,” said Vindman. “As data centers and artificial intelligence drive growing demand for electricity, we need to make sure the companies benefiting from that growth pay their fair share. My bill puts ratepayers first and protects hardworking Virginians from being stuck with higher utility bills to subsidize billion-dollar corporations.”
Under the legislation, covered data centers and high-density computing facilities with electricity demands of at least 20 megawatts would be required to cover the incremental costs of serving their electricity needs. This would help ensure that the costs of infrastructure and electricity service needed to support these facilities are borne by the companies driving that demand, rather than shifted onto everyday ratepayers.
BACKGROUND
Vindman has been a champion for holding data centers and electric utilities accountable.
In August 2026, he introduced the Smart Data Center Policy Act to prevent data center development near neighborhoods, schools, and parks.
Vindman also introduced the Home Energy Affordability Act to limit how often utilities can change residential utility rates and change prices for everyday Virginians, as well as the Utility Hikes Transparency Act, which would create the first comprehensive, machine-readable federal database of retail utility rate changes in the United States.
He has also fought against corruption in the energy sector by championing the Energy Utility Lobbying Ban Act, which would bar former government officials from lobbying on behalf of the companies they used to regulate.
What’s more, Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion Energy, raising concerns about its potential impact on electricity rates and Virginia consumers.
Most recently, he delivered remarks at a Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing on the proposed merger, urging regulators to reject the proposal and put the interests of ratepayers ahead of corporate profits.
###
title: Vindman Introduces ‘Make Data Centers Pay Act’ to Protect Virginians from Rising Electricity Costs

Justice Department Opens Investigation of Pennsauken, New Jersey’s Allegedly Unconstitutional Permit Delays
Today, the Justice Department opened an investigation to determine whether Pennsauken, New Jersey deprives citizens of their right to bear arms through egregious and unjust delays in issuing firearm licenses. The Second Amendment protects the right to keep and bear firearms — including the right to carry firearms. The investigation focuses on the Pennsauken Township Police’s permitting system; the investigation does not support any armed obstruction of federal or local law enforcement.
“I have directed the Civil Rights Division, through our Second Amendment Section, to defend law-abiding citizens from local authorities who infringe on the right to safely carry legal firearms,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “Our investigation aims to discover if allegations of unconstitutional delays in firearm permitting are true, and if so, to fix it.”
It is a violation of the Second Amendment for government officials to delay issuing permits to purchase or carry firearms. In 2022, the Supreme Court held in New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n, Inc. v. Bruen that a state’s permitting process is put towards “abusive ends” when “lengthy wait times in processing license applications or exorbitant fees deny ordinary citizens their right to public carry.” Here, it is alleged that Pennsauken, through the Pennsauken Township Police Department, uses just such “abusive ends” to improperly limit Second Amendment rights.
The Civil Rights Division’s Second Amendment Section enforces the Second Amendment. If you believe your right to keep and bear arms is being infringed, please submit a complaint through www.justice.gov/crt/second-amendment-section.
title: Justice Department Opens Investigation of Pennsauken, New Jersey’s Allegedly Unconstitutional Permit Delays

FDA Launches the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to Develop a Holistic, Fit-For-Purpose Framework for Rare Disease Drug Development
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 14, 2026—The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a division within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to reimagine the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. As outlined in a new white paper, the Initiative will develop an optimized, fit-for-purpose framework that reflects the realities of rare disease drug development by considering the nuances of each disease, patient needs, product type and the evidence that can be realistically generated in small patient populations.
To solicit feedback on the Rare Disease Framework Initiative from patients and disease advocates, industry, and others, the FDA will host an October 28 meeting at the FDA’s White Oak campus. The meeting will be facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA.
“Americans with rare diseases cannot afford a regulatory system that treats every condition the same,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Under President Trump, FDA is rethinking rare disease drug development by putting patients at the center and matching regulatory requirements to the realities of small patient populations. We will remove unnecessary barriers, embrace cutting-edge science, and accelerate promising treatments while upholding FDA’s rigorous standards.”
“Patients and families living with rare diseases have few or no approved treatment options, and the burden of uncertainty can extend across every part of their lives,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “As we learn more about rare diseases and better understand the breadth of suffering they cause, we must ensure that America’s regulatory system remains at the forefront — prepared to respond to emerging science, anticipate the needs of patients and families, and help bring safe and effective therapies to those who need them. The FDA will fight hard for patients by building a more consistent, predictable, and innovative approach to rare disease drug development while maintaining the rigorous standards Americans expect from the FDA.”
The FDA has long used regulatory flexibility and developed targeted programs to support innovation in the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. These efforts have led to meaningful advances for patients and families. Nevertheless, with only 5% or so of rare conditions having an FDA-approved treatment, the FDA agrees with patients, drug developers, and providers that more must be done to speed the development of safe and effective treatments for rare diseases. In developing the framework, the FDA is committed to the following:
- Providing greater clarity, consistency, and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance and transparent communication.
- Embedding the patient’s voice both early, and at clearly defined milestones, in the drug development and review process.
- Further leveraging external expertise to support customization of regulatory review.
- Building shared resources, robust training, and institutional knowledge on rare disease drug development and review.
- Applying risk-based approaches, particularly to chemistry, manufacturing, and controls review and pre-approval inspections.
- Championing the use of cutting-edge science, novel methods and innovative statistical approaches in rare disease drug development.
The Initiative is led by the FDA’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, partnering with the Office of the Commissioner, the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.
“Patients with rare diseases and their families deserve a regulatory process that addresses the uniqueness of each of their conditions while maintaining the FDA’s rigorous standards,” said the Hub’s Director, Amy Comstock Rick, J.D. “A bold vision to reimagine the regulatory framework for rare disease drug development that builds on key learnings and milestones is necessary to meet this moment. This new framework will enhance consistency and predictability for both sponsors and for patients.”
Further opportunities to provide input will follow the public meeting, including sector-specific roundtables, Requests for Information, and internal FDA feedback sessions. This feedback will inform the detailed development of a new framework, which might include potential new or revised guidance, revisions to regulations, staff training, and organizational changes.

HHS Declares Public Health Emergencies for Florida, Alabama following Hurricane Isaias
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 14, 2026—U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. yesterday determined that public health emergencies exist in Florida and Alabama as a result of Hurricane Isaias. The determinations follow President Trump’s October 9 emergency declarations for both states (Florida, Alabama). The President’s declarations and the Secretary’s determination allow HHS to authorize temporary waivers and modifications of certain requirements. These flexibilities help the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) support healthcare providers and suppliers serving people enrolled in Medicare, Medicaid, and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP) in the covered emergency areas.
“Under President Trump’s leadership, HHS is giving healthcare providers in Florida and Alabama the flexibility to keep caring for patients in the wake of Hurricane Isaias,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We are helping them maintain essential services, respond quickly as needs change, and keep care available throughout the response and recovery.”
“When a storm disrupts someone’s ability to get care, the need is immediate and personal,” said Sean Kaufman, HHS Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response at the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR). “I want the people affected by Hurricane Isaias to know that we are here to help. Our federal teams worked alongside state and local partners to understand what communities needed and to support the healthcare services they depend on.”
Prior to landfall, ASPR pre-positioned regional staff in areas at risk from the storm to monitor the impacts on public health and healthcare systems and provide technical assistance in anticipation of state requests. Healthcare System Assessment Teams also deployed to evaluate the storm’s impact on healthcare facilities.
In addition, ASPR shared HHS emPOWER datasets with states in the storm’s path. These data can help responders identify, by geographic area, the number of Medicare beneficiaries relying on electricity-dependent medical equipment or certain essential healthcare services, including facility-based dialysis and home healthcare.
Individuals experiencing emotional distress related to Hurricane Isaias can contact the Disaster Distress Helpline by calling or texting 1-800-985-5990. Managed by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), this toll-free, multilingual, crisis support service is available 24/7 to all residents in the U.S. and its territories who are experiencing emotional distress related to natural or human-caused disasters. Callers can be connected with counselors in more than 100 languages via third-party interpretation services by indicating their preferred language to the responding counselor.
In declaring the public health emergency and authorizing flexibilities for CMS providers, suppliers, and beneficiaries, Secretary Kennedy acted within his authority under the Public Health Service Act and Social Security Act. These actions and flexibilities are retroactive to October 6, 2026, in the state of Florida and October 7, 2026, in the state of Alabama.
