This year’s Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank provide an important opportunity to engage on current global economic challenges as well as our work with partners and the international financial institutions to support a pro-growth agenda, macroeconomic and financial stability, and poverty reduction. We thank Thailand for hosting us for the Annual Meetings.
In the United States, President Trump’s America First Investment Policy is promoting robust economic growth and prosperity, fiscal prudence, energy abundance, and regulatory modernization. Internationally, we are getting back to basics by forging a broad consensus on the need to promote growth as the key condition on which durable prosperity depends. As G20 President, the United States is focused on promoting strong economic growth, and has prioritized increasing productivity, addressing global imbalances, engaging with the private sector, advancing financial literacy, improving the sovereign debt architecture, and promoting financial sector innovation and regulatory modernization. When focused on their core missions, the IMF and World Bank are well-placed to help advance these important objectives.
The IMF is making progress at getting back to basics. Through recent policy reviews, the IMF is upgrading its policy toolkit for surveillance and lending and restoring its focus on its core responsibilities. This includes the external sector issues at the heart of the IMF’s mandate, strengthening surveillance of debt vulnerabilities in low-income countries, and making the financial sector surveillance more risk-based. Moreover, the IMF has rightly focused on strengthening program design to enhance the effectiveness of IMF-supported reform programs to durably address balance of payments challenges and restore external viability.
One area where this refocus must go further is in the IMF’s work on global imbalances. This especially includes strengthening its analysis and engagement on the role non-market policies and practices and exchange rates play in driving external imbalances. Policymakers around the world are having difficult discussions about how to sustain market-based systems amid distortionary policies from some economies that skew competition and hurt employment. The IMF was founded to prevent these kinds of distortive policies and negative spillovers, and must exercise its voice on this critical issue or risk being sidelined.
With recent major policy reviews complete, the hard work of implementation begins. The United States will hold the IMF accountable for translating these reforms into stronger surveillance, more effective lending, and more robust assessment of debt sustainability. Successfully delivering on the IMF’s core mandate will require commitment from IMF management to be an unflinching truth-teller through surveillance and to hold borrowers accountable in IMF-supported programs. That same commitment is required of the authorities undertaking painful but necessary macroeconomic adjustments and structural reforms.
The IMF must continue to prioritize its work and focus its resources on its core mandate. New and emerging issues warrant IMF engagement only where they are clearly macrocritical and within the Fund’s mandate, and adding new priorities should require reducing lower-value work, rather than continually expanding the Fund’s agenda such as financing provided through the Resilience and Sustainability Trust that lacks a clear linkage to balance of payments pressures and veers into development-policy lending.
The IMF has sufficient resources to accomplish its mission. The United States remains committed to a strong, quota-based, and adequately resourced IMF, and we continue to work to secure congressional approval for the 16th General Review of Quotas. Future quota reviews should be based on resource adequacy needs, as reflected in the recently approved Diriyah Guiding Principles on IMF Quota and Governance Reforms. Any future quota realignment should reflect members’ relative position in the world economy and be based on a new quota formula.
After years of mission creep, the World Bank is beginning to refocus on its core mission of reducing poverty and raising economic growth. Over the last year, the Bank has strengthened its development agenda by further implementing its jobs initiative, removing inefficient and distortionary climate finance targets, beginning to phase out lending to certain advanced client countries that have not needed Bank support for years, taking steps to better implement its graduation policy, and devising a strategy for supporting a more diversified minerals value chain.
These are necessary steps in returning the Bank to its core mission, but significantly more is needed. The Bank must promote country self-reliance by deploying resources where they are most needed and impactful, graduating more advanced countries from Bank support, delivering better access to reliable, affordable, and abundant energy, and increasing competition and quality in Bank-financed procurement to improve development outcomes. And, in doing these things, the Bank must be more efficient and selective, pursuing operations with the greatest development impact, rather than simply pushing as much money as possible out the door.
We expect the Bank to phase out sovereign lending to countries that have long since met the graduation policy criteria so that the Bank can refocus its resources where they are most needed and impactful. Despite being long overdue, the planned phase outs of lending to China and Poland represent an important milestone for both countries. As the Bank continues to implement the graduation policy, we expect to see Graduation Progress Notes that meaningfully assess where graduation-eligible countries fall short of meeting the graduation criteria, and associated Country Partnership Frameworks focusing Bank programming on addressing those shortcomings. As the Bank enters the longest period in its history without a country graduating from lending eligibility, World Bank Management should take concrete steps to ensure that graduations resume.
Similarly, the International Development Association (IDA) must facilitate graduation so that it can focus its resources on the poorest countries where its investments in foundational infrastructure, as well as in reforms that promote debt sustainability and transparency, enhanced domestic resource mobilization, and strong public financial management, help countries develop and stand up to coercive and opaque lending terms from some creditors. As we discuss IDA’s resources over the next 15 months, IDA must clearly identify its accomplishments in boosting growth, and reducing poverty. We also support extending the deadline for low-income countries to subscribe to the shares allocated under the 2018 capital increases, helping them preserve and strengthen their representation and voice in the institution.
Contributing to country self-reliance also requires the Bank to focus more on the sectors most critical to development and industrialization, chief among them reliable and affordable energy. Energy abundance sparks economic abundance. We continue to support the World Bank and African Development Bank goal to extend energy access to 300 million more people in Africa. Achieving this goal will require the Bank to take a technology-neutral approach rather than restricting borrower choice, including by removing constraints on its support for natural gas and positively responding to borrower demand for gas projects. Accordingly, the World Bank Group should formally retire its prohibition on financing upstream gas and oil. The Bank cannot credibly invoke country ownership while categorically excluding upstream projects before their development merits are even assessed.
We welcome the recent approval of an IDA project to secure near-term gas supply, prepare mid-and downstream investments, and develop gas strategies in West Africa. Ultimately, success must be measured by whether countries gain the energy access needed to drive growth, create jobs, and reduce poverty. We therefore welcome the move to focus on outcomes rather than on arbitrary targets. To further support energy abundance, the United States is also making an initial contribution to the Nuclear Energy Assistance Trust Fund, which will help countries lay the groundwork for future nuclear energy investments.
Critical minerals are foundational inputs to growth and economic security. We welcome the Bank’s recently approved Metals and Minerals Implementation Plan. The Bank has an important role to play through policy and regulatory reform, investing in enabling infrastructure and local processing capacity, project finance and de-risking, and strengthening natural resource management. This includes deep-sea mining, where the Bank can play a catalytic role by providing knowledge and guidance in a nascent sector.
Directing resources to countries most in need is not enough; the Bank must position those resources to deliver value. Procurement policies that reward distortive industrial policies, encourage subsidies, and incentivize corruption and collusion ultimately undermine development, stifle the private sector, and result in higher long-term costs. The Bank must pursue procurement reforms that result in greater competition and quality. We recognize recent efforts to expand the use of quality-based procurement approaches, boost the use of local labor, and improve industry outreach, but much of this was necessary just to move closer to the value-for-money objective embodied in the Procurement Framework adopted over a decade ago. The Bank needs to assess where its current procurement framework, policies, and implementation are still not delivering competition and quality needed for long-term development and adopt further reforms and capacity-building measures to address those shortcomings. The Bank’s peer institutions are implementing a robust procurement reform agenda. We expect the World Bank to lead on these efforts rather than fall behind.
The International Finance Corporation (IFC) can play an important role in mobilizing private capital to support economic growth and private sector development. But higher mobilization levels are not a substitute for the harder work of creating markets and crowding in truly private investment in poorer, less creditworthy countries. We call on the IFC to redouble efforts to meet its 2018 capital increase pledge to make 40 percent of new commitments in the poorest and most fragile countries. The IFC’s rate of progress towards this commitment has fallen unacceptably short, underscoring the need to align the institution more closely with its core mission.
Finally, the IMF and World Bank are ultimately taxpayer-funded public institutions whose budgets should reflect the narrower set of operations that comes with refocusing on their core missions. We appreciate the flat real administrative budget growth being pursued at both institutions this fiscal year, and expect to see this same approach in future years. Both institutions and their Governors can and should go further, including by indefinitely freezing – and even reducing – Executive Board budgets and salaries, which now have a combined annual cost over $200 million. The reduction in the IMF Board’s core budget this year is an important first step in this direction. The Boards are significantly more expensive, both in overall and per-capita terms, than at other international financial institutions. Every unnecessary dollar spent on the Boards is a dollar that cannot be used to reduce poverty, promote macroeconomic stability, or foster growth. The Bank, Fund, and their members must do more to restrain these inexcusably bloated budgets. We also call on the IMF to divest from the Bretton Woods Recreation Center and the Concordia Hotel.
Streamlining policy priorities will allow both the World Bank and IMF to focus limited public resources on effectively fulfilling their core mandates while responding to crises. We look forward to working with Management, staff, and other shareholders, to accomplish this task.
###
title: Statement from U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent for the World Bank Development Committee and IMF International Monetary and Financial Committee

New Jersey Brothers Plead Guilty to Stealing More Than $2.6 Million, Collectively, in Tax Refunds
Two New Jersey brothers pleaded guilty in September to stealing more than $978,126 and $1,643,172, respectively, in tax refunds.
According to court documents and statements made in court, in early 2023, Ronald Chrichlow, of Somerset, and Gordon Chrichlow, formerly of Carteret, each filed a false 2022 Form 1041, U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts, on behalf of their trusts. These Forms 1041 falsely reported that the trusts made tax payments to the IRS when they had not and claimed refunds of $978,126 and $1,643,172, respectively. Pursuant to these false filings, in March 2023, the IRS issued Ronald Chrichlow a U.S. Treasury check for $978,126 and Gordon Chrichlow a U.S. Treasury check for $1,643,172. With his proceeds, Gordon Chrichlow purchased a Porsche Taycan for approximately $117,364 and bought a house for approximately $686,258.
In August 2023, the IRS assigned a revenue officer to collect the fraudulently obtained refunds. In response to IRS collection efforts, the Chrichlow brothers mailed to the IRS amended 2022 Forms 1041 for their trusts that removed the originally claimed tax payments. They also mailed 2022 Forms 1040-NR, U.S. Nonresident Alien Income Tax Return, on which they falsely claimed not to be residents of the United States and falsely claimed that their 2022 income was tax exempt pursuant to a tax treaty.
The Chrichlow brothers also willfully failed to file their personal income tax returns in some years, despite earning income. Ronald Chrichlow earned $960,000 in income between 2021 and 2024, but did not file income tax returns between 2022 and 2024. For 2021, he filed a false tax return falsely reporting tax payments he did not make in order to claim a tax refund of $93,228 to which he was not entitled. Gordon Chrichlow willfully failed to file his 2021 through 2024 tax returns, despite earning more than $1.4 million in gross income in those years.
The Chrichlow brothers also filed false COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan applications on behalf of their business entities in 2020 that reported false numbers of employees and false gross receipts, in order to receive loans and grants to which they were not entitled.
Ronald and Gordon Chrichlow each pleaded guilty to one count of theft of government funds. Ronald Chrichlow is scheduled to be sentenced on January 12, 2027, and Gordon Chrichlow is scheduled to be sentenced on January 27, 2027. They each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the cases.
Trial Attorneys Melissa Siskind and Likhitha Butchireddygari of the Fraud Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the cases.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: New Jersey Brothers Plead Guilty to Stealing More Than $2.6 Million, Collectively, in Tax Refunds

EPA Administrator Zeldin Announces American Farmer First Policy During Three-Day Swing in Iowa and Wisconsin
WASHINGTON – Earlier this week, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin traveled across Iowa and into Wisconsin for a number of meetings and engagements with farmers, industry leaders, veterans, and local officials where he highlighted the Trump EPA’s efforts to support American farmers, advance right-to-repair efforts, strengthen domestic energy production, and improve water infrastructure.
During his swing through Iowa, Administrator Zeldin announced EPA’s proposal to reallocate 100% of additional 2025 small refinery exemption volumes under the Renewable Fuel Standard at the Dubuque County Farm Bureau in Iowa. The proposal keeps the agency’s promise to propose 100% reallocation by the end of October and furthers the Trump Administration’s commitment to open stable markets for American farmers to sell their crops. If finalized as proposed, the 100% reallocation will ensure that farmers in Iowa and across the country do not lose the demand for their crops, while also unleashing American energy.
The announcement came on the heels of Administrator Zeldin and U.S. Representative Ashley Hinson’s (R-IA-02) tour of Big River United Energy ethanol facility in Dyersville, Iowa. The visit highlighted the role of American biofuels, which will benefit from EPA’s proposal if finalized, in supporting farmers, rural economies, and domestic energy production.
On Sunday, October 11, Administrator Zeldin visited Summit Products, a member of the Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA), in Altoona, Iowa. While there he discussed EPA’s implementation of its February Right to Repair guidance and President Trump’s Freedom to Fix memo. The President’s memo directed EPA to deliver two things: ensure every American has the Freedom to Fix their vehicle and reduce the reliance on California’s emission certification process for aftermarket vehicle products. He highlighted EPA’s work to ensure farmers and equipment operators have the right to repair their own equipment instead of being forced to take it to a dealer, which is often more expensive. Administrator Zeldin touted EPA’s July decision to recognize SEMA as a certification authority for aftermarket vehicle parts.
To celebrate National Farmer’s Day on Monday, October 12, Administrator Zeldin participated in a farmers’ roundtable at Savor the Barn in Monticello, Iowa. Administrator Zeldin met with representatives from the Iowa Farm Bureau, Iowa Soybean Association, Iowa Corn Growers Association, and local agricultural producers to discuss EPA actions to grow the agriculture economy while maintaining strong environmental protections including EPA’s work on to end deratements caused by Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) system failures, the agency’s E15 waivers, EPA’s Waters of the United States (WOTUS) proposal, and more.
Later in the day, Administrator Zeldin and Representative Hinson spent time with local veterans at the Veterans Freedom Center in Dubuque, Iowa. During the visit they heard powerful stories about veterans helping veterans as they transition back home. The pair ended the day by touring Dubuque’s Water & Resource Recovery Center, where a $2 million federally funded project is planned to support upgrades to the facility’s capacity to treat high-strength waste. The improvements are intended to help the facility better serve local residents and businesses.
Administrator Zeldin ended his 3-day Midwest swing by meeting up with Representative Derrick Van Orden (R-WI-03) in Cuba City, Wisconsin where they toured the sixth generation Tranel Family Farms. The Trump EPA’s work reversing DEF deratements, restoring the Right to Repair, and applying common sense to environmental regulations were major topics throughout the visit.
title: EPA Administrator Zeldin Announces American Farmer First Policy During Three-Day Swing in Iowa and Wisconsin

text:
Dingell, Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Delay 340B Rebate Model, Protect Access to Affordable Medicine
  
  
    
      Washington, D.C. ,
      October 14, 2026
    
    
    
    
  
  
  
  
  
  
    
      U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rob Bresnahan, Jr. (R-PA-08), Tracey Mann (R-KS-01), and Lois Frankel (D-FL-22) introduced the 340B Rebate Model Delay Act, bipartisan legislation to delay implementation of the federal government’s 340B rebate model, citing concerns that the new system could create significant financial and administrative risks for healthcare providers and patients.
“Families in Michigan are already struggling to pay for healthcare,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “Safety-net providers are not in the financial position to front this money, especially in light of Medicaid cuts, and will either have to hike up prices for patients or stop offering lifesaving drugs. This bill would delay the implementation of this rebate model so we can ensure people’s lives are not put at risk.”
Under the rebate model, participating providers would pay the full price of certain prescription drugs upfront and receive the 340B discount later through rebates. This could create cash-flow pressures, increase administrative burdens, and make it more difficult for community health centers, hospitals, and other safety-net providers to maintain access to affordable medications.
“Patients and providers should not have to bear the risks of an untested change to a program that helps deliver affordable medicines to communities across the country,” said Congressman Bresnahan. “Congress needs more time to evaluate the potential financial and administrative consequences of the rebate model and ensure that any changes to 340B protect patients and the providers who serve them.”
“Rural hospitals and health care providers across the Big First District rely on the 340B program to stretch limited resources and continue providing quality care close to home,” said Congressman Mann. “The new rebate model would force these providers to pay higher upfront costs and wait to be reimbursed, putting unnecessary financial strain on facilities that already operate on tight margins. This legislation provides certainty for our rural health care providers by stopping the rebate model through 2028 and protecting their ability to serve patients in rural communities.”
“Safety-net hospitals and community health centers are lifelines for low-income families, seniors, and people without health insurance,” said Congresswoman Lois Frankel. “Our bipartisan bill stops a new requirement forcing these providers to pay full price for prescription drugs and then wait for rebates. Their limited resources should go toward caring for patients, not waiting for drug companies to pay them back. We should be making it easier for people to get the medicine they need, not putting more financial strain on the hospitals and clinics they depend on.”
The 340B Drug Pricing Program allows eligible healthcare providers serving underserved communities to purchase covered outpatient drugs at discounted prices and stretch limited resources to provide care.
Bill text can be found HERE.
title: Dingell, Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Delay 340B Rebate Model, Protect Access to Affordable Medicine

USDA Makes Historic $3.3B Loan to Build Electric Generation Facility in Georgia
(Washington, D.C., October 14, 2026) – Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins announced a historic $3.3 billion loan to Oglethorpe Power Corporation to help finance its Smarr Combined-Cycle electric generating facility in Monroe County, Georgia, during a visit to the construction site. This new facility will deliver dependable, affordable power for generations while helping meet America’s growing energy needs.
This loan is the largest ever delivered in the history of USDA Rural Development’s Rural Utilities Service and comes at a critical time for investing in American energy. As stated by President Trump, the United States is experiencing a surge in electricity demand from rapid technological advancements. This project strengthens the nation’s electrical grid, and lower-cost financing will help keep electricity affordable for Georgia families.
"Historic times call for historic actions, and this tremendous investment in America’s electric power grid is evidence of President Trump’s focus on powering our nation forward," said Secretary Brooke L. Rollins. "Great things are happening with our rural electric cooperatives nationwide, and Oglethorpe Power is one example in Georgia through this project, which will generate reliable electricity, create jobs, and bring significant investment to rural America."
"We are proud to partner with Oglethorpe on this significant investment in America's rural energy infrastructure," said USDA Under Secretary for Rural Development Glen Smith. "As we celebrate National Cooperative Month, this announcement highlights the vital role rural electric cooperatives play in powering our communities, supporting local economies, and strengthening American energy independence. President Trump and Secretary Rollins are doubling down on investments in our power grid to ensure rural America remains a driving force behind our nation's economic prosperity."
“This historic loan will allow us to build the reliable generation Georgia families, farms and businesses need at a lower cost, helping our member cooperatives keep electricity affordable for the communities they serve,” said Annalisa Bloodworth, President and CEO of Oglethorpe Power. “We are grateful to USDA and RUS for their longstanding partnership and for providing the lower-cost financing that helps electric cooperatives make critical investments in reliable, affordable power.”
Oglethorpe Power is a generation cooperative owned by 38 electric distribution cooperatives that serve nearly 5 million people across Georgia. It supplies wholesale power through a diverse energy portfolio that includes natural gas, coal, nuclear, and hydroelectric resources, helping its member cooperatives provide reliable, affordable electricity to the Georgians they serve.
For more information on USDA Rural Development investments in rural America, visit the Rural Data Gateway. The Rural Data Gateway is an online tool that strengthens USDA Rural Development partnerships with rural people, entrepreneurs, government officials and Congress by making agency investment data accessible to the public.
If you’d like to subscribe to USDA Rural Development updates, visit our subscriber page.
###
title: USDA Makes Historic $3.3B Loan to Build Electric Generation Facility in Georgia

Rep. Panetta Leads Call for Transparency, Accountability in the Administration’s Global Health Strategy
Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) wrote a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio requesting greater transparency and stronger oversight of the Trump Administration’s “America First Global Health Strategy.” Rep. Panetta led 34 other lawmakers in calling for the public release of global health agreements and detailed answers about how the Administration will measure results, monitor spending, and respond to the misuse of U.S. taxpayer dollars.
Following the dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and the transfer of foreign assistance responsibilities to the U.S. Department of State, the Administration announced roughly $16 billion in bilateral assistance programs for 36 countries. Under the new model, assistance goes directly to foreign governments. However, only a handful of the agreements have been made publicly available, and the lawmakers raised concerns that many participating governments have a history of corruption involving foreign assistance.
“While we applaud efforts to build up global health mechanisms that fight HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, Ebola and other infectious diseases, this new model raises significant concerns about the efficient and transparent use of U.S. taxpayer dollars,” wrote Rep. Panetta and his colleagues. “Given that the Administration’s dismantling of USAID was triggered by alleged wasteful spending, we want to ensure this new foreign assistance model is free of waste, fraud and abuse.”
The lawmakers highlighted the multiple layers of oversight USAID used to monitor funding provided to nongovernmental organizations and other implementing partners, including contracting officers, program officials, technical experts, and the USAID Office of Inspector General. They cited testimony from the U.S. Government Accountability Office and the USAID Office of Inspector General indicating limited ability to track or audit funds sent directly to foreign governments. While acknowledging the need to modernize foreign assistance, the lawmakers warned that shifting to government-to-government assistance requires clear safeguards to protect taxpayer dollars.
“Failure to implement these programs thoughtfully, while ensuring accountability to the taxpayer, jeopardizes American leadership in the global health space, which is second to none. It also encourages nations to seek partnerships with our adversaries, while making America less safe, less strong and less prosperous,” continued the lawmakers.
The lawmakers requested written responses explaining how the Administration will define success and monitor whether the health agreements meet their objectives, who will oversee that work, and what staffing, technical expertise, and funding will support it. They also asked the State Department to identify the systems and safeguards it will use to track and audit spending and explain how it will respond to allegations or evidence of misuse, including whether it will immediately suspend assistance.
To ensure taxpayers can review these commitments, the lawmakers called for all existing and future global health agreements to be made publicly available. They requested a detailed explanation if the State Department cannot release the agreements.
The letter was also signed by Reps. Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Sanford Bishop (GA-02), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Jim Costa (CA-21), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Jared Golden (ME-02), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Bill Keating (MA-09), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Dave Min (CA-47), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Johnny Olszewski (MD-02), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Dina Titus (NV-01), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25).
The full text of the letter is available here and below:
Dear Secretary Rubio,
We write to express concerns about transparency and oversight of the Administration’s new bilateral international assistance model, which grants money directly to foreign governments. Following the dissolution of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID), and the transfer of foreign assistance to the U.S. Department of State, the Administration announced roughly $16 billion in bi-lateral assistance programs for 36 countries and launched the America First Global Health Strategy. While we applaud efforts to build up global health mechanisms that fight HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, Ebola and other infectious diseases, this new model raises significant concerns about the efficient and transparent use of U.S. taxpayer dollars.
Since the bi-lateral international assistance agreements were signed with host countries, only a handful have been made available to the U.S. public for review. Furthermore, many of the foreign governments that have signed Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with the State Department have a history of corruption with respect to foreign assistance.
USAID had several layers of accountability mechanisms built to help monitor funds sent to nongovernmental organizations (NGO) and other implementing partners, including country-based contracting officers, programmatic officials and U.S.-based technical officials, as well as the USAID Office of Inspector General (OIG). Testimony from the U.S. Government Accountability Office and the USAID OIG indicate that there is limited ability to track or audit U.S. taxpayer dollars sent directly to foreign governments. While many development stakeholders agree that a foreign assistance model based primarily on international NGOs needs improvement and modernization, the wholesale adoption of government-to-government assistance without accountability or transparency raises serious questions.
Given that the Administration’s dismantling of USAID was triggered by alleged wasteful spending, we want to ensure this new foreign assistance model is free of waste, fraud and abuse. We therefore request written responses to the following questions:
1) Please detail how the Administration will monitor and evaluate these health agreements to ensure they meet their objectives. How will success be defined?
2) Who will be charged with monitoring and evaluating these bi-lateral assistance agreements? What resources, including staffing, technical capacity, and financial support, are being deployed to support these efforts?
3) How will the State Department respond to allegations or evidence of improper use of U.S. taxpayer dollars used in foreign assistance? Do you plan to immediately cut off all aid if U.S. taxpayer money is not used for its intended purpose? If not, please explain why.
4) Please detail how the Administration plans to track and audit U.S. taxpayer dollars sent to foreign governments to ensure they are used for their purposes of supporting global health programs. What systems, tools, and safeguards are in place to ensure adequate monitoring and evaluation?
5) We request that all previously signed, as well as all future, global health agreements be made publicly available. If you are unable to do so, please provide a detailed explanation of why you can’t make these agreements publicly available for review to U.S. taxpayers.
Failure to implement these programs thoughtfully, while ensuring accountability to the taxpayer, jeopardizes American leadership in the global health space, which is second to none. It also encourages nations to seek partnerships with our adversaries, while making America less safe, less strong and less prosperous.
Thank you for your attention to these questions as we work toward a shared goal of ensuring quality oversight of a critical tool in our national security apparatus.
Sincerely,
###
title: Rep. Panetta Leads Call for Transparency, Accountability in the Administration’s Global Health Strategy

The legislation marks Ansari’s first bill passed into law
WASHINGTON – Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) celebrated the recent signing into law of her bipartisan Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act, legislation to increase transparency and accountability for taxpayer-funded federal projects that are significantly over budget or behind schedule. President Donald Trump signed the bill into law following its passage in both chambers of Congress.
“The American people deserve transparency and accountability for how their tax dollars are spent, especially as families struggle with the rising costs of everyday essentials,” said Rep. Ansari. “While the level of corruption across the federal government right now is stunning and unprecedented, this is a truly longstanding, bipartisan issue. Taxpayers deserve this transparency. And now they’ll have a great deal more.”
Text of Rep. Ansari’s Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act HERE.
The Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act requires the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to compile and submit an annual report to Congress identifying qualifying taxpayer-funded projects and detailing changes to their scope, estimated costs, and projected completion dates. The reporting requirement will give the public greater insight into federal projects experiencing significant delays or cost overruns.
The House of Representatives originally passed the legislation in July 2026. The Senate approved the bill in September, sending it to the President for his signature and final enactment into law.
Follow @RepYassAnsari on all social media platforms and visit Ansari.House.govto learn more.
###
title: Rep. Ansari Celebrates Her Bipartisan Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act Becoming Law

PHOTO RELEASE: Congresswoman Lee Delivers Remarks at 2026 National Clean Energy Week
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) delivered remarks during the 10th annual National Clean Energy Week’s Policymakers Symposium. She discussed the importance of fully harnessing our domestic geothermal resources, especially as the United States continues to face both increasing energy demands both at home and abroad.
As southern Nevada’s sole representative on the House Natural Resources Committee, Congresswoman Lee is doing everything possible to build the clean energy economy. She passed her Geothermal Energy Advancement Act, a bipartisan, six-bill geothermal permitting reform package, the most significant geothermal legislation in more than half a century. The package includes Lee’s bipartisan, bicameral Streamlining Thermal Energy through Advanced Mechanisms (STEAM) Act to expedite geothermal exploration and development, and her Geothermal Energy Opportunity (GEO) Act, which would reform — and speed up — the federal permitting process for geothermal projects.
###
title: PHOTO RELEASE: Congresswoman Lee Delivers Remarks at 2026 National Clean Energy Week

HHS Issues Final Demand to Medical Organizations to Answer for Sex-Rejecting Procedures for Minors
WASHINGTON, D.C.—OCTOBER 14, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) today sent letters to leading medical organizations requesting that they state clearly whether they continue to support sex-rejecting procedures for minors and account for the evidence-base and HHS reports showing the harms these interventions inflict on minors in their guidance and position statements.
The letters were sent to the World Professional Association for Transgender Health (WPATH), the American Medical Association, American Psychiatric Association, American Psychological Association, Endocrine Society, and others.
“When medical organizations set standards that shape the care of children, they have a responsibility to explain the evidence behind those standards,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “HHS has asked these organizations for clear answers about their current positions, the evidence supporting their guidance, and whether they intend to change it. Parents and clinicians deserve transparency, and we expect these organizations to provide it.”
HHS previously requested a substantive response from these organizations regarding their positions on sex-rejecting procedures for children and any planned updates to their guidance or position statements.
The Department is now requesting a clear statement of the current position of these organizations on sex-rejecting procedures for minors, identification of any planned revisions to their respective guidance, and a timeline for those changes. HHS expects a written response within 10 business days.
Today’s action is the latest step in the Trump Administration’s sustained effort to protect children from sex-rejecting procedures and bring transparency and accountability to so-called “gender medicine” in pediatric care. HHS has moved to bar hospitals participating in Medicare and Medicaid from performing these procedures on children and prohibit federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for them; exposed potentially fraudulent insurance coding associated with sex-rejecting procedures on minors; and released research examining ideological influences associated with support for these clinical practices.
Organizations that set standards of care and medical guidelines for children and shape accepted medical practice have a responsibility to answer for the consequences of their guidance. The Trump Administration will make sure they do.

HUD Makes It Easier to Build More Housing
Updated FHA policy encourages new housing supply by removing outdated restrictions for Multifamily Build to Rent communities.
October 14, 2026
WASHINGTON - HUD today announced that its Federal Housing Administration (FHA) is expanding access to quality rental housing by allowing Build to Rent communities to qualify for FHA-insured financing under two of its Multifamily mortgage insurance programs. Effective immediately, this update makes it easier to finance new rental homes and helps increase the supply of rental housing, particularly in light of manufactured housing innovation.
“America needs more affordable housing,” said Secretary Scott Turner. “We’re eliminating barriers to spur development, expand rental options, and improve housing affordability for hardworking American families.”
Build to Rent communities are multifamily rental properties that consist of single-family homes, duplexes, or triplexes, including both site-built and manufactured homes. These properties will now be treated under the same terms and conditions as traditional multifamily rental developments, subject to the specific requirements outlined in today’s Mortgagee Letter.
“Expanding housing supply, including new rental housing, is essential to improving affordability,” said Joe Gormley, currently overseeing the FHA and Office of Housing. “Combined with other initiatives we are working on at HUD, including chassis removal in our manufactured housing programs, we are unshackling the market to deliver housing where it’s needed most.”
FHA’s updated policy reflects growing demand for single-family, duplex, and triplex rental housing, as well as the expanding presence of professionally managed Build to Rent developments. The policy applies to FHA's Section 221(d)(4) program for new construction and Section 223(f) program for acquisition or refinancing of recently developed rental communities.
This change supports President Trump's efforts to remove barriers to housing and aligns with Executive Order 14376, Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers.

Congressman Gonzalez Delivers Over $9 Million in Federal Funds for Cameron County
Federal funds will expand public parking for commercial truckers at Los Indios Port of Entry
Washington, D.C.—Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) announced $9,182,608 in federal funds for Cameron County to reconstruct approximately 0.35 miles of Rio Grande Avenue and provide access to a new public commercial motor vehicle parking facility near the Los Indios Port of Entry. The project will include roughly 305 dedicated parking truck spaces. This investment will also support roadway improvements, driver amenities, security features, an automated weight station, and intelligent parking system technology.
“South Texas is an international hub for trade and commerce, and our infrastructure must keep pace with heightened demands,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “As working families continue to struggle with rising costs, this $9.1 million federal investment will provide commercial truckers with support to maintain efficient operations when supplying our region and the rest of the country with goods and materials. As your Congressman, I proudly passed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that authorized this funding, and I will continue working to ensure our ports of entry and the workers who keep it running have the resources they need to operate efficiently.”
“We’re extremely grateful to the U.S. Department of Transportation for awarding Cameron County over $9 million for the Los Indios Bridge Commercial Motor Vehicle (CMV) Parking Facility,” said Cameron County Judge Eddie Treviño, Jr. “Logistics and cross-border trade are vital to Cameron County’s economy. This investment will strengthen our connections with Mexico and improve our regional trade infrastructure by providing truck drivers with a dedicated, safe place to rest before continuing their routes. In turn, this project will help support more efficient cross-border commerce and strengthen supply chains across the nation.”
Today’s announcement was made possible by Congressman Gonzalez’s support of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which was enacted in 2021 and provided $1.2 trillion to modernize America’s infrastructure, including roads, bridges, water and wastewater, clean energy and broadband access. Through the law’s five-year funding process, $7.25 billion was allocated to the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects (INFRA) program to strengthen America’s supply chains and improve road safety nationwide. The Los Indios Port of Entry is one of 14 projects receiving designated funding for truck parking in Fiscal Year 2026.

Florida Man Sentenced to Prison for Tax Refund Fraud
A Florida man was sentenced on October 6, 2026, to 36 months in prison for filing a false tax return on behalf of a trust he controlled as part of a $4.2 million refund fraud scheme.
According to court documents and statements made in court, McDonald Preval, of Miami, filed numerous false tax returns for himself and trusts he claimed to control. The trust tax returns reported that the trusts had earned significant income and made tax withholding payments to the IRS, purportedly entitling the trusts to large tax refunds. In fact, the trusts did not have the claimed income, and did not make payments in the amounts claimed on the returns, and therefore were not entitled to the refunds Preval claimed. He also filed tax returns for 2023 that did not include the income from his employment. The false tax returns Preval caused to be filed on behalf of purported trusts and himself collectively sought tax refunds totaling more than $4.2 million. Preval obtained more than $580,000 from his scheme, which he used to pay off the mortgage loan on his house and other personal expenses.
Preval pleaded guilty to one count of filing a false tax return. In addition to a term of imprisonment, U.S. District Judge Cecilia M. Altonaga ordered Preval to pay $580,647 in restitution to the IRS and to serve one year of supervised release.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated the case.
Trial Attorneys Melissa Siskind and Kavitha Bondada of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Florida Man Sentenced to Prison for Tax Refund Fraud

OREGON LAWMAKERS URGE CONTINUED SUPPORT FOR OREGON’S HAZELNUT INDUSTRY
Eugene, OR – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led members of Oregon’s congressional delegation in a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins that calls on the Department to deliver critical federal support to Oregon’s hazelnut industry under the federal Section 32 purchase program.
“The hazelnut industry is a massive and integral part of our state’s agricultural economy; its size and longevity represent generations of farmers and handlers who have dedicated their lives to producing and distributing a product many communities depend on for their livelihoods,” wrote the lawmakers.
The lawmakers’ letter calls on USDA to include Oregon hazelnuts, which account for 99 percent of hazelnuts produced in the United States, in this year’s Section 32 purchases, supporting growers, harvesters, processors, and agricultural economies primarily in Oregon’s Willamette Valley during a period of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty in a global market.
They stressed, “In recent years, disruptions in important export markets caused by these compounding issues have been particularly difficult for certain kernel sizes and grades that are high-quality, marketable food products but have fewer commercial outlets. These imbalances and market losses create uncertainty and pressure for our farmers and producers and threaten the steady distribution needed to prevent compounding product surpluses year-to-year.”
In addition to Merkley, the letter was signed by U.S. Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), and Val Hoyle (OR-04).

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Delivers $200 Million Truck Parking Expansion Across the Country in Major Win For American Truckers
Funds will cover 14 expansion projects across 12 states to tackle truckers’ #1 problem when hauling critical cargo
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced a $200 million investment to expand truck parking in 12 states through the Department’s Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight & Highway Projects (INFRA) program. These investments will expand public parking for hardworking truckers along America's most critical freight corridors and help reduce fatigue-related accidents, improve supply chain efficiency, and deliver significant savings.
Reminder: 40% of truckers spend over an hour a day searching for parking—costing our national economy billions in wasted time. Limited safe, public commercial vehicle parking is also a safety issue – forcing truckers to park in harm's way.
“American truckers are finally getting the attention and support they deserve thanks to President Trump,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “These patriotic men and women work hard to ensure our store shelves are stocked, our gas stations are fueled, and our packages are delivered. They shouldn’t have to spend over an hour looking for a safe place to rest at the end of the day. This nationwide investment will make America’s truckers safer, enhance our supply chains, and reduce freight costs.”
The investments are going toward 14 truck parking projects in 12 states, including:
- $11.95 million to the Georgia Ports Authority to build the Port of Savannah Commercial Motor Vehicle Parking Area adjacent to Georgia State Route 21 in Garden City, Georgia. This facility will have approximately 275 commercial vehicle spaces.
- $24.5 million to the Iowa Department of Transportation to expand and modernize commercial motor vehicle parking at six public rest areas along I-80 in Mitchellville, Wilton, Victor, Minden, and Underwood.
- $6 million to the North Carolina State Ports Authority to construct approximately 140 dedicated commercial motor vehicle parking spaces and approximately 50 container staging positions at the Port of Wilmington in New Hanover County, North Carolina.
- $5 million to the City of Fort Worth to construct approximately 100 new commercial motor vehicle parking spaces at the Pilot Travel Center in Fort Worth, Texas, along I-35.
- $9 million to Cameron County, Texas, to reconstruct approximately 0.35 miles of Rio Grande Avenue to provide access to a new public commercial motor vehicle parking facility near the Los Indios Port of Entry that will include approximately 305 dedicated truck parking spaces.
- $15 million to the Wisconsin Department of Transportation to expand commercial motor vehicle parking by approximately 106 spaces between two safety rest areas along a rural area of I-41 in Dodge County, Wisconsin.’
“Truck parking is one of the most persistent challenges faced by American truckers today, and under President Trump and Secretary Duffy, we’re tackling it head on,” said Federal Motor Carrier Administrator Derek D. Barrs. “This investment will deliver hundreds of new spots across the country, helping hardworking truck drivers get the rest they need and reducing dangerous roadside parking on some of America’s most important corridors.”
These investments were made via the INFRA program, which bolsters America’s supply chains and improves road safety for families by building highways, bridges, and port infrastructure nationwide.
See the full list of awards HERE.
Additional Information:
The Trump Administration has delivered historic wins for the American trucker in its effort to make American roads safe again. Since April 2025, USDOT has invested more than $300 million in truck parking grants.
In July 2026, the Administration delivered an additional $62 million to address the truck parking shortage in Kentucky, Wyoming, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Illinois via the Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development (BUILD) grant program.

October 14, 2026
Pressley, City of Boston Announce More Than $16 Million to Modernize Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park
Pressley, City of Boston, Sec. Matias, State Rep. Consalvo Announce Initial Phase of Renovations that include Energy Retrofits, Accessibility Upgrades, Sustainable Infrastructure, and Workforce Opportunities
BOSTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), alongside Mayor Michelle Wu, Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities (EOHLC) Secretary Juana Matias, Representative Rob Consalvo, and Boston Housing Authority (BHA) Administrator Kenzie Bok,joined residents to announce more than $16 million in state, city, and federal funding to modernize the Fairmount public housing community in Hyde Park. This announcement represents the latest investment in the city’s public housing communities.
The funding includes $1M of Community Project Fund investment secured by Congresswoman Pressley and Senators Edward Markey and Elizabeth Warren, a $10 million High Leverage Asset Preservation Program (HILAPP) grant from EOHLC, and $5 million in City of Boston capital funding for the Fairmount Modernization Project. The Boston Public Health Commission has granted funds for open space improvements and community garden installations. Together, the funding will create a more accessible and resilient community.
“Residents in the Massachusetts 7th not only deserve a safe, stable place to call home, but also one that reflects modern-day needs in accessibility, resiliency, and sustainability—and this essential funding to modernize the Fairmount Apartments will do exactly that,” said Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley. “This investment is a reflection of community input realized and I’m grateful for every engaged resident who made their voice heard. I’m proud to deliver this funding alongside our city and state partners in Mayor Wu, Secretary Matias, Administrator Bok, Rep. Consalvo, and others to invest in existing public housing and improve livability for our communities.”
“Over the last five years, Boston has built nearly 16,000 new units of housing throughout our neighborhoods. In order to make our city a home for everyone, we must also preserve and modernize the affordable homes that already exist,” said Mayor Michelle Wu. “I’m grateful to all our partners for helping secure funding for this comprehensive, multi-phase renovation of the Fairmount Apartments, and I look forward to working with residents to deliver beautiful, upgraded homes for these families.”
“The Boston Housing Authority is so grateful to our city, state, and federal partners for investing in our public housing communities,” said Kenzie Bok, Administrator of the Boston Housing Authority. “With this funding, Fairmount will remain a welcoming place for families to call Hyde Park home for decades to come.”
The BHA is kicking off a Master Planning process for the Fairmount community, creating an area-wide vision while beginning a first phase of physical improvements. The initial phase of upgrades will focus on modernizing unit interiors, making 5% of apartments fully accessible, electrifying heating and hot water systems, and adding cooling. It will also include building envelope improvements and installing green stormwater infrastructure to support the community’s long-term sustainability and climate resilience.
“Thanks to Governor Healey’s Affordable Homes Act, HLC has been able to expand the funding needed to improve the state’s public housing system,” said Housing and Livable Communities Secretary Juana Matias. “We’re not just building new housing, but investing in the homes we already have and the people who live in them. The preservation of Fairmount Apartments is exactly what that commitment looks like.”
“I am thrilled that this enormous investment is happening at the Fairmount Housing Development, literally blocks away from my home here in Hyde Park,” said State Representative Rob Consalvo. “This partnership between the State, City, and Federal government will ensure that the residents of this development will be able to live in safe, modern and accessible units now and for years to come.”
An additional federal investment secured by the Congressional delegation is going to support flood mitigation for affordable housing developments, including BHA properties. The city and BHA have collaborated on multi-site stormwater projects serving the Fairmount, Gallivan, and Franklin Field communities, an effort bolstered by this federal backing. The project will fund a community garden and new rain gardens to mitigate stormwater pollution and prevent flooding. Through Boston’s PowerCorps program, local residents will be trained to build and maintain the rain gardens while earning green career credentials.
“As the District 5 City Councilor, Chair of the Boston City Council’s Housing Committee, and someone who grew up in public housing, I know firsthand how important it is for families to have a place they can be proud to call home,” said Councilor Enrique Pepén. “This $16 million investment in the Fairmount Apartments is exactly the kind of commitment our residents deserve, one that strengthens our communities, improves quality of life, and ensures families can continue to thrive in the neighborhoods they call home. I’m grateful to our state and federal partners for their collaboration and commitment to making this important investment possible.”
“This $16 million investment is an exciting step forward in advancing affordable, accessible, and high-quality housing for residents of Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park,” said Councilor Ruthzee Louijeune. “By investing in our public housing communities, we are strengthening neighborhoods and ensuring that families have safe, stable homes where they can thrive. I look forward to seeing the lasting impact these improvements will have on Fairmount residents for years to come.”
Fairmount Apartments in Hyde Park was constructed in 1951 and includes over 200 units of state public housing.
As a Member of the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance of the House Financial Services Committee (FSC), Rep. Pressley has consistently advocated for policies that affirm housing as a human right and center the dignity and humanity of all people.
In June 2026, the 21st Century Road to Housing Act passed Congress and included four bills led by Congresswoman Pressley that would address the housing crisis and increase pathways to equitable and affordable housing. The bills will address bias in home valuations, expand affordable housing, strengthen oversight of corporate landlords, and help families reach financial stability. The bill became law despite Donald Trump’s refusal to sign it.
Rep. Pressley’s four bills in the housing package include:
- The Appraisal Modernization Act. This bill would promote equity and combat systemic bias in the home appraisal process that has disadvantaged many current and aspiring homeowners—especially homeowners of color.
- The Innovation Fund Act. This bill would establish a grant program to reward communities that are taking innovative steps to increase housing supply.
- The Renter Resource Center Act. This bill would protect renters and strengthen oversight of corporations by creating a database of institutional investors that buy single-family homes, requiring HUD to provide resources to renters, and more.
- Helping More Families Save Act. This bill would help families receiving federal housing assistance achieve financial independence as a pathway to wealth building by modernizing and expanding HUD’s Family Self-Sufficiency (FSS) program.

SCHNEIDER INTRODUCES LEGISLATION TO PROTECT ACCESS TO ONLINE RESOURCES FOR LGBTQ STUDENTS
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL –Today, during LGBTQ history month, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) introduced legislation to ensure critical online LGBTQ resources are not blocked at schools and public libraries. Currently, public schools and libraries that receive discounted telecommunications and internet rates through the Federal Communication Commission (FCC) E-Rate program must enforce an internet safety policy that in some cases leads to the blocking of useful LGBTQ resources. The Don’t Block LGBTQ Act would clarify that schools and public libraries that block LGBTQ resources would lose access to discounted rates under the E-rate program.
“During LGBTQ History Month, we celebrate the countless LGBTQ Americans who have strengthened our communities and helped move our country forward,” said Schneider. “LGBTQ Americans, especially young people, deserve access to information, support, and resources that can make a meaningful difference in their lives. I'm proud to introduce this legislation to ensure LGBTQ individuals are not prevented from receiving support – whether asking health questions, responding to bullying, or seeking advice about coming out to family and friends.”
According to the American Psychological Association the majority of LGBTQ+ youth have turned to a mental health professional or experienced symptoms of anxiety. Access to resources on where to reach for help is critical to ensuring youth have the support they need.
View the full bill text here.
title: SCHNEIDER INTRODUCES LEGISLATION TO PROTECT ACCESS TO ONLINE RESOURCES FOR LGBTQ STUDENTS

ROCHESTER, MN – Today, U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon visited Minnesota as part of her Returning Education to the States Tour.
Secretary McMahon began her visit at Great Oaks Academy, a public charter school serving students in grades K-10. The visit included a student choir ensemble performance, a recitation of the Pledge of Allegiance in Latin, and a presentation by a fifth-grade poetry class. Afterward, she participated in a Teachers Roundtable to discuss instructional practices and faculty experiences.
Next, Secretary McMahon toured Dakota County Technical College to see how students are preparing for in-demand industries, observing programs for veterinary technology, process technology, and electrical linework. Following the tour, she joined members of the Minnesota State Legislature for a lunch and roundtable discussion focused on returning more education decision-making back to the state and local levels.
Alongside U.S. Representatives Brad Finstad and Pete Stauber, Secretary McMahon wrapped the day at Rochester Community and Technical College. The group toured the campus's hands-on training labs, checking out the dental simulation, peace officer simulation, and automotive spaces.
“Minnesota is the 44th stop on the Returning Education to the States Tour,” said U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. “What our visits across the state make clear is that a truly responsive education system cannot be driven by federal mandates. From foundational civics and early literacy to high-tech medical and trade labs, success happens when local educators and state leaders have the autonomy to build programs that directly match the unique academic and workforce needs of their own communities.”
Background:
On her Returning Education to the States Tour, Secretary McMahon is traveling to all 50 states to hear directly from teachers, parents, students, and community leaders about what is working in their communities and to compile a toolkit of best practices to share with states across the nation. Learn more about Secretary McMahon’s Returning Education to the States Tour here.
title: U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon Visits Minnesota on Returning Education to the States Tour

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Small Business Administration announced today the opening of a Disaster Loan Outreach Center in Washoe County to assist businesses, private nonprofit organizations, and residents affected by the Bug and Hawk Fires occurring Aug. 8 – Sept. 9.
Beginning Thursday, Oct. 15, SBA customer service representatives will be on hand at the Disaster Loan Outreach Center in Reno to answer questions and assist with the disaster loan application process. Walk-ins are welcome, and in-person appointments can be scheduled in advance at appointment.sba.gov.
The hours of operation are as follows:
WASHOE COUNTY
Disaster Loan Outreach Center
North Valleys Community Center
Opens on Thursday, Oct. 15 at 9 a.m.
Monday – Friday, 9 a.m. – 4 p.m.
Closes permanently Friday, Oct. 30 at 4 p.m.
“When disasters strike, SBA’s Disaster Loan Outreach Centers perform an important role by assisting small businesses and their communities,” said Chris Stallings, Associate Administrator of the Office of Disaster Recovery at SBA. “At these centers, our specialists help business owners and residents apply for disaster loans and learn about the full range of programs available to support their recovery.”
Businesses and nonprofits are eligible to apply for business physical disaster loans and may borrow up to $2 million to repair or replace disaster-damaged or destroyed real estate, machinery and equipment, inventory, and other business assets.
Homeowners and renters are eligible to apply for home and personal property loans and may borrow up to $100,000 to replace or repair personal property, such as clothing, furniture, cars, and appliances. Homeowners may apply for up to $500,000 to replace or repair their primary residence.
Applicants may be eligible for a loan increase of up to 20% of their verified physical damage, for mitigation purposes. Eligible mitigation improvements may include insulating pipes, walls and attics, weather stripping doors and windows, and installing storm windows to help protect property and occupants from future disasters.
The SBA’s Economic Injury Disaster Loan program is available to small businesses, small agricultural cooperatives, and private nonprofit organizations — including faith‑based organizations — with financial losses directly related to the disaster. The SBA is unable to provide disaster loans to agricultural producers, farmers, or ranchers, except for small aquaculture enterprises.
Economic Injury Disaster Loan’s are available for working capital needs caused by the disaster and are available even if the small business or private nonprofit did not suffer any physical damage. The loans may be used to pay fixed debts, payroll, accounts payable, and other bills which could not be paid due to the disaster.
Interest rates are as low as 4% for businesses, 3.625% for nonprofits, and 3% for homeowners and renters, with terms up to 30 years. Interest does not begin to accrue, and payments are not due until 12 months from the date of the first loan disbursement. The SBA determines eligibility and sets loan amounts and terms based on each applicant’s financial condition.
To apply online, visit sba.gov/disaster. Applicants may also call SBA’s National Support Network Center at (866) SBA-HELP or email disastercustomerservice@sba.gov for more information on disaster assistance. For people who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
The filing deadline to return applications for physical property damage is Nov. 10. The deadline to return economic injury applications is June 11, 2027.
###
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of business ownership. As the only go-to resource and voice for small businesses backed by the strength of the federal government, the SBA empowers entrepreneurs and small business owners with the resources and support they need to start, grow, expand their businesses, or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA Opens Disaster Loan Outreach Center in Reno

Congressman Christian Menefee Hosts First-Ever Telephone Town Hall with Hundreds of Houston Constituents
HOUSTON, TX — Yesterday, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) hosted his first-ever telephone town hall, connecting with hundreds of constituents across Texas’s 18th Congressional District for an hour-long discussion on the issues affecting Houston families. During the event, Congressman Menefee answered questions directly from constituents on a wide range of topics, including rising costs, healthcare, the war in Iran, environmental protections, and opportunities to work across the aisle with Republicans to address challenges facing the district. He also shared updates on his ongoing work in Congress and throughout the Houston community.
"Hearing directly from the folks I represent is the most important part of my job," said Congressman Christian D. Menefee. "Families across Houston are working hard, but their paychecks aren't going as far as they used to. They're worried about paying for groceries, keeping their healthcare, and making sure their communities are safe. These are the concerns I'm hearing every day, and they're exactly what I'm fighting to address in Washington."
Affordability was a major focus of the conversation, with one constituent, Tyler, asking what Congressman Menefee was doing to address rising grocery prices as families struggle to stretch their paychecks. In response, Menefee highlighted his support for legislation to raise wages, expand tax credits, and lower everyday expenses, including the Living Wage for All Act, the Paycheck Fairness Act, and legislation to establish a permanent $300 monthly Child Tax Credit. Drawing on his own upbringing, Menefee discussed how programs such as WIC, free and reduced-price school lunches, Pell Grants, and GI Bill benefits helped his family and shaped his commitment to protecting the social safety net.
Throughout the town hall, participants also responded to three live survey questions addressing some of the most pressing issues facing the country. An overwhelming 93% of respondents said their groceries, rent, or utility bills have become more expensive, while 90% said they oppose President Trump and Republicans' war in Iran. Additionally, 53% reported that they or someone they love had been affected by Republicans' Medicaid cuts.
"These results tell us exactly what families across Houston are worried about," said Congressman Menefee. "People are tired of watching their bills go up while Washington Republicans make life harder for working families. They're worried about losing their healthcare, and they want an end to this war. I'm going to keep taking their concerns directly to Washington and fighting for the relief they deserve."
The town hall builds on Congressman Menefee's ongoing efforts to remain accessible and responsive to the residents of Texas's 18th Congressional District. Since taking office, Menefee and his team have closed more than 500 constituent service cases and helped recover over $1 million for constituents navigating federal agencies.
Congressman Menefee plans to host additional telephone town halls to continue connecting with constituents, answering questions, and providing updates on his work in Houston and Washington. Constituents can learn more about his work or request assistance with a federal agency by visiting Menefee.House.Gov or calling the main District Office at 713-655-0050.
Click HERE to listen to the full town hall.
title: Congressman Christian Menefee Hosts First-Ever Telephone Town Hall with Hundreds of Houston Constituents

Texas Residents Charged with Promoting Illegal Tax Shelter
A federal grand jury in Dallas, Texas returned an indictment on September 22, 2026, charging four Texas residents with conspiracy to defraud the United States and other crimes for promoting an illegal tax shelter.
According to the indictment, Texas residents Duncan John MacDonald, Sarah Duren, Richard Ronald Cayce, and Thomas Weickgenant promoted and sold a fraudulent trust scheme that was used to shelter more than $1.5 billion of income, causing an estimated tax loss to the IRS of more than $200 million. The defendants allegedly sold clients the tax shelter for fees that often exceeded $100,000 by fraudulently telling clients that they could assign their income to sham trusts to defer paying taxes in perpetuity, all while continuing to enjoy the benefit and control over their assets and income. The defendants also allegedly encouraged some clients to backdate their trusts and file amended income tax returns claiming refunds for prior years’ taxes.
The indictment also alleges that Weickgenant, who allegedly filed false tax returns for tax shelter clients, obstructed IRS efforts to audit those clients. Weickgenant’s alleged obstruction included instructing clients not to speak with the IRS and encouraging at least one client not to comply with a U.S. District Court order to enforce an IRS summons.
The indictment further alleges that MacDonald and Duren, common-law spouses, evaded income taxes on the millions they received in fees from selling the tax shelter. To do so, the couple allegedly concealed MacDonald’s ownership of the tax shelter business and lied to federal investigators. They also allegedly filed false tax returns, used trusts to conceal their receipt of income, and paid personal living expenses through trusts and nominee accounts held in the names of third parties. Allegedly, Cayce, who owned the distributorship licensing the trust tax shelter, likewise received millions of dollars in fees, which he failed to report on his income tax returns.
Additionally, according to the allegations, MacDonald fraudulently solicited $2 million from investors to purportedly purchase shares in a business promoting the tax shelter by allegedly developing digital trusts. Instead, MacDonald allegedly used the $2 million to purchase luxury goods for himself, including a Rolls Royce Ghost (pictured below top with MacDonald) and the downpayment for a yacht (pictured below bottom). At the time he received funds from investors, MacDonald allegedly was under a court-ordered injunction prohibiting him from selling securities not registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
MacDonald's Rolls Royce Ghost MacDonald's yacht.

Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Ryan R. Raybould for the Northern District of Texas made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief William Montague and Trial Attorney Max Willner-Giwerc of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Eric B. Chen of the Northern District of Texas are prosecuting the case.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
