Federal tax incentive leveraged billions of dollars in private investment to preserve historic buildings, create housing and jobs and revitalize communities nationwide

Interior_Press@ios.doi.gov

WASHINGTON — The Department of the Interior today announced the release of the annual economic impact report for the Federal Historic Tax Credit for fiscal year 2025, highlighting the program's substantial contributions to American jobs, housing creation, private investment, economic growth and community revitalization.

The report, prepared by Rutgers University's Center for Urban Policy Research through a cooperative agreement with the National Park Service, found that Historic Tax Credit-supported rehabilitation projects generated an estimated $9.6 billion in private economic investment, supported approximately 163,000 jobs and generated $6.8 billion in income and $9.2 billion in gross domestic product.

"Historic preservation is an investment in America's future," said Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum. "The Historic Tax Credit demonstrates how preserving the buildings and places that tell America's story can also create jobs, encourage private investment and strengthen communities. This is the kind of economic activity that delivers value to the American people while ensuring that historic properties remain productive assets for generations to come."

In FY 2025, the National Park Service certified 939 completed historic rehabilitation projects, representing approximately $9.6 billion in total rehabilitation investment, while approving 1,170 proposed projects. The related Federal Tax Incentives for Rehabilitating Historic Buildings Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2025 , which provides statistical information on program activity was issued in March 2026.

The economic benefits extended well beyond the construction industry. FY 2025 Historic Tax Credit-related activity generated approximately $6.8 billion in income, $9.2 billion in GDP and $18.1 billion in total economic output to the U.S. economy.

Historic preservation with nationwide economic benefits

The reports demonstrate that the Historic Tax Credit is not limited to major cities or large redevelopment projects. In FY 2025:

﻿24% were located in communities with populations below 25,000.

45% of certified rehabilitation projects were located in low- and moderate-income census tracts.

72% were located in economically distressed areas.

36% of projects had qualified rehabilitation expenditures of less than $1 million.

10% had qualified rehabilitation expenditures of less than $250,000.

34% were located in communities with populations below 50,000.

24% were located in communities with populations below 25,000.﻿

The FY 2025 report also documents the program's cumulative impact. Since the first completed rehabilitation project was certified in FY 1978, the Historic Tax Credit has leveraged approximately $269.2 billion in inflation-adjusted rehabilitation investment, generated 3.6 million jobs, produced $285.1 billion in GDP and $569.8 billion in economic output.

Supporting housing creation

The report identifies how the program supports the creation of new housing and the rehabilitation of existing housing, including affordable housing. In FY 2025:

11,544 new housing units were created through the adaptive reuse of historic buildings.

10,390 existing housing units were rehabilitated.

53% of the 21,934 total created or rehabilitated housing units were low- and moderate-income units.

Since the program’s inception, over 377,000 new housing units have been created, and some 330,000 existing housing units have been rehabilitated, with about a third of the total consisting of low- and moderate-income units.

Bringing historic buildings back to life

The report highlights projects demonstrating how the Historic Tax Credit can transform long-vacant and underused properties.

In Temple, Texas , the rehabilitation of the historic Hawn Hotel, Arcadia Theatre and an adjacent commercial building transformed a block of vacant buildings into a mixed-use development featuring 59 new housing units, commercial space and an events venue. The $32.4 million combined project helped bring new life to the city's historic downtown.

In Lawrence, Massachusetts , the vacant 1848 Stone Mill was converted into 86 apartments, including 69 affordable housing units as part of the $53 million rehabilitation, while retaining the building's historic industrial character.

In Little Rock, Arkansas , a long-vacant 400,000-square-foot former Veterans Administration Hospital Building was converted into 200 new housing units as part of the largest historic tax credit rehabilitation project ever completed in the state.

In Logan, Utah , a $565,000 rehabilitation transformed [ https://veterans%20administration%20hospital%20building/]Dale's Sinclair Service Station, a 1955 Streamline Moderne gas station, into a retail flower and gift store.

The full Annual Report on the Economic Impact of the Federal Historic Tax Credit for Fiscal Year 2025 is available online.

About the Historic Tax Credit Program

The Federal Historic Preservation Tax Incentives Program was established in 1976 and is administered by the National Park Service’s Technical Preservation Services. It provides a 20% federal income tax credit to owners who undertake a substantial rehabilitation of a historic building used for business or other income-producing purposes while maintaining the property's historic character.

The National Park Service evaluates the historic significance of properties and reviews proposed and completed rehabilitation work to determine whether it meets the program's preservation requirements. The IRS administers the tax aspects of the program.

Congress gave the Department of Energy tens of Billions of dollars to build out the power grid and cut the costs that families pay to heat and cool their homes. But the Trump Administration is still holding that money back and letting politics decide which projects survive. This President’s corruption is already sending Americans’ energy bills higher. The Constitution gives Congress the power of the purse. We will keep pressing until this money reaches the projects and families it was meant for,” said Kaptur and Murray.

Olszewski and McBride Introduce ASSURE Act to Expand Voter Registration Opportunities
(Washington, DC) – Maryland Congressman Johnny Olszewski today introduced the ASSURE Act to expand opportunities for eligible Americans to register to vote ahead of this year’s midterm elections. The bill would embed voter registration into everyday interactions with the federal government. Delaware Congresswoman Sarah McBride joined Olszewski as an original co-sponsor of the legislation. 
With the midterm elections just weeks away, voter registration deadlines are fast approaching across the country. In Maryland, the deadline to register is today, October 13. 
“As a government teacher, I spent years teaching my students that democracy only works when people participate in it,” said Congressman Olszewski. “That participation requires something basic: making sure people can register to vote and have their voices heard. If someone is interacting with their government to access veterans benefits, Social Security, or another federal service, we should use that opportunity to make sure they know how to register to vote.”
“Access to the ballot box should be a basic promise of our democracy, not a privilege that depends on who occupies the White House,” said Congresswoman McBride. “The ASSURE Act puts that principle into practice by restoring voter registration opportunities that President Trump has rolled back and ensuring Americans have access to reliable election information. At a moment when this administration continues to undermine voting rights, particularly for Black Americans and communities of color, this work is more urgent than ever. I’m grateful to Rep. Olszewski for his leadership on this legislation, and I’ll keep fighting to ensure every eligible voter can make their voice heard.”
The ASSURE Act – short for the Agency Support for Secure and Universal Registration Enhancement Act – codifies a Biden-era executive order, later reversed by President Trump, that directed federal agencies to integrate voter registration opportunities into services Americans already use. It also restores a longstanding policy – also reversed by President Trump – that permits nonpartisan groups to provide voter registration assistance and civic participation information at naturalization ceremonies for new Americans.
Together, these measures would give eligible Americans more opportunities to register without having to seek out a separate government office, website, or registration event.
Olszewski has made expanding civic participation and strengthening democratic institutions a central focus of his work in Congress. He has also supported legislation to make Election Day a national holiday and require states to offer same-day voter registration.
“We should make it easier for eligible Americans to participate in our democracy – not put up unnecessary barriers,” Congressman Olszewski said. “The ASSURE Act is a simple idea: meet people where they are, make registration easier, and make our democracy more accessible to everyone who is eligible to participate.”
title: Olszewski and McBride Introduce ASSURE Act to Expand Voter Registration Opportunities

“This serious situation underscores why winning the global super intelligence race is a national security prerogative — and why President Trump’s leadership in creating the Super Intelligence Force is so important,” said Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. “I thank Director Patel and our FBI partners for their diligence and swift action. Thank you to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and our law enforcement partners for their support — and we will continue working closely with our partners across the U.S. government and private sector to keep American businesses and citizens safe and to ensure our country maintains its competitive edge.”

This arrest highlights our relentless efforts in partnership with the FBI to identify and prosecute those who seek to steal our technology, as alleged in the complaint.”
According to the complaint, Alfozan had been employed as an engineer by OpenAI since July 2025. On or about Sept. 30, OpenAI personnel discovered a surreptitious audio recording device (Recording Device 1) inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room inside one of their buildings in San Francisco. OpenAI determined that the device, which had been concealed in toilet paper, was installed on or about Sept. 28, and that its contents were encrypted.
Recording Device 1
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage inside OpenAI’s office showed that Alfozan appeared near the executive conference room on multiple dates prior to the device’s discovery, although he had no authority to access or to participate in meetings occurring in the executive conference room. According to the complaint, meetings in the executive conference room where Recording Device 1 was discovered frequently involved discussions of highly confidential technical, commercial, and strategic information, including proprietary research, product plans, and business-development opportunities, as well as nonpublic information about Open AI’s technical progress and strategic decisions, capabilities, priorities, government engagements, and commercial relationships.
According to the complaint, prior to Sept. 28, Alfozan used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about Open AI’s building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars, “leadership and exec” locations, and external partner meetings. Moreover, a chatbot account associated with Alfozan’s spouse (which shared multiple identifiers and attributes with Alfozan’s own chatbot account) submitted prompts between Sept. 24 and Sept. 30 related to building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device, including inquiries about “build[ing] a continuous audio recorder,” “customiz[ing] Wi-Fi . . . connectivity,” “improv[ing] audio and live listening,” and “encrypt[ing] the SD card,” among other things. The same chatbot account also submitted prompts specifically related to Recording Device 1, including its custom header and unique MAC address, between Sept. 27 and Sept. 28.
The complaint further alleges that on Oct. 5, Alfozan entered the executive conference room and appeared to look behind the television into which Recording Device 1 had been inserted, as captured below:
Image of Alfozan
Finally, the complaint alleges that, also on or about Oct. 5, Alfozan left a bag unattended in a different room in an OpenAI building. OpenAI security personnel found and opened Alfozan’s bag, inside which they discovered — among other things, including Alfozan’s wallet and ID — another recording device (Recording Device 2) similar to Recording Device 1.
If convicted, Alfozan faces a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison and a $250,000 fine, followed by 3 years of supervised release.
The FBI is investigating the case.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicolas Parker for the Northern District of California is prosecuting the case with valuable assistance from Trial Attorney Kate Tagert of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section.
This prosecution is in support of National Security Presidential Memorandum 11 (NSPM-11) designed to support American superiority in super intelligence technology.
title: Saudi National Arrested for Installing Surreptitious Audio Recording Device at OpenAI

Neguse, Bennet, Hickenlooper Urge Federal Agencies to Restore Cell Service in Boulder County
Lafayette, CO — Following recent reports of unacceptable cellular service issues across Boulder County, Congressman Joe Neguse and Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper penned a letter to the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) urging the agencies to meet with cellular carriers immediately and resolve the issues.
The three major cellular carriers apparently limited their Boulder County coverage earlier this year to comply with federal signal transmission rules surrounding the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone north of Boulder. These federal signal limits protect ongoing research at several government agencies, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the U.S. Geological Survey.
“We write to urge your agencies to assist in resolving major reported cellular network outages in Boulder County, Colorado, following signal adjustments made to comply with National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) regulations protecting the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone,” wrote Neguse, Bennet, and Hickenlooper.
The lawmakers also pressed the NTIA and FCC to find a collaborative solution that will quickly address community concerns, particularly preserving access to cellular coverage as a vital public safety resource.
“Full cell phone coverage is indispensable to everyday life. When people leave their homes, they expect to be able to use their cell phones for navigation, payment, and communication with others. Cell phones are also vital for public safety in Boulder County, which is prone to rapidly escalating wildfires.”
They concluded with a call for swift solutions and asked that the FCC and NTIA keep congressional offices and local governments updated on the outcome of the requested meeting and progress toward restoring full connectivity.
“[W]e respectfully request that FCC and NTIA officials meet with carriers immediately in order to find a solution that will allow them to restore functional cellular service to their customers as soon as possible. We also request that you update our offices and local governments on the outcome of that meeting and report back to us on your progress as all parties work to restore full connectivity,” the lawmakers concluded.
Read the full letter HERE and below:
October 13, 2026
The Honorable Brendan Carr
Chairman
Federal Communications Commission
45 L Street NE
Washington, DC 20554
The Honorable Arielle Roth
Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information
Administrator, National Telecommunications and Information Administration
1401 Constitution Avenue NW
Washington, DC 20230
Dear Chairman Carr and Assistant Secretary Roth,
We write to urge your agencies to assist in resolving major reported cellular network outages in Boulder County, Colorado, following signal adjustments made to comply with National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) regulations protecting the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone.
As we understand it, in late 2024, the NTIA Institute for Telecommunication Sciences (ITS) notified three major cellular carriers that they needed to modify their signals received within the Table Mountain Radio Quiet Zone, the 50-mile radius where federal regulations limit radio transmission frequency that could otherwise interfere with the research of the ITS, National Institute of Standards and Technology, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and U.S. Geological Survey. The three major carriers have publicly stated that they have since adjusted their signals to comply with Table Mountain frequency limits.
However, these signal adjustments appear to have significantly downgraded cellular network coverage for Boulder County consumers. Our constituents in the nearby towns of Longmont and Niwot have filed more than 100 formal complaints with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) reporting that they cannot make phone calls or use data on their cell phones, even when their devices indicate full network coverage. While the three major carriers have publicly indicated they will further upgrade their networks to compensate for the necessary signal reductions, our constituents lack vital cell connectivity in the interim.
Full cell phone coverage is indispensable to everyday life. When people leave their homes, they expect to be able to use their cell phones for navigation, payment, and communication with others. Cell phones are also vital for public safety in Boulder County, which is prone to rapidly escalating wildfires. Our constituents use their cell phones to notify their families and friends that they are safe during wildfire season and to warn neighbors of unpredictable wildfire shifts. For example, the 2021 Marshall Fire, which killed two people and burned nearly 1,000 structures, progressed so rapidly that many residents would not have known to immediately evacuate had they not been alerted by a phone call or text from someone they knew.
Given all of the foregoing, we respectfully request that FCC and NTIA officials meet with carriers immediately in order to find a solution that will allow them to restore functional cellular service to their customers as soon as possible. We also request that you update our offices and local governments on the outcome of that meeting and report back to us on your progress as all parties work to restore full connectivity.
Sincerely,
###
title: Neguse, Bennet, Hickenlooper Urge Federal Agencies to Restore Cell Service in Boulder County

Ocasio-Cortez, McClain Delaney, Beyer, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth Lead Calls to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports
Press Release
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Don Beyer (VA-08), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), and Sarah Elfreth (MD-03) are leading a congressional letter urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.
The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.
“Last month, the Federal Aviation Administration surprisingly launched an AI tool to help control air traffic over three major National Capital Region Airports, with plans to expand nationwide in the following 90 days. They did so without publishing a safety evaluation or sufficiently consulting air traffic controllers and safety experts. We are urging Transportation Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford to stop the rollout until we have answers. This administration may treat Big Tech companies with impunity, but air traffic control leaves zero margin for error,” said Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
“When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know that every system guiding their flight has been thoroughly tested and that the people keeping them safe have the training they need,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “After the devastating crash over DCA that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first. I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong.”
The FAA’s rush to deploy a system that could affect the lives of millions of Americans is especially concerning for residents of this region, who are still grappling with questions about air safety following last year’s fatal crash at DCA. Before deploying its AI-enabled SMART air traffic control tool, the FAA must demonstrate, through air traffic controller feedback and independently verified testing, that this technology is safe and reliable, and it must clearly communicate those findings to the public,” said Congressman Don Beyer.
"Families across Baltimore count on BWI to get them where they’re going safely. Yet the Trump Administration recklessly rolled out an untested AI air traffic tool there without publishing a safety evaluation or adequately consulting the air traffic controllers who keep us safe. There is no room for error in our skies. I am proud to co-lead this letter calling for public transparency and answers from Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford on how this system was tested, who was consulted, and how it will be evaluated. Until they provide answers that ensure that this technology is safe, the FAA must pause its use," said Congressman Kweisi Mfume.
“The airspace in the DC region is incredibly complicated and demands the highest standard of safety and reliability from Air Traffic Control. We need to be extremely cautious about implementing AI tools into the systems responsible for the safety of our skies. I urge the FAA to prove that the system does not pose a risk to the public before allowing its use," said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.
“Every day, our airports and their staff ensure tens of thousands of worldwide travelers are safe and secure – including here at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport in Maryland’s Third District. While we fully recognize the need to modernize our air traffic control systems, we cannot pursue modernization at the expense of public safety, especially when it comes to implementing new technologies like AI,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “As AI safety concerns are top of mind for our neighbors, this is another instance where we cannot afford to miss the moment on regulating this technology. I also am determined to continue to work with my colleagues to ensure our hardworking air traffic controllers have every resource they need to do their jobs and ensure the safety of our passengers.”
At a time when AI safety concerns are sky high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.
The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.
The lawmakers request answers in three areas:
- Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.
- Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.
- Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.
The letter calls for a pause until lawmakers can better understand the FAA’s decision-making, rollout process, and evaluation plan. The co-leads emphasize that modernizing air traffic control must prioritize safety, transparency, and the expertise of the people responsible for keeping our skies safe.
###
title: Ocasio-Cortez, McClain Delaney, Beyer, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth Lead Calls to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports

text:
Sánchez, House Democratic colleagues oppose rule denying legal immigrants tax credits
WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Linda Sánchez (D-Calif.) led her House Democratic colleagues today in calling on the Trump administration to withdraw a proposed IRS rule that would strip certain legal immigrants of refundable tax credits.
The rule would reclassify these credits as “Federal public benefits” under the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA), imposing strict citizenship requirements on recipients. It is similar to a failed attempt by the Department of Health and Human Services last year to block certain legal immigrants from health services, an effort the courts struck down.
“The rules regarding the eligibility criteria for refundable tax credits are clearly defined by Congress in the Internal Revenue Code, and PRWORA was clearly never intended to separately address them,” the members wrote. “Yet, this proposed regulation would strip hundreds of thousands of people of their deserved tax refunds by redefining refundable tax credits as ‘Federal public benefits’ under PRWORA, harming our constituents, their families, and our communities.”
The members continued, “The administration’s apparent desire to change the law to attack immigrant communities does not change Congress’s intent when it passed PRWORA, nor does it change the law.”
In addition to Sánchez, the letter was signed by Representatives Mike Thompson (D-Calif.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Gwen Moore (D-Wis.), Sylvia Garcia (D-Texas), Jan Schakowsky (D-Ill.), Danny Davis (D-Ill.), Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.), Judy Chu (D-Calif.), Jesús “Chuy” García (D-Ill.), Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.), Steven Horsford (D-Nev.), Dan Goldman (D-N.Y.), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.)
The full text of the letter is available HERE and follows:
October 7, 2026
Honorable Frank Bisignano 
Chief Executive Officer
U.S. Internal Revenue Service
1111 Constitution Avenue NW
Washington, DC 20224
Honorable Scott Bessent
Secretary
U.S. Department of the Treasury 
1500 Pennsylvania Ave, NW 
Washington, DC 20220
Dear Secretary Bessent and CEO Bisignano,
We write to express our strong opposition to the proposed rule on the Application of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 (PRWORA) to the Refunded Portion of Certain Federal Refundable Tax Credits. The rules regarding the eligibility criteria for refundable tax credits are clearly defined by Congress in the Internal Revenue Code, and PRWORA was clearly never intended to separately address them. Yet, this proposed regulation would strip hundreds of thousands of people of their deserved tax refunds by redefining refundable tax credits as “Federal public benefits” under PRWORA, harming our constituents, their families, and our communities.
Congress has modified these credits since PRWORA was enacted (most recently in Public Law 119-21 (2025)) but never made the changes Treasury proposes in this rule. Therefore, Congress clearly did not intend to import PRWORA’s limits on eligibility for federal public benefits into these refundable tax credits. In fact, Congress’s decision in P.L. 119-21 to limit the American Opportunity Tax Credit to people with a valid Social Security number would be nonsensical under Treasury’s reading of the statute, because those without one would have already been excluded. The Congressional Budget Office would not have estimated this provision to reduce the deficit by $247 million had the assertions in this proposed rule been accurate. Similarly, Congress’s decision in the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2018) to limit Child Tax Credit eligibility to people with a valid Social Security number would not have made sense if PRWORA already imposed a much stricter interpretation.
The administration’s apparent desire to change the law to attack immigrant communities does not change Congress’s intent when it passed PRWORA, nor does it change the law. As the notice of rulemaking states, “Section 401(c)(1)(B) of PRWORA (8 U.S.C. 1611(c)(1)(B)) defines the term “Federal public benefit,” in relevant part, as “any retirement, welfare, health, disability, public or assisted housing, postsecondary education, food assistance, unemployment benefit, or any other similar benefit for which payments or assistance are provided to an individual, household, or family eligibility unit by an agency of the United States or by appropriated funds of the United States. ” Tax credits are absent from that list, which clearly consists of direct assistance programs delivered through federally funded programs. Congress would have explicitly specified tax credits if it had intended their inclusion. Wholly adopting a novel and unsupported interpretation of PRWORA to fit President Trump’s anti-immigrant agenda goes directly against the law as written and congressional intent.
In fact, PRWORA separately addressed the issue of immigrants qualifying for refundable credits when it originally passed in 1996. Section 451 of PRWORA restricted the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) by barring those without a Social Security Number from the tax credit. The remaining eligible population is a much broader group than those deemed “qualified” immigrants under that law. If Congress intended to restrict refundable tax credits to only “qualified” immigrants, it would have not included this separate section in a distinct section of that law.
The proposed regulation relies on the 2020 Department of Justice Office of Legal Counsel opinion stating that any payment to a taxpayer may be classified as a benefit under PRWORA regardless of congressional intent and history. The proposal fails to justify why this new interpretation, upending 30 years of precedent, is valid given Congress’s past decisions to make very clear which immigrants were or were not eligible for refundable tax credits. Had Congress intended to bar immigrants from taking advantage of refundable tax credits, it would have clarified the statute in any of the numerous changes made to PRWORA or refundable tax credits in the years since 1996.
We urge you to withdraw this proposed regulation, which has no basis in the law, upends decades of precedent and runs counter to congressional intent.
Sincerely,
###
title: Sánchez, House Democratic colleagues oppose rule denying legal immigrants tax credits

Construction Business Owner Charged with Employment Tax Scheme and Failing to File Returns
A federal grand jury in Greenbelt, Maryland returned an indictment today charging a Maryland man with failing to account for and pay over employment taxes withheld from the wages of his company’s employees and failing to file tax returns.
According to the indictment, Martin Herrera Navarrete, of Glenn Dale, was the sole owner and sole corporate officer of Navarrete Brothers Construction, Inc., a commercial construction company. Navarrete was allegedly responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare, and income taxes from his employees’ wages and paying those withholdings over to the IRS. From the first quarter of 2008 through the last quarter of 2025, Navarrete allegedly failed to pay any of the withheld taxes to the IRS. In total, the indictment alleges that Navarrete failed to pay more than $3 million in taxes owed to the IRS during this period. Additionally, from 2020 through 2024, Navarrete allegedly failed to file his own personal tax returns and corporate tax returns.
Navarrete is charged with failing to pay over and account for employment taxes, failing to file corporate tax returns, and failing to file personal tax returns. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison for each count of failing to account for and pay over employment taxes and a maximum penalty of one year in prison for each count of failing to file tax returns. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Kelly O. Hayes of the District of Maryland made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorney Catriona Coppler of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Joshua Rosenthal of the District of Maryland are prosecuting the case.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Construction Business Owner Charged with Employment Tax Scheme and Failing to File Returns

USDA Announces $86.6 Million Investment into the U.S. Specialty Crop Industry
(Washington, D.C., October 13, 2026) – The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) today announced it is awarding $86.6 million in grant funding to support the specialty crop industry through the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program (SCBGP). The program funds innovative projects designed to enhance the competitiveness of specialty crops.
“Today I am proud to announce USDA will be investing more than $86 million across 56 states and territories through the Specialty Crop Block Grant Program. These 609 state projects represent the Trump Administration’s commitment to innovation, marketing, and research—ensuring specialty crop businesses are at the forefront of markets all around the world,” said Secretary Brooke L. Rollins. “Putting farmers first will continue to drive economic growth and strengthen the fabric of rural communities across America.”
States and territories are providing subawards to projects that address the needs of U.S. producers of fruits, vegetables, tree nuts, dried fruits, horticulture, and nursery crops. The funded projects help businesses throughout the specialty crops distribution chain by enhancing food safety, supporting research, developing new and improved seed varieties and specialty crops, fighting pests and diseases, educating communities about healthy eating, and making it easier and more affordable to get specialty crops to market.
USDA’s Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is investing $86.6 million in approximately 609 state projects across 56 states and territories.
Projects include:
- Michigan will use over $2.64 million through subawards to enhance the competitiveness of specialty crops including apples, asparagus, beans, blueberries, Christmas trees, herbs, mushroom, and grapes throughout the state.
- Georgia will use over $1.7 million across 2 research projects, 9 education and outreach projects, and 2 marketing projects in support of the state's pecan, blueberry, pepper, strawberry, peach, apple, Vidalia onion, and citrus growers.
- Ohio will use over $800,000 for projects to enhance competitiveness of apples, leafy greens, brassicas, herbs, maple syrup, honey, and nuts throughout the state.
- Pennsylvania will use over $1.1 million on research, education and outreach, and marketing of mushrooms, potatoes and apples.
- Texas will use over $2 million for projects to enhance competitiveness of grapes, watermelons, pecans, onions, and spinach.
- Florida will use over $4.3 million on research, education and outreach, and marketing of mangoes, blueberries, sweet corn, and muscadine grapes.
- North Carolina will use over $1.5 million to enhance competitiveness of sweet potatoes, fir trees, tomatoes, blueberries, apples, canary melons, and centipede grass seed.
For more information and to view a complete list of funded projects, visit the AMS SCBGP webpage.
AMS supports U.S. food and agricultural product market opportunities, while increasing consumer access to fresh, healthy foods through applied research, technical services, and congressionally funded grants.
To learn more about AMS’s investments in enhancing and strengthening agricultural systems, visit www.ams.usda.gov/grants.
###
title: USDA Announces $86.6 Million Investment into the U.S. Specialty Crop Industry

Ranking Members Morelle, Meeks Host Queens, NY Shadow Hearing on Election Security, Fighting Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting
With voting underway, lawmakers and voting rights leaders gathered in Queens to defend mail-in voting, combat intimidation and protect election integrity
Queens, NY – Last week, Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25), Committee on House Administration, and Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05), House Foreign Affairs Committee, hosted a public shadow hearing with members of the New York delegation to confront the Trump administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Experts at the shadow hearing included:
- Bethany Li, Executive Director of the Asian American Legal Defense and Education Fund
- John Cusick, Assistant Counsel at the Legal Defense Fund
- Brian Lemek, President and Executive Director of the Defend the Vote Action Fund
Experts outlined voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation in the 2026 midterm election. The hearing examined federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. Experts detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25). “The election is here and we are protecting every American’s right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. We need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face, and we will fight to protect our elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option. I want to thank Ranking Member Meeks for hosting this convening and the New York delegation for continuing to be on the front lines.”
“The right to vote is the heart of our democracy,” said Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05). “As the Trump administration continues to attempt to disenfranchise minority communities and cheat their way to a Republican majority in Congress, it is important that we do not waver in our fight to preserve the right to vote. I applaud my colleagues and the experts for showing up, setting the record straight, and empowering voters to cast their ballots.”
“Election security and voting rights are under attack by President Trump and we must do all we can stop this assault on the sacred right to make our voices heard at the ballot box,” said Congresswoman Grace Meng (NY-06). “The President is pushing to add a citizenship question to the 2030 census and remove the collection of race and ethnicity data to manipulate voting maps and to dilute the political representation of diverse communities. He has consistently engaged in fearmongering about the security of mail-in voting, citing false accusations of fraud, and encouraged the use of voter suppression and intimidation tactics to make it harder for Americans to participate in the democratic process. And the Supreme Court’s conservative majority has further gutted the Voting Rights Act, weakening the political power of minority voters. Despite all these unconscionable and reckless attacks, we will never stop fighting to protect the right to vote, which is the foundation of our great democracy. I thank Congressmembers Morelle and Meeks for organizing this shadow hearing in Queens to keep a light shined on one of the most crucial issues facing New York and the nation, and thank you as well to all the witnesses who testified.”
“My grandparents, immigrants from Poland, worked hard to become U.S. citizens and earn the right to vote,” said Congressman Paul Tonko (NY-20). “Their unwavering belief in our democracy instilled in me the importance of that right for all citizens. At a time when this Trump administration is seeking to undermine our election system and disenfranchise entire communities, it is more important than ever to stand up and defend this fundamental right. I’m grateful to my colleagues for holding this important hearing and doing all in our power to ensure the American people’s voices are heard.”
“Republicans continue to push lies and intimidate voters across the country to depress voter turnout and sow distrust in our elections at all levels,” said Congressman Adriano Espaillat (NY-13). “We have a duty to ensure the safety of everyone at the ballot box not only this November, but for every election. Democracy requires our most ardent protection and hosting these hearings are part of the ongoing mission to serve all Americans who deserve fair, free, and safe elections.”
Ranking Member Morelle and the Committee on House Administration is charged with the oversight of federal elections, including considering proposals to amend federal election law and monitoring congressional elections across the U.S.
Watch a recording of the event here.
###
title: Ranking Members Morelle, Meeks Host Queens, NY Shadow Hearing on Election Security, Fighting Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting

Construction Company Owner and Employees Indicted for Wide Ranging Tax and Financial Fraud Schemes
A federal grand jury in the Eastern District of New York returned an indictment on September 23, 2026, charging Arthur Nelson, of Staten Island and Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, Joseph Free, of Staten Island, Paul Vasquez, of Englishtown, New Jersey, and Ulysses Jude Devocion, of Queens County, New York with various crimes, including conspiring to defraud the IRS, tax evasion, willfully failing to withhold and pay over employment taxes, failing to file income tax returns, helping to file false corporate tax returns, interfering with the administration of the internal revenue laws, conspiracy to commit wire fraud, failure to file reports of foreign bank accounts, and obstruction of justice.
According to the indictment, Nelson owned and operated various construction subcontracting companies, including MTB AMG Inc. and PAL AMG Inc., which installed glass on commercial businesses, MTB Metal Fabricators Inc., which provided manufacturing services, and Wired NYC LLC, which provided electric installation services. Nelson’s companies were based in Brooklyn until March 2022 when they relocated to New Jersey.
Free allegedly worked as a construction foreman for the Nelson Companies from March 2017 to approximately 2022. Vasquez allegedly was the senior director of operations until approximately 2025. Devocion was an accountant and office manager, from approximately 2021 and 2023.
As alleged in the indictment, from April 2017 through May 2024, the four defendants caused Nelson’s employees to be paid weekly wages with no amounts withheld for federal employment taxes. These unreported wages totaled at least approximately $5 million. Further, they allegedly falsely classified and caused the false classification of personal expenses as business expenses and filed or caused the filing of false federal tax returns, including quarterly employment tax returns, corporate tax returns, and individual income tax returns. They also allegedly caused the Nelson Companies to issue false wage and tax statements, commonly known as W-2s, to its employees. Nelson also underreported his business gross receipts by approximately $13 million.
As alleged in the indictment, from July 2019 through March 2025, Nelson, Devocion, and Vasquez engaged in a scheme to submit false financial documents relating to Nelson and the Nelson Companies to other companies in order to obtain money or property in amounts to which they were not entitled, including, for example, loans, mortgages, lines of credit, credit cards, and surety bonding contracts.
Nelson is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, six counts of willful failure to withhold and pay over employment taxes, one count of attempting to interfere with the due administration of the internal revenue laws, two counts of tax evasion, one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and two counts of willful failure to file reports of foreign bank and financial accounts (“FBAR”). Free is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, one count of attempting to interfere with the due administration of the internal revenue laws, one count of willfully aiding and assisting in the presentation of a false and fraudulent tax return, and one count of willfully failing to file an individual income tax return. Vasquez is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, one count of attempting to interfere with the due administration of the internal revenue laws, and one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Devocion is charged with one count of conspiracy to defraud the United States, one count of willfully failing to file an individual income tax return, one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, and obstruction of justice in connection with his testimony before the grand jury.
If convicted, the defendants face a maximum penalty of twenty years in prison for conspiracy to commit wire fraud and for obstruction of justice; five years in prison for conspiracy to defraud the United States, for each count of willful failure to withhold and pay over employment taxes, for each count of tax evasion, and for each count of failing to file an FBAR; three years in prison for each count of aiding and assisting the filing of false tax returns and for interfering with the due administration of the revenue laws; and one year in prison for each count of willful failure to file a tax return. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorneys Richard Kelley and Michael C. Vasiliadis of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section are prosecuting the case.
An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

text:
Vindman Joins Local Elected Officials and Advocates in Calling on Regulators to Put Main Street Ahead of Wall Street
Fairfax, Va. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) delivered remarks at the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing at the Fairfax County Government Center, urging regulators to reject the proposed NextEra-Dominion merger over concerns about its impact on Virginia families and utility ratepayers.
Vindman joined local elected officials and community advocates in raising the alarm about the proposed merger, which he warned could further drive up electricity costs for Virginians already struggling with rising utility bills.
 
Vindman Joins Advocates & Local Officials in Rallying Against the NextEra-Dominion Merger 
Prior to the hearing, Vindman joined advocates for a rally outside the Fairfax County Government Center, where attendees called for greater accountability and stronger protections for Virginia ratepayers.
“Virginians are already paying too much to keep the lights on, and the last thing hardworking families need is a merger that could send their utility bills even higher,” said Vindman. “The State Corporation Commission has a responsibility to protect the people it serves. That means looking out for Main Street, not Wall Street. I urge the Commission to reject this bad deal for Virginians.”
Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger. He has continued to raise concerns about rising electricity costs, corporate accountability, and the need to ensure that Virginia families are not forced to shoulder the costs of unchecked data center growth.
Vindman’s remarks, as prepared, are below. Click here to watch a video of his testimony.
—
Good evening. Thank you for holding this public event so you can hear directly from Virginians.
I’m Congressman Eugene Vindman, and I represent about 800 thousand residents in Virginia’s Seventh District.
I’m here tonight for a simple reason: I believe the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion is a bad deal for Virginians.
I urge the Commission to reject it.
I was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to speak out against this merger.
And I did so in a letter to the Commission, which I hope you all read.
Virginians are already paying too much to keep the lights on. I hear it everywhere I go.
Families are opening their utility bills each month wondering how much more they can possibly be expected to absorb.
This merger gives them every reason to worry that those bills will go even higher.
Here’s the thing about utilities: Virginians don’t get to shop around for their electricity provider.
Where you live determines who keeps your lights on and your home warm in the winter.
That gives utility companies enormous power, and with that power comes a responsibility to the people they serve.
It is not a license to squeeze more money out of hardworking families.
NextEra’s own record should concern us. Customers of its Florida subsidiary have seen their utility bills rise by 33 percent. Now NextEra wants to take control of the utility serving millions of Virginians.
NextEra sees enormous profits to be made in Virginia, particularly with the explosion of data centers.
But I’ve been crystal clear: data centers must pay their fair share.
Virginia families should not be subsidizing corporate expansion through higher electricity bills.
This Commission’s job is to protect Main Street, not Wall Street.
My concerns do not start and end with rates, however. I am very concerned about what this merger would do to the company’s accountability structure.
Dominion is a Virginia company. Its decisions affect Virginia families, Virginia businesses, and Virginia communities every single day.
Under the proposed ownership structure, three-quarters of the new company’s board would be controlled from Florida.
And there are serious questions about NextEra’s conduct in Florida. The company agreed to a $150 million settlement over allegations involving political interference. That sounds like corruption.
That record raises concerns about the influence this company could wield over Virginia’s energy future.
When Virginians have a problem with their power bill, they deserve answers here in Virginia.
I surveyed my constituents about this deal.
More than 950 Virginians responded, and 80 percent opposed the merger.
Their concerns were remarkably consistent, worried about higher bills, less accountability, and even more power concentrated in the hands of a massive utility.
Those concerns deserve to be taken seriously.
This Commission has a responsibility to protect Virginia ratepayers.
Electricity is an essential service, not a luxury. And the privilege of serving millions of Virginians comes with an obligation to put those customers first.
I respectfully urge you to put Virginia families ahead of Wall Street profits and reject this merger.
Thank you.
###
title: Vindman Takes Fight Against NextEra-Dominion Merger Directly to Virginia SCC Hearing

text:
Third-Largest Penalty in Treasury History; Largest in OCC History
WASHINGTON—Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced enforcement actions imposing more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America (“the Bank”), the second-largest bank in the United States, for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws. These actions include the third-largest penalty in Treasury history and the largest in the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) history.
- The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a $1.2 billion penalty for the Bank’s failure to mitigate and report priority national security risks, including Chinese Money Laundering Networks and illicit finance along the southwest border.
- The OCC assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for the Bank’s deficient and ineffective BSA/AML (anti-money laundering) compliance program.
- The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an $11.6 million settlement agreement with the Bank over apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including on Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.
“Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our economic and national security,” said Secretary Scott Bessent. “When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire U.S. financial system to significant illicit finance risks. Today’s actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law.”
Together, these actions underscore the importance of effectively complying with U.S. AML/CFT and sanctions requirements. Given the converging nature of AML/CFT and sanctions-related risks, financial institutions should ensure their AML and sanctions compliance efforts are effectively integrated and mutually reinforcing.
FAILURE TO REPORT OVER $5 BILLION IN SUSPICIOUS ACTIVITY TO FINCEN
As part of its resolution with FinCEN, Bank of America admits that it willfully violated the BSA and failed to (1) implement and maintain an AML program that met the minimum requirements of the BSA and FinCEN’s implementing regulations, (2) conduct due diligence for correspondent accounts for foreign financial institutions, and (3) file suspicious activity reports (SARs).
The central failures identified through FinCEN’s investigation involved deficiencies related to Bank of America’s suspicious transaction identification and reporting and customer due diligence (CDD) processes. As these issues arose, Bank of America prioritized its revenues and minimized the impact on its required compliance resources. The nature and extent of the Bank’s resulting reliance on law enforcement inquiries, requests by other financial institutions, and similar interventions over its own internal, automated controls to identify potentially suspicious activity meant that the Bank effectively outsourced to third parties a substantial portion of its proactive detection and reporting obligations. The Bank also allowed suspicious activity to accumulate uninvestigated for extended periods without investigation, resulting in late reporting of limited utility to law enforcement.
Bank of America maintained this approach and failed to take meaningful action even in the face of testing that highlighted significant problems. Similarly, the Bank’s CDD processes failed to account for customers’ extensive reliance on payments from unknown third parties. The Bank failed to timely and meaningfully respond to mounting red flags involving these customers—including potential ties to narcotics trafficking proceeds—even after compliance personnel escalated concerns related to possible trade-based money laundering and fraud.
As a result of these failures, Bank of America failed to timely report to FinCEN over $5 billion dollars in suspicious transactions, with over $1 billion of this activity implicating national security-related and other priority illicit finance risks, including suspicious transactions indicative of Chinese Money Laundering Networks, fraud, and potential trade-based money laundering with a substantial nexus to the southwest border.
The Consent Order published today requires Bank of America to work with a third party to complete a lookback to identify and report to FinCEN suspicious transactions that went undetected due to the failures noted above. Bank of America also must undergo an independent review of the effectiveness of its suspicious activity monitoring, CDD, and foreign correspondent account due diligence programs, as well as its data governance framework as it pertains to information used in its AML program. The independent reviews are tailored to the violations and will evaluate the effectiveness of Bank of America’s AML program in addressing priority risks, including (1) the U.S. Southwest border, cartels, and potential narcotics trafficking; (2) Iran; and (3) Russia.
DEFICIENT AND INEFFECTIVE COMPLIANCE PROGRAM
The OCC’s penalty is in response to Bank of America’s violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. The Bank is also subject to a December 2024 cease-and-desist order (2024 Order), which required the bank to address its deficient BSA/AML compliance program.
The Bank’s BSA/AML compliance program is deficient and ineffective. Its transaction monitoring system resulted in the Bank failing to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions. This caused large numbers of late SARs involving billions of dollars. Many of the late SARs had indicia of money laundering. The Bank knew for years that it was failing to escalate potentially suspicious activity to investigators for review to determine if a SAR should be filed but failed to correct this serious BSA violation.
In addition, the Bank’s BSA Officer and staff lacked sufficient skills and expertise to effectively manage its BSA/AML program. Key BSA personnel did not receive appropriate training regarding suspicious activity identification, investigation, and reporting, which resulted in inaccurate and late SARs. The BSA audit function failed to identify longstanding BSA concerns that examiners subsequently uncovered.
After agreeing to the 2024 Order, the Bank still failed to prioritize BSA/AML compliance. The Bank did not complete many of the significant steps needed to establish an effective BSA/AML compliance program and its program continues to have significant breakdowns. For example, more than a year after the 2024 Order, the Bank still failed to escalate potentially suspicious activities to investigators for review. Additionally, the Bank processed potential trade-based money laundering transactions due to a systemic gap in its transaction monitoring program. Bank management failed to ensure the Bank had an effective BSA/AML compliance program and continued to minimize the program’s significant deficiencies.
APPARENT SANCTIONS VIOLATIONS ACROSS MULTIPLE PROGRAMS
The Bank has agreed to settle with OFAC its potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple sanctions programs. These apparent violations occurred when Bank of America channeled correspondent banking payments through blocked banks due to technical and human error, allowed designated individuals to make payments and withdraw funds due to poor sanctions alert calibration, failed to promptly update watchlists following OFAC designations, and mishandled business accounts associated with blocked persons due to human error. As a result of these compliance failures, Bank of America processed millions of dollars in payments in apparent violation of sanctions programs targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism.
The settlement amount of $11.6 million reflects OFAC’s determination that Bank of America’s apparent violations were non-egregious and largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. This settlement amount also reflects no reduction to the base penalty, including no mitigation for remedial measures or cooperation. As part of the settlement, Bank of America has made significant compliance commitments regarding training, testing and audit, and future communication and cooperation with OFAC.
COMPLIANCE CONSIDERATIONS
Effective AML/CFT programs protect U.S. national security by preventing financial institutions from being used to facilitate money laundering and terrorist financing. Such programs must be risk-based and commensurate with an institution’s size, risk profile, and products and services. In this matter, Bank of America failed to reasonably design its proprietary transaction monitoring system to address its risks and failed to make meaningful improvements despite testing that revealed significant deficiencies in identifying and timely reporting suspicious activity. Financial institutions cannot disregard mounting red flags or internal warnings about ineffective controls, whether under the guise of innovation or otherwise. Nor can they rely on law enforcement inquiries, referrals from other financial institutions, or other external sources as substitutes for their own effective internal monitoring and controls. Bank of America’s transaction monitoring failures resulted in material dependence on external referrals to identify potentially suspicious activity, rather than the Bank’s own controls to identify and investigate such activity.
Meaningful, risk-based customer due diligence is critical to meeting AML/CFT obligations. Financial institutions must maintain and update customer risk profiles throughout the customer relationship to reflect relevant information, including customer activity, products and services, and geographic exposure. When new information indicates heightened risks or raises AML/CFT concerns, financial institutions must take timely, meaningful action commensurate with those risks. Merely documenting concerns or engaging in prolonged internal reviews without appropriate corrective action does not satisfy an institution’s compliance obligations.
TREASURY WHISTLEBLOWER INCENTIVE PROGRAM
Through FinCEN, Treasury maintains a whistleblower incentive program for violations of the BSA and certain national security laws such as the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000 and the statutory requirements in 31 U.S.C. 5323 are otherwise met. FinCEN is currently accepting whistleblower tips. More information about the whistleblower program can be found here.
###
title: U.S. Treasury Announces Record Enforcement Actions Against Bank of America

Hoyer Statement on Federal Raid on Congresswoman Omar's Home
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after federal agents raided the Washington, D.C. residence of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar (MN-05):
“I am deeply concerned that Rep. Ilhan Omar, an elected Member of Congress, had her home raided by federal immigration authorities after President Trump repeatedly attacked her legitimacy as an American and threatened to take action in response to her repeated opposition to his policies. It is essential that the levers of justice are never politicized. We are a nation of laws, not individuals. If law enforcement has probable cause to conduct a search or pursue charges against a sitting Member of Congress, officials ought to do so with the highest level of transparency and the utmost professionalism. Just as federal officials should always exercise sound judgment, care for individual rights, and respect for our Constitution in any encounter, no matter what directives they receive from political appointees. I will continue to monitor this situation closely and will be keeping Rep. Omar and her family in my thoughts.”
title: Hoyer Statement on Federal Raid on Congresswoman Omar's Home

SCHNEIDER BLASTS TRUMP DECISION TO LIFT SANCTIONS ON RUSSIAN DIESEL
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10), a member of the House Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee, released a statement opposing President Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel in a bid to lower diesel prices in the U.S. as prices shoot up to over $6 a gallon.  
“Nearly five years since the start of Russia’s unprovoked, illegal war against Ukraine, President Trump inexplicably continues to side with Putin and his anti-democracy agenda,” said Schneider. “Meanwhile, as American soldiers are fighting and dying in Trump’s ill-conceived war with Iran, and American families are paying the price at the pump, Russia is helping Iran target U.S. forces. President Trump is finding new ways to help Putin and worsen the state of the war in both Ukraine and the Middle East. For the more than 20 months he has been in office, Trump has had the power to impose sanctions on Russia and bring an end this war. He has chosen to do neither. Now, by lifting sanctions and allowing the United States to buy Russian diesel, the President is filling Putin’s coffers while doing little to lower diesel prices here. I will work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to block Trump’s purchases of Russian oil and stand with Ukraine in its fight for independence, sovereignty, and the West’s security.”
title: SCHNEIDER BLASTS TRUMP DECISION TO LIFT SANCTIONS ON RUSSIAN DIESEL

Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Launder Proceeds of $6M Medicare Fraud Scheme
A Cape Cod man pleaded guilty today to a money laundering conspiracy for laundering proceeds in connection with a more than $6 million health care fraud scheme.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Leo Anzivino Jr., 35, of Falmouth, Massachusetts, conspired with others to launder health care fraud proceeds. Specifically, Anzivino agreed to be the straw or nominee owner of Advanced Medical Supply Corp. (Advanced), located in Rochester, New Hampshire, even though his co-conspirators were in fact the beneficial owners and managers of Advanced. Advanced submitted more than $6 million in claims to Medicare for durable medical equipment (DME) — such as knee braces and back braces — that Medicare beneficiaries did not need and that doctors did not prescribe. Instead, Advanced supported these claims using fake orders from physicians who did not actually write or submit those orders. Medicare paid more than $3 million as a result of these false and fraudulent claims.
Medicare beneficiaries returned boxes of DME to Advanced with notes stating that they had not ordered the products and alleging a fraud or scam, as depicted below.
Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that the Beneficiary “Did Not Order” the Medical Products and that it was a “FRAUD!!” Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that the Medical Products Were Sent “Without Prior Consent of My Physician or Myself” Note from Medicare Beneficiary Accompanying DME Return Stating that “This Must Be Some Type of Medicare Scam”
Anzivino helped hide his co-conspirator’s involvement with Advanced by being listed as the owner of Advanced on the Medicare enrollment paperwork. He also submitted false and fraudulent bank account opening documents to a bank in New Hampshire, falsely certifying that he was the sole owner of 25 percent or more of the equity interests of Advanced when others, including a co-conspirator, were Advanced’s true owners.
Anzivino then laundered the fraud proceeds by, at his co-conspirator’s direction, seeking to transfer more than $1 million from the Advanced bank account in New Hampshire to companies that were affiliated with the co-conspirator. When told by a bank employee that the bank had not reached a level of confidence that the other companies were legitimate, and that Anzivino should do his own research into these companies, Anzivino instead opened a bank account at another bank with branches in Massachusetts.
In addition, Anzivino learned that Advanced’s ability to bill Medicare would be revoked for various deficiencies, including an inability to verify proof of his ownership of Advanced. Anzivino then sent messages to another individual discussing that revocation, explaining that “All the ppl who gave me money are going to come back for it now my shits revoked,” stating that his co-conspirator “still wants me to wire him money,” and claiming that “I ain’t wiring shit.” Despite this, over the next five weeks, Anzivino proceeded to wire $1,494,938.09 across three separate transactions, each in excess of $10,000.
In 2024, the government seized approximately $353,768.29 in assets tied to the alleged scheme from Advanced’s bank account.
Anzivino pleaded guilty to one count of money laundering conspiracy. He is scheduled to be sentenced Jan. 21, 2027 and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division; U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan for the District of New Hampshire; Special Agent in Charge Roberto Coviello of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Inspector General (HHS-OIG); and Special Agent in Charge Ted E. Docks of the FBI Boston Field Office made the announcement.
HHS-OIG and FBI investigated the case with valuable assistance from IRS-Criminal Investigation and the Department of War Office of Inspector General’s Defense Criminal Investigative Services.
Trial Attorneys John Howard and Tiffany Wynn of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Hunter and Matthew Vicinanzo for the District of New Hampshire are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.
title: Cape Cod Man Pleads Guilty to Conspiring to Launder Proceeds of $6M Medicare Fraud Scheme
