While in Iowa, Administrator Zeldin Proposes 100% Reallocation for Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemption Volumes and Opens Markets for American Farmers
WASHINGTON – While in Peosta, Iowa, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin announced revisions to the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) “Set 2” rule volumes to keep the historic and necessary volumes intact and increase target markets for American farmers. In response to the higher than projected 2025 small refinery exemption (SRE) decisions and the needs of American farmers, the agency is proposing two options for revisions, both of which would reallocate 100% of the difference between projected and actual exempted volumes for 2025 SREs.
The Trump EPA understands the importance of providing a predictable and stable market for farmers, refiners, and American consumers to both maintain economic competitiveness and keep energy prices low. The proposal reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensuring America’s hardworking farmers continue to have a robust and growing market for their crops, while also unleashing American energy.
“In each action taken, EPA works to deliver for all Americans. From our farmers to our energy workers, each has an important role to play in growing our economy and ensuring America’s energy independence,” said EPA Administrator Zeldin. “As soon as we got into office, American farmers asked the Trump EPA not to give them handouts but create avenues for them to enter additional markets. As our farmers continue to harvest their crops, today’s proposal is working to maintain a strong and durable market for them to sell to.”
“American biofuel producers have stepped up to the plate to provide record production, helping to fuel our nation and provide more market opportunities for our farmers. I’m thrilled to see Administrator Zeldin act on this growing momentum and provide a path forward to 100% reallocation by 2027,” said U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins. “The American biofuel industry provides over $100 billion in economic activity and supports over 100,000 American jobs while helping to deliver on President Trump’s energy dominance agenda. The Trump Administration will continue to stand by and deliver results for our farmers.”
“The Trump administration is carrying through on its promise to support Iowa family farmers and biofuel producers. I worked closely with the White House, along with Sen. Ernst and Reps. Hinson, Miller-Meeks, Nunn and Feenstra, to secure full reallocation for all exempted biofuels, and I appreciate the Trump administration following through in a timely fashion. Today’s decision is a major boost for Iowa’s rural economy and the 31,000 Iowa jobs that biofuels directly employ,” said Senator Chuck Grassley (R-IA).
“As farmers continue to harvest their crops across Iowa, we must reaffirm our commitment in providing certainty and reliable markets,” said Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA). “Reallocating the waived small refinery exemption volumes into the 2026 and 2027 Renewable Volume Obligations will strengthen our farm economy, bolster domestic markets, and lower prices for consumers. I thank President Trump and Administrator Zeldin for taking this important step to put farmers first and ensure they have the resources needed to succeed.”
“Farmers across Southeast Iowa are feeling the squeeze, and they need a market they can count on. I’ve worked to make this a reality because Iowa farmers deserve reliable markets for the crops they grow. This announcement helps deliver on that goal, creating more demand for Iowa corn and soybeans,” said Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA-01). “I’m grateful to Administrator Zeldin and President Trump for following through, and I will always fight to put Iowa farmers first.”
“Biofuels should be front and center in any plan to unleash domestic energy production and lower costs at the pump. Earlier this year, the administration announced the strongest biofuels blending targets in history, driving demand for Iowa ag products and new investment in our rural communities,” said Representative Ashley Hinson (R-IA-02). “Today’s proposal reflects the 100% reallocation agreement I helped secure in August—making sure refinery exemptions don’t reduce demand for homegrown biofuels and our farmers and producers are made whole. With farmers facing such difficult conditions right now, getting this across the finish line is a big deal. I’m grateful to Administrator Zeldin for working with me to protect the Renewable Fuel Standard, and I’ll keep pushing relentlessly for Iowa farmers and biofuels producers throughout this process.”
“Homegrown ethanol and biodiesel help us drive down the price of fuel at the pump for families and boost demand for what we grow in Iowa. Our farmers and biofuel producers built this market, and I fought to protect it because it keeps more of that fuel flowing to drivers and keeps the demand with Iowa farmers instead of foreign oil producers. I’ll keep working with Administrator Zeldin to get this rule finalized so families and farmers get the certainty they deserve,” said Representative Zach Nunn (R-IA-03).
When EPA promulgated the “Set 2” rule, the agency estimated the volume of hardship exemptions that small refineries would receive for their 2025 renewable fuel obligations. The August 31,2026, SRE decisions for those 2025 obligations exceeded EPA’s expectations, and an additional 770 million renewable identification numbers (RINs) worth of renewable fuels were exempted from RFS obligations. EPA is now proposing to fully reallocate this volume, to ensure farmers maintain and increase access to their markets. The agency recognizes the importance of getting stakeholder input on the best approach to do so. Therefore, EPA is seeking public comment on two proposed approaches:
- Proposed approach one: EPA would divide the additional 2025 SRE volume equally between the 2026 and 2027 compliance years.
- Proposed approach two: EPA would reallocate all the additional 2025 SRE volume to the 2027 compliance year
EPA will take public comments on the proposal until December 4, 2026.
Additionally, the proposed revision to the 2026 standards may extend the existing 2026 compliance reporting deadline of March 31, 2027. If finalized, this proposal will ensure that all the benefits of the “Set 2” rule will be realized for American farmers.
Today’s announcement is part of the Trump Administration’s all of government approach to opening markets for American farmers. By supporting a strong RFS program, EPA is working to keep generational farmers thriving and rural communities economically rich—Congress’ intent for the program.
Background
Announced on March 27, 2026, by President Trump during the Great American Agriculture Celebration, the historic “Set 2” rule realigned the RFS program with Congress’ original intent of increasing the use of homegrown American biofuels, putting American farmers first. In the 20th year of the RFS program, the final rule sets the highest renewable fuel volumes in the history of the program. With EPA estimating the final rule would generate over $10 billion for rural economies and create over 100,000 new jobs in the agricultural and manufacturing sectors, the Trump EPA’s action created a larger, more stable, and more reliable domestic market for U.S. crops.
title: While in Iowa, Administrator Zeldin Proposes 100% Reallocation for Additional 2025 Small Refinery Exemption Volumes and Opens Markets for American Farmers

Sixth North Carolina Return Preparer Sentenced in $23.9 Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme
The owner of a North Carolina tax return preparation business was sentenced on October 1, 2026, to 60 months in prison for conspiring to prepare false returns claiming fraudulent refunds based on COVID-19 tax credits.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Nejlai Mitchell owned and operated a tax return preparation business out of Lumberton, North Carolina, and Hope Mills, North Carolina. From approximately April 2022 through May 2023, Mitchell and seven employees filed false tax returns seeking fraudulent refunds based on the paid sick and family leave credit, a credit passed by Congress to aid struggling businesses during the COVID-19 global pandemic. The conspiracy resulted in a total of approximately $23.9 million in fraudulent tax refund claims. The IRS paid out approximately $13,890,697 of that amount.
Five other return preparers have also been sentenced for their roles in the scheme. The co-conspirators prepared federal tax returns for clients that included materially false items. On September 3, 2026, Tiffany Moody was sentenced to 26 months in prison. On July 8, 2026, Shaneen Ray was sentenced to 18 months in prison, Eyoubo McBurney was sentenced to 18 months in prison, and Sylvia Swindell was sentenced to 16 months in prison. On July 9, 2026, Katrena Stanback was sentenced to six months in prison.
Mitchell pleaded guilty to conspiracy and preparing and filing false tax returns. The tax return preparation business’s office manager, Whitnee Leach, pleaded guilty in May 2026 to participating in the same conspiracy and filing false tax returns. The remaining five defendants pleaded guilty to preparing and filing false tax returns for clients. Jeannie Negron pleaded guilty in August 2025 to the same charges.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney W. Ellis Boyle of the Eastern District of North Carolina made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorney Caroline Pearson and Assistant U.S. Attorney Ethan Ontjes of the Eastern District of North Carolina are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Sixth North Carolina Return Preparer Sentenced in $23.9 Pandemic-Relief Fraud Scheme

Kaptur, Murray: As Families Pay More & More for Energy, Reports Show Trump Energy Department Withholding Billions and Playing Politics
Toledo, OH – Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, released the following statement on the Trump Administration holding back or cutting off Billions of dollars Congress provided the Department of Energy to bring new energy online and lower Americans’ energy costs. Four recent reports detail how, over the last 18 months, President Trump’s policies have raised energy costs for families and delayed and defunded critical energy investments.
“President Trump hasn’t just sent gas prices through the roof with his war with Iran; he and his Administration have systematically held up and cut off energy investments Congress has made that should be lowering families’ energy bills. Congress gave the Department of Energy tens of Billions of dollars to build out the power grid and cut the costs that families pay to heat and cool their homes. But the Trump Administration is still holding that money back and letting politics decide which projects survive. This President’s corruption is already sending Americans’ energy bills higher. The Constitution gives Congress the power of the purse. We will keep pressing until this money reaches the projects and families it was meant for,” said Kaptur and Murray.
Congress provided funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the annual Energy and Water Development appropriations bills for a variety of cost-cutting energy investments. The funding supports power lines, grid upgrades, home energy savings, and bringing more power online. But starting in January 2025, the Trump Administration froze funds for energy programs and kept them frozen after Kaptur and Murray demanded answers. The Department announced the cancellation of 24 awards worth $3.7 Billion in May 2025 and another 321 worth nearly $8 Billion on October 1, 2025. In July 2026, the Department’s lawyers admitted in court that the October cancellations were based solely on the politics of each recipient’s state.
Four reports released recently show the Department of Energy is failing to spend money Congress provided—driving up Americans’ costs—and it is letting politics drive its decisions:
- Recent analysis from Energy Innovation, which includes state-level impacts, found that the Trump Administration’s energy policy changes since January 2025, including the Department’s cancellation of hydrogen hub funding, will cost households an additional $920 Billion for energy from 2026 through 2040, or about $6,500 more in energy costs per household.
- The Department of Energy Alumni Network and Lawyers for Good Government reported that a year after the Department cancelled hundreds of awards, 61 percent of terminated awards remain in limbo, 69 percent of the awards the Department said it would keep have received negligible funding in the past six months, and another 1,731 projects worth $3.9 Billion have heard nothing from the Department.
- The Natural Resources Defense Council published internal Department records, obtained through a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit, indicating that DOE’s committee reviewing awards for termination was made up entirely of political appointees and Department of Government Efficiency staff. This follows DOE’s earlier admission in court that its decision to cancel energy projects “was based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state.”
- The EFI Foundation found that 94 percent of the $57.5 Billion Congress provided DOE through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act has still not reached recipients, and $29.3 Billion, or 51 percent, has not been legally committed to any project.
# # #
title: Kaptur, Murray: As Families Pay More & More for Energy, Reports Show Trump Energy Department Withholding Billions and Playing Politics

The Energy Department Announces Intention to Support Adding 2.5 GW of Grid Capacity and 800 Jobs
October 13, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced plans to lower electricity costs and strengthen grid reliability by supporting the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) in funding 84 transmission and distribution projects across eight states. The projects are expected to add approximately 2.5 gigawatts (GW) of grid capacity to help mitigate outages and create greater grid resilience. The TVA award is for approximately $581 million in total, including $250 million in federal funding and about $331 million in applicant cost-share funding.
As part of the Resilience Amplified: Multi-Market Grid Interconnection Initiative funding award under the Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) project, the investments will help ensure 2.58 million families and businesses have access to the affordable, reliable, and secure power they need. The project is estimated to support about 800 jobs.
“Since day one, President Trump has recognized that years of misguided energy policies under the previous administration left our bulk power system less robust than it should be,” said U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy James P. Danly. “America is blessed with an abundance of natural resources and some of the most advanced technology in the world, but we must have the generation and transmission infrastructure necessary to support our rapidly growing economy and its electricity needs. These investments with TVA will help reduce congestion, improve efficiency, and make better use of our existing transmission system to lower costs for ratepayers while delivering affordable, reliable, and secure energy essential to American prosperity.”
“America's electric grid cannot become a roadblock to economic growth,” said Office of Electricity (OE) Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza. “By bringing TVA and local utilities together, we're helping reduce costly outages and deliver more power where it's needed. That means fewer disruptions for families, more opportunities for businesses, and a stronger foundation for American jobs.”
The award builds on DOE's selection of TVA for the Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades (SPARK) program. Together, the GRIP and SPARK projects for TVA represent nearly $741 million in planned grid investment, including approximately $329.8 million in federal support, and are expected to add more than 4,300 MW of additional grid capacity.
Under SPARK, TVA plans to upgrade about 125 miles of existing transmission lines across Tennessee, Alabama, and North Carolina using advanced conductors and grid-management technology. The $159.7 million project is expected to add approximately 1,900 MW of transmission capacity and reduce congestion.
Final federal funding, project scope, schedules, and other award conditions remain subject to executed DOE agreements and applicable environmental, permitting, regulatory, and Tribal reviews.
title: Energy Department Backs Major Grid Expansion Across Eight States to Strengthen Reliability and Lower Electricity Costs

CVS Agrees to Pay $315M for Illegally Filling Unlawful Opioid Prescriptions and for Submitting False Claims to the Federal Government
CVS Pharmacy Inc., a Rhode Island-based pharmacy chain, and its related corporate entities (collectively, CVS) have agreed to pay $315 million to resolve allegations that, from October 17, 2013 through December 2, 2025, CVS illegally filled prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances in violation of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA), and then sought payment for many of those invalid prescriptions from Medicare and other federal healthcare programs in violation of the False Claims Act (FCA).
“Not only does this settlement hold bad actors accountable for their fraudulent activities, but Americans are safer because of it,” said Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward Jr. “Today’s settlement is a significant milestone in the Justice Department’s efforts to combat the opioid epidemic by cracking down on pharmacies who unlawfully fulfill prescriptions for controlled substances.”
“Today’s settlement requires CVS to implement additional safeguards to ensure that prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances are dispensed only when medically appropriate,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The remedial measures in this agreement — including proactive monitoring of opioid prescribing patterns — will provide critical protections for patients and federal healthcare programs. The Department of Justice will continue to take steps to prevent the unlawful dispensing of opioids.”
“The opioid epidemic has affected families and communities across Rhode Island and throughout the nation,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Charles C. Calenda for the District of Rhode Island. “Pharmacies that dispense controlled substances must maintain effective compliance systems to identify and respond to warning signs that prescriptions may be unlawful or medically unnecessary. This settlement demonstrates the importance of those obligations and the consequences of failing to implement safeguards designed to prevent the improper dispensing of controlled substances.”
The settlement resolves allegations in the government’s complaint, which the United States filed on Dec. 13, 2024, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island, that CVS knowingly filled prescriptions for controlled substances that lacked a legitimate medical purpose, were not valid, and/or were not issued in the usual course of professional practice. The United States alleged that CVS dispensed prescriptions for dangerous and excessive quantities of opioids, opioid prescriptions filled too early, and “trinity” prescriptions, a dangerous and abused combination of an opioid, a benzodiazepine, and a muscle relaxant. CVS also allegedly filled prescriptions for controlled substances from “pill mill” prescribers who issued large numbers of controlled substance prescriptions without any medical purpose. Further, the United States alleged that CVS pharmacists filled these prescriptions despite clear red flags indicating that there was a high likelihood that the prescriptions lacked a legitimate medical purpose, were not valid, or were not issued in the course of professional practice. Many of these prescriptions were ultimately billed to and reimbursed by federal healthcare programs.
The complaint further alleged that CVS’s violations stemmed from corporate-imposed performance metrics, incentive compensation, and staffing policies that prioritized corporate profits over patient safety. CVS failed to employ enough pharmacists to serve patients, comply with CVS’s legal obligations, and meet corporate performance metrics. In addition, CVS’s policies allegedly prevented pharmacists from warning one another about certain problematic prescribers.
In addition to the monetary payment announced today, CVS has entered into a memorandum of agreement with DEA to address its future obligations in dispensing controlled substances. This agreement requires CVS to establish a hotline for both employees and the public to report suspected illegal dispensing of controlled substances, proactively monitor the dispensing patterns of its pharmacies to identify and address potentially illegal dispensing, and establish a process to evaluate prescribers suspected of illegal prescribing.
“This settlement agreement highlights DEA’s commitment to protecting the health and safety of Americans while holding CVS accountable for dispensing unlawful prescriptions and endangering the public,” said DEA Assistant Administrator Cheri Oz. “DEA is unwavering in its commitment to protect public health and ensuring pharmacies adhere to the highest standards of responsible dispensing. We will continue to work closely with law enforcement, regulatory agencies, and the healthcare community to prevent the misuse of controlled substances, and we will hold those who jeopardize the safety of our citizens accountable.”
“Behind every unlawful prescription is a patient who could be put in harm’s way,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG). “The allegations in this case point to warning signs that should never be overlooked. HHS OIG will not tolerate conduct that jeopardizes lives, and we will continue to pursue those who betray the trust placed in them.”
The civil settlement resolves a civil lawsuit filed by Hillary Estright, a former CVS employee, under the whistleblower provision of the FCA, which authorizes private parties to sue on behalf of the United States and receive a share of any recovery. It also permits the United States to intervene and take over such lawsuits, as it did here. The amount to be recovered by the private whistleblower has not yet been determined. The qui tam case is captioned United States ex rel. Hillary Estright v. CVS Health Corporation, et al., No. 22-cv-00222 (D.R.I.).
This year the Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the Administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect, and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s FCA enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. FCA matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s FCA work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the Civil Division’s Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section, and the Enforcement & Affirmative Litigation Branch, along with the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices for the District of Rhode Island, Eastern District of Virginia, Eastern District of Texas, and District of Hawaii. The DEA’s Office of Diversion Control, Los Angeles Field Division, Richmond District Office, and Office of Chief Counsel led this case with substantial assistance from Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General, Defense Criminal Investigative Service, Defense Health Agency (DHA), Office of Personnel Management (OPM), Department of Labor (DOL) Office of Inspector General, and the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).
The investigation and resolution of this matter illustrate the government’s emphasis on combating healthcare fraud. One of the most powerful tools in this effort is the False Claims Act. Tips and complaints from all sources about potential fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, can be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services at 800-HHS-TIPS (800-447-8477).
The United States is represented in this matter by attorneys from the Justice Department’s Civil Division Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section (Assistant Director Natalie Waites and Trial Attorneys Claire Norsetter and Megan Engel) and Enforcement & Affirmative Litigation Branch (Deputy Director Lisa Hsiao and Trial Attorneys Kathleen Brunson and Katherine Ho), as well as from the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices for the District of Rhode Island (Assistant U.S. Attorney Rachna Vyas), Eastern District of Virginia (Assistant U.S. Attorney John Beerbower), Eastern District of Texas (Assistant U.S. Attorney James Gillingham), and District of Hawaii (Assistant U.S. Attorney Tracy J. Weinstein).
The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.

Former Tennessee Business Owner Sentenced for Employment Tax Fraud
A former Tennessee business owner was sentenced today to 3 years’ probation and ordered to pay $1,048,840 in restitution to the United States for willfully failing to pay over employment taxes to the IRS on behalf of the company she owned and operated.
According to court documents and statements made in court, Mari Alexander, 52, was the sole owner and president of a mental-health counseling center with multiple locations throughout Tennessee. Alexander controlled the counseling center’s financial affairs and was responsible for withholding Social Security, Medicare and federal income taxes from the wages of employees and paying those funds over to the IRS each quarter, as well as filing quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS. From 2015 through 2020, however, Alexander willfully failed to pay over to the IRS the payroll taxes she collected from the counseling center’s employees, and willfully failed to file more than 20 quarterly employment tax returns with the IRS. In total, Alexander caused a tax loss to the United States of more than $1 million.
On April 15, 2026, Alexander pleaded guilty to one count of willful failure to account for and pay over employment taxes.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s Nation Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Braden H. Boucek for the Middle District of Tennessee made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation investigated this case.
Trial Attorney Michael L. Jones of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Former Tennessee Business Owner Sentenced for Employment Tax Fraud

text:
Stanton, Ansari, Grijalva Press GardaWorld Over Unanswered Questions After Company Secures New $1.2 Billion ICE Contract
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Greg Stanton (AZ-04) led Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) in demanding answers from GardaWorld Federal Services (GWFS) following its latest $1.2 billion contract to expand immigration detention facilities in Florence, Arizona. The lawmakers also pressed the company to answer questions it failed to address in a previous inquiry related to the Surprise warehouse facility.
The new contract, awarded September 21, raises fresh concerns about transparency and coordination with local governments. According to reporting, the Town of Florence was not notified of the planned expansion and had no additional information about the contract.
"It is deeply concerning that, despite the significant scale of these projects and their potential impact on surrounding communities, local governments continue to learn about them only after contracts have been awarded," the lawmakers wrote.
The letter also presses GWFS on questions left unanswered from the lawmakers’ March 2026 inquiry into its contract with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to convert a warehouse in Surprise into an immigration detention facility. In its April response, GWFS deferred many questions to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and failed to address basic questions about its own detention experience, staffing, facility assessments, and subcontracting plans. The lawmakers are demanding full answers.
The lawmakers also raised concerns about GWFS' previously undisclosed role in the environmental review of the Surprise warehouse. The City of Surprise revealed that a company representative had requested information for the assessment, despite neither GWFS nor federal agencies publicly disclosing its involvement.
The lawmakers are requesting written responses within 15 business days of receipt of the letter, including answers about:
- Experience and staffing: GWFS' qualifications to manage both projects, personnel overseeing operations, and plans to subcontract construction, medical care, staffing, or facility management.
- Facility safety: Structural and code-compliance assessments of the Surprise warehouse, including plans for ventilation, extreme heat mitigation, fire safety, and medical care.
- Environmental review: GWFS' role in the Surprise environmental assessment and its experience conducting comparable federal reviews.
- Florence expansion: Specific projects, facilities, and task orders planned under the $1.2 billion contract, including their scope and cost.
- Local coordination: Consultations with Surprise, Florence, Maricopa and Pinal counties, school districts, and public safety agencies.
- Taxpayer costs: Whether GWFS or DHS will cover increased demands for emergency medical services, fire protection, and law enforcement rather than shifting those costs to local taxpayers.
"The communities surrounding the Surprise and Florence facilities deserve transparency," the lawmakers concluded.
Read the full letter HERE.

text:
One Year After Trump Promised Full Reversal of Funding Cuts, First Responders Statewide are Still Without Millions in Federal Investments 
BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee’s Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology, led members of the New York Congressional Delegation in urging the Department of Homeland Security to immediately release $87 million in FY2025 Homeland Security Grant Program (HSGP) funding that is still owed to New York. Their letter, sent to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, highlights the danger of withholding this funding from one the largest states in the nation and a top target for international and domestic terrorism.
“One year ago, President Trump promised to restore New York counterterrorism funding in full after slashing the state’s allocation by nearly 90 percent. Yet today, DHS refuses to release $87 million that is still missing,” said Congressman Kennedy. “As Ranking Member of the Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee, I know how critical these preparedness investments are. They help law enforcement and first responders across New York, from Buffalo to Manhattan, plan for emergencies, train for real world terrorism threats, and get the equipment they need to keep our communities safe. These preparedness grants were born out of the aftermath of the deadliest terror attack in American history, a tragedy that changed New York State forever. DHS’s refusal to restore $87 million for the state is not just reckless – it poses a direct threat to public safety.”
In September 2025, DHS issued HSGP award notifications that cut New York’s allocation by 86 percent, or $187 million, leaving the state with just $30 million compared to roughly $220 million in FY24. In October 2025, following bipartisan advocacy, President Trump committed to restoring full funding at approximately $220 million. After a court order in Noem v. Illinois that found Trump unlawfully cut emergency grant funding, the administration released $100 million, but $87 million is still owed to New York.
The missing funds affect every county in the state, including Erie and Niagara, and represent $11 million in losses for New York City. The letter warns that without full restoration, DHS is severely limiting local law enforcement’s ability to plan, train tactical teams, procure equipment, and conduct operations. Created in the wake of the September 11th attacks, HSGP has protected New York State for decades. The delegation underscored that the funds are due 25 years after 9/11 and one year after the President’s promise.
The full text of the letter can be found here.

text:
The Department of Justice Announces Results of Law Enforcement and Private Industry Joint Disruption Week Targeting Online Scam Accounts and Transnational Criminal Networks Operating in West Africa
Note: B-roll and photos related to the enforcement actions can be obtained at: https://spaces.hightail.com/space/UACsRDqzHp
Transnational criminal scam networks operating from West Africa suffered major disruptions last week during a coordinated international “Joint Disruption Week,” an effort that produced arrests, seizures, and the largest-ever takedown of fraudulent social media accounts linked to scam centers in the region, announced the Department of Justice.
“Criminals beware: Law enforcement from around the world are working together, and with private industry, to find you, stop your schemes, and bring you to justice,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “The Criminal Division’s Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative (CSI) was built for this brand of collaboration. The millions of bogus social media accounts taken down and dozens of arrests that took place as part of Joint Disruption Week are just the beginning. I want to thank the United Kingdom (UK)’s National Crime Agency (NCA) and its Director General, Graeme Biggar, for hosting this effort, as well as everyone who participated. I am especially grateful to the courageous law enforcement officers in Ghana and Nigeria who put themselves in harm’s way to seize evidence and arrest the criminals who prey on innocent people.”
“Transnational fraud demands a transnational response,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia, founder of the Scam Center Strike Force. “I have partnered with the NCA and the Crown Prosecutor for England and Wales to push forward cases on both sides of the Atlantic; criminals are not hindered by borders and neither are we. We will deploy our team wherever in the world transnational criminals target innocent victims.”
The “Joint Disruption Week” events mark the first coordinated effort focused specifically on West Africa, underscoring the growing global commitment to dismantling increasingly sophisticated transnational scam networks.
The operation included members of the U.S. Department of Justice, the Scam Center Strike Force under the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, FBI, U.S. Secret Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), the UK’s NCA, the Nigerian Joint Case Team on Cybercrimes, the Nigeria Police Force - National Cybercrime Center, Ghanaian Cyber Security Authority, and private sector partners.
Additional participants included law enforcement agencies from Australia, Canada, Ghana, India, New Zealand, Nigeria, along with INTERPOL and additional cybercrime units. Several tech giants also played a key role. The large-scale effort was hosted by the UK NCA in London.
“Thanks to brilliant partnership with the Department of Justice and the private sector, across multiple African countries, we arrested dozens of criminal actors, seized hundreds of devices, identified at least $11 million in potentially freezable funds, and truly saved lives,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “This is what happens when law enforcement executes with precision across the interagency. We are demolishing Scam Centers across the globe and crushing a criminal industry preying on American citizens.”
“Fraud is a global problem and it takes partnership working across international boundaries to tackle it,” said Nick Sharp, Deputy Director of Fraud at the NCA. “Hosting such a rich and dedicated team of law enforcement and technology companies at NCA’s headquarters enabled us to utilize the power of partnerships and strike back at a significant set of criminals who inflict misery on thousands of victims of fraud. Fraudsters can operate from anywhere and will target victims both domestically and globally. The NCA will continue to work with international and private sector partners to tackle fraudsters working upstream, overseas and online. Collaborating in this way sends a clear signal to criminals that the combined capabilities of law enforcement and industry means that we will relentlessly pursue them and the infrastructure they rely on no matter where they operate.”
During the week beginning Oct. 6, investigators and industry partners exchanged real-time intelligence across jurisdictions, enabling rapid identification and disruption of scam centers in Nigeria, Ghana, and other African countries. Many of the targeted operations were tied to schemes victimizing individuals in the United States, UK, and other countries around the world.
Several private industry partners, including Meta, Adobe, Binance, Coinbase, Cyjax, Elliptic, Chainalysis, Flashpoint, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Silent Push, Starlink and TRM Labs collaborated with international law enforcement in the event, and voluntarily took action on their own networks to disrupt scammers using their platforms to perpetrate fraud. These companies reported to the Department that they “removed more than 3.7 million accounts, Pages and Groups targeting people in the U.S., UK and beyond, and shared leads on over 30 suspected scam centers with law enforcement, resulting in dozens of arrests, the rescue of trafficking victims, and cryptocurrency seizures. In total over $11 million dollars in potential freezable funds were identified by the private sector partners. Meta played a key role in coordinating the event and encouraging broad private sector participation to maximize scam compound disruption.
Among the key accomplishments:
A consortium of international law enforcement agencies made 28 arrests of individuals tied to the criminal scam operations, including:
- In Ghana, in the Accra suburb of Sasaabi, authorities arrested 19 individuals and seized 303 electronic devices. In addition, authorities identified 117 victims of human trafficking that are now pending repatriation to Nigeria. An additional 89 victims of the scam were identified with an approximate loss of $8.3 million. During the last week of September alone, authorities made scores of arrests at six locations, identified 34 trafficking victims, and seized 129 electronic devices. The Ghana operation was led by the Ghana Cyber Security Authority, Ghana Police Service Criminal Investigation Department, National Security Service, with support from the NCA, FBI, and Nigeria’s Economic and Financial Crimes Commission.
- In Nigeria, authorities arrested nine individuals during the enforcement period, and 53 electronic devices.
- The disrupted schemes included law enforcement impersonation scams, digital “arrest” extortion schemes, cryptocurrency investment fraud (also known as “pig butchering”), and a variety of other online fraud operations targeting global victims.
According to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), investment scams were reported 72,984 times in 2025, with cryptocurrency investment fraud comprising 72 percent of that category. Reported losses from these scams rose from $3.96 billion in 2023 to $5.8 billion in 2024. Reported losses for investment scams with a cryptocurrency nexus rose 24 percent in 2025 to over $7.2 billion, according to IC3’s released 2025 annual report. Those figures, based largely on victim reports, are believed to significantly underrepresent actual losses, as many victims do not report to law enforcement. According to one government report, a conservative estimate of the annual value of funds stolen by scam syndicates worldwide approached $64 billion as of the end of 2023.
Strengthening Accountability for Transnational Scam Operations
Criminal scam centers operating in West Africa mirror those uncovered in Southeast Asia — highly organized enterprises that recruit workers, train them in social engineering, and deploy multi‑platform fraud campaigns targeting global victims. While technology companies can significantly disrupt online infrastructure used to perpetuate these schemes, true accountability requires sustained law enforcement action against the individuals and organizations behind them.
The FBI, The Scam Center Strike Force, and its international partners remain committed to advancing this model of public‑private collaboration and expanding global efforts to dismantle criminal networks responsible for online fraud.
On March 6, 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order directing the Administration to prioritize cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes draining American families of their life savings. Through the Executive Order, President Trump is unleashing every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cyber-enabled fraud. The Criminal Division’s Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative, Scam Center Strike Force under U.S. Attorney Pirro, and the Homeland Security Task Force National Coordination Center (NCC) are critical in executing the mission outlined in the President’s Order.
The Department of Justice’s Criminal Division, through its Cyber-Enabled Scam Initiative (CSI), works to disrupt and stop cyber-enabled criminal networks that prey on Americans. CSI brings together expert prosecutors from across the Division to accelerate the prosecution of cyber-enabled financial crimes, including investment and crypto scams, government imposter schemes, romance and inheritance scams, financially motivated sextortion, lottery and sweepstakes scams, and other predatory schemes. With nationwide jurisdiction and global reach, CSI leverages every available tool to dismantle criminal operations, pursue bad actors, recover criminal proceeds, and obtain justice for victims. The Criminal Division partners with U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country.
The Scam Center Strike Force was officially launched by U.S. Attorney Pirro in November 2025 to address the growing threat posed by Chinese organized crime syndicates operating scam centers, primarily in Southeast Asia. The Strike Force targets cryptocurrency investment fraud, cyber-enabled fraud, human trafficking, and money laundering operations that have cost American victims billions of dollars. The Scam Center Strike Force has been joined in its work by the FBI, the U.S. Secret Service, Justice Department’s Criminal Division, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, IRS Criminal Investigation, and HSI, as well as the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Alaska, Hawaii, Eastern North Carolina, Rhode Island, and Western Washington. The Strike Force works in collaboration with other federal agencies, including the Treasury and State Departments. The Strike Force works in strategic partnership with private industry and calls on all U.S. businesses to take more proactive steps to protect users from scam operations.
The Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF)’s NCC, established by Executive Order, is responsible for coordinating Federal efforts to detect, disrupt, dismantle, and deter — including by involving the private sector as appropriate — cyber-enabled criminal activity conducted by foreign Transnational Criminal Organizations and associated networks that target U.S. persons, businesses, critical infrastructure, or public services.

text:
Sanctions Disrupt CDN’s Integrated Commercial Operations Supporting Violenceand Cross‑Border Corruption
WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 11 entities connected to the U.S.-designated Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) Cartel del Noreste (CDN). Those designated include individuals and businesses involved in quarter horse racing, construction, trucking, and the oil and gas sector, highlighting the cartel’s diverse commercial footprint. CDN’s evolution from its predecessor, Los Zetas—responsible for some of the deadliest mass‑casualty attacks in Mexican history—underscores the severity of CDN’s continued threat to the United States and the region.
“Today’s action exposes Cartel del Noreste’s exploitation of the horse racing sector to launder illicit proceeds and finance cartel operations,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “This action marks Treasury’s most significant effort to date to disrupt Cartel del Noreste’s financial infrastructure. Treasury, in close coordination with our law enforcement partners, remains committed to protecting the U.S. financial system from misuse by violent cartels.”
CDN’s stronghold sits directly across the border from Laredo, Texas, the busiest port of entry (POE) on the southern border, where nearly 40 percent of all commercial traffic between the United States and Mexico crosses. This deep entrenchment in cross-border industries, combined with CDN’s ability to infiltrate local governments, steer public contracts, and manipulate regional elections, undermines legitimate authority and destabilizes communities on both sides of the border.
In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans in close coordination with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025. OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons.
Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks. OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, including the U.S. Border Patrol, the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, as well as assistance from the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the U.S. Marshals Service. OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. Additionally, OFAC coordinated on this action and previous actions against CDN with the Government of Mexico’s financial intelligence unit, the Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF).
The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886 (collectively, E.O.13224, as amended), which targets terrorists and their supporters. This is OFAC’s fourth and largest action to date targeting CDN networks during the Trump Administration. On May 21, 2025, OFAC designated two high-ranking members and arms traffickers of CDN. On August 6, 2025, OFAC designated three high-ranking members and one associate of CDN, including famous narco-rapper El Makabelico. Earlier this year, on April 14, 2026, OFAC designated three entities and three associates of CDN, including Casino Centenario, a casino just miles from the U.S. border, and Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez, criminal advisor to CDN.
CARTEL DEL NORESTE
Based in Mexico directly across from one of the busiest American border crossings, CDN is a violent terrorist cartel founded by the notorious brothers Miguel Angel “Z-40” Trevino Morales and Oscar Omar “Z-42” Trevino Morales. CDN has been involved in the trafficking of narcotics and other illicit drugs, including fentanyl, crystal methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and cocaine. CDN, formerly known as Los Zetas, has engaged in horrific violence over the years. This year marks the fifteenth anniversary of the August 25, 2011 deadly Los Zetas arson attack on a casino in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico. This arson attack killed 52 people and injured dozens more, with a majority of those killed being women. This firebombing became one of the deadliest cartel attacks against civilians in Mexican history.
Z-40 and Z-42 were arrested by Mexican authorities in 2013 and 2015, respectively, but maintained control over the cartel utilizing corrupt attorneys, including Juan Pablo Penilla Rodriguez, whom OFAC designated in April 2026. The Trevino brothers were transferred from Mexico in February 2025 and are currently facing drug trafficking, racketeering, firearms, and money laundering charges in the District Court for the District of Columbia, with a maximum sentence of life imprisonment. CDN, then known as Los Zetas, was identified by the United States as a specially designated foreign narcotics trafficker on April 15, 2009, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act). On July 24, 2011, Los Zetas was named as a transnational criminal organization (TCO) in the annex to E.O. 13581. On December 15, 2021, OFAC designated CDN pursuant to E.O. 14059. On February 20, 2025, the U.S. Department of State designated CDN as an FTO and as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT).
AMERICAN QUARTER HORSE RACING – A ZETAS TRADITION
CDN has a long history of money laundering through the American Quarter Horse racing industry. Between 2008 and 2012, Z-40 and Z-42 bought and sold racehorses with drug money and trained and raced them in the United States. Over a 30-month period, Zetas-affiliated front persons and shell companies spent $16 million in New Mexico, Oklahoma, California, and Texas to support the operation and laundered upwards of $22 million for the cartel. In June 2012, the U.S. Government seized 455 horses at an Oklahoma horse farm, racing venues, and training farms.
CDN’s involvement in horse racing continues to this day. Club La Molienda (La Molienda) is a horse racetrack, restaurant, and bar located on the outskirts of Nuevo Laredo that is controlled by CDN. As the most prominent racetrack in Nuevo Laredo, La Molienda generates revenue for CDN, charging entrance fees for those racing their horses at the track as well as for spectators.
CDN leaders and members purchase horses, including many from the United States, to race at La Molienda. La Molienda is controlled by Z-40 but is ultimately overseen by various CDN leaders and associates while Z-40 is incarcerated in the United States.
Before a successful bilateral U.S.-Mexico action in April 2026 suspended operations of Casino Centenario, La Molienda and Casino Centenario entered a strategic gambling partnership allowing people to bet on races at La Molienda from the premises of Casino Centenario. In coordination with OFAC’s April 2026 designation of Casino Centenario and related entities, on the same day, Mexico’s UIF took action and the Secretaría de Gobernación suspended the activities of these CDN-linked entities.
OFAC designated La Molienda pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CDN.
INSIDE THE WINNER’S CIRCLE – TRACKSIDE ASSOCIATES OF CDN
Gamaliel Garza Garcia (Garza Garcia) is a Mexico-based businessman, horse racing enthusiast, and an associate of CDN. Garza Garcia is involved in horse racing in both Mexico and the United States, racing at some of the most prestigious tracks in California and New Mexico. Garza Garcia and his horses frequently race at La Molienda.
Garza Garcia’s company, Construcciones y Edificaciones Garza Elias S.A. de C.V. (CEGESA), has been utilized by CDN to funnel money to election campaigns of CDN’s preferred political candidates. Additionally, CEGESA has corruptly obtained government contracts and then sub-contracted that work to CDN-affiliated individuals. CEGESA is a major recipient of government contracts in the north of the country, including from the governments of the municipality of Nuevo Laredo and the state of Tamaulipas.
Garza Garcia created the Nuevo Laredo-based material supply company Concretos y Productos Asfalticos del Norte, S.A. de C.V. (COPASA) to vertically integrate the illicit construction contract scheme. CEGESA performed or subcontracted the work, while COPASA provided the materials. As of early 2026, CEGESA and COPASA were some of the only construction companies authorized by CDN to perform construction work in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas.
Garza Garcia controls Cuadra San Dibanh, an Anahuac, Nuevo Leon-based Quarter Horse racing barn. Cuadra San Dibanh frequently races at La Molienda and other major racetracks throughout Mexico.
Garza Garcia also owns and controls an extensive corporate network of construction and fuel companies in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas. This includes the following six companies, all based in Nuevo Laredo:
- Construaceros del Fuerte, S.A. de C.V., a construction company;
- Inova NLD Desarrollos Inmobiliarios, S.A. de C.V., a construction company;
- Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas company;
- Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas company;
- Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas company; and
- Transportadora de Gas de Nuevo Laredo, S.A. de C.V., a fuel and gas transportation company.
Gamaliel Garza Elias (Garza Elias), Garza Garcia’s son, is being designated for his role in CEGESA, where he is involved in the day-to-day operations of CEGESA. Garza Elias has also delivered cash to fund election campaigns for CDN’s preferred political candidates in Mexico.
OFAC designated Garza Garcia pursuant to E.O. 14059, for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, CDN. Garza Garcia is also being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, CDN.
OFAC designated CEGESA; COPASA; Cuadra San Dibanh; Construaceros del Fuerte, S.A. de C.V.; Inova NLD Desarrollos Inmobiliarios, S.A. de C.V.; Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V.; Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V.; Propane Trading Group, S.A. de C.V.; and Transportadora de Gas de Nuevo Laredo, S.A. de C.V. pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Garza Garcia.
OFAC designated Garza Elias pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended,for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CEGESA.
OTHER PLAYERS IN THE NUEVO LAREDO PLAZA
Pablo Cesar Guajardo Alvarez (Guajardo), known as “Takia,” is a current CDN plaza boss of Nuevo Laredo and former leader of CDN’s sicarios. Plaza bosses are in charge of all cartel activity in their area of responsibility. Guajardo was arrested in 2020 for his connection to the January 4, 2017 assassination of Ricardo Martinez Chavez and four public servants, but has since been released. Guajardo has been involved in arms trafficking on behalf of CDN.
OFAC designated Guajardo pursuant to E.O. 14059, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, CDN.
Tamex Leasing or Tamex Logistics (Tamex) is a Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas-based trucking company involved in the smuggling of narcotics into the United States. Tamex’s truckyard in Nuevo Laredo has been the originator of at least two cocaine shipments bound for the United States. Seized by law enforcement, these shipments were stored in hidden compartments of the trailers’ brake drums and totaled 52 kilograms. Francisco Javier Inzunza Partida (Inzunza) is a dispatcher for Tamex who was involved in dispatching the two trailers seized for concealed narcotics.
OFAC designated Tamex and Inzunza pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production.
SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS
As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC. In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons.
Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions. In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons. The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause
U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions. Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.
Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions. OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority.
The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior. For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List.

For Immediate Release: October 13, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

Montclair, N.J. — Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) issued the following statement after the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers used the parking lot of the federal government's Roxbury Township warehouse facility to stage and process 14 detained individuals on two separate occasions in September.

“DHS has finally admitted what we suspected all along: ICE used the Roxbury property to process and stage detainees on multiple occasions, potentially in violation of a court order restricting its use as an immigration detention facility. After weeks of denying that the property was being used for immigration enforcement operations, DHS has finally confirmed to my office that ICE used the site to process 14 detained individuals on September 4 and 8. Let’s be clear: This was no accident. ICE officers deliberately misled the municipality and state by conducting processing operations with supervisory knowledge. According to communications with my office, only after whistleblowers raised concerns, did they cease activity. The fact that ICE describes potential illegal activity as ‘routine operating procedures’ should alarm every New Jerseyan,” said Congresswoman Mejia.

“ICE does not get to cherry-pick which laws to follow. I will continue to demand answers, pursue oversight, and work with state officials to ensure this property is never again used outside the law. ICE cannot be trusted to police itself. An agency that operates with impunity and answers to a Secretary who encourages suffering in detention must be abolished and replaced with a fair, just, and humane immigration system that respects due process and human dignity,” said Mejia.

Washington, D.C.—Today, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Rick Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Aviation André Carson (D-IN) and 21 Democratic members of the T&I Committee wrote to United States Government Accountability Office (GAO) Acting Comptroller General of the United States Orice Brown requesting an audit of the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) deployment of the AI-based SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories) and FMDS (Flow Management Data and Services) platforms.
“As the Government Accountability Office has previously reported, the Federal Aviation Administration has struggled for decades to modernize the technology and infrastructure supporting the nation’s air traffic control (ATC) system, resulting in outdated systems that undermine the safety and reliability of U.S. aviation,” the members wrote.
“While technological modernization is essential, the FAA’s development and implementation of FMDS and SMART have generated considerable concern from Members of this Committee and key aviation stakeholders. Concerningly, the nation’s frontline aviation safety workforce apparently had little to no input into SMART’s development and have received limited training and information during the current deployment process,” the members continued.
The members also highlighted the need for proper safety guardrails, writing, “The use of artificial intelligence within SMART has rightfully raised serious questions about its reliability and safety benefits, particularly on its potential to interfere with decision-making by experienced air traffic controllers or to hallucinate safety-critical information.”
“Transparency and accountability in the development and deployment of modern, data-driven air traffic control tools are essential to airspace safety,” they continued.
The Members concluded by requesting GAO to assess the FAA’s (1) safety risk management analysis of SMART and FMDS; (2) plans to test, evaluate and certify the platforms for operational use; (3) performance metrics used to determine the safety, effectiveness and reliability of SMART; and (4) deployment strategy, including coordination with key stakeholders.

U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today announced nine recipients of the prestigious Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award for their exceptional contributions to research and development supporting the U.S. Department of Energy’s missions in science, energy, and national security.
October 13, 2026
WASHINGTON—U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright today announced nine recipients of the prestigious Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award for their exceptional contributions to research and development supporting the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) missions in science, energy, and national security.
“This year’s Lawrence Award recipients exemplify the ingenuity and determination that drive America’s leadership in science and technology,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “From achieving fusion ignition to advancing critical materials and high-performance computing, these scientists and engineers are tackling some of our nation’s most complex challenges and translating groundbreaking research into real-world capabilities. Their work strengthens our nation’s energy security, drives American innovation, and ensures the United States remains at the forefront of scientific discovery.”
Established in 1959, the Lawrence Award recognizes mid-career U.S. scientists and engineers for groundbreaking achievements across nine scientific and engineering categories. The award is among the longest-running and most prestigious science and technology honors bestowed by the U.S. government.
The 2026 Ernest O. Lawrence Award recipients are:
- Eric J. Schelter, Ph.D. (University of Pennsylvania) – Atomic, Molecular, and Chemical Sciences – Honored for his “fundamental chemical studies of energy-critical metals leading to new methods for their selective and sustainable separations.”
- Patrick Chain, Ph.D. (Los Alamos National Laboratory and New Mexico Consortium) – Biological and Environmental Sciences – Honored for his “pioneering work in genomics and microbiome science, including discoveries of new bacterial-fungal interactions and revolutionizing the field by democratizing access to advanced bioinformatics tools.”
- Samuel W. Williams, Ph.D. (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory) – Computer, Information, and Knowledge Sciences – Honored for his “pioneering contributions in performance modeling, hardware/software design optimization, and novel computer architecture for high-performance computing, enabling modeling of complex computational solutions, and increasing analysis speed, simulation accuracy, and computational efficiency.”
- Thomas Epps, III, Ph.D. (University of Delaware) – Condensed Matter and Materials Sciences – Honored for his “fundamental contributions to chemistry and materials science with applications in the chemical upcycling of polymeric waste, generation of high-performance materials from biomass feedstocks, and development of membranes for lithium-ion battery technologies.”
- Gregg Beckham, Ph.D. (National Laboratory of the Rockies and University of Colorado Boulder) – Energy Science and Innovation – Honored for his “transformative research in the conversion of lignocellulosic biomass and waste plastics via biology, chemistry, and engineering, yielding building blocks for sustainable fuels, chemicals, and materials.”
- Andrea L. Kritcher, Ph.D. (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory) – Fusion and Plasma Sciences – Honored for her “exceptional design efforts leading to the first-ever achievement of fusion ignition in the Laboratory, which is of major scientific impact to institutional and national missions, the private sector, and fusion interests within academia.”
- Charles C. Polly, Ph.D. (Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory) – High Energy Physics – Honored for his “exceptional scientific and technical contributions to low-energy precision measurements in particle physics, most notably leadership of the experimental measurement of the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon with the Muon g-2 experiment.”
- Michael Reed, Ph.D. (Nevada National Security Site) – National Security and Nonproliferation – Honored for his “vital contributions to national and international nuclear emergency response through the Advanced Visualization & Integration of Data (AVID) software, which broke existing paradigms by simultaneously fusing all radiological data into a single interface connected seamlessly to world-wide expertise.”

DOE will honor the recipients at a hybrid award ceremony in Washington, D.C., on November 13, 2026. The ceremony will be broadcast live online, and a recording will be available following the event. Amo Highlights Rhode Island’s Blue Economy at Roger Williams Oyster Farm and Hinckley Yacht Services
Bristol, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) continued his 2026 Blue Economy Tour today with visits to Roger Williams University’s shellfish farm and research facilities and Hinckley Yachts’ expanded Portsmouth facility, highlighting the research, skilled workers, and businesses driving Rhode Island’s maritime economy.
At Roger Williams, Amo toured the shellfish farm, hatchery, and research labs with faculty and researchers to discuss advances in shellfish production, aquaculture, and blue biotechnology, as well as opportunities to prepare students for careers in the Blue Economy. They also discussed federal policies to support aquaculture, fisheries, and environmental conservation. At the newly expanded Hinckley Yachts facility in Portsmouth, Amo met with workers and discussed the skilled trades and maritime jobs that keep Rhode Island moving.
“Rhode Island’s Blue Economy means cutting-edge research, skilled jobs, and businesses building the future right here in the Ocean State,” said Congressman Gabe Amo. “At Roger Williams, researchers are advancing aquaculture and blue biotech. At Hinckley, skilled workers are building and servicing world-class yachts. I’m looking forward to bringing what I learn on this tour back to Washington to help inform how to grow these industries, create opportunities for Rhode Islanders, and protect our ocean.”
“We were pleased to welcome Congressman Gabe Amo to Roger Williams University as a stop on his Blue Economy Tour. At RWU, marine research, hands-on student learning, and partnerships with Rhode Island’s aquaculture industry come together to address real-world challenges facing our coastal communities,” said Margaret Everett, Provost, Roger Williams University.” Touring our Marine and Natural Sciences building and CEED facilities offered an opportunity to showcase how university research and education support a sustainable blue economy and help prepare the next generation of marine science professionals.”
"CEED’s research, education, and collaborations support a thriving, sustainable aquaculture industry in Rhode Island. With our industry partners, we’re advancing aquaculture technology and blue biotechnology, while preparing the next generation of professionals to address challenges facing our coastal ecosystems,” said Koty Sharp, Director, Roger Williams University Center for Economic & Environmental Development. “We’re excited to share with Congressman Amo how university research can power our state’s growing Blue Economy.”
“Hinckley is investing in our flagship Portsmouth yard to create a premier facility that reinforces Rhode Island’s leadership in the marine trades and reflects the craftsmanship at the heart of our business,” said Peter Clark, Chief Development Officer, Hinckley Yachts. “By modernizing the yard and enhancing the working environment, we aim to attract the next generation of marine trades talent while providing our highly skilled team with opportunities to build rewarding, long-term careers.”
Background
Congressman Amo kicked off his 2026 Blue Economy Tour with a visit to REGENT Craft, where he helped cut the ribbon on their new electric Seaglider factory.
Rhode Island’s Blue Economy directly employs 36,000 Rhode Islanders and contributes over $5 billion to the state’s gross domestic product every year.
In 2024, Congressman Amo toured Rhode Island’s First Congressional District to highlight the Ocean State’s leadership in the Blue Economy across labor, education, business, and defense.

Underwood Secures More Than $500,000 in Federal Funding for Child Care, Youth Homelessness, Suicide Prevention, University Research, and More in Northern Illinois
WASHINGTON — This week, Representative Lauren Underwood announced a new round of federal funding she has secured for child care, youth services, university research, and crisis intervention in northern Illinois.
As a member of the Appropriations Committee, Underwood has made securing federal resources for our community a top priority. The following funds will support programs in the 14th District with federal resources:
Lewis University, Romeoville, Illinois – $125,000
Lewis University in Romeoville has been awarded $125,000 in federal funding through the Center for Mental Health Services at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
This grant will help stand up a network of supports to meet the growing mental health needs of Lewis University students. The program will provide screenings, assessments, referrals for services, training, education, and an awareness campaign. Project Safety Net will also help identify students who are at risk for suicidal behavior, increase protective factors that promote mental health, and reduce risk factors for suicide.
Youth Service Bureau of Illinois Valley, Ottawa, Illinois – $235,524
Youth Service Bureau of Illinois Valley in Ottawa has been awarded $235,524 in federal funding through the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) at the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
This grant helps create and strengthen community-based programs that meet the immediate needs of runaway and homeless youth under 18 years old. The grant is through the Basic Center Program at ACF, which also works to reunite young people with their families or locate appropriate alternative placements.
Northern Illinois University, DeKalb, Illinois – $34,064
Northern Illinois University has been awarded $34,064 in federal funding through the Office of Public Health and Science at the Department of Health and Human Services.
This grant will fund a project researching the responsible conduct of research into AI, Open Science, and Partnerships.
City of Aurora, Aurora, Illinois – $128,000
The City of Aurora has been awarded $128,000 in federal funding through Office of Justice Programs at the Department of Justice (DOJ).
This grant will fund the City of Aurora’s Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) Training Program Initiative. The purpose of this project is to expand specialized training for public safety personnel to improve responses to individuals experiencing mental illness or behavioral health crises. The project will take place in Aurora, IL and will serve community members who interact with police, school resource officers, dispatchers, and detention personnel. The initiative will train and certify approximately 45 personnel through the Illinois Law Enforcement Training and Standards Board’s 40 hour CIT curriculum.

Phoenix Tax Preparer Convicted for Willfully Filing False Tax Returns
A federal jury in Phoenix, Arizona, convicted a man for aiding and assisting in the filing of false tax returns, and for filing false personal income tax returns.
Pacific Kashosi, the owner of African Union Tax Services, a tax preparation business, was convicted of 18 counts of aiding and assisting in the preparation of false tax returns for clients of his business and two counts of filing his own false tax returns.
According to the evidence presented at trial, Kashosi prepared false tax returns for his clients that reported false Covid tax credits, false fuel credits and false business losses. The false tax returns claimed thousands of dollars in fraudulent refunds. Kashosi was also convicted of filing false 2022 and 2023 federal income tax returns that did not report any of the nearly $900,000 in return preparation fees he received. Kashosi caused a large portion of the fraudulent refunds claimed on his clients’ returns to be wired into his bank accounts.
Kashosi faces a statutory maximum sentence of three years in prison for each count of conviction along with a period of supervised release, restitution, and monetary penalties. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief Andrew Kameros of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Kevin Rapp of the District of Arizona are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Phoenix Tax Preparer Convicted for Willfully Filing False Tax Returns
