News Release
US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties
MONROE, NY – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited six construction employers for willful and serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at the site of a planned 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building and proposed a combined $648,094 in penalties.
The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an allegation of struck-by and collapse hazards associated with a large excavation at the Monroe Commons project – also known as Magna Square development – a planned 4-story, approximately 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building with retail, office space, and a 39-room hotel located on an 18-acre site. The excavation had a steep, unstable embankment nearly 75 feet high which was not adequately sloped or shored.
OSHA issued a total of 23 serious and five willful citations to the project’s general contractor and five subcontractors for failing to protect employees from cave-in, struck-by, and chemical hazards; neglecting to shield employees from falling or rolling rock and soil from an excavation face; and not ensuring daily inspections of excavations were conducted by a competent person.
Advanced Plan and Build LLC, and subcontractors Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. – operating as Drip Drop Waterproofing Inc. – and The Paving Masters LLC received citations for willfully exposing employees to cave-in and struck-by hazards from an unprotected excavation. OSHA also cited Advanced Plan and Build and The Paving Masters for their willful failure to ensure that the excavation, which was between 21 and 75 feet deep, was designed by a registered professional engineer.
Subcontractors Century Max Industries Corp., DelValle Contractor, and Prime Structure Inc. were cited for serious violations for failing to protect employees from cave-in and struck-by hazards. DelValle and Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. also received citations for serious violations related to lack of fall protection and chemical hazards.
OSHA proposed the following penalties: Advanced Plan and Build LLC—$175,444; Century Max Industries Corp.—$46,340; DelValle Contractor—$19,151; Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc.—$198,615; Prime Structure Inc.—$19,860; and The Paving Masters LLC—$188,684.
The employers have 15 business days from receipt of its citations and penalties to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.
Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.
title: US Labor Department finds 6 New York, New Jersey construction employers exposed workers to safety hazards, assesses combined $648K in penalties

Following a comprehensive, multi-phase due diligence review, the Department of War has determined that significant operational and managerial improvements at General Dynamics Bath Iron Works (BIW) have established the capacity and stability necessary to support the potential construction of a second guided-missile destroyer (DDG).
The Department's thorough review evaluated production throughput, schedule adherence, quality assurance benchmarks, supply chain resilience, and workforce optimization at the Bath, Maine shipyard. Based on verifiable performance enhancements and leadership initiatives implemented across the facility, the Department concluded that building an additional Arleigh Burke-class (DDG 51) destroyer at BIW is feasible and strategically advantageous for the Navy's fleet, should Congress secure the necessary funding.
"Our national security requires an industrial base that can respond to demands for increased speed and volume," said Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg. "After a rigorous review, Bath Iron Works has proven it has the capacity and stability to support construction of a second destroyer. While the operational improvements we have seen at BIW are a significant step in the right direction, the shipyard must continue this momentum to fully resolve legacy production challenges – sustained performance is essential. The Department will continue to partner with contractors who prioritize execution, accountability, and the rapid modernization of our forces."
"Today's decision by the Department of War validates the capacity of Bath Iron Works (BIW) and the hard work of its highly skilled 6,800 employees who build the best ships in the world. I have advocated for a second destroyer to be included in this year's budget, and I worked with the Administration during its careful review and repeated visits to BIW to verify the ability of the shipyard to construct another ship while continuing to complete its current workload," said Senator Susan Collins (ME). "This certification will help keep our Navy strong and support BIW as a steady source of good-paying Maine jobs. I will continue to work to ensure our shipbuilders have the resources to meet the Navy's needs at a time when China is relentlessly expanding its fleet."
The decision to certify the shipyard's capacity for a second destroyer aligns with the Administration's broader, aggressive campaign to revitalize the U.S. Maritime Industrial Base and outmatch global pacing threats. To counter aggressive ship-construction timelines by foreign adversaries, the Department is prioritizing long-term stability and capacity-building across the domestic shipbuilding supply chain.
Through targeted modernization investments, workforce development initiatives, and streamlined procurement processes, the Administration is actively expanding America's sovereign shipbuilding capacity. Ensuring that key shipyards like Bath Iron Works can reliably scale and sustain high-rate production is a cornerstone of the Department's strategy to maintain global maritime dominance and protect American interests worldwide.
title: Department of War Certifies Production Capacity for Second Guided-Missile Destroyer at Maine's Bath Iron Works

Secretary Wright issues an emergency order to stabilize the mid-Atlantic grid and mitigate the risk of blackouts
October 12, 2026
WASHINGTON—U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright issued an emergency order to mitigate blackout risks in the mid-Atlantic ahead of a period of elevated demand, a high rate of planned generator outages during the autumn maintenance season, and numerous planned transmission outages. The order directs PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) to dispatch specified units and to order their operation as needed to maintain reliability and authorizes PJM to direct backup generation resources to operate as a last resort before declaring an Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) 3 or during an EEA 3. 
PJM is authorized to call upon its Transmission Owners and Electric Distribution Companies to implement the order as needed. The order was issued pursuant to an application from PJM submitted on October 11, 2026. 
“This order will help ensure millions of American families and businesses across the mid-Atlantic have access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity by making additional power generation, including backup power, available to use as needed,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “While past leaders’ energy subtraction policies have made the grid more vulnerable to the risk of blackouts when the sun doesn’t shine or the wind doesn’t blow, this administration remains committed to using every available tool to prevent blackouts.” 
DOE estimates more than 35 GW of unused backup generation remains available nationwide. 
The order is effective October 13, 2026, through October 16, 2026.
title: Energy Secretary Secures Mid-Atlantic Grid Ahead of Anticipated Stressed System Conditions

WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) and the U.S. Department of War (DoW) announced a new memorandum of agreement building on the Smaller War Plants Commission (SWPC) to expand access to strategic capital for small businesses in the defense industrial base. By aligning DoW’s strategic-investment capabilities through its Economic Defense Unit (EDU) with SBA’s lending and investment expertise, the partnership will help defense-critical manufacturers, suppliers, and innovators access more capital to grow production, strengthen domestic supply chains, and deliver for America’s warfighters. The agreement advances the SWPC mission to identify, support, and scale the small businesses essential to America’s military strength.
“The American military is already the strongest fighting force the world has ever known, and President Trump has made clear that we will keep it that way—not by accepting a hollowed-out industrial base, but by building an Arsenal of Freedom that can outproduce, out-innovate, and outlast any adversary,” said Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. “The Smaller War Plants Commission will now be able to surge strategic capital to the small businesses that build the ships, munitions, microelectronics, materials, components, and technologies our warfighters rely on. Together, the Department of War and SBA are restoring the industrial dominance that underwrites America’s military advantage and securing peace through strength.”
“When we established the Smaller War Plants Commission, we committed to putting the full weight of the federal government behind the small manufacturers that comprise 70 percent of America’s defense industrial base,” said SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “Together with the Department of War, we are delivering on that promise by supercharging the flow of strategic capital to American defense suppliers to accelerate growth, innovation, and asymmetric advantage for our warfighters. Thanks to President Trump, we are ending the era of foreign dependence and rebuilding the industrial strength that supports the Arsenal of Freedom and keeps America free and strong.”
Last month, the SBA and DoW established the SWPC as a historic, whole-of-government effort to expand the domestic capacity that supports the world’s strongest military. The Commission draws its name from the World War II-era Smaller War Plants Corporation and the Small Defense Plants Administration, SBA predecessor agencies that connected small manufacturers with the financing, contracting tools, and technical support they needed to scale their critical role in building the Arsenal of Freedom.
Building on the SWPC framework, the agreement creates an integrated capital pathway for qualified small businesses that support America’s defense industrial base by aligning the DoW Economic Defense Unit (EDU) with the SBA Office of Investment and Innovation (OII) and Office of Capital Access. EDU will identify firms with financing needs through its Business Operators for National Defense (BOND) efforts and refer potential loan candidates to SBA, which will leverage its existing 7(a) and 504 lender networks to help connect eligible firms with SBA-backed capital.
The agreement also enables SBA to support EDU’s execution of Department of War-funded redeemable preferred-equity investments in small and medium-sized businesses that create, expand, or restore industrial capacity critical to national security—including munitions, platforms, technological processes, essential materials, and the exploration, development, and mining of strategic and critical metals and minerals. SBA will provide due diligence, underwriting, transaction support, and portfolio-management assistance, while EDU retains responsibility and ultimate decision-making authority for its investments.
Through the new MOA, the agencies will:
- Identify defense-critical businesses: Through the Department of War’s Business Operators for National Defense efforts, EDU will identify small businesses engaged in defense-industrial-base activities that need financing and refer prospective loan candidates to SBA.
- Connect firms to SBA-backed capital: SBA will leverage its existing capital networks to support the financing needs of eligible businesses referred by EDU, consistent with applicable program requirements.
- Deploy strategic preferred equity: EDU may originate and source Department of War-funded redeemable preferred-equity investments for businesses that create, expand, or restore industrial capacity critical to national security.
- Apply SBA investment expertise: SBA will support potential equity investments through legally authorized due diligence, underwriting, investment structuring, transaction documentation, monitoring, and management support—helping ensure investments are disciplined, mission-focused, and positioned to strengthen the defense industrial base.
- Drive results and accountability: The agencies will establish joint investment guidance, conduct quarterly portfolio reviews and resource planning, and collaborate on annual reporting on investment performance and exits.
Under President Trump’s leadership, the SBA and DoW are taking concrete action to expand the domestic industrial capacity that strengthens America’s supply chains, equips our warfighters, and sustains the world’s strongest military. Through the Smaller War Plants Commission, qualified small businesses can connect with federal resources designed to help them grow, innovate, and support America’s defense industrial base. To learn more about available resources, visit www.sba.gov/swpc.
# # #

The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of entrepreneurship. PRESS RELEASE

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELERATES VIRGIN ISLANDS-PUERTO RICO FRIENDSHIP DAY

U.S. Virgin Islands—Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett joins our local community in celebrating Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Weekend, culminating today on Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Day. The holiday honors the deep and enduring bonds of family, culture, and shared history between the people of the U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico. Today is also Indigenous Peoples’ Day, a recognition of the first peoples of the Caribbean and the Americas, whose presence and legacy remain woven into the identity of our islands.

“The Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico are bound by far more than the waters between us,” said Congresswoman Plaskett. “From enslaved Africans who escaped the Danish West Indies to find freedom in Puerto Rico, to Puerto Ricans who came to our islands in the early 1900s to cut cane and seek opportunity, to the families who live, work, and worship across our shores today, we share a common thread of resilience, culture, food, faith, and kinship. On this Friendship Day and Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we are reminded that as people of color, telling our own stories is essential. When we tell them with truth and pride, we preserve our history, strengthen our unity, and ensure our children know who they are.”

In observance of Virgin Islands–Puerto Rico Friendship Day, all of Congresswoman Plaskett’s offices in Washington, D.C., St. Croix, and St. Thomas are closed today, Monday, October 12, 2026. The offices will reopen for regular business hours on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. Should you need assistance during those days when the offices are closed, please call 340-778-5900 on St. Croix or 340-774-4408 on St. Thomas, leave a message and someone will respond in short order.

Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 16 Individuals for Election Crimes
Today the Justice Department announced charges involving 16 individuals, including an illegal alien, in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes across the country. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of U.S. citizenship in order to register to vote or to vote, voting on behalf the deceased, voting multiple times in the same election, false statements on citizenship applications, and unlawful procurement of citizenship.
Case details are as follows:
District of New Mexico
Patrick Perea, 62, has been indicted by a federal grand jury on one count of fraudulent voting. Perea attempted to cast his deceased wife’s absentee ballot in the November 2024 general election by submitting it to the Bureau of Elections of the Bernalillo County Clerk’s Office in Albuquerque.
Eastern District of Pennsylvania
An illegal alien and three aliens have been charged with voting by an alien.
- Hacina Saadi, 48, an illegal alien from France, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
- Pakistani national Jamil Ahmad, 50, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
- Pakistani national Nighat Jamil, 47, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
- Portuguese national Paulo Silva, 54, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with voting by an alien during the 2024 election.
Southern District of Alabama
Two aliens have been charged with voting as an alien.
- Peruvian national Silvia Delgado Phelps, 78, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with voting as an alien. Phelps allegedly voted in multiple elections in Baldwin County, Alabama, despite not being a U.S. citizen.
- Jamaican national Staciann Pollion Davis, 42, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with voting as an alien. Davis allegedly voted in the November 2024 general election in Clarke County, Alabama, despite not being a U.S. citizen.
Northern District of Alabama
Forrest Scott Woody, 68, of Hendersonville, North Carolina, has been charged with illegally voting more than once. According to the indictment, Woody voted twice in the 2024 general election. In particular, he voted in Calhoun County, Alabama, after having already voted in the same election in Henderson County, North Carolina.
Western District of Missouri
Cuban national Andre’s Garcia, 64, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with two counts of illegally voting in federal elections in November 2022 and November 2024. Garcia knew he was not a U.S. citizen but nevertheless claimed to be one when registering to vote in 2004 and again in 2013. Garcia has allegedly voted regularly for the last 20 years in at least 15 elections, including at least 13 federal elections.
District of Idaho
Canadian national Stanley Walton, 82, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with unlawfully voting in the 2022 general election. Walton allegedly voted even though he was not a U.S. citizen.
District of New Jersey
Lizabeth Almonte Rosa, 24, a naturalized U.S. citizen from the Dominican Republic, has been charged by criminal complaint with voting by an alien in a federal election and unlawfully procuring citizenship. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court, Rosa was not a citizen when she was registered to vote.
Southern District of Ohio
British national Cary Ann Patterson, 59, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. The complaint alleges that Patterson voted in November 2024. According to court documents, in 2005, the Gallia County Board of Elections received a voter registration card for Patterson in which “Yes” was marked in response to the question, “Are you a U.S. citizen?” Based on Gallia County Board of Elections records, Patterson allegedly voted in at least 10 elections as an alien.
Northern District of Ohio
Two aliens have been charged with unlawfully voting in a federal election.
- Pakistani national Arshed Zuberi, 69, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with illegally voting in a federal election as an alien. He allegedly registered to vote in September 2015 and August 2016. On voter registration forms, Zuberi’s signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Voting records from the Cuyahoga County Board of Elections show that he voted in at least six elections.
- Filipino national Eliza M. Moss, 63, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by criminal complaint with unlawfully voting in a federal election as an alien. According to voting records, Moss registered to vote in September 2004 and in February 2023. On voter registration forms, her signature appears next to the declaration “I declare under penalty of election falsification I am a citizen of the United States.” Moss allegedly voted in several primary and general elections. According to the criminal complaint, Moss told investigators that the person who helped fill out her registration told her that she could vote despite not being a citizen.
District of Hawaii
Polish national Dawid Nalepa, 45, has been charged by information with unlawfully voting as an alien. Nepela came to the United States in or around 2020 through the Visa Waiver Program, which he overstayed before applying for permanent resident status. Nalepa was not a U.S. citizen when he allegedly cast a vote in the November 2024, general election. Nalepa understood he was not a citizen at the time he cast his ballot.
Western District of Kentucky
Canadian national Sandra Madeline Watson, 59, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged with illegal voting by an alien in a federal election. Watson allegedly voted in an election held for the purpose of electing a candidate for the office of the President, Vice President, member of the Senate, or member of the House of Representatives, knowing she was not a U.S. citizen.
A complaint, indictment, and information merely contain accusations. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 16 Individuals for Election Crimes

Following President Trump’s Executive Order, USDA Urges States to Review Wolf Management Policies and Strengthen Engagement with Ranchers
(Washington, D.C., October 12, 2026) – Today, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins urged state partners to review their wolf management policies, strengthen engagement with livestock producers, and work with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to address wolf predation. This outreach follows President Trump’s Executive Order 14425, titled “Supporting America’s Ranchers,” and builds on the Trump Administration’s commitment to give producers the tools they need to protect their herds and livelihoods.
“For too long, America’s ranchers have dealt with wolves threatening and killing their livestock, their livelihoods, and the family operations they have spent generations building,” said Secretary Brooke L. Rollins, “As ranchers await federal clarity on this issue, I am urging states to listen to their producers, review state-specific wolf protections, and work with USDA wherever possible to protect livestock, including through lethal removal when requested by the appropriate authorities and authorized by law. The most pro-rancher Administration in history will continue standing with our ranchers and working to rebuild the Great American Cattle Herd.
“American ranchers have been forced to deal with apex predators devastating livestock for far too long despite these protected species exceeding recovery goals long ago,” said Representative Hageman. “Those who work around the clock to keep our shelves stocked and neighbors fed deserve to be fairly compensated for losses from D.C.-protected predators like the grey and Mexican wolf. I am pleased to see President Trump and Secretary Rollins taking steps to relieve our ranchers of unnecessary predators on their lands and deliver due compensation when losses happen.”
USDA is encouraging states to engage directly with ranchers and raise awareness of how to report suspected predation to the appropriate state agencies or the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS). USDA’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) Wildlife Services provides wolf damage management assistance at the request of the appropriate state agencies or the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS). Requests for lethal removal must come from those authorities and be supported by the requisite agreements, environmental analyses, and compliance with state and federal law. APHIS currently supports state and federal partners through more than 40 agreements.
Wolf predation can increase producers’ costs through livestock losses, management expenses, and reduced livestock weights. Under the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, USDA’s Farm Service Agency increased Livestock Indemnity Program (LIP) payment rates for qualifying predation losses to 100% of the determined market value. Eligible producers who lose livestock to qualifying wolf attacks should contact their local Farm Service Agency office for eligibility and application information.
For more information, please visit: https://www.usda.gov/form/ranchers-first

RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts AAPI Roundtable in Palisades Park
Highlights Work to Lower Costs, Protect Communities, Support Small Businesses and Discuss Challenges in the AAPI Community
Above: Gottheimer hosts AAPI Roundtable.
PALISADES PARK, NJ —Tuesday, October 6, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a roundtable with Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) leaders and community members from across North Jersey at the Palisades Park Library to discuss the challenges facing the AAPI community and what Washington can do to help. Joined by local elected officials, community organizations, educators, health care advocates, small business owners, and cultural and ethnic associations, Gottheimer outlined his work on health care, affordability, small business, anti-Asian hate, public safety, immigration, and education, and heard directly from participants about what their neighbors need most.
“The AAPI community represents different ethnicities, languages, faiths, and traditions, but the same drive to strengthen our communities. That’s why I’m working so hard in Washington and across the aisle to support you. But celebrating this community isn’t enough,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).
Across the Fifth District, roughly 127,000 residents are Asian American, or about one in six. This includes nearly half of Englewood Cliffs and more than forty-three percent of Fort Lee. Palisades Park, which has the highest percentage and density of Korean residents of any town in the country, is located within the District.
Gottheimer, a member of the Korea, India, Taiwan, Asia Pacific American, and Pacific Islands Caucuses and Co-Chair of the American Sikh Congressional Caucus, discussed the following priorities and his relevant legislation with attendees:
- Mental Health Emergency Care: Gottheimer secured $2 million to expand the behavioral health emergency department at New Bridge Medical Center in Paramus, growing it from 19 to 49 beds, with 30 beds dedicated to mental health and substance abuse treatment and 50 new clinical jobs. He is also part of the bipartisan push to extend and reform the ACA enhanced premium tax credits.
- Affordability: As Co-Chair of the bipartisan SALT Caucus, he is pushing the SALT Deductibility Act to fully restore the SALT deduction. His Tariff Impact Act would require the Congressional Budget Office to review the economic impact of any new tariff before they take effect.
- Medicaid and CHIP: New restrictions on lawfully present immigrants, part of the OBBB law that he voted against, recently took effect. Roughly 300,000 New Jersey residents could lose Medicaid or fail to get it, mostly because of paperwork.
- Small Business: Under a policy that took effect March 1, 2026, the SBA no longer backs loans to businesses with any non-citizen ownership. Even a green card holder with a 1 percent stake disqualifies a business. In FY2024 alone, the agency backed 8,900 loans worth $7.2 billion to Asian-owned businesses.
- Anti-Sikh Hate: Gottheimer introduced the Sikh American Anti-Discrimination Act with Congressman David Valadao (R-CA) in January 2026. It would create a DOJ Task Force on Anti-Sikh Discrimination, set a federal definition of anti-Sikh hate, develop education programs, and report annually to Congress. New Jersey is home to roughly 100,000 Sikhs.
- Public Safety: Gottheimer announced $42 million in FEMA funding in July 2026, split between $21 million statewide and $21 million for Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties. It covers radios, drones, K-9 units, and security upgrades for houses of worship such as cameras, alarms, guards, and reinforced doors. His bipartisan Invest to Protect Act would authorize $50 million a year for five years to help police departments with fewer than 200 officers with recruitment, training, mental health resources, and body cameras. He invited houses of worship that have not applied for Nonprofit Security Grants to call his office.
- Immigration: More than 1.2 million people are stuck in the employment-based green card backlog, nearly eighty percent from India, with a projected 179-year wait for an Indian EB-2 applicant. He voted to eliminate the per-country caps on employment-based green cards and says the country can secure the border and enforce its laws while treating people fairly.
- ICE Oversight: Gottheimer introduced the ICE Standards Act in January 2026, after the Minneapolis shootings. It would require stronger training, body and dash cameras, clear uniforms and ID, efforts to verify citizenship before detention, and limits on enforcement at schools, hospitals, and houses of worship. He also visited Delaney Hall and worked to secure the release of a 17-year-old girl, Ariadna, in time for her high school graduation.
- Education: Gottheimer discussed the administration’s freeze of $23 million in English learner funding for New Jersey and cancellation of nearly $1 billion in school mental health grants. He supports doubling the Pell Grant and pointed to the roughly $5 billion the American Rescue Plan he helped write, negotiate, and pass in 2021, and delivered to Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institutions. He also introduced a resolution recognizing AANAPISI Week.
Gottheimer was joined by Assemblywoman Ellen Park, Chair of AAPI Caucus, Assemblywoman Shama Haider, Assemblyman Al Barlas, Mayor of Palisades Park Chong Paul Kim, Mayor of Harrington Park Joon Chung,Yogi Virk, President of the Sikh Chamber of Commerce, Daniel Song, Palisades Park County Committee Member, Closter Councilman Christopher Cho, Palisades Park Councilman Charlie Changkyun Shin, Mahwah Councilwoman Michelle Crowe Paz, Englewood Cliffs Councilman Philip Zhi Liang, River Edge Councilwoman Priti Dhariwal, Sara Kim, Senior Director of Public Health and Research Center at Korean Community Services NY & NJ, Teresa Baik, Director of Education of Korean Community Services NY & NJ, Farhat Khan, President of the Cultural Society of Bergen County, Palisades Park Councilman Christopher Kwak, Eun Ju Hong, President of the Korean American Association of Fort Lee, Tom Choi, Vice President of the Korean American Association of Fort Lee, Jae-eun Ahn, Vice President of the Korean American Association of Fort Lee, Christina Kim, with the Fort Lee Fire Prevention, Serena Pak, Director of the Youth Council of Fort Lee, Hyunjung Kim, Advisor of ComposTogether at the Youth Council of Fort Lee, Harrington Park, Ludi Hughes, Chairwoman of Asian American Heritage Council of NJ and Chairwoman/Founder of the Filipino American Festival, Inc, Amber Reed, Co-Executive of AAPI of New Jersey, John Sohn, President of the Korean American Nail Assocation of NJ, Ellen Jeon, Executive Director and Advisor of the Asian American Youth Council, Anne Y. Kim Cha, President of the Korean American Senior Citizens Association of NJ, Donald Yu, Vice President of the Korean American Senior Citizens Association of NJ, Ella Chorong Lee, Library Director of the Palisades Park Public Library.

Congressman Don Davis Joins Congressional Ferry Caucus to Advocate for Eastern North Carolina’s Coastal Communities
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) announced he has joined the Congressional Ferry Caucus. As a member of the caucus, he will join 17 of his colleagues to focus on federal investment in our nation's ferry system.
"Ferries in eastern North Carolina's coastal communities are essential. They connect kids to school, residents to doctor visits, and workers to their jobs," said Congressman Don Davis. "As a new member of the bipartisan Congressional Ferry Caucus, my focus is to advocate for more federal investment in the ferry system so that coastal communities can remain connected."
The State of Washington operates the largest ferry system in the nation, and North Carolina's ferry system follows as the second-largest.
There are a total of seven scheduled ferry routes that link eastern North Carolina communities. Ferries provide access to basic needs and necessities, support the local economy through tourism and trade, and are still a significant part of their daily lives. Ferry transportation is vital to our residents and businesses along the coast.
Representatives Emily Randall (WA-06), Nick Begich (AK-AL), John Garamendi (CA-08), and Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) are the founding members of the caucus, which was created in June 2025 to raise awareness in Washington, D.C., of our nation's ferry system among Congressional members and their staff.
title: Congressman Don Davis Joins Congressional Ferry Caucus to Advocate for Eastern North Carolina’s Coastal Communities

Rep. Salinas and Tualatin Celebrate New Hydropower System Turning Drinking Water Into Clean Energy
First-of-its-kind hydropower project helps the city cut emissions, lower energy costs and advance climate goals
Tualatin, OR — The City of Tualatin is celebrating the completion of a first-of-its-kind hydropower project that allows the city’s drinking water to create clean, renewable energy. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) joined city leaders, representatives from Oregon’s Department of Energy and project partners, including Energy Trust of Oregon and Portland General Electric (PGE), to mark the completion of the 56-kilowatt in-pipe hydropower system at the Tualatin City Services facility. The project is expected to generate more than 270,000 kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity each year — enough to fully power the City Services facility and save the city an estimated $26,000 each year.
“Building a more affordable future demands innovative ideas. That’s exactly what Tualatin is doing with their new in-pipe hydropower project,” said Rep. Salinas. “Adding clean energy like hydropower to our water systems and solar to our homes and buildings can help bring down energy costs and combat the affordability crisis. Projects like this show how communities can create clean energy by making the most of the infrastructure we already rely on. Strong local partnerships and federal support can help make more of these projects possible.”
Along with the system, the city also installed additional infrastructure that will eventually help keep operations running during major outages or emergencies. In the future, the city plans to add a microgrid and large battery capable of powering critical municipal buildings on its own.
“Building a more resilient Tualatin is central to our climate action plan,” said Frank Bubenik, mayor of Tualatin. “This project shows how we can use innovative infrastructure to strengthen reliability and lay the groundwork for future backup power. It’s the kind of smart investment that can improve reliability, reduce energy costs and help protect our community for the long term.”
The system is installed where drinking water from Bull Run Reservoir enters Tualatin’s water distribution system. Developed by Oregon-based InPipe Energy, the system captures unused pressure to generate 24/7 carbon-free electricity without interrupting water delivery.
Energy Trust of Oregon, a nonprofit funded by customers of investor-owned utilities’ that helps communities, organizations, and families connect to clean, renewable energy provided more than $270,000 in cash incentives for the project and supported the project’s design.
Across Oregon, Energy Trust is working with cities, water districts and rural communities to turn critical municipal infrastructure into new sources of reliable, local clean energy. Renewable energy projects — whether hydropower, solar or battery-supported systems — help communities cut energy costs and strengthen resilience in the face of climate-related challenges.
“When cities are willing to explore innovative ideas, they can unlock far more value from the infrastructure than they already have,” said Tracy Scott, director of energy programs with Energy Trust of Oregon. “This project will generate renewable power while helping Tualatin reduce its energy costs year after year, leaving more resources available for other community priorities. That’s the kind of practical, lasting value we’re looking to help communities achieve.” This project was also partially funded by PGE’s Green Future Renewable Development Fund, which is made possible by PGE Green Future customers who support impactful small-scale local renewable energy projects.
“It’s the incredible support of PGE customers who are helping bring local clean energy projects like this one in Tualatin to life,” said PGE local government affairs senior manager, Meredith Armstrong. “Through our Green Future program, PGE customers are choosing to support impactful renewable energy projects for healthier and more energy resilient communities.”
These funds were combined with a grant from the Oregon Department of Energy and an anticipated federal investment tax credit. Altogether, grants, incentives and anticipated tax credits covered more than 85% of the project’s $920,000 total cost.
The environmental benefits of this project extend beyond energy generation. The area surrounding the turbine was replanted and landscaped to meet Backyard Habitat Certification Program standards, using native, wildlife-friendly plants to create habitat for pollinators and wildlife. The Backyard Habitat Certification Program is a collaboration between Columbia Land Trust and Bird Alliance of Oregon.
As the City continues implementing its Climate Action Plan, Tualatin’s project demonstrates how communities can use existing infrastructure to generate clean energy, reduce costs and advance climate goals. It’s an example of how local innovation and strong partnerships can create lasting benefits for the community.
###
title: Rep. Salinas and Tualatin Celebrate New Hydropower System Turning Drinking Water Into Clean Energy

VICTORY ON THE HUDSON: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND LOCAL ADVOCATES CELEBRATE SUCCESS OF RYAN’S LAW THAT PERMANENTLY BANS BARGES ON THE HUDSON RIVER
VICTORY ON THE HUDSON: Congressman Pat Ryan and Local Advocates Celebrate Success of Ryan’s Law that Permanently Bans Barges on the Hudson River
After years of relentless advocacy by Congressman Ryan, bipartisan lawmakers, and local advocates, the “Hudson River Protection Act” – which permanently bans harmful, polluting barges from docking in the Hudson River – is now law
Ryan joined local advocates, including representatives from Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson, to celebrate the community victory years in the making; Ryan first introduced the bill in 2023 following attempts to allow dangerous barges to anchor in the Hudson, contaminating drinking water for Hudson Valley residents and destroying the environment
POUGHKEEPSIE, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan joined local experts and advocates to celebrate the success of his Hudson River Protection Act. After years of relentless advocacy by Congressman Ryan, bipartisan elected officials at the local, state, and federal levels, and community experts and advocates, Ryan’s bill permanently banning harmful, polluting barges from docking in the Hudson is now law.
Ryan first introduced the Hudson River Protection Act in 2023, following attempts to erode protections preventing harmful, polluting barges from using the Hudson River as a parking lot – threatening to contaminate drinking water for more than 100,000 Hudson Valley residents and destroy the environment. He has been fighting for years, alongside the Hudson Valley community – with the invaluable partnership of organizations including Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson – to advance this legislation.
“If there’s one thing we can all agree on it’s making sure our drinking water is clean and that our Hudson River is safe and protected. For far too long, big corporations have polluted and put at risk our precious River in pursuit of profits. But not anymore. The Hudson is more than a river – it’s the lifeblood and the heartbeat of our community,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Today we celebrated the years of effort by every single member of our Hudson Valley community. I especially want to thank my partners at Riverkeeper and Scenic Hudson for their tireless work and commitment to protecting the Hudson. Never again will big corporations be able to turn our River into a parking lot for dangerous barges, polluting the drinking water for 100,000 of our neighbors. This victory proves that when the Hudson Valley stands up with one voice to demand change, we can accomplish anything.”
“As the Coast Guard reviews comments and finalizes its rulemaking barring new anchorages along the Hudson River, we look back to celebrate the Hudson River Protection Act as a powerful testament to what we can accomplish when communities come together to defend the river they depend on,” said Riverkeeper Associate Director of Government Affairs Jeremy Cherson. “For nearly a decade, Riverkeeper and thousands of New Yorkers have fought to ensure that the Hudson is protected from the risks posed by new commercial vessel anchorages. This law honors that persistence by safeguarding critical habitat, protecting drinking water for more than 100,000 people, and making clear that the Hudson is not a place for industrial exploitation. We’re grateful to Congressman Pat Ryan, our partners, and the countless Hudson Valley residents who raised their voices and refused to let the river’s future be put at risk.”
“The Hudson 7 is an intermunicipal council representing seven Mid-Hudson municipalities that rely on the Hudson River as a drinking water source. More than 107,000 people in Dutchess and Ulster Counties depend on the river for their drinking water, with five treatment plants drawing directly from the Hudson to serve communities including Rhinebeck, Esopus, Lloyd, Hyde Park, and Poughkeepsie,” said Gary Bassett, Mayor of the Village of Rhinebeck and Chair of the Hudson 7. “The river doesn’t follow municipal boundaries. A spill doesn’t stop at a town line, and a flood doesn’t stop at a county line. Protecting this shared resource requires regional cooperation and strong federal leadership. Today, we thank Congressman Ryan for his sustained leadership in advancing the Hudson River Protection Act.”
“Residents of Ulster County have a deep and abiding appreciation for the Hudson River. County Executive Metzger recognizes and supports the more than 9,000 county residents who draw their drinking water from the Hudson River, and the thousands more who enjoy fishing, boating, picnicking, and hiking along the waterfront. On behalf of the Department of Environment, we express our appreciation to Congressman Ryan and the advocacy groups who worked tirelessly to secure passage of this legislation,” said Andy Bicking, Director of Ulster County’s Department of Environment.
“Without the Hudson River Protection Act, our river was at risk of becoming a busy highway and parking lot for marine vessels carrying crude oil or other dangerous cargo. Scenic Hudson is proud to have partnered with Congressman Ryan to finally put an end to this threat. The Hudson River Protection Act, introduced and championed by the Congressman, will permanently prevent efforts to add new upper Hudson River anchorages, protecting the ecological health of the river and the health of those who rely on it for drinking water and recreation. Scenic Hudson will continue to partner with our friends in the Hudson Valley, Albany, and Washington to vigilantly protect this critical waterway,” said Carli Fraccarolli, Scenic Hudson's Government Relations Manager.
Congressman Ryan’s “Hudson River Protection Act” bans additional barge anchorages in the Hudson, which pollute the drinking water for more than 100,000 Hudson Valley residents and damage the Hudson’s diverse ecosystem.
In 2023, when the Coast Guard issued an Marine Safety Information Bulletin (MSIB) signaling an attempt to erode protections preventing commercial vessels from anchoring in the Hudson River, Ryan immediately raised the alarm, warning of devastating environmental and health impacts for the river ecosystem and broader community.
After a more than two month delay, Michael Emerson, the Director of Marine Transportation Systems, provided a woefully insufficient response that left the door open for dangerous oil barges to line the Hudson.
In October of 2023, Ryan was joined by Riverkeeper, Scenic Hudson and the Hudson 7 in demanding the Coast Guard uphold the anchoring ban. Ryan gave a speech on the House Floor, calling on Hudson Valley families to join the fight and shared a form for those interested to register their opinion. The new MSIB, issued in November 2023 in response to overwhelming community outrage, temporarily paused the Coast Guard’s plan to allow dangerous barges to line the Hudson River but doubled down on their plan to allow unlimited anchoring in the future.
Congressman Ryan’s greatest concern has been that the Hudson River serves as the primary water supply for seven communities in his district, and serves as the backup drinking water supply for our nation’s largest city, New York City. Additionally, more oil barges on the Hudson will increase the risks of a catastrophic spill. This is especially concerning for the more than 100,000 people that draw their drinking water from the Hudson River.
Barges often carry oil, asphalt, and other hazardous materials, which pollute the river with their noisy generators and “stadium” lighting. The Hudson River and its connected waters are also home to more than 200 species of fish and provide spawning and nursery habitat for striped bass, shad, and herring that support fisheries up and down the entire Atlantic coast. The River has seen significant efforts to restore the habitats of endangered fish species which are jeopardized by barge anchors dragging along the River bottom.
President Trump signed the “Hudson River Protection Act” into law as part of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), wherein Congressman Ryan secured numerous other wins including a pay raise for troops.
###
title: VICTORY ON THE HUDSON: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND LOCAL ADVOCATES CELEBRATE SUCCESS OF RYAN’S LAW THAT PERMANENTLY BANS BARGES ON THE HUDSON RIVER

Homeland Security Task Force Arrests Alvaro Pulido Vargas to Face Charges in Multibillion-Dollar Venezuelan Money Laundering and Bribery Schemes
Note: A copy of the 2021 indictment can be found here and a copy of the 2019 indictment can be found here.
A Colombian national charged in two separate federal indictments involving the alleged laundering of more than $2 billion in connection with Venezuelan government bribery schemes will make his initial appearance on the afternoon of Tuesday, October 13, in the Southern District of Florida to face federal prosecution.
According to court documents, Alvaro Pulido Vargas, also known as “German Enrique Rubio Salas,” 62, of Colombia, was indicted in 2019 and again in 2021 for his alleged involvement in separate schemes to launder proceeds of bribery and fraud involving Venezuelan government officials of the Nicolás Maduro regime. Prior to these alleged offenses, Pulido Vargas had a prolific history of drug trafficking, including a 1997 conviction in Italy under the alias of German Enrique Rubio Salas.
“Alvaro Pulido Vargas is no longer a fugitive from justice,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Pulido is charged in two separate, significant money laundering schemes, both using the U.S. financial system to hide the profits from his bribery and greed off the backs of the Venezuelan people. The message to anyone who brings their foreign bribery or money laundering schemes inside our borders: the U.S. Justice Department will pursue these schemes and prosecute those who perpetrate them.”
“Alvaro Pulido Vargas was charged years ago with participating in massive money laundering and bribery schemes tied to the Maduro regime,” said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones for the Southern District of Florida. “The allegations describe a profound betrayal of the Venezuelan people; corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine, and housing for personal enrichment. Today, because of the persistence and coordination of our federal law enforcement and international partners, Pulido Vargas is in the Southern District of Florida to face those charges. Those accused of exploiting the American financial system should understand that distance, borders, and time will not shield them from the reach of the American legal system. We will continue working with our partners at home and abroad to bring defendants before an American court to answer for the charges against them.”
“Alvaro Pulido Vargas is accused of moving vast amounts of illicit money through a corrupt network that exploited the Venezuelan people and abused the U.S. financial system,” said said Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Administrator Terrance Cole. “For years, DEA and our HSTF partners have pursued Pulido Vargas across borders. Today, that pursuit has brought him to the Southern District of Florida. Those who finance criminal networks and believe money, influence, or international borders will shield them from U.S. justice are mistaken. DEA will relentlessly pursue the people and financial networks that fuel corruption, money laundering, and transnational crime threatening the United States and our partners.”
“Today’s arrest demonstrates that HSI and our Homeland Security Task Force partners will relentlessly pursue the illicit financial networks that enable corruption, transnational criminal activity, and the exploitation of vulnerable populations,” said Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. “Working with our domestic and international law enforcement partners, HSI will continue to follow the money, disrupt complex money-laundering schemes, and hold accountable those who allegedly use the U.S. financial system to conceal criminal proceeds.”
The 2021 Indictment
In October 2021, a federal grand jury returned an indictment charging Pulido Vargas and four co-defendants with laundering proceeds from an alleged bribery scheme involving approximately $1.6 billion in Venezuelan government contracts to provide food and medicine.
According to the Indictment, from approximately July 2015 through at least 2020, Pulido Vargas and his co-conspirators secured lucrative government contracts through the Comité Local de Abastecimiento y Producción (CLAP)—a Venezuelan government-controlled program intended to provide food and medicine to the Venezuelan people—by paying bribes to Venezuelan officials.
The defendants allegedly inflated the costs of the contracts to fund the bribes and enrich themselves. They also allegedly laundered proceeds through bank accounts in Antigua, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and elsewhere.
As a result of the scheme, Pulido Vargas and his co-conspirators allegedly received approximately $1.6 billion from the Venezuelan government and transferred approximately $180 million through or to the United States, including bank accounts in the Southern District of Florida.
Pulido Vargas is charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering and four counts of money laundering, each carrying a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison.
The 2019 Indictment
In a separate case, Pulido Vargas and Alex Nain Saab Moran — a Maduro regime ally — were indicted in July 2019 for allegedly laundering approximately $350 million in connection with a bribery scheme involving Venezuela’s government-controlled currency exchange system.
According to the Indictment, from approximately November 2011 and through at least September 2015, Pulido Vargas and Saab Moran conspired with others to launder proceeds of an illegal bribery scheme through bank accounts in the United States.
Pulido Vargas and Saab Moran allegedly obtained a contract with the Venezuelan government to construct low-income housing units. They subsequently exploited Venezuela’s government-controlled exchange rate by submitting false and fraudulent import documents for goods and materials that were never imported into Venezuela and bribing Venezuelan government officials to approve those documents.
To conceal the illicit proceeds, Pulido Vargas and Saab Moran allegedly wired money related to the scheme to bank accounts in the Southern District of Florida and transferred approximately $350 million out of Venezuela through the United States and into overseas accounts they owned or controlled.
Pulido Vargas is charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering and seven counts of money laundering in connection with this scheme.
The DEA Miami Field Division, FBI Miami, and HSI Miami are investigating these cases.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Monique Botero for the Southern District of Florida and Deputy Chief Joseph Palazzo of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section are prosecuting the cases, together with Assistant Chief Katherine Raut of the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section.
This arrest and prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Miami comprises of agents and officers from the DEA Miami Field Division, FBI Miami, and HSI Miami with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Miami.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Homeland Security Task Force Arrests Alvaro Pulido Vargas to Face Charges in Multibillion-Dollar Venezuelan Money Laundering and Bribery Schemes

Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, called on the Department of State Office of the Inspector General (OIG) to launch an immediate investigation into U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle’s reported dealings with a foreign company and a political donor. In a separate letter, Meeks requested that Guilfoyle appear before committee Members to answer questions under oath.
The investigation request follows Wall Street Journal reports that Guilfoyle gave a foreign company’s lobbyist access to official meetings, promoted the company’s commercial interests, and accepted company-sponsored private air travel. The Journal also reported that, while her nomination was pending, Guilfoyle requested $100,000 from political donor Eric Deters to cover personal debt while seeking intervention by senior Trump administration officials in his tax and legal matters.   
“The reported messages between Ambassador Guilfoyle and Mr. Deters demonstrate that the Ambassador sought to conceal the source of the payment by arranging an anonymous wire transfer and that she repeatedly admonished Mr. Deters not to put any details of their financial arrangement in writing,” said Ranking Member Meeks. “While Mr. Deters claims he ultimately did not transfer the requested $100,000, it must be determined whether Ambassador Guilfoyle solicited funds from any other source.” 
Meeks asked OIG to investigate potential violations of federal law, Department regulations, and ethics requirements, including conflicts of interest and abuse of authority.
“Together, these reports paint a disturbing picture of an ambassador using her official position and access to senior political appointees to advance the private interests of those willing to pay,” said Ranking Member Meeks. 
These letters follow Ranking Member Meeks' October 1 request for answers from Secretary of State Marco Rubio about Amb. Guilfoyle’s reported conduct. Ranking Member Meeks has called for her removal should these allegations be substantiated. 
View the letter to State OIG here and the letter to Amb. Guilfoyle here.

text:
Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

October 10, 2026

The Trump Administration has mobilized an immediate response to the 7.7 magnitude earthquake that struck Panama on October 9. The State Department deployed Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) technical teams to conduct expert structural assessments of damage and potential immediate assistance needs at the request of the Panamanian government. Department of War teams are assisting with the response through the U.S.-Panama Bilateral Security Cooperation Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). Ambassador Kevin Cabrera and the State Department continue to liaise with President José Raúl Mulino and the Panamanian government as they assess the damage.

Disaster Assistance Response Team and Search and Rescue Experts Mobilized

The State Department mobilized a Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) to coordinate and support the emergency response, including two USAR technical teams, with 20 people total, bringing a range of assessment, search, and rescue expertise. These USAR team members arrived in Panama within 24 hours of the earthquake. The USAR technical teams will conduct aerial and on-the-ground assessments and provide additional technical assistance in coordination with local authorities. The Department also authorized Panama’s Air and Naval Service to use two INL-supported helicopters for earthquake relief.

Humanitarian Assistance

The Department has committed to provide $5 million in assistance to support trusted on the ground implementers conducting relief efforts.

SOUTHCOM Logistical Support

Demonstrating the value of ongoing security cooperation efforts between Panama and the United States, the Department of War is supporting aerial damage assessments in the Azuero peninsula and Cocle, including joint assessments with the DART, Embassy staff, and Panamanian officials. The State Department is coordinating with SOUTHCOM to determine if additional logistical support will be required.

Supporting Americans in Panama

The Trump Administration has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans. The Department of State is providing consular assistance to U.S. citizens in the affected area and their families. We are not aware of any American casualties at this time. Our Consular Affairs hotline is available 24/7 for affected Americans in need of support at +1-202-501-4444 from abroad and +1-888-407-4747 from the U.S. and Canada. We strongly encourage Americans in the affected areas to monitor local news, follow the emergency instructions provided by local authorities, and enroll in STEP.state.gov to receive important emergency information.

title: The United States Mobilizes Immediate Response to the Panama Earthquakes

Comisionado Residente y congresistas presentan legislación para fortalecer el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández (D-PR) junto a los congresistas Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA), Darren Soto (D-FL) y Gus Bilirakis (R-FL) presentaron el Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 10747), legislación bipartita que busca corregir una disparidad histórica en el financiamiento de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico, cambiando la fórmula federal para calcular los pagos y aplicando el mismo ajuste por costos geográficos que se utiliza para las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses.
“Estamos priorizando lo básico: que nuestros adultos mayores tengan acceso a los médicos y servicios de salud que necesitan. Este año logramos un aumento importante en los fondos de Medicare Advantage para Puerto Rico. Ahora queremos dar el próximo paso y corregir de una vez y por todas la disparidad que por años ha afectado a la Isla”, dijo el Comisionado Residente Hernández.
“Como medico de emergencias, sé que cuando la atención está fuera de alcance, los adultos mayores pagan el precio”, dijo el Congresista Raúl Ruiz, M.D. “Los puertorriqueños pagan Medicare en los mismos términos que todos los estadounidenses, y sin embargo, a sus planes Medicare Advantage se les paga cerca de un 40 por ciento menos. Esa brecha ha reducido las redes de proveedores, recortado beneficios y puesto bajo presión a médicos y hospitales. Este proyecto de ley es una solución específica y de sentido común. Agradezco a los representantes Bilirakis y Soto, y a al Comisionado Residente Hernández, por trabajar conmigo para brindar a los adultos mayores la cobertura justa que se han Ganado.”
“Estoy orgulloso de unirme al comisionado residente de Puerto Rico Hernández y a los representantes Bilirakis y Ruiz para presentar la Ley bipartidista de Equidad en Medicare Advantage para Puerto Rico, con el fin de realizar ajustes geográficos a los niveles de referencia de Medicare Advantage en la isla e igualarlos a los de las Islas Vírgenes de los Estados Unidos. Esto nos acerca a lograr la plena paridad entre la isla y el territorio continental. Los puertorriqueños son ciudadanos estadounidenses y merecen el mismo acceso a los beneficios de atención médica que todos los estadounidenses”. dijo el Congresista Darren Soto.
“Los adultos mayores merecen acceso confiable a los servicios de salud de calidad que se han ganado a través de Medicare, sin importar dónde vivan”, expresó el congresista Gus Bilirakis. “Medicare Advantage desempeña un papel importante en la atención médica de los beneficiarios en todo Puerto Rico. Debemos garantizar que el programa reciba un financiamiento justo y sostenible para que nuestros adultos mayores puedan seguir recibiendo atención de sus médicos y contando con los tratamientos y beneficios que necesitan. Me enorgullece unirme a los congresistas Ruiz, Soto y Hernández para presentar el proyecto de ley bipartidista Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act, que busca corregir las desigualdades que han persistido por años, mejorar el acceso a los servicios de salud y brindar mayor estabilidad a los pacientes y a los proveedores de atención médica.”
“Esta legislación representa un paso importante para atender un problema estructural que por años ha afectado los pagos de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico. Con aproximadamente el 96% de los beneficiarios de Medicare en la Isla acogidos a Medicare Advantage, la metodología utilizada para establecer las tarifas de referencia para Puerto Rico debe reflejar la realidad del mercado al que sirve. Agradecemos al congresista Ruiz, a los representantes Bilirakis y Soto, y al comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández Rivera por unirse en una solución bipartita que utilizaría a las Islas Vírgenes de Estados Unidos como referencia geográfica comparable y ayudaría a fortalecer el acceso a servicios de salud para cientos de miles de beneficiarios en Puerto Rico. MMAPA respalda firmemente esta iniciativa y espera continuar colaborando con el Congreso y los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS) para promover un programa de Medicare Advantage más estable y sostenible para Puerto Rico”, expresó Solage De Lahongrais, presidenta de la Asociación de Productos de Medicaid y Medicare Advantage de Puerto Rico (MMAPA).
Más de 650,000 puertorriqueños dependen de Medicare Advantage para recibir sus servicios de salud, lo que convierte al programa en una pieza fundamental del sistema de salud de Puerto Rico. Sin embargo, la fórmula federal que determina cuánto dinero reciben los planes médicos se basa, en parte, en los gastos de los pacientes de Medicare tradicional, que representan una pequeña minoría en la Isla. Esto provoca que los pagos se calculen utilizando información que no refleja adecuadamente los costos de ofrecer servicios médicos en Puerto Rico, lo que ha contribuido a una disparidad en el financiamiento del programa durante años.
El Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act busca corregir de manera permanente esta disparidad. A partir de 2027, el proyecto requeriría que Medicare utilice para Puerto Rico el mismo ajuste por costos geográficos que aplica a las Islas Vírgenes estadounidenses al calcular los pagos a los planes Medicare Advantage. Este cambio busca que los fondos federales respondan mejor a los costos de ofrecer servicios de salud en la Isla.
La medida permitiría establecer una fórmula de financiamiento más justa y estable, reducir la dependencia de ajustes administrativos que se revisan año tras año y dar mayor certeza a los pacientes, médicos, hospitales y demás proveedores de salud que dependen del programa.
La legislación se presenta en un momento importante para los beneficiarios de Medicare Advantage en Puerto Rico. A pocos días de comenzar el periodo anual de inscripción abierta de Medicare, cientos de miles de adultos mayores se preparan para evaluar sus opciones de cubierta médica para el próximo año. El proyecto representa un nuevo paso en las gestiones que ha impulsado el comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández desde el Congreso para corregir las desigualdades en el financiamiento del programa.
A principios de este año, cuando los Centros de Servicios de Medicare y Medicaid (CMS, por sus siglas en inglés) propusieron un aumento nacional de apenas 0.09% en los pagos de Medicare Advantage para 2027, el Comisionado Residente encabezó una carta bipartita firmada por 17 congresistas, incluidos Raul Ruiz y Darren Soto, para reclamar un trato más justo para Puerto Rico. Tras estas gestiones y los esfuerzos del sector de salud de la Isla, CMS anunció un aumento de aproximadamente 4% para Puerto Rico, superior al promedio nacional de alrededor de 2.5%.

Hernández, Ruiz, Soto, and Bilirakis Introduce Bill to Strengthen Medicare Advantage Funding in Puerto Rico
WASHINGTON, DC — Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR), alongside Representatives Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-CA), Darren Soto (D-FL), and Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), introduced the Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act of 2026 (H.R. 10747), bipartisan legislation that would fix a longstanding Medicare Advantage funding disparity by changing how Washington calculates payments to Puerto Rico, using the same standard applied to the U.S. Virgin Islands.
“We are prioritizing the basics: ensuring that our seniors have access to the doctors and healthcare services they need. This year, we secured a significant increase in Medicare Advantage funding for Puerto Rico. Now, we are taking the next step to fix a longstanding funding disparity that has affected the Island for years,” said Resident Commissioner Hernández.
"As an emergency physician, I know that when care is out of reach, seniors pay the price," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. "Puerto Ricans pay into Medicare on the same terms as every American, yet their Medicare Advantage plans are paid about 40 percent less. That gap has shrunk provider networks, cut benefits, and strained doctors and hospitals. This bill is a targeted, common-sense fix. I thank Representatives Bilirakis and Soto and Resident Commissioner Hernández for working with me to give seniors the fair coverage they have earned.”
"Seniors deserve reliable access to the high-quality health care they have earned through Medicare, regardless of where they live," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "Medicare Advantage plays an important role in delivering care to beneficiaries across Puerto Rico, and we must ensure the program is funded fairly and sustainably so seniors can continue accessing the doctors, treatments, and benefits they rely upon. I'm proud to join Representatives Ruiz, Soto, and Hernández in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to address longstanding disparities, strengthen access to care and provide greater stability for patients and providers.”
“I am proud to join Puerto Rico Resident Commissioner Hernández and Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz in introducing the bipartisan Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act to make geographic adjustments to Medicare Advantage benchmarks in Puerto Rico to match those of the U.S. Virgin Islands. This takes us closer to achieving full parity between the Island and the mainland. Puerto Ricans are American citizens, and they deserve access to the same healthcare benefits as all Americans.” said Congressman Darren Soto.
“This legislation represents an important step toward addressing a longstanding structural challenge in Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico. With approximately 96% ofMedicare beneficiaries on the Island choosing Medicare Advantage, the methodology used to establish Puerto Rico’s benchmarks must reflect the reality of the market it serves. We thank Congressman Ruiz, Representatives Bilirakis and Soto, and Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández Rivera for coming together on a bipartisan solution that would use the U.S. Virgin Islands as a comparable geographic reference and help strengthen access to care for hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. MMAPA strongly supports this effort and looks forward to continuing to work with Congress and CMS to advance a more stable and sustainable Medicare Advantage program for Puerto Rico”, said Solage De Lahongrais, President of the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA).
More than 650,000 Puerto Ricans rely on Medicare Advantage for their healthcare coverage, making it a cornerstone of the island’s healthcare system. Yet a key part of the federal funding formula relies on healthcare spending among traditional Medicare patients, who represent only a small fraction of beneficiaries in Puerto Rico. As a result, payments are calculated using a limited picture of healthcare costs on the island, contributing to a longstanding funding disparity.
The Puerto Rico Medicare Advantage Fairness Act seeks to permanently address one of the disparities in the federal payment formula. Beginning in 2027, the legislation would require the geographic adjustment used to calculate Medicare Advantage payments in Puerto Rico to match the adjustment applied to the U.S. Virgin Islands.
This change would help establish a fairer, more stable funding structure for Puerto Rico, reduce the need for year-to-year administrative adjustments, and provide greater certainty for the patients, physicians, hospitals, and healthcare providers who depend on the program.
This legislation comes at a critical time for Puerto Rico's patients and healthcare providers. With Medicare's annual open enrollment period just days away, hundreds of thousands of seniors will soon be reviewing their coverage options for the coming year. This legislation marks the next step in the Resident Commissioner’s ongoing efforts in Congress to close this funding gap.
Earlier this year, when the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed a national Medicare Advantage payment increase of just 0.09% for 2027, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández led a bipartisan letter signed by 17 members of Congress, including Representatives Raul Ruiz and Darren Soto, urging CMS to address the payment disparity affecting Puerto Rico. Following this effort and continued advocacy from Puerto Rico’s healthcare sector, CMS announced an increase of approximately 4% for the island, exceeding the national average of roughly 2.5%.

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) authorized the emergency exchange to alleviate supply disruption due to inclement weather in the Gulf of America
October 10, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the authorization of an emergency exchange of up to 4 million barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) to address supply disruptions due to inclement weather in the Gulf of America. Under the terms of the exchanges, participating companies will return the borrowed crude oil with additional premium barrels in 2027, helping replenish and strengthen the SPR at no additional cost to taxpayers. 
“With this emergency exchange, the Energy Department is acting swiftly to help maintain refinery operations, limit disruptions to fuel supplies, and ensure American families and businesses continue to have access to affordable, reliable, and secure energy” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “In addition to helping minimize supply disruptions, these emergency exchanges will also require Exxon and BP to return more barrels to the Reserve than are currently being withdrawn, saving taxpayers millions of dollars. Rest assured, the Trump Administration is committed to strengthening America’s energy security at every opportunity.”
The Department has authorized exchanges of up to 2 million barrels each for ExxonMobil and BP America. ExxonMobil's exchange will accelerate deliveries of previously awarded SPR crude oil to address immediate supply needs. 
DOE will continue working with industry partners to support reliable fuel supplies and respond to hurricane-related disruptions. 
For more information about the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, visit energy.gov.
title: Energy Department Authorizes Strategic Petroleum Reserve Exchange to Address Supply Disruptions Due to Hurricane
