Rep. Chu Leads 29 Members of Congress Demanding Answers on Barriers to Release from ICE Detention
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) led 29 Members of Congress in a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Mullin, Attorney General Blanche, and Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) Acting Director Owen demanding answers about rising immigration bond denials, increasingly unaffordable bond amounts, and concerns about the independence of immigration judges under the Trump administration.
Immigration bond allows eligible individuals to be released from immigration detention while their cases proceed, subject to certain conditions, including appearing for future court proceedings. But since President Trump took office, bond denials have increased substantially, while individuals granted bond are increasingly being required to pay amounts that many families cannot afford.
According to data cited in the letter, immigration bond requests more than doubled from 34,845 in 2024 to 80,130 in 2025, an increase of approximately 130 percent. Meanwhile, the percentage of bond requests denied by immigration judges rose from approximately 36 percent in 2024 to 43 percent in 2025, reaching 55 percent in the first three months of 2026. The national median bond amount, which stood at $6,000 between January 2024 and November 2025, rose to $7,500 after November 10, 2025, with the average reaching $9,211.
These trends are particularly alarming at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, which Rep. Chu has fought to close for more than a decade. Since November 2025, immigration judges have denied 57 percent of bond requests from individuals detained at Adelanto, compared to 39 percent during the preceding period. The median bond amount at Adelanto has also climbed to $10,000, well above the national median. In one particularly troubling case, a man who had lived in the United States for 25 years, maintained steady employment, supported a family, and had no criminal record was assigned a $50,000 bond, an amount an amount immigration practitioners say has traditionally been reserved for exceptional cases.
The Members also raised serious concerns about potential interference with immigration judges' ability to make independent bond determinations. Following reports that judges were being required to provide written justifications to supervisors when granting bond, EOIR released heavily redacted records in response to a Freedom of Information Act request, leaving critical questions unanswered about what instructions or guidance immigration judges may have received.
In their letter, the Members wrote:
"Taken together, these developments paint a disturbing picture. The sharp increase in bond denials and bond amounts, coupled with unresolved questions regarding potential directives and supervisory practices governing immigration judges, raises serious concerns about whether immigration judges retain sufficient independence to make individualized bond determinations based on the facts and applicable law."
“Everyone deserves a fair shot at freedom while they fight their case,” said Rep. Chu. “But under this administration, more people are being denied bond, and those who are granted it are facing amounts their families simply cannot afford. Immigration judges must be free to make decisions based on the facts and the law, not political pressure. The Trump administration owes the American people answers about whether immigration judges are being pressured to deny bond rather than make independent decisions based on the facts and the law.
“This sharp increase in bond denials shows yet again how the Trump administration is manipulating the court system to advance its anti-immigration agenda while jeopardizing the independence of judges and due process for families caught in the system,” said Kel White, Associate Director, Public Education & Training at Acacia Center for Justice. “The few people who do receive bonds are told to pay an exorbitant amount and in cash. Not only is this unheard of, especially for people with no criminal record, it is nearly impossible for a parent to do. Courts must rely on facts and the law, not an out of control anti-immigrant agenda, otherwise this is a slap in the face of meaningful due process.”
"The widespread use of bond denials and excessive bonds, regardless of the individual facts of a case, underscores why our immigration courts must be truly independent. Immigration judges should be empowered to independently interpret the law and weigh the facts of each individual case, not be reduced to rubber stamps for the administration’s detention policies. The growing practice of denying bond or imposing exorbitant bonds on people with no criminal history comes at a significant cost to not only the individuals caught in the web of injustice, but there is a cost to American taxpayers. At a time when families are struggling with affordability and rising healthcare costs, taxpayers are being asked to foot the bill for the unnecessary detention of people who have lived in our communities for decades and have no criminal record," said Benjamin Johnson, Executive Director of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA).
The letter was signed by Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Lou Correa (CA-46), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Daniel Goldman (NY-10), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Jerry Nadler (NY-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Juan Vargas (CA-52), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and Maxine Waters (CA-43).

Committee (AFSC), American Immigration Lawyers Association, Americans for Immigrant Justice, Asian Americans Advancing Justice - Atlanta, Asian Americans Advancing Justice | AAJC, Asylum Clinic KC, WASHINGTON— Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent announced today a key senior appointment at the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Dr. Judy Shelton will serve as a Counselor in the Office of the Secretary.
Shelton is an economist and author specializing in international financial and currency issues. She previously served as U.S. Director of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and as Chairman of the National Endowment for Democracy. She has testified numerous times before Congress as an expert witness on international financial relations and has consulted with national security officials on global economic developments.
At Treasury, Shelton will advise the Secretary on currency policy, with a particular focus on evaluating financial conditions in China.
Prior to joining Treasury, Shelton served as a Senior Fellow at the Independent Institute. She also served as a Senior Research Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University, where she authored The Coming Soviet Crash and Money Meltdown. She holds a Ph.D. in Business Administration from the University of Utah.
Shelton began her professional career as a National Fellow at the Hoover Institution, where she received a postdoctoral fellowship to study the impact of Western capital on the Soviet economy. Throughout her career, she has specialized in analyzing the internal monetary and financial conditions of nations and their impact on exchange rates.

WASHINGTON – Today, Reps. Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY) and Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ) introduced a House resolution recognizing World Contraception Day and calling for expanded access to contraception and reproductive health care in the United States and around the world.
 
“Access to contraception is fundamental to giving people the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies, families, and futures,” said Rep. Velázquez. “Yet millions of people still face barriers to getting the care and information they need. On World Contraception Day, we are reaffirming that contraception is essential health care and that everyone deserves affordable, reliable access to it. I am proud to join Congresswoman Grijalva in continuing this fight for reproductive freedom at home and around the world.”
 
“Everyone deserves access to contraception and the freedom to make decisions about their own health and future,” said Rep. Grijalva. “Too many people still face barriers to the care they need, especially in communities that have been underserved for far too long. On World Contraception Day, we’re standing up for affordable, accessible reproductive health care for everyone.”
 
The resolution highlights persistent barriers to contraceptive access in the United States and globally. An estimated 218 million women in economically developing countries have an unmet need for modern contraception. In the United States, one-third of adult women who have attempted to obtain prescription contraception have reported barriers to access, while more than 19 million women of reproductive age who need publicly funded contraception live in areas without reasonable access to a health center offering the full range of contraceptive methods.
 
The resolution also recognizes longstanding racial, ethnic, and socioeconomic disparities in reproductive health care and the barriers faced by communities of color, Native people, immigrants, people with disabilities, LGBTQ+ individuals, and people living in areas with limited access to reproductive health providers.
 
Among other provisions, the resolution calls on Congress and the administration to expand access to free or affordable contraception, ensure access to medically accurate information and comprehensive insurance coverage, address contraceptive deserts and reproductive health disparities, and expand access and coverage for over-the-counter birth control and other forms of contraception.
 
The resolution further recognizes the broader benefits of contraceptive access, including allowing people to plan and space pregnancies and pursue their educational, career, and life goals.

title: Velázquez, Grijalva Lead Resolution Recognizing World Contraception Day

Dexter, Bonamici, Merkley Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit to Portland ICE Facility After Reports of Denied Access to Legal Counsel
PORTLAND, OR – Today, Congresswomen Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and U.S. Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-OR) conducted an unannounced congressional oversight visit to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) processing facility on Macadam Avenue in Portland following troubling reports that attorneys were repeatedly denied access to detained clients.
“No one should be denied access to legal counsel, regardless of their immigration status,” Congresswoman Dexter said. “It is a major concern when attorneys are repeatedly prevented from meeting with their clients. ICE is not above the law, and the Trump administration must be held accountable for how people are treated in federal custody. We are demanding answers, transparency and accountability.”
Rep. Dexter’s office received information from the Portland Immigrant Rights Coalition that attorneys were denied access to four clients on 12 separate occasions Tuesday. These reports, coupled with an uptick in ICE enforcement activity in the Portland area, prompted the lawmakers to conduct an oversight visit to demand answers and examine conditions at the facility.
“I just conducted a Congressional oversight visit at the ICE processing facility in Portland with Rep. Dexter and Senator Merkley,” Congresswoman Bonamici said. “ICE is not making us safer and this surge is increasing fear in the community. I encourage everyone to make a safety plan and take care of each other. I will not stop advocating for safe communities, due process, and humane immigration reform.”
“ICE and Border Patrol agents are terrorizing our friends and neighbors,” Senator Merkley said. “Time after time, they are trampling civil rights, denying due process, and utilizing secret police tactics, totally wrong in our democratic republic. I'll keep doing all I can to stop them.”
During the visit, the lawmakers asked about access to lawyers, the treatment of people in ICE custody, and whether the facility was complying with federal law. The visit builds on Rep. Dexter’s ongoing work to hold federal immigration enforcement accountable and protect the dignity and legal rights of people in ICE custody.

Congresswoman Lee, Senator Cortez Masto Highlight Legislation to Help Human Trafficking Survivors
LAS VEGAS, NV – Today, at the Harry Reid International Airport, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) announced the reintroduction of their bipartisan, bicameral Jimmy Deal Trafficking Survivors Assistance Act. They were joined by Clark County Commission Chairman Michael N. Naft, and Lauren Boitel, Co-Founder of the Nevada Policy Council on Human Trafficking. This legislation will help survivors of human trafficking access air travel to escape their abusers and get the care they need.
“When fleeing violence and abuse, many human trafficking survivors do not have access to the identification documents they need to travel by plane, like drivers’ licenses or passports. Human traffickers often control access of victims’ identification documents, and when trafficking victims flee, many must leave their documents behind,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “Our legislation will facilitate air travel for these survivors so that they may return to their families and communities and begin to heal.”
“Jimmy Deal was an American hero – a man who made it easier for survivors of human trafficking to get approved for air travel without their IDs,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “Our legislation, introduced in his honor, will make it easier for human trafficking survivors to escape their captors and get the help they need. We will keep pushing to make sure it becomes law.”
The legislation recognizes the late TSA officer James “Jimmy” Deal, who took the role of Assistant Federal Security Director in the Reno-Tahoe International Airport and led the effort to raise awareness of human trafficking at the airport, while also working with agencies in Nevada to assist victims of human trafficking to escape.
“As one of the nation’s busiest airports, Harry Reid International Airport has both an opportunity and a responsibility to help raise awareness of human trafficking and connect people with resources. Supporting survivors means recognizing the challenges they may face beyond escaping a trafficking situation, including something as fundamental as having the identification needed to travel. This legislation helps address that barrier and reinforces the important role airports can play in helping survivors reach safety,” said Chairman Naft.
“No survivor should have to navigate the journey to safety alone. When someone finds the courage to leave exploitation, they deserve compassion, dignity, and support—not additional barriers because they lack identification or are navigating an unfamiliar and overwhelming system. The Jimmy Deal Trafficking Survivors Assistance Act helps ensure survivors can access trauma-informed assistance and trusted support to reach safety and begin rebuilding their lives, and we are grateful to Congresswoman Lee and Senator Cortez Masto for advancing a more compassionate, survivor-centered response to human trafficking,” said Lauren Boitel, Co-Founder of the Nevada Policy Council on Human Trafficking.
The Jimmy Deal Trafficking Survivors Assistance Act will:
- Encourage collaboration between Transportation Security Administration (TSA) agents and non-profits that provide services to trafficking survivors.
- Create a process to assist trafficking survivors with air travel by:
  - Establishing a “Trafficking Survivor Point of Contact” (TSPoC) position by the TSA at each airport where it conducts screenings of passengers and property.
  - Calling for the establishment of contact, communication, and relationships between service-providing organizations and the TSPoCs to pre-emptively create avenues for identity verification of escaping survivors.
- Include requirements of adequate training for each TSPoC to create a more seamless process with specialized focus. 
  - Required trainings and responsibilities incorporate trauma-informed services and ensure that survivors and escapees are supported throughout the process of reunification with their families and communities.
###
title: Congresswoman Lee, Senator Cortez Masto Highlight Legislation to Help Human Trafficking Survivors

A California businessman has been sentenced to three and a half years in federal prison for fraudulently obtaining more than $14 million in small business loans under the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (“CARES”) Act.
DARREN CARLYLE SADLER participated in a scheme to fraudulently obtain loans pursuant to the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”), which was created by the CARES Act to provide financial relief for small businesses during the Covid-19 pandemic. In 2020, Sadler submitted and caused the submission of at least 63 PPP loan applications for himself and his clients. The applications falsely represented, among other things, the number of employees and the average monthly payroll of the purported businesses. The false applications resulted in the issuance of more than $14 million in loans to Sadler and his clients, including $1.3 million in loans for Sadler himself. Sadler also received more than $1.9 million in fees from clients for fraudulently obtaining the loans on their behalf.
Sadler used the fraud proceeds to rent a villa for several months during the pandemic and to travel across the country on private jets to meet clients at bank branches to secure fund transfers. He also purchased luxury vehicles, including a Rolls Royce, multiple Mercedes-Benzes, and a Land Rover.
Sadler, 40, of Sacramento, Calif., pleaded guilty last year to a federal wire fraud charge. On Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Thomas M. Durkin sentenced Sadler to 42 months in federal prison and ordered him to pay more than $14,692,762 in restitution. The government also seized a bank account controlled by Sadler worth more than $1.8 million, which was turned over to the government pursuant to court order.
The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the FBI; Nicholas Bucciarelli, Inspector-in-Charge of the Chicago Division of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service; and William W. Kirk, Inspector General of the U.S. Small Business Administration, Office of the Inspector General.
“It is uncontroverted that defendant’s offense conduct was serious and borne of greed,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Kartik K. Raman argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum. “To enrich himself, defendant engaged in an extremely large, complex scheme that defrauded an important pandemic financial assistance program during a time of great uncertainty.”
Consistent with the Administration’s priorities to identify, investigate, and prosecute criminal fraud in the federal government entitlement and benefit programs, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Illinois has been taking a fresh look at Covid-19 fraud.
On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: California Businessman Sentenced to Three and a Half Years in Federal Prison for Orchestrating $14 Million COVID-Relief Fraud

text:
DOE urges PJM to require large new electricity users to pay for the generation and infrastructure needed to serve them.
October 9, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced its support for the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (FERC) guidance that would help ensure lower electricity costs for American families and businesses across the PJM Interconnection LLC's (PJM) region spanning across the mid-Atlantic. DOE filed a Notice of Intervention and Statement of Position with FERC supporting its recommendation for PJM’s proposed Reliability Backstop Procurement. FERC recommends PJM submit revised tariff provisions to implement appropriate cost allocation and other reforms. FERC’s recommendations are consistent with President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge, ensuring large electricity users pay for the generation and infrastructure needed to serve them. 
This action follows the Trump Administration’s call in January 2026 for PJM to adopt market rules to strengthen grid reliability and reduce electricity costs. Specifically, the Administration asked PJM to hold an emergency power auction and to accelerate the development of reliable power generation. The Trump administration was joined by governors from all 13 states who participate in the PJM grid.
“The Trump Administration remains committed to doing everything it can to lower electricity costs, grow the supply of American energy and strengthen grid reliability,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “That’s why President Trump created the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, and the Energy Department supports having large electricity users pay for reliable new power generation.”
“In January, the Trump Administration recognized early warning signs of capacity shortfalls in PJM and joined the Governors of all 13 PJM states in issuing a Statement of Principles to PJM, calling for PJM to adopt market rules to strengthen grid reliability and reduce electricity costs for American families and businesses,” said U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy James P. Danly. “By increasing transparency and preventing unjust cost shifts onto existing customers, the proposed reforms advance President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge while ensuring Americans continue to have access to affordable, reliable, and secure electricity.”
DOE supports an urgent procurement that would:
- Lower electricity costs for Americans by ensuring large load users pay for new generation and infrastructure.
- Protect households and businesses from subsidizing large loads.
- Use accurate and transparent demand information.
- Allow large loads to build, bring, or buy the capacity needed to serve them.
DOE urges PJM to comply promptly with FERC’s order and adopt durable market reforms that support reliable generation and protect American families and businesses.
title: Energy Department Supports FERC’s Call for PJM to Protect Ratepayers and Build More Reliable Power

DURHAM, NC (October 9, 2026) — Today, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Low Emission Anesthetics Act to incentive the use of certain low-emission anesthetic gases by health care facilities.
Certain traditional anesthetic gases including desflurane or nitrous oxide used by healthcare providers have been found to have an outsized impact on greenhouse gas emissions, despite the existence of proven low-emission anesthetic gases like isoflurane or sevoflurane.
“While it is clear that the climate crisis is being driven by large corporations and fossil fuels, Congress has a duty to explore all routes to make meaningful reductions to greenhouse gas emissions—and anesthetic gasses are one way we can make a difference. Moving away from anesthetic gases that have an outsized impact on greenhouse gas emission while viable alternatives already exist in the market is one small step we can take to be better environmental stewards,” said Congresswoman Valerie Fosuhee (NC-04). “I am proud to introduce the Low Emission Anesthetics Act to encourage the use of anesthetic gases that are less harmful to the environment, and I will continue to fight to keep the environment safe for generations to come.”
Specifically, the Low Emission Anesthetics Act would establish a low-emission anesthetic gas credit for any health care facility making strides to phase out high-emissions anesthetic gases, with escalating tax credits for facilities making significant strides in this area.
The full text of the Low Emission Anesthetics Act can be found here.
title: Rep. Foushee Introduces Legislation to Promote Use of Low-Emission Anesthetic Gases

text:
Morrison met with local leaders as proposed federal rule threatens services for children and families
BROOKLYN PARK, MN – U.S. Representative Kelly Morrison (MN-03) visited Parents in Community Action (PICA) Head Start in Brooklyn Park this week to meet with local Head Start leaders, tour the facility, and hear directly from staff about the critical services they provide to children and families in the community.
Rep. Morrison met with leaders from PICA and the Minnesota Head Start Association to discuss the state of Head Start in Minnesota and the potential impact of a recently proposed rule from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that would significantly overhaul the program’s federal standards. The visit marked Rep. Morrison’s second visit to PICA Head Start in Brooklyn Park.
PICA operates 11 Head Start centers across Hennepin County, including two in Minnesota’s Third Congressional District. In addition to early childhood education, PICA provides comprehensive services to the children and families it serves, including dual-language classrooms, services for children with disabilities, and transportation to medical and dental care.
“Head Start does so much more than provide early childhood education. It helps make sure children are healthy, cared for, and thriving while giving parents the reliable child care they need to work and support their families,” said Congresswoman Kelly Morrison. “As an OB-GYN and a mom of three, I know how important these early years are for a child’s health and development. I’m grateful to the incredible staff at PICA for sharing directly with me what they are seeing and what they need from leaders in Washington. I will continue working to protect Head Start and make sure Minnesota children and families have the support they need to thrive.”
For more than 60 years, Head Start has provided early childhood education, health, nutrition, and other services to children and families across the country.
- In Minnesota alone, more than 12,000 children and their families rely on Head Start.
- Head Start provided approximately 8 million hours of child care to Minnesotans in 2024.
- More than 75 percent of Minnesota Head Start parents are in the workforce and rely on child care for their employment.
The visit comes as the Trump Administration is considering a proposed rule that would remove or weaken more than 90 percent of Head Start’s federal performance standards. The proposed changes would affect standards governing early learning, health and mental health services, classroom safety and staffing, services for children with disabilities, and other supports that have long been central to the Head Start model. The proposal would also eliminate existing federal staff-to-child ratio and group-size requirements and reduce required program hours and days.
Rep. Morrison has repeatedly advocated for protecting Head Start and the families it serves. Last month, she joined her colleagues in urging HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to withdraw the proposed rule that would gut the program. This week, Rep. Morrison also joined 190 Members of Congress in calling on HHS to withdraw the proposal and preserve Head Start’s longstanding quality standards and comprehensive services for children and families.
###
title: U.S. Rep. Kelly Morrison Visits Brooklyn Park Head Start, Highlights Importance of Program for Minnesota Families

text:
Leader of Global Violent Extremist Network ‘764’ Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Sexually Exploit Minors
Prasan Nepal, 21, also known by the online moniker “Trippy,” of High Point, North Carolina, pleaded guilty yesterday to conspiracy to commit sexual exploitation of a child.
“This is the latest victory in the FBI’s work with partners to dismantle the violent 764 network,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Prasan Nepal, a leader of 764, pleaded guilty for his role in exploiting juveniles - not only breaking the law himself but recruiting others to participate in the heinous conduct targeting kids online through sexual assault, pornography, animal crushing, and more. Dismantling 764 and their online network has been a top priority for this FBI, with a nearly 500% increase in 764 related arrests last year with our state and local partners. We are finding these criminal actors all over the country no matter where they operate. Let there be no doubt that the FBI and our partners will use all our resources to protect children and bring to justice those who commit acts of terrible abuse. “
“Nepal used his leadership role within 764 to orchestrate the systematic exploitation, torture, and psychological destruction of children for the twisted satisfaction of an online network built on cruelty and chaos,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “He directed unspeakable crimes and then treated the suffering of the group’s victims as currency to be traded among his co-conspirators. We will not rest until every member of this network, and others like it, are held accountable.”
“This case exposes a world where cruelty is currency, violence is entertainment, and children are treated as targets in a game of domination and control,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro for the District of Columbia. “What Nepal and his co‑conspirators built was not just a criminal operation, it was a deliberate campaign to corrupt the vulnerable and dismantle the guardrails of civilized society. Yesterday’s plea is a victory for every child they sought to harm, and a warning to anyone who believes they can hide behind an encrypted screen: we will find you, and we will stop you.”
Nepal operated as a senior leader within “764,” a nihilistic violent extremist network that, according to court documents, engaged in a wide range of criminal conduct across the United States and abroad — including coordinated efforts to exploit minors, extort vulnerable victims, and inflict psychological harm as part of an organized ideology promoting chaos and societal destabilization.
According to court documents, Nepal and co‑defendant Leonidas Varagiannis, known as “War,” served as core leaders of 764 and its inner subgroup, 764 Inferno.
From approximately 2021 through 2025, Nepal and others used encrypted platforms to coordinate the exploitation of minors worldwide. They directed members, enforced “rules,” managed recruitment, and oversaw the production and circulation of materials used to manipulate and coerce victims.
Membership in 764 required prospective recruits to produce “content” that furthered the group’s extremist and abusive aims. Individuals who complied gained status; those who did not were excluded. Nepal and Varagiannis maintained strict control over membership, monitored activity, and issued instructions designed to expand the network’s reach and increase the volume of exploitative material.
Court documents detail the involvement of co‑conspirators operating inside the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area. One D.C.-based individual allegedly stored network material on digital devices within the District and participated in conduct aimed at coercing minor victims. Other U.S.-based co‑conspirators engaged in coordinated online extortion schemes that targeted minors in multiple states and foreign jurisdictions.
The stored content included images of the words “764 Kills” written in red on a wall and a video of 15-year-old minor victim standing topless with her breasts exposed, talking to someone on a live chat while she poured bleach on her arm and set her arm on fire.
Federal investigators have identified more than a dozen active co‑conspirators associated with Nepal and Varagiannis, many of whom operated under aliases and interacted regularly in encrypted group channels. Their activities reflected an organized, hierarchical structure designed to recruit vulnerable victims, generate exploitative material, and cultivate notoriety within the network.
764 and 764 Inferno were built on a shared extremist ideology that embraced social collapse and celebrated violence. Members used encrypted applications to:
- Identify vulnerable minors online,
- Manipulate victims into compliance,
- Coerce individuals using threats and intimidation,
- Distribute extremist and exploitative content, and
- Promote members based on the severity of material they helped generate.
The defendants and their co-conspirators around the world used the Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) and other gore and violent material to create digital “Lorebooks,” which were used as digital currency within the 764 network, traded, archived in encrypted “vaults,” and used as a means to recruit new members or maintain status within the network.
The defendants instructed other members in grooming tactics and set content production expectations for new recruits. In multiple instances, defendants threatened and caused their victims to engage in self-mutilation, online and in-person sexual acts, harm to animals, sexual exploitation of siblings and others, acts of violence, threats of violence, suicide, and murder.
A guide instructing members on “grooming” victims into producing content for 764 and advised members to target particularly vulnerable victims, such as individuals with depression or mental illness.
According to court documents, the defendants exploited at least eight minor victims across multiple jurisdictions, with some content traced back to children as young as 13 years-old. The network’s activities spanned from late 2020 through early 2025.
The guide also provided instructions on “Extortion,” and advised prospective 764 members to manipulate girls and to groom them into providing personal information that could then be used to force them to create “blood content.”
Nepal joined 764 in or around early 2021, and worked with others known and unknown, including Individual 1, to establish the group. After Individual 1’s arrest on or about Aug. 25, 2021, Nepal emerged as a leader of 764 and remained in that position through April 2025.
In his capacity as a member and leader of 764, Nepal used several online monikers, including, “Leather Jacket,” “Rebirth,” “Indras Jester,” and “KingKrampus,” but he was most widely known in 764 Inferno as “Trippy.”
Nepal was arrested in 2025 and charged alongside Varagiannis as part of a sweeping international investigation involving the District of Columbia, federal field offices across the United States, and law enforcement authorities abroad. Yesterday’s plea represents one of the most significant developments yet in dismantling 764’s leadership structure.
Variagiannis is currently being held at Grevena Prison in northern Greece and is expected to have a trial in the next six months on charges related to child pornography and participation in a criminal organization.
Nepal faces a minimum penalty of 15 years in prison and a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison. Sentencing is set for March 5, 2027.
This case is being investigated by the FBI Washington Field Office with significant assistance from the FBI New York Field Office, FBI Charlotte Field Office, and international partners. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of North Carolina also provided invaluable assistance.
The case is being prosecuted by Trial Attorneys Justin Sher and James Donnelly of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Karen Shinskie and Janani Iyengar for the District of Columbia.
The Justice Department remains vigilant against the threat of NVE networks like 764 that operate within the United States and around the globe. NVEs often target vulnerable individuals, including minors, using social media platforms to share CSAM and gore material, and groom victims toward committing acts of violence. Victims are often extorted, coerced, compelled, and blackmailed into complying with NVE demands, including self-mutilation, online and in-person sexual acts, harm to animals, sexual exploitation of siblings and others, acts of violence, threats of violence, suicide, and murder. For more information on how to protect children and others, read about the online risks here: https://www.fbi.gov/how-we-can-help-you/parents-and-caregivers-protecting-your-kids and the FBI’s March 2025 public service announcement.
This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc.
title: Leader of Global Violent Extremist Network ‘764’ Pleads Guilty to Conspiracy to Sexually Exploit Minors

Scott Calls on Watchdog to Investigate Whether or Not HHS Lied in Litigation
WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03) urged the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Inspector General to investigate HHS’s potential submission of inconsistent or fraudulent information in active litigation.
On February 6, 2025, Ranking Member Scott calledGAO’s requests, citing potential discrepancies between what was produced in litigation and would be provided to GAO.
Furthermore, during the Committee’s oversight hearing on April 17, 2026, Secretary Kennedy could not provide a clarification when questioned by Ranking Member Scott whether the Department is providing false or inaccurate information in litigation and failed to follow up with information on the matter.
“On May 17, 2026, I wrote to Secretary Kennedy to follow-up and request a detailed explanation about what the Department meant when it informed GAO that it could not cooperate or accommodate an observational walkthrough, artifacts, screenshots, and other documentation out of concern for discrepancies with what HHS produced in litigation and what it would provide to GAO, and whether HHS did provide false, incomplete, or inaccurate information in litigation.6 I have given the Department ample opportunity to respond to my requests and refute the assertion that it has provided misinformation to one or more courts and yet have received no response to date,” wrote Ranking Member Scott.
“Accordingly, given the serious nature of the allegation, I request the Office of Inspector General to initiate an investigation immediately of whether HHS has provided false, incomplete, or inaccurate information, materials, items, or other documentation in litigation since January 20, 2025.”

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Constitution and Limited Government, today joined Senator Peter Welch (D-VT), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on The Constitution, Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and Congressman Dave Min (CA-47), Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ Anti-Corruption Task Force, in raising questions about the role of cabinet members in securing presidential pardons, as part of their ongoing investigation into executive clemency actions since January 20, 2025. 
The bicameral group of lawmakers are looking into whether U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin used their access to inappropriately influence President Trump’s decision to grant full presidential pardons to convicted felons Trevor Milton and Troy Lake.
“Public reports of high-profile individuals—including yourself—appealing directly to the President on behalf of pardon recipients risk subversion of the established pardon review processes by financial influence and political access,” write the lawmakers. “Article II, Section 2, Clause 1 of the U.S. Constitution authorizes the President to ‘grant Reprieves and Pardons for Offenses against the United States, except in Cases of Impeachment.’ The U.S. Supreme Court has characterized executive clemency as ‘an act of grace’ exercised for the ‘public welfare.’ President Trump’s use of this authority appears to deviate from this traditional purpose.”
The lawmakers conclude: “Congress has a compelling interest in ensuring that the constitutional pardon power is exercised with fairness and transparency. Given these circumstances, we are seeking additional information to better understand the extent to which influence and access have overridden the standard pardon review process.”
In their letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., the lawmakers request answers about Secretary Kennedy’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to pardon convicted fraudster Trevor Milton, who defrauded and misled investors regarding technology and products related to his company, Nikola Corporation. The victims of Mr. Milton’s fraud include individuals who lost their retirement savings and others who had never invested in the stock market before. President Trump’s pardon eliminated Milton’s obligation to potentially pay $660 million in court-ordered restitution to his victims. Milton did not serve any of his four-year prison sentence.
“According to public reporting, you personally appealed to the President to grant Mr. Milton a pardon, arguing that he had been unfairly prosecuted by the previous administration’s Justice Department. Days before granting Mr. Milton’s pardon request, President Trump reportedly told him to call you and thank you for convincing the President to grant him a pardon,” write the lawmakers. “Your reported involvement in this matter is particularly troubling, given that Mr. Milton reportedly donated $750,000 to the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) Political Action Committee (PAC), which was launched in late 2024 by senior members of your presidential campaign to unite your supporters behind President Trump. Public reporting also indicates that Mr. Milton and his wife donated approximately $1,800,000 to President Trump’s 2024 reelection campaign a month before the election.”
In their letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin, the lawmakers demand answers about the administrator’s reported role in President Trump’s decision to grant a full presidential pardon to Troy Lake, and a subsequent corporate pardon to Lake’s company, Elite Diesel Service Inc. Lake’s conviction arose from allegations that he and his company disabled the monitoring components of emissions control systems on hundreds of heavy-duty commercial trucks.
The lawmakers write: “According to public reporting, two friends of Mr. Lake petitioned you in an August 2025 email, urging you to reach out to the President to request a pardon. Mr. Lake’s wife publicly attributed progress on her husband’s pardon efforts to your subsequent intervention. Such progress included a phone call with Sean Hayes, a White House attorney who works closely on pardons.”
The lawmakers’ letters seek information from HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin regarding:
    - The nature of their relationships with the pardoned felons;
- The process by which clemency requests were initiated and considered;
- Whether intermediaries, lobbyists, or advocates were involved;
- Any contacts with Trump Administration officials or associates;
- Their role in any other clemency decisions made by the Trump Administration;
- Whether financial contributions or payments were made in connection with clemency efforts; and
- The extent of third-party advocacy supporting the requests.
Read the lawmakers’ full letters to HHS Secretary Kennedy and EPA Administrator Zeldin.
###
title: Scanlon, Welch, Blumenthal, Min Initiate Probe into Improper Influence of Cabinet Members in Trump Pardons

Ranking Members Raskin, Himes Urge Kash Patel to Abandon Russia Trip Hosted By Putin’s Security Service Amid Espionage Concerns
FBI Director’s Planned Visit with Putin’s Security Service Raises Serious Alarms Over Russian Espionage and FBI Intelligence Sharing
Washington, D.C. (October 9, 2026)—Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Jim Himes, Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, are urging Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel to cancel his reported trip to Russia next month, raising urgent national security concerns about his plans to visit Moscow and St. Petersburg as the FBI expands cooperation with Russian and Chinese law enforcement agencies. Patel will reportedly be hosted by Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), the successor to the Soviet-era KGB, which has a documented history of conducting espionage operations against American officials and personnel.
“Winston Churchill described Russia as ‘a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma.’ Now, we have a puzzle buried in a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside that enigma: Why is the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) visiting a hostile foreign power that has been committing war crimes, conducting influence operations against U.S. elections, conducting malicious cyberattacks against our critical infrastructure, and helping our adversaries target and kill American soldiers?” wrote the Ranking Members. “In the interest of national security, we ask you to reconsider. Call off this trip.”
The trip comes amid reports that Patel is personally leading an initiative to forge closer ties between the FBI and Russian and Chinese law enforcement agencies, including personnel exchanges and intelligence sharing. While the Administration strikes a big anti-China pose, Patel has reportedly already provided Chinese officials unprecedented access to American intelligence personnel, diplomatic personnel, government facilities and contractors, despite longstanding warnings that foreign intelligence services will exploit such access to conduct espionage.
The timing raises additional concerns. In the last two weeks, President Trump signed sweeping sanctions targeting Russia’s economy over its war against Ukraine. Meanwhile, Russia continues to conduct espionage and cyberattacks against the United States and its allies, and has reportedly provided Iran with intelligence to help refine aerial attacks on American troops in the Middle East. DOJ also recently revealed a Russian intelligence-linked murder-for-hire plot targeting a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C.
Patel’s hosts are no ordinary law enforcement partners. Russia’s FSB has a documented history of surveilling American officials, planting recording devices and conducting honey trap operations targeting U.S. personnel. Compounding these concerns, Patel received $25,000 for participating in a documentary produced by a filmmaker with Kremlin ties, in which he openly dismissed U.S. intelligence assessments of Russian election interference and claimed Moscow was not among America’s “true enemies.”
The Ranking Members are calling on Patel to cancel his trip and, if he insists on proceeding, are requesting a closed-door briefing on the FBI’s expanding cooperation with foreign adversaries and the security precautions surrounding his odd visit. The briefing must address the FBI’s efforts to increase cooperation with Russia, China and other designated foreign entities; any internal concerns or objections to those efforts; who proposed the trip and why; Patel’s complete itinerary, planned meetings and traveling companions; and precautions to protect against Russian espionage, including technological safeguards, and additional counterintelligence measures.
Click here to read the letter.
title: Ranking Members Raskin, Himes Urge Kash Patel to Abandon Russia Trip Hosted By Putin’s Security Service Amid Espionage Concerns

Crow Hosts Election Security Roundtable with Colorado Leaders
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, hosted an election security roundtable alongside local officials from Denver County and Arapahoe County. Crow’s roundtable was an opportunity for elections officials, law enforcement, and other leaders to coordinate and discuss efforts to keep Colorado’s election system strong.
Joining Crow’s roundtable were Denver District Attorney John Walsh, Arapahoe County District Attorney Amy Padden; Arapahoe County Clerk and Recorder Joan Lopez; Arapahoe County Sheriff Tyler Brown; and Ben Hess from the Committee for Safe and Secure Election.
At the roundtable, Colorado leaders discussed ensuring Coloradans have the right information to help them vote early; security protocols that keep ballot drop-off boxes secure; and exercises used by law enforcement officers and local officials to help them prepare for any potential incidents before, during, and after Election Day.
“Colorado’s elections are the gold standard. Our same-day registration, open primaries, and mail-in-ballot program not only encourage one of the highest voter turnout rates in the nation but are also extremely safe and secure,” said Congressman Crow. “I assembled this roundtable to ensure that our leaders are working together to protect our elections at every turn. Every qualified Coloradan must have the chance to make their voice heard without fear or intimidation.”
Congressman Crow has long fought to ensure that all Coloradans are able to make their voices heard at the ballot box. He voted against Congressional Republicans’ voter suppression bills, while working to ensure our elections are secure from bad actors through his leadership on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. Crow is also leading the fight to root out corruption in our elections, including through his End Dark Money Act and SHINE Act to crack down on dark money’s influence on U.S. elections.

title: Crow Hosts Election Security Roundtable with Colorado Leaders

Congressman Don Beyer (VA-08) is leading a congressional letter with co-leads Representatives April McClain Delaney, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Kweisi Mfume, Suhas Subramanyam, and Sarah Elfreth urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.
The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.
The FAA’s rush to deploy a system that could affect the lives of millions of Americans is especially concerning for residents of this region, who are still grappling with questions about air safety following last year’s fatal crash at DCA. Before deploying its AI-enabled SMART air traffic control tool, the FAA must demonstrate, through air traffic controller feedback and independently verified testing, that this technology is safe and reliable, and it must clearly communicate those findings to the public,” said Congressman Don Beyer.
“When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know that every system guiding their flight has been thoroughly tested and that the people keeping them safe have the training they need,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “After the devastating crash over DCA that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first. I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong.”
“Last month, the Federal Aviation Administration surprisingly launched an AI tool to help control air traffic over three major National Capital Region Airports, with plans to expand nationwide in the following 90 days. They did so without publishing a safety evaluation or sufficiently consulting air traffic controllers and safety experts. We are urging Transportation Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford to stop the rollout until we have answers. This administration may treat Big Tech companies with impunity, but air traffic control leaves zero margin for error,” said Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. 
"Families across Baltimore count on BWI to get them where they’re going safely. Yet the Trump Administration recklessly rolled out an untested AI air traffic tool there without publishing a safety evaluation or adequately consulting the air traffic controllers who keep us safe. There is no room for error in our skies. I am proud to co-lead this letter calling for public transparency and answers from Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford on how this system was tested, who was consulted, and how it will be evaluated. Until they provide answers that ensure that this technology is safe, the FAA must pause its use," said Congressman Kweisi Mfume. 
“The airspace in the DC region is incredibly complicated and demands the highest standard of safety and reliability from Air Traffic Control. We need to be extremely cautious about implementing AI tools into the systems responsible for the safety of our skies. I urge the FAA to prove that the system does not pose a risk to the public before allowing its use," said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.
“Every day, our airports and their staff ensure tens of thousands of worldwide travelers are safe and secure – including here at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport in Maryland’s Third District. While we fully recognize the need to modernize our air traffic control systems, we cannot pursue modernization at the expense of public safety, especially when it comes to implementing new technologies like AI,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “As AI safety concerns are top of mind for our neighbors, this is another instance where we cannot afford to miss the moment on regulating this technology. I also am determined to continue to work with my colleagues to ensure our hardworking air traffic controllers have every resource they need to do their jobs and ensure the safety of our passengers.”
At a time when AI safety concerns are sky high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.
The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.
The lawmakers request answers in three areas:
    - Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.
- Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.
- Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.
The letter calls for a pause until lawmakers can better understand the FAA’s decision-making, rollout process, and evaluation plan. The co-leads emphasize that modernizing air traffic control must prioritize safety, transparency, and the expertise of the people responsible for keeping our skies safe.
title: Beyer Joins Call with McClain Delaney, Ocasio-Cortez, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports

text:
HHS Launches Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit Program to Support Mothers and Babies
MORGANTOWN, WV—OCTOBER 9, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) today launched the Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit (NEST) Program at West Virginia University Medicine Golisano Children’s Hospital in Morgantown, West Virginia, marking the next phase of a federal initiative designed to support mothers and babies during the critical first days and weeks after birth.
Led by HHS through the Office of Intergovernmental and External Affairs (IEA) in coordination with the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), NEST provides families with a one-time kit of essential newborn and postpartum supplies, maternal health items, and trusted information and resources around the time of birth.
“President Trump is putting mothers, babies, and strong families at the center of his health agenda,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Through NEST, HHS is delivering essential supplies and trusted health information directly to families around the time of birth, including in rural and underserved communities. I thank Governor Morrisey for partnering with us to launch this next phase in West Virginia and help more mothers care for themselves and their newborns.”
“West Virginia is proud to help launch NEST and put practical support directly into the hands of mothers and families,” said Governor Patrick Morrisey. “These kits will help new parents get some of the basic necessities they need while easing some of the financial pressure that comes with welcoming a new baby. We appreciate the Trump Administration and our federal partners for working with us to give West Virginia mothers and babies a healthy start.”
NEST builds on the Department’s Newborn Supply Kit initiative, first launched in 2023. In the 2024 evaluation, 99% of surveyed recipients said they would recommend the kit to another new parent, 76% said it helped reduce anxiety, and 72% reported reduced financial stress.
In 2026, Congress provided funding to continue the work of the Newborn Supply Kit. Through HRSA, HHS awarded $5 million in funding to the CDC Foundation to support implementation of NEST. The CDC Foundation also partners with HHS through an established public-private partnership supporting evaluation of the program.
As NEST expands, HHS is emphasizing geographic diversity and reaching areas of greatest need, including maternal care deserts, rural communities, and other medically underserved areas.
“Every child deserves the healthiest possible start in life, and every mother should have the support she needs during pregnancy and after her baby is born,” said HRSA Administrator Tom Engels. “NEST will provide families with essential supplies and trusted resources when they need them most, while helping reach mothers and babies in rural and medically underserved communities. Through this investment, the Trump Administration is strengthening support for families and helping parents care for themselves and their newborns during this critical time.”
Each NEST Kit includes practical supplies for both mom and baby, including diapers and wipes, an infant thermometer, postpartum recovery and breastfeeding supplies, a blood pressure monitor, and other newborn essentials. Families also receive trusted information on postpartum health, infant safety and care, feeding and nutrition, and available programs and resources.
NEST Kits are distributed through hospitals, federally qualified health centers, and other organizations providing maternity care to mothers late in pregnancy or around the time of birth. Through these trusted partners, HHS is working to reach families in communities across the country while prioritizing areas where mothers and babies face greater barriers to care and resources.
Through NEST, HHS is building on what families and healthcare providers said worked: providing useful, high-quality supplies at a moment when families need them most, while connecting mothers with trusted information to help care for themselves and their newborns.
For more information, visit hhs.gov/newbaby.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

title: HHS Launches Newborn Essentials Support Toolkit Program to Support Mothers and Babies

Washington, D.C. (October 9, 2026)—Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Jim Himes, Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, are urging Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel to cancel his reported trip to Russia next month, raising urgent national security concerns about his plans to visit Moscow and St. Petersburg as the FBI expands cooperation with Russian and Chinese law enforcement agencies. Patel will reportedly be hosted by Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB), the successor to the Soviet-era KGB, which has a documented history of conducting espionage operations against American officials and personnel.
“Winston Churchill described Russia as ‘a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside an enigma.’ Now, we have a puzzle buried in a riddle wrapped in a mystery inside that enigma: Why is the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) visiting a hostile foreign power that has been committing war crimes, conducting influence operations against U.S. elections, conducting malicious cyberattacks against our critical infrastructure, and helping our adversaries target and kill American soldiers?” wrote the Ranking Members. “In the interest of national security, we ask you to reconsider. Call off this trip.”
The trip comes amid reports that Patel is personally leading an initiative to forge closer ties between the FBI and Russian and Chinese law enforcement agencies, including personnel exchanges and intelligence sharing. While the Administration strikes a big anti-China pose, Patel has reportedly already provided Chinese officials unprecedented access to American intelligence personnel, diplomatic personnel, government facilities and contractors, despite longstanding warnings that foreign intelligence services will exploit such access to conduct espionage.
The timing raises additional concerns. In the last two weeks, President Trump signed sweeping sanctions targeting Russia’s economy over its war against Ukraine. Meanwhile, Russia continues to conduct espionage and cyberattacks against the United States and its allies, and has reportedly provided Iran with intelligence to help refine aerial attacks on American troops in the Middle East. DOJ also recently revealed a Russian intelligence-linked murder-for-hire plot targeting a prominent Russian dissident in Washington, D.C.
Patel’s hosts are no ordinary law enforcement partners. Russia’s FSB has a documented history of surveilling American officials, planting recording devices and conducting honey trap operations targeting U.S. personnel. Compounding these concerns, Patel received $25,000 for participating in a documentary produced by a filmmaker with Kremlin ties, in which he openly dismissed U.S. intelligence assessments of Russian election interference and claimed Moscow was not among America’s “true enemies.”
The Ranking Members are calling on Patel to cancel his trip and, if he insists on proceeding, are requesting a closed-door briefing on the FBI’s expanding cooperation with foreign adversaries and the security precautions surrounding his odd visit. The briefing must address the FBI’s efforts to increase cooperation with Russia, China and other designated foreign entities; any internal concerns or objections to those efforts; who proposed the trip and why; Patel’s complete itinerary, planned meetings and traveling companions; and precautions to protect against Russian espionage, including technological safeguards, and additional counterintelligence measures.
Click here to read the letter.
title: Ranking Members Himes, Raskin Urge Kash Patel to Abandon Russia Trip Hosted By Putin’s Security Service Amid Espionage Concerns

Liccardo Leads Bipartisan Push to Bring Whale Alerts to West Coast Mariners
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Bay Area Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16) led a bipartisan effort to leverage technology to protect whales on the West Coast. His recent letter to the U.S. Coast Guard, the Federal Communications Commission, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration requests an expansion of Automatic Identification System (AIS) messaging technology to send whale-safety information directly to mariners along the West Coast.
“With at least 145 gray whale collisions already reported along the West Coast in 2026, we must do more to keep both whales and mariners safe,” said Liccardo. “By implementing AIS whale-safety messages, we can give real-time warnings to mariners and help them avoid deadly collisions, without disrupting maritime activities."
Liccardo and his cosigners request the agencies identify areas where AIS messaging could support voluntary speed reductions messages, determine whether existing whale detection programs can transmit information directly to mariners through AIS, and identify ways to streamline approval timelines while maintaining navigation and spectrum safeguards.
On the East Coast, federal agencies and regional partners already use AIS messaging to send vessel location-specific alerts in whale speed reduction zones. Expanding AIS whale-safety messaging to the West Coast would use technology already familiar to mariners to provide additional information about whale activity.
“Expanding this capability is particularly relevant along the West Coast, where vessel traffic and whale activity increasingly overlap,” the lawmakers wrote.
The effort builds on Liccardo’s Save Willy Act, which would establish a “Whale Desk” at the Coast Guard’s San Francisco station to centralize whale sightings and alert vessel operators when whales enter the Bay.
“Using AIS technology to identify high-risk areas and alert mariners in real time can help prevent deadly vessel collisions with whales off California while keeping vital maritime traffic moving safely,” said Geoff Shester, Director of Fishery Innovation and Senior Scientist at Oceana. “This proven technology would give agencies and ship operators a practical, science-based tool to protect whales and improve safety in our busy coastal waters for all who use them.”
“Vessel strikes are a leading cause of death and serious injury for large whales and can result in substantial property damage for mariners as well as pose a significant safety risk to those onboard. IFAW has worked tirelessly in the pursuit of reducing the threat of vessel strikes and strongly supports the use of AIS as a warming system for mariners. We're grateful to Representatives Liccardo, Case, Krishnamoorthi, Min, Moylan, and Pallone for championing the use of AIS to improve mariner safety and help reduce the risk of vessel strikes on whales along the West Coast," said Kathleen Collins, International Fund for Animal Welfare Senior Marine Campaign Manager.
Congressmembers Ed Case (HI-01), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Dave Min (CA-47), Frank Pallone (NJ-06), and James Moylan (Guam) signed the letter.
Read the full letter here.
title: Liccardo Leads Bipartisan Push to Bring Whale Alerts to West Coast Mariners

NEWARK, NJ – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) and her legal counsel filed a brief requesting that the full U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit hear her case en banc.
The appeal highlights major constitutional problems with the charges the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ) brought against McIver arising out of her May 2025 oversight inspection of Delaney Hall, ICE detention facility in her district. This move for hearing en banc comes after a divided panel of three Third Circuit judges refused to dismiss the case against McIver in August.
By appealing, McIver continues her fight to protect her constitutional and statutory authority to oversee ICE, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and the rest of the executive branch. The full text of the brief can be found here.
“As I have said since last May, oversight is my job. I am pursuing this step in no small part because every single day since last May, we have seen only more terror surrounding Delaney Hall—from brutality outside of its gates to retribution behind its walls and horror stories from the detainees I’ve spoken with on my many visits. What’s happening here and in ICE facilities nationwide only further proves why members of Congress need to be able to do this critical oversight work to protect people—work that Trump’s administration wants to stop by locking me in prison for 17 years,” said McIver. “Members of Congress have a right to do oversight even, and especially, when the administration does not like what they find. I will fight like hell to protect that right. I will continue to oppose these baseless charges and this intimidation, and I will keep doing my job, not without fear, but in spite of it.”
Paul J. Fishman, counsel to McIver, added context about the stakes of the case and the court’s August ruling on the same issues.
“This case is about whether the Executive Branch can interfere with and try to intimidate members of Congress who are doing the oversight the Constitution requires of them. Congresswoman McIver has been incredibly brave in taking on a fight against an administration that targeted lawmakers and others for speaking out when they see abuses,” said Fishman. “The executive branch should not and cannot be allowed to use its power over criminal prosecutions to retaliate against those it would like to silence.”
The charges against McIver stem from an oversight visit she conducted at Delaney Hall, a controversial ICE detention center in her district, in May, 2025. She is the only member of Congress under indictment by the Trump DOJ for performing constitutionally protected oversight of ICE and, if convicted, faces up to 17 years in federal prison.
###
title: McIver Moves For Appeal To Be Heard En Banc By Third Circuit, Refuses to Back Down

Goodlander joins 190 colleagues urging Secretary Kennedy to withdraw proposed rule that would dismantle safeguards for early education, child safety, and health services.
Concord, N.H. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) joined House and Senate colleagues this week in urging U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to withdraw a proposed rule that would weaken Head Start standards protecting children and supporting working families across New Hampshire.
The letter opposes the Administration’s proposed “Reducing Federal Burden for Head Start Programs” rule, warning that it would remove more than 90 percent of existing program standards and undermine the high-quality early education, health services, and family support that make Head Start a lifeline for families.
“Every child in New Hampshire deserves a safe place to learn, grow, and get a fair shot at success. Head Start helps deliver on that promise while helping hardworking parents stay in the workforce and provide for their families,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “At a time when Granite Staters are struggling to find and afford childcare, Secretary Robert F. Kennedy is brazenly trying to dismantle Head Start, and make it harder for kids and families to get the care they need. That is unacceptable. I’m fighting to protect Head Start and make quality childcare more affordable and accessible for New Hampshire families.”
The lawmakers warn that the proposal would eliminate federal requirements governing staff-to-child ratios and class sizes, weaken staff qualifications and safety training, and roll back standards for developmental screenings, dental care, and mental health services. They also raise concerns that shorter program hours would leave working parents scrambling to find additional childcare, while new documentation requirements would create barriers for families with the greatest needs.
The letter further objects to removing detailed protections for children with disabilities and children experiencing homelessness, and to changes that would undermine instruction for dual-language learners.
Read the full letter HERE.
BACKGROUND ON GOODLANDER’S ADVOCACY FOR CHILDREN AND WORKING FAMILIES
Congresswoman Goodlander is working to lower childcare costs, expand access to early education, and support the educators and programs New Hampshire families rely on.
- Defending Head Start: Goodlander previously joined the Democratic Women’s Caucus in urging Secretary Kennedy to withdraw the same proposed rule, opposing efforts to weaken standards for child safety, early learning, health services, and support for children with disabilities.
- Making quality childcare more affordable: Goodlander helped introduce the Child Care for Working Families Act, which would cap working families’ childcare expenses at seven percent of income, expand the supply of quality care, and increase wages for early childhood educators. The legislation would also support full-day, full-year Head Start programs and higher wages for Head Start workers.
- Helping children and families get to school: Goodlander introduced the bipartisan PATH to Education Act to improve affordable, reliable transportation to Head Start centers and educational institutions. The bill would help connect transit routes to schools and better align transportation schedules with program hours.
- Investing in New Hampshire’s childcare workforce: Goodlander helped secure nearly $1 million for Nashua Community College’s Early Childhood Education Center. The center will help prepare future early childhood educators and expand access to quality childcare, with opportunities for students to observe, collaborate, and teach alongside Head Start teachers.
- Expanding childcare in New Hampshire communities: Goodlander helped secure federal Community Project Funding, including $1 million for Bristol’s Tapply-Thompson Community Center, $688,000 for the Gorham Community Learning Center, and $1.6 million for Sullivan County’s Regional Childcare Enhancement Project. These investments will support a new community center in Bristol, conversion of a vacant bank into a childcare facility in Gorham, and a new childcare center on Sullivan County’s Unity Campus.
###
title: Goodlander Pushes Back Against Trump Administration Plan to Dismantle Head Start, Protects New Hampshire Children and Working Families
