HHS Announces Up to $27.8 Million for Falls Prevention
WASHINGTON, D.C.— OCTOBER 9, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Administration for Community Living (ACL), today announced the recipients of three falls prevention initiatives totaling up to $27.8 million over three years. The funding will expand proven programs, strengthen connections between health care providers and community organizations, and help states and local partners reach more older adults before a fall leads to injury or loss of independence.
Falls are the leading cause of injury for people 65 and older. One in four older adults falls every year, and a fall is rarely just a fall. It can result in an injury or hospital stay, and non-fatal falls account for an estimated $80 billion in healthcare spending per year. A fall can also shake a person’s confidence and make everyday activities — from walking and shopping to visiting friends — more difficult. Healthcare and aging network providers can help prevent many falls by identifying risks early. They can then connect older adults with programs and support that build strength, improve balance, and make their homes safer.
The three initiatives put prevention first and advance the Trump Administration’s Make America Healthy Again agenda. They will connect screening with community support, expand proven programs statewide, and help organizations deliver and sustain them.
“A fall can change an older American’s life in an instant, and we can prevent many of these injuries,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “HHS is connecting healthcare screening with proven community programs to identify risks earlier, improve strength and balance, and help older adults maintain their independence. These investments will reduce injuries and healthcare costs while helping more Americans remain safely in their homes and communities.”
To reduce that risk, these awards will expand two complementary approaches:
- The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Stopping Elderly Accidents, Deaths & Injuries (STEADI) initiative helps health care providers screen for, assess, and address fall risk.
- Stepping On, an evidence-based community falls prevention program, helps older adults improve strength and balance and address risks related to medications, vision, footwear, and home safety. Together, the approaches connect screening with action.
“Knowing someone is at risk is only the first step. What makes the difference is a clear path from screening to support that people can trust and use,” said Mary Lazare, ACL Principal Deputy Administrator. “These awards build that path while giving states and community partners the tools to reach more people and deliver programs that work.”
Three Investments, One Prevention Strategy
Goal: Scaling Through Clinical-Community Partnerships
Program: A Demonstration to Scale Innovative Person-Centered Approaches to Falls Prevention through Clinical-Community Partnerships
Recipient: National Council on Aging, Arlington, VA
Award: $4,781,733
The National Council on Aging will work to scale STEADI and Stepping On through clinical-community partnerships in five geographies. Rapid cycle evaluation will be used to improve the impact of the interventions as they are scaled.
Goal: Expanding Proven Programs Statewide
This funding will help states expand STEADI and Stepping On and address the many factors that increase fall risk. Recipients will strengthen referral networks, prepare more local organizations to deliver the programs, and share lessons with other states and communities.
Goal: Helping Communities Sustain What Works
Program: National Falls Prevention Resource Center
Recipient: National Council on Aging, Arlington, VA
Award: $7,500,000
The National Falls Prevention Resource Center will provide ACL’s aging and disability networks with training, tools, and individualized assistance to deliver and sustain high-quality falls prevention programs. It will also help organizations learn from one another and preserve the elements that make proven programs effective.
Falls Prevention Is a National Priority
Research shows that falls among older adults are preventable through person centered, evidenced based interventions. However, there are gaps in widespread adoption and implementation of these strategies. Through ACL, HHS is coordinating a cross-agency effort, informed by the National Falls Prevention Action Plan. It unites ACL, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Health Resource and Services Administration, CMS’s Center for Clinical Standards and Quality, the National Institute of Aging, and Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. Together, these agencies will move beyond siloed approaches to deliver significant progress in reducing falls over the next three years.
Learn more about ACL’s Falls Prevention Program here.

Rep. Panetta Convenes Local Healthcare Leaders to Address Challenges Ahead of Medicare Open Enrollment
Rep. Panetta convened a roundtable to discuss provider shortages
and service challenges ahead of October 15 Medicare open enrollment.
To watch his remarks, click HERE or on the above photo.
For additional photos, click HERE.
Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) brought together local physicians, hospital leaders, and community health providers at Santa Cruz Community Health to address seniors’ challenges accessing care ahead of Medicare open enrollment and discuss his bipartisan efforts to ensure they have coverage they can afford and rely on. With Medicare open enrollment set to start October 15, the roundtable and subsequent press availability focused on local provider shortages, rising prescription drug plan premiums, and the need for Medicare payments to keep pace with the cost of providing care.
For many seniors in California’s 19th Congressional District, choosing Medicare coverage does not guarantee they can find a local doctor accepting new patients. Medicare physician reimbursements have failed to keep pace with inflation, making it harder for practices to recruit and retain physicians and continue serving seniors in a region with a high cost of living. These pressures leave beneficiaries facing fewer options and longer waits for the benefits they earned through a lifetime of work.
“As Medicare open enrollment begins October 15, seniors deserve coverage that they paid into and can rely on. Too often in our community, however, having coverage does not mean having access to care,” said Rep. Panetta. “That’s why I helped author, introduce, and am working to pass the bipartisan Strengthening Medicare for Patients and Providers Act and the Patients First Act that would strengthen physician payments and reduce administrative burdens, helping keep local doctors in practice so seniors can access the care they earned.”
“I appreciate the opportunity to share ideas with Congressman Panetta for strengthening Medicare to better support patients and providers. The Medicare Hospice Benefit has not been updated since its introduction in 1982, despite significant changes in disease trajectories and treatments. Safety-net providers like Hospice of Santa Cruz County increasingly care for patients with complex needs and short stays, yet the current Medicare reimbursement does not adequately reflect the intensity or cost of providing this care. Without meaningful updates to the benefit, high-quality hospices like ours face growing challenges in sustaining the level of care our patients need and deserve,” said Cathy Conway, CEO, Hospice of Santa Cruz County.
A 2022 California Medical Association survey found that 76% of responding physicians reported that traditional Medicare payments do not cover their costs of providing care, and 87% reported difficulty recruiting and retaining physicians because of low Medicare payment rates and the high costs of operating a practice in California. Additionally, 41% said they planned to close their practices to new Medicare patients.
Rep. Panetta co-leads the bipartisan Strengthening Medicare for Patients and Providers Act to index physician payments to inflation and better reflect the cost of delivering care. He also helped introduce the bipartisan Patients First Act to strengthen physician payments, support primary care, and reduce administrative burdens. Together, these proposals would help sustain practices and improve seniors’ access to care.
Rep. Panetta’s bipartisan REAL Health Providers Act, signed into law this year, will require annual updates to Medicare Advantage provider directories beginning in 2028 so seniors have more accurate information when choosing coverage. He previously voted for the Inflation Reduction Act’s cap on annual out-of-pocket Medicare Part D prescription drug costs and its option to spread those expenses across the year.
For additional photos, click HERE.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) joined Congressman Pat Ryan (N.Y.-18) and four of their Democratic Veteran colleagues in the U.S. House in introducing legislation to prevent the president from weaponizing the military to interfere with elections. Specifically, the bill would empower Congress to stop or reverse any domestic troop deployment ordered by the president.
The introduction follows months of threats and actions by the Trump Administration to interfere with the November midterm elections and amid new reports from the Atlantic that advisors close to the President are encouraging him to declare martial law. Trump has repeatedly refused to rule out declaring a national emergency on elections, has already deployed thousands of U.S. troops against U.S. citizens in American cities, and suggested that Republicans should “nationalize” the midterm elections and “take over” the voting process. When asked directly in a House Armed Services Committee (HASC) hearing, a senior Trump military official refused to rule out troop deployments to polling sites.
“As a 25-year Army veteran, I know our troops should never be asked to carry out the political will of a president at the expense of our democracy. Our military swears an oath to the U.S. Constitution and the American people, not any one president or political party,” said Vindman. “The prospect of using our armed forces to influence or interfere with our elections is dangerous and fundamentally at odds with the oath every service member takes. Congress must make clear that our military cannot be weaponized to interfere with Americans’ right to vote, and that our elections must remain free from intimidation, and military interference.”
“Patriots in uniform sign up to fight for fundamental American freedoms – not against them. Trump using U.S. servicemembers as political pawns is straight-up un-American, and we’re not going to let him get away with it,” said Ryan. “Trump and those around him are scared – they know the American people are fed up with the war in Iran and skyrocketing prices. Instead of working to lower costs, Trump and his team are cooking up ways to intimidate voters, refusing to rule out domestic troop deployments. This bill provides a necessary check on the President. If he deploys troops, Congress can and will stop him. We won’t let this chickenhawk president exploit our servicemembers just because he can’t face the fact that the American people are fed up with his failed agenda of higher costs and unprecedented corruption.”
Joining Vindman and Ryan are fellow Democratic veterans and U.S. Representatives Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-02), Chris Deluzio (Pa.-17), Chrissy Houlahan (Pa.-06), and Jimmy Panetta (Calif.-19).
Senator Elissa Slotkin (Mich.) introduced companion legislation in the Senate. The bicameral legislation also includes $1 billion in new resources for state and local law enforcement on the ground.
BACKGROUND
Vindman is a 25-year Army veteran and member of the Democratic Veterans Caucus; Vindman also sits on the House Armed Services Committee, where he has become the leading voice of opposition to Trump’s war in Iran.
###
title: Vindman Supports Legislation to Prevent Illegal Domestic Troop Deployments and Voter Intimidation Ahead of Midterm Election

News Release
Keith Sonderling sworn in as 31st US Secretary of Labor
WASHINGTON – Keith Sonderling was sworn in today as the 31st U.S. Secretary of Labor during a ceremony administered by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in the Oval Office.
Sonderling has led the U.S. Department of Labor as Acting Secretary since April 2026. He previously served as Deputy Secretary of Labor after confirmation by the U.S. Senate in March 2025.
President Donald J. Trump announced Sonderling’s nomination on June 29, and the Senate confirmed the nomination Sept. 30. Sonderling was officially sworn into office Oct. 2.
“It is the honor of my life to serve as the 31st Secretary of Labor and continue my service to the Department under President Trump’s leadership,” said Sonderling. “I believe President Trump is the greatest President for the American worker and job creator. My mission is to ensure that American workers have the skills and resources they need to seize the incredible job opportunities being created across the country thanks to the tireless work of this Administration.”
Upon announcing his nomination, President Trump said, “Throughout his career, Keith has proven his dedication to delivering strong results for the Hardworking People of our Country, and I know he will do an incredible job in his new role.”
While serving as Deputy Secretary of Labor, Sonderling oversaw the department’s day-to-day operations, including strategic planning, budget formulation, financial management, information technology, and human resources.
From September 2020 to August 2024, Sonderling served as a Commissioner of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, including as Vice Chair from 2020 to 2021. During his tenure, he became a leading global voice on super intelligence in the workplace, publishing extensively and speaking around the world on SI and the future of work. Following his service at the EEOC, Sonderling led President Trump’s Department of Labor transition team before returning to the Department in January 2025.
During President Trump’s first term, Sonderling served as Acting Administrator, Deputy Administrator, and Senior Policy Advisor of the department’s Wage and Hour Division from 2017 to 2020.
In June 2026, President Trump designated Sonderling as Acting Director of the U.S. Office of Government Ethics, a position he continues to hold concurrently with his service at the Department of Labor. During President Trump’s second term, Sonderling has also served as Acting Director of the Institute of Museum and Library Services and Acting Under Secretary of Commerce for Minority Business Development.
Before entering government service, Sonderling was a partner at Gunster, one of Florida’s oldest and largest law firms, where he practiced labor and employment law.
title: Keith Sonderling sworn in as 31st US Secretary of Labor

Landsman, Khanna, Frankel, Fitzpatrick Reintroduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve How College Campuses Handle Reports of Sexual Violence
Cincinnati, OH – Today, Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH), Congressman Ro Khanna (D-CA), and Congresswoman Lois Frankel (D-FL), and Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) reintroduced bipartisan legislation to improve how colleges and universities handle reports of sexual violence and ensure greater transparency, accountability, and student support.
Sexual violence remains a serious issue on college and university campuses across the country. Students often face challenges when it comes to reporting assaults, finding support, and trying to navigate a complex disciplinary system.
Representatives Landsman, Khanna, Frankel, and Fitzpatrick reintroduced the Campus Accountability and Safety Act to improve the way colleges and universities address and report incidents of sexual assault – which would ensure a uniform and fair process for investigations and additional support for students on campus.
The Campus Accountability and Safety Act would:
- Increase transparency and reporting requirements under the Clery Act by mandating an institution’s website include campus safety policies, an annual security report, instructions for filing a complaint, and statistics of sexual misconduct allegations on campus.
- Create sexual and interpersonal violence specialists to serve as confidential aides for victims and coordinate support services.
- Establish a standard procedure to handle sexual assault cases and ensure on-campus personnel are well-trained.
- Ensure individuals who report sexual misconduct in good faith are not punished for acts of self-defense, or alcohol or drug use, that is revealed by that report.
- Create a campus grant program to address and prevent sexual assault, sexual harassment, and domestic violence on campuses.
Congressman Landsman:
“Students have to be kept safe on college campuses. The reports of sexual violence at colleges and universities make it clear that changes are needed. Our bipartisan effort will ensure there’s way more transparency, accountability, and support for students.”
Congressman Khanna:
“After the horrific allegations at Cornell, LSU, and the countless stories we have heard from survivors on campuses across the country, Congress must act to protect survivors and ensure there is accountability. Due to stigma, many survivors don’t report sexual violence, much less pursue justice through their university’s system, and many perpetrators are never held accountable. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan bill with my colleagues to increase transparency, provide resources for survivors, and reduce barriers in the reporting process."
Congresswoman Frankel:
“Students can’t learn if they are not safe. No student should have to fear sexual harassment, violence, or stalking while pursuing an education. The horrifying allegations recently brought to light at Cornell underscore the urgent need for action. Survivors of sexual abuse deserve confidential support and to be heard and treated with dignity. This legislation strengthens transparency and accountability and makes clear that keeping students safe is a fundamental responsibility of every college and university,”
Congressman Fitzpatrick:
“Sexual assault on college campuses continues to be a crisis that demands our immediate action. And, as with all crimes, weak enforcement and insufficient accountability only embolden perpetrators to act with impunity. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation is a commitment to our students that we are taking action: action to ensure their safety and action to hold our educational institutions accountable by transforming how sexual assault and violence are handled and addressed. By demanding greater transparency, enforcing stringent accountability measures, and providing essential resources and support to victims, we can eliminate the toxic culture of inaction that has plagued our campuses for too long and create a safer environment for our students.”
###
title: Landsman, Khanna, Frankel, Fitzpatrick Reintroduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve How College Campuses Handle Reports of Sexual Violence

PHOENIX – In honor of Hispanic Heritage Month, Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) celebrated the 50th anniversary of Los Abogados, Arizona’s Hispanic Bar Association, with a Congressional Record recognition honoring the organization’s five decades of service, advocacy, leadership, and commitment to expanding opportunity within Arizona’s legal community.
“It is an honor to recognize Los Abogados and the incredible work they have done to build community, create opportunities, and advance the interests of Arizona’s Latino communities,” said Rep. Ansari. “At a time when we are seeing fundamental rights come under attack this work is more important than ever. I will continue fighting in Congress to protect Arizonans’ rights and conducting oversight to ensure accountability and equal justice.”
The celebration hosted at Univision Studios in Phoenix featured the unveiling of a commemorative 50th Anniversary artwork by Los Abogados’ Artist of the Year, Michael Padilla, and a panel moderated by Congresswoman Ansari with Danny Ortega, Marian Zapata-Rossa, and Salvador Macias on the organization’s history, impact, and future.
READ TEXT OF ANSARI’S CONGRESSIONAL RECORD
Mister Speaker, I rise today to honor the 50th anniversary of Los Abogados, Arizona’s Hispanic Bar Association.
Founded in 1976 by Latino lawyers and law students, Los Abogados has spent five decades building community, creating opportunities, and advancing the interests of Arizona’s Latino communities within the legal profession and beyond.
Today, Latinos comprise only approximately roughly 5% to 6% of all licensed lawyers in the United States. Through programming, mentorship, leadership development, and community engagement, Los Abogados works to address the systemic and cultural barriers that Latinos continue to encounter throughout their legal careers.
For 50 years, Los Abogados has remained steadfast in its commitment to diversity and inclusion, advocacy, and education. The Hispanic Bar Association actively promotes diversity within Arizona’s legal and judicial professions. Supporting Latino lawyers and expanding their representation is essential to narrowing the significant representation gap and ensuring that our legal system better reflects the communities it serves.
Los Abogados’ Civil Rights Committee supports the equitable and just application of civil rights, advocating for Arizona’s Latino communities. The committee organizes “Continuing Legal Education” seminars to update legal professionals about current voting rights, civic engagement, and racial profiling positions. Additionally, Los Abogados hosts citizenship fairs, providing essential immigration resources and assistance to Arizonans.
As we commemorate this important milestone, we recognize Los Abogados for 50 years of service, advocacy, and leadership. I congratulate its members, past and present, and commend their enduring commitment to strengthening Arizona’s legal community and ensuring greater access, representation, and opportunity for all.
On behalf of the United States Congress, I extend my deepest gratitude and congratulations to Los Abogados on their 50th Anniversary.
###
title: Ansari Celebrates Los Abogados’ 50th Anniversary with Congressional Record Recognition

Pocan, Bacon Introduce Resolution Recognizing National PrEP Day
WASHINGTON, D.C. -
U.S. Representatives Mark Pocan (WI-02) and Don Bacon (NE-02) today introduced a resolution recognizing October 10, 2026, as National PrEP Day and highlighting the importance of access to pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a critical tool for preventing HIV.
“PrEP is one of the most effective tools we have to prevent HIV, yet too many people who could benefit from it continue to face barriers to access,” said Rep. Pocan, Chair of the Congressional HIV/AIDS Caucus. “National PrEP Day is an opportunity to raise awareness, reduce stigma and ensure people across the country know about this proven HIV prevention tool.”
“PrEP is a proven tool that can prevent HIV, and we should make sure people who can benefit from it know it is available and can access it,” said Rep. Bacon. “National PrEP Day is an opportunity to raise awareness, improve access and give people the information they need to protect their health. I'm joining Rep. Pocan on this bipartisan resolution supporting evidence-based efforts to prevent HIV and help more Americans access the care they need.”
When taken as prescribed, PrEP reduces the risk of acquiring HIV through sex by about 99 percent. Despite the effectiveness of PrEP, disparities in access and uptake persist due to factors including cost, stigma and barriers to health care.
Cosponsors include Representatives Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Mark Takano (CA-39) and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).
The resolution is endorsed by MISTR, NMAC, and PrEP4All.

Under President Trump, the United States has acted decisively to defend U.S. sovereignty and U.S. citizens against the threat of the International Criminal Court (ICC). To date, the United States has imposed sanctions on 17 persons pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14203 “Imposing Sanctions on the International Criminal Court.” Today, the Department of State announces additional actions to defend U.S. sovereignty and neutralize the threat posed by the ICC.

The ICC is being designated pursuant to section 1(a)(ii)(A) of Executive Order 14203. *

Concurrent with this designation, the Department of the Treasury is issuing a set of general licenses (GLs) authorizing certain transactions involving the ICC to protect U.S. interests. A 180-day GL authorizing certain activity involving the ICC, including for the maintenance of its operations; A GL authorizing certain IT-related activities, including cloud and software services; A GL authorizing activity related to the ICC pension plan; and A GL authorizing certain activity related to the ICC detainees.

A GL authorizing certain IT-related activities, including cloud and software services;

A GL authorizing activity related to the ICC pension plan; and

A GL authorizing certain activity related to the ICC detainees.

For more details please reference OFAC’s website .

The 180-day maintenance GL is intended to provide time for States Parties to demonstrate meaningful progress on diplomatic and legal resolutions that address fundamental U.S. concerns regarding the ICC. This GL can be adjusted in response to the success or failure of such efforts to address our concerns.

Watch Secretary Rubio’s video message announcing U.S. sanctions on the ICC on the Department of State’s YouTube channel.

* Sanctions Implications

As a result of today’s sanctions-related actions, and subject to applicable licenses and exceptions, all property and interests in property of the ICC that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless exempt or authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, including those general licenses described above. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page .

ICYMI: Pelosi Joins Congressional Efforts to Protect Federal Services and Uphold Americans’ Rights
Washington, D.C. — Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi joined Congressional Democratic colleagues in a series of recent letters, legislative proposals and court briefs addressing federal policies affecting San Franciscans. The efforts include calls to release housing and energy assistance funding, maintain Medicare and Head Start protections, preserve public lands and access to historical records, and protect voting rights and student survivors of sexual assault.
Protecting health care and essential services for children and families:
Pelosi joined colleagues in urging the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to reverse its decision to end the Medicare Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration, which has helped lower prescription drug coverage premiums for nearly 25 million seniors and people with disabilities. Ending the program without a plan to maintain lower costs would increase out of pocket costs for the most vulnerable San Franciscans.
Read the full letter here.
To defend early childhood education, Pelosi joined 190 of her colleagues in a bicameral letter demanding that the Department of Health and Human Services withdraw its proposal to remove more than 90 percent of Head Start’s federal performance standards. Members warned that the proposal would weaken classroom safety protections, diminish the already struggling child care workforce and reduce critical health screenings and essential services. Members warned the Administration that these changes would undermine critical childhood development and leave working families without reliable child care.
Read the full letter here.
Keeping San Franciscans housed and helping them afford their energy bills:
Pelosi joined colleagues in urging the Department of Housing and Urban Development to release overdue guidance on preventing Emergency Housing Voucher funding shortfalls, warning that delays put families at risk of losing their critical rental assistance and becoming unhoused. With more than 44,000 vouchers still in use, including 920 in San Francisco, Members demanded answers from HUD to prevent interruptions in housing assistance.
Read the full letter here.
Pelosi also joined colleagues in urging the Department of Housing and Urban Development to immediately release the delayed funding notice for Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS grants and expedite renewal awards. As a proud author of HOPWA, the only federal program dedicated to the housing needs of people living with HIV/AIDS, this initiative supports housing development and provides critical rental assistance and resources for individuals and their families. Any disruptions to HOPWA, including expiring grants and uncertainty over renewals, threatens to interrupt these critical services and put people at risk of homelessness.
Read the full letter here.
Pelosi joined 116 of her colleagues in a bipartisan letter urging the Department of Health and Human Services to distribute Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program funding as soon as possible, which impacts 3,052 households in San Francisco. Members warned the Administration that repeated funding delays and high energy costs could leave families without heat or force them to choose between heating their homes and paying for food, medication or rent.
Read the full letter here.
Defending California’s public lands:
Pelosi joined 156 of her colleagues in a bipartisan, bicameral letter urging Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to abandon a proposed transfer of land within Yosemite National Park to provide access to a privately owned ranch. Members argued that the unprecedented transaction would brazenly benefit a private landowner and diminish public access to the historic, world-renowned park, and vigorously opposed the misuse use of the Land and Water Conservation Fund.
Read the full letter here.
Pelosi joined colleagues in overwhelmingly opposing the Administration’s shameless actions with the Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monuments, which removed nearly three million acres from protection. Members warned that opening these lands to mining and drilling threatens sacred Tribal sites, wildlife habitats, scientific resources and local recreation economies. The letter also condemns the dissolution of the Bears Ears Commission and the lack of meaningful Tribal consultation.
Read the full letter here.
Preserving San Francisco’s history:
Pelosi joined a bipartisan, bicameral letter led by Representatives Kevin Mullin and Judy Chu urging the National Archives and Records Administration to oppose closure of its San Bruno facility. Members warned the Archives that dispersing its records to six facilities across the country would make it harder for families and researchers to access California’s history, including records related to the Chinese Exclusion Act and the incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II. 
Read the full letter here.
Pelosi also cosponsored the National Archives Protection Act, which would require congressional approval before the National Archives and Records Administration could close or significantly restrict access to existing regional facilities. The legislation would protect access to historical and personal records, many of which have not been digitized and can only be viewed in person, helping families and ensure researchers easily explore our history.
Read the full bill here.
Safeguarding voting rights and Americans’ personal information:
Pelosi joined a bipartisan group of current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to sustain an injunction blocking the Administration’s new Postal Service restrictions on mail-in voting in place. The brief argues that the Administration cannot unilaterally impose mail-ballot requirements on states or bar election officials from using the Postal Service to send ballots. Members emphasized that the Constitution assigns authority over federal election rules to states and Congress, and that Congress has not authorized the Postal Service to exercise the powers claimed by the Administration.
Read the full brief here.
Pelosi joined a bipartisan group of current and former Members of Congress in urging the Supreme Court to reject the Administration’s emergency request to implement a federal citizenship verification database that risks disenfranchising voters. The brief argues that linking Social Security records to a government-wide system for bulk searches of sensitive personal information is illegal This action is another overt effort by this Administration to undermine the Congress and violate the separation of powers as envisioned by our Founders.
Read the full brief here.
Protecting students from sexual harassment and assault:
Pelosi joined colleagues in calling for an immediate investigation by the Department of Education’s Office of Inspector General into the Department’s failure to adequately enforce Title IX protections for student survivors. The letter urges investigators to examine whether staffing cuts, regional office closures and changes in enforcement priorities have delayed investigations and undermined accountability for campus sexual harassment and assault.
Read the full letter here.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Lou Correa (CA-46) and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) today reintroduced a resolution remembering and honoring the life and legacy of Alex Odeh. The resolution acknowledges Alex's impact on his community and the country, and reaffirms the importance of pursuing justice against those responsible for his death.
“Alex Odeh was a teacher, a poet, and a man of peace, and he was murdered in our community simply for speaking up for civil and human rights,” said Correa. “He was a voice for peace and dignity in Orange County. Remembering him is the least we can do, and pursuing justice for his family is our obligation.”
Rep. Correa represents the district where Alex and his family lived and where the attack took place.
“Alex Odeh dedicated his life to achieving true equality and equity for all. For daring to push for a better tomorrow, Alex was assassinated by members of the Jewish Defense League, and his killers have yet to be brought to justice,” said Tlaib. "This horrific act of anti-Arab and anti-Palestinian violence was, and is not, new. But this violence will never silence us. Those who continue to fear-monger and incite hate against us will not win. Arab and Palestinian Americans are still here, loud and proud, carrying on Alex’s legacy.”
Read the bill text here.
About Alex Odeh
Alex was born in Jifna, Palestine, and lived in Orange County, California, for most of his adult life, including Santa Ana. He was a peace activist who worked to promote civil liberties for Arab-Americans in the United States. Alex Odeh was the Southern California Regional Director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC).
On October 11, 1985, Alex was killed when a pipe bomb exploded as he entered the ADC regional office in Santa Ana, California. Although the primary suspects have long been known, no one has been brought to justice. The investigation remains open.
title: CORREA, TLAIB REINTRODUCE RESOLUTION HONORING ALEX ODEH

USPS responds to Delaware delegation on future of Ocean View Post Office
USPS confirms search for potential new location as delegation continues push for permanent solution, greater transparency
OCEAN VIEW, Del. — U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senators Chris Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester (all D-Del.) today announced that they have received a formal response from the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) regarding the continued closure and future of the Ocean View Post Office.
The response follows a letter from the delegation to Postmaster General David Steiner demanding greater transparency, a clear timeline, improved interim services, and a permanent solution for Ocean View residents who have been without a fully functioning local Post Office for more than a year.
The Ocean View Post Office closed for emergency repairs in October 2025 after problems with the facility were identified. USPS initially announced plans to repair the building, then announced in June that further evaluations had determined a full rebuild was necessary, with construction expected to begin in spring 2027 and conclude that fall.
In its latest response to the delegation, however, USPS said additional engineering concerns prompted officials to further evaluate their plans. USPS is now conducting a search for existing properties in the Ocean View community to determine whether leasing a new location would be preferable to constructing a new facility on the existing property.
“For more than a year, the people of Ocean View have dealt with changing plans and far too much uncertainty about the future of their Post Office,” said Congresswoman McBride and Senators Coons and Blunt Rochester. “We appreciate that USPS is seriously analyzing every option to restore full postal service to Ocean View, however that looks. But residents still deserve what we asked for in our letter: a permanent solution, a clear timeline, and regular, transparent communication about how USPS intends to get there. We will continue pressing USPS until Ocean View has the reliable, fully functioning Post Office this community deserves.”
USPS also addressed concerns raised by the delegation regarding interim postal services. The agency said it is preparing to replace the existing collection box at 220 Atlantic Avenue with a larger collection box, though the 11 a.m. pickup time will remain unchanged. USPS had previously announced in April that the larger box would be installed by May 30. The agency acknowledged the delay and said it expects the new box to be installed soon.
While the Ocean View facility remains closed, retail and Post Office Box services continue to operate through the Bethany Beach Post Office, just over two-and-a-half miles away, while carrier delivery continues through the Sussex County Carrier Annex in Frankford.
The delegation had also requested an in-person meeting with Postmaster General Steiner. USPS indicated that it is willing to meet with the delegation and committed to contacting congressional staff when it has a substantive update regarding the facility search. The delegation will continue working with USPS, state and local officials, and Ocean View residents to press for a timely permanent solution and ensure the community is kept informed as the process moves forward.
###
title: USPS responds to Delaware delegation on future of Ocean View Post Office

Illinois Woman Sentenced to 31 Months in Prison for Distributing and Conspiring to Create and Distribute Sexual Torture and Mutilation Videos of Baby Monkeys
Amanda Leigh Fourez, of Catlin, Illinois, was sentenced yesterday to 31 months in prison and three years of supervised release in connection with her involvement with online groups dedicated to creating and distributing videos depicting acts of extreme violence and sexual abuse against monkeys in violation of the federal Animal Crushing statute.
Fourez pleaded guilty in April to distributing animal crush videos and conspiring with others to create and distribute the videos.
According to court documents and statements made during the sentencing hearing, Fourez paid thousands of dollars to commission bespoke sexual torture videos of monkeys, and later she distributed the obscene crush videos online. She was a member of several chat groups and private payment groups dedicated to the creation, distribution, and discussion of sexual and violent videos depicting monkeys being tortured, including baby and adult monkeys being burned and their genitals mutilated.
During the sentencing hearing, the court denied Fourez’s motion for a downward variance. The court observed that the videos that Fourez created and distributed were “shocking and violent” and documented “agonizing torture” of animals. The court further noted that the sentence should deter others from this serious conduct.
Another member of these groups, Joseph Garrett Buckland, of Mount Pleasant, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to create and distribute animal crush videos in April and is set to be sentenced on Jan. 13, 2027 for his role in the conspiracy ring.
“We stand ready to prosecute this depraved conduct,” said Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Justice Department’s Energy and Natural Resources Division (ENRD). “We appreciate the collaboration of HSI and the U.S. Attorney’s Office in rooting out this conspiracy and prosecuting the case.”
“Amanda Fourez commissioned mutilation of helpless animals on video, and then disseminated those gruesome videos to an online community of people who were seeking content that portrayed the infliction of severe pain and suffering,” said U.S. Attorney Troy Rivetti for the Western District of Pennsylvania. “Today’s sentencing demonstrates the ongoing commitment of the Department of Justice and our law enforcement partners to investigating and prosecuting these serious federal crimes involving cruelty to animals.”
“The conduct in this case was unimaginably cruel and highlights the depraved nature of the online networks HSI is committed to dismantling,” said Special Agent in Charge Matt Wright of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) New Orleans. “HSI will continue to utilize advanced investigative techniques and vital law enforcement partnerships to track those who facilitate these heinous crimes across international borders.”
HSI New Orleans’ Cyber and Human Exploitation Investigations investigated the case.
Trial Attorney Emily R. Stone of ENRD’s Environmental Crimes Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alyssa Angotti and Kelly M. Locher for the Western District of Pennsylvania are prosecuting the case.
title: Illinois Woman Sentenced to 31 Months in Prison for Distributing and Conspiring to Create and Distribute Sexual Torture and Mutilation Videos of Baby Monkeys

EPA Deputy Administrator Fotouhi Wraps Two-Day Swing in Virginia, Joins Representative Kiggans to Announce Over $90 Million for Chesapeake Bay Program
WASHINGTON — Last week, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Deputy Administrator David Fotouhi was joined by U.S. Representative Jen Kiggans (R-VA-02) to announce more than $90 million in funding for 83 projects in Smithfield, Va. The funding coming from Small Watershed Implementation and Innovative Nutrient and Sediment Reduction grants and matching funds, will help to improve water quality and reduce nutrient and sediment pollution throughout the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The pair got to see firsthand the impact the funding can have during a tour of the living shoreline at Windsor Castle Park, a key project providing a tangible example of how federal investments support practical, on-the-ground restoration and coastal resilience.
“My visit to Virginia was yet another example of why it’s so important to meet with state and local leaders and speak directly to them about how EPA can best support their communities,” said EPA Deputy Administrator Fotouhi. “Our announcement on Friday to provide tens of millions of dollars in additional funding to the Chesapeake Bay program proves how the Trump Administration is investing in improving water quality, reducing nutrients and sediment entering the watershed, and keeping our ecosystems healthy for generations to come.”
The announcement was part of a two-day swing in Virginia where he met with state and local leaders to discuss how the Trump EPA can continue advancing cooperative federalism with the state to protect human health and the environment. On Thursday, Deputy Administrator Fotouhi met with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Norfolk District following the completion of the Norfolk Harbor and Thimble Shoal Channel deepening project. Port-related activity like this supports more than 570,000 jobs and approximately $63 billion in Virginia gross state product annually. As the port continues to expand its infrastructure, Deputy Administrator Fotouhi and USACE focused on how efficient permitting and coordination among federal agencies can help ensure these projects continue.
Next, Deputy Administrator Fotouhi traveled to Virginia Beach to meet with Mayor Bobby Dyer and City Manager Patrick Duhaney. Mayor Dyer is a newly appointed member of EPA’s Local Government Advisory Committee (LGAC), an advisory group comprised of state and local officials who help advance the agency's core mission while Powering the Great American Comeback. Their discussion focused on local infrastructure priorities and the federal-local partnership.
Deputy Administrator Fotouhi ended his trip with a visit at the Atlantic Wood Industries Superfund Site. This site is a 50-acre industrial waterfront property along the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River, where EPA has led a multi-phase cleanup addressing contaminated soil, groundwater and more than 30 acres of river sediment, including the dredging of approximately 360,000 cubic yards of contaminated sediment. The visit highlighted progress of the cleanup and ongoing efforts to measure its impact on the health of the Elizabeth River ecosystem, including through tissue sampling of oysters and other aquatic species. The Trump EPA’s Superfund Solutions initiative aims to expedite cleanups at sites across the country so that they can return to productive reuse in their communities.
title: EPA Deputy Administrator Fotouhi Wraps Two-Day Swing in Virginia, Joins Representative Kiggans to Announce Over $90 Million for Chesapeake Bay Program

RELEASE: Gottheimer Urges FDA to Establish Clear Standards for Rare Disease Status
Protect Patients with Sarcoidosis and Other Serious Illnesses Bipartisan Letter Warns That Unclear Standards Could Strip Rare Disease Status From Conditions Like Sarcoidosis
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Founder and Co-Chair of the Congressional Sarcoidosis Caucus, and thirty-eight of his colleagues sent a bipartisan letter to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and U.S. Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Marty Makary urging the agencies to establish clear, consistent standards for defining rare disease patient populations.
“When 95 percent of rare diseases do not have cures, we cannot risk discouraging innovation in areas where scientific progress is rapidly outpacing regulatory adaptation,” the letter reads. “These challenges are not merely technical — they have real implications for patients… This means if the FDA considers prevalence rate with the higher estimate as the prevailing rate, diseases like Sarcoidosis are no longer capable of receiving crucial rare disease funding to find cures even though the patient population that needs treatment is well below the current FDA standard for rare.”
The letter raises concerns about the lack of clear, consistent FDA standards on how patient populations should be defined, how prevalence should be measured, and what evidentiary standards sponsors must meet. Advances in genomics and precision medicine are enabling researchers to identify increasingly specific disease subtypes, but the FDA has no clear roadmap for how to characterize those populations in regulatory submissions. The letter warns that this uncertainty can lead to unpredictable regulatory outcomes and discourage investment in therapies for small or complex patient populations.
This lack of clarity is already causing harm. Diseases like sarcoidosis, multiple myeloma, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, and pulmonary hypertension — serious, often life-altering conditions — risk losing rare disease status depending on how patient populations are counted. For example, while some estimates place sarcoidosis prevalence just above 200,000, only about 60,000 patients actually require treatment. If the FDA relies on the higher estimate, diseases like sarcoidosis could lose access to rare disease-specific research funding and incentives, even though the population that needs treatments is well below the 200,000-person threshold.
The lawmakers urge HHS and the FDA to:
- Establish standardized definitions for how patient populations are delineated, including the role of genetic, biomarker, and clinical criteria.
- Issue clear guidance on acceptable methodologies for calculating and submitting prevalence data, including preferred data sources, timeframes, and analytic approaches.
- Outline how real-world data and registry-based studies should be incorporated into regulatory submissions.
- Provide greater transparency into how population definitions and prevalence estimates are evaluated during review.
- Clarify the role of treatment-eligible patient populations in determining rare disease status.
- Engage patient groups, researchers, and industry to develop consensus-driven best practices for population identification and data submission.
The letter is co-signed by Reps. Jake Auchincloss (D-MA), Don Bacon (R-NE), Nanette Díaz Barragán (D-CA), Wesley Bell (D-MO), André Carson (D-IN), Yvette Clarke (D-NY), Steve Cohen (D-TN), Jim Costa (D-CA), Danny Davis (D-IL), Don Davis (D-NC), Madeleine Dean (D-PA), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), Lois Frankel (D-FL), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH), Adam Gray (D-CA), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ), French Hill (R-AR), Jim Himes (D-CT), Jonathan Jackson (D-IL), Hank Johnson (D-GA), Ro Khanna (D-CA), Darin LaHood (R-IL), Mike Lawler (R-NY), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Sarah McBride (D-DE), Max Miller (R-OH), Kelly Morrison (D-MN), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), Mark Pocan (D-WI), Linda Sánchez (D-CA), Eric Sorensen (D-IL), Darren Soto (D-FL), Tom Suozzi (D-NY), Shri Thanedar (D-MI), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL).
The letter builds on Gottheimer’s longstanding work on sarcoidosis and rare diseases. He has led an annual bipartisan appropriations letter urging research funding for sarcoidosis through the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), founded the Bipartisan Congressional Sarcoidosis Caucus, and has met with patients, advocates, and leading medical professionals from across New Jersey to discuss the disease. Importantly, Gottheimer secured language in the Fiscal Year 2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations bill that passed out of committee this year. The language encourages the NHLBI to advance research into sarcoidosis — the first-ever mention of the disease in this appropriations bill.
Gottheimer, a Rare Disease Caucus member, is also leading Gwenn’s Law, which would increase the number of women in NIH clinical research trials to help drive treatments and cures for rare diseases, and Cameron’s Law, which would restore the Orphan Drug Tax Credit to support rare disease drug development.
###
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Urges FDA to Establish Clear Standards for Rare Disease Status

text:
USDA Encourages Producers and Residents to Prepare for Hurricane Isaias
(Washington, D.C., October 9, 2026) – The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) reminds communities, farmers and ranchers, families and small businesses in the path of Hurricane Isaias that USDA has programs that provide assistance in the wake of disasters. USDA staff in regional, state, and county offices stand ready to assist as conditions develop and to support recovery.
USDA’s Disaster Resource Center and Disaster Assistance Discovery Tool offer easy access to information on programs that support recovery from natural disasters. USDA also encourages residents and producers to contact their local USDA Service Center to determine which programs may meet their needs.
Food safety guidance:
Heavy winds, flooding, and power outages can jeopardize stored food. USDA recommends the following steps to keep food safe:
- A refrigerator will keep food below 40°F for up to 4 hours during an outage. A full freezer stays cold for about 48 hours (24 hours if half full). Keep doors closed as much as possible.
- Keep an appliance thermometer in both the refrigerator and freezer to check temperatures if power is lost.
- Freeze containers of water ahead of the storm or make ice in containers to help keep food cold in the refrigerator and freezer.
- Freeze refrigerated items you may not need immediately—such as leftovers, milk, and fresh meat or poultry—to extend their safe storage time.
- Consider purchasing 50 pounds of dry or block ice if a long outage is expected; this can keep an 18-cubic-foot freezer cold for two days.
- Group foods together in the freezer to help them stay cold longer.
- Keep several days’ worth of ready-to-eat foods that do not require cooking or cooling.
For food safety questions, call the Meat and Poultry Hotline at 1-888-674-6854 (Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m. ET), or email MPHotline@usda.gov. Meat and poultry businesses may contact the FSIS Small Plant Help Desk online 24/7, call 1-877-FSIS-HELP (1-877-374-7435) or email InfoSource@usda.gov.
Protecting pets and livestock:
The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) urges everyone in the potential path of the hurricane to prepare now:
- Plan for evacuation—know how you will evacuate and where you will go. If it is not feasible to evacuate livestock, provide strong shelter and adequate food and water.
- If moving livestock across state lines, contact the receiving state’s State Veterinarian’s Office. APHIS Veterinary Services state offices can also assist.
- Follow instructions from emergency officials and evacuate if asked to do so.
Risk management and disaster assistance for agricultural operations:
USDA offers several programs to help producers recover from hurricane impacts. Producers with Federal Crop Insurance or Noninsured Crop Disaster Assistance Program (NAP) coverage should report losses to their crop insurance agent or local Farm Service Agency (FSA) office within 72 hours of discovering damage and follow up in writing within 15 days.
Other key programs from USDA include:
- Livestock Indemnity Program and Emergency Assistance for Livestock, Honeybees, and Farm-raised Fish.
- Tree Assistance Program for damaged orchards and vineyards.
- Emergency Conservation Program and Emergency Forest Restoration Program for land and forest recovery.
- Producers should document all losses and contact their local USDA Service Center as soon as possible.
The Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) also provides financial and technical assistance through the Environmental Quality Incentives Program and can support local governments through the Emergency Watershed Protection Program.
FSA also offers financial support to farmers and ranchers impacted by natural disasters, including:
- Direct and guaranteed farm loans, including operating and emergency farm loans, to producers unable to secure commercial financing.
- Low interest emergency loans for producers in designated disaster areas to help recover from production and physical losses.
- Loan servicing options for borrowers unable to make scheduled payments due to circumstances beyond their control.
Loans help producers replace property, livestock, equipment, feed and seed, cover living expenses, refinance farm-related debts and more.
Producers can also use tools on farmers.gov, including the Disaster Assistance Discovery Tool and Disaster Assistance-at-a-Glance fact sheet, to identify applicable recovery programs. For crop insurance claims, contact your insurance agent. For FSA or NRCS programs, reach out to your local USDA Service Center.
USDA’s Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA) also works closely with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and stands by to support requests from state and local authorities for emergency nutrition assistance. In disaster situations, FNA helps communities meet immediate nutrition needs when it matters the most.
###
title: USDA Encourages Producers and Residents to Prepare for Hurricane Isaias

text:
Schakowsky, Trahan, Kean Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect FTC Whistleblowers as The Social Reckoning Hits Theaters
WASHINGTON– As The Social Reckoning, a new film about Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen, hits theaters nationwide, Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), and Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) today introduced bipartisan legislation to protect whistleblowers who disclose wrongdoing at their current or former workplaces that fall under the jurisdiction of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC).
The FTC Whistleblower Act of 2026 would protect current and former employees from retaliation when they disclose violations of consumer protection and antitrust laws to the FTC. The legislation would also establish incentives for whistleblowers to come forward with information about unlawful conduct.
“Frances Haugen took an enormous risk when she came forward with information about what was happening inside Facebook,” said Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky. “Her courage helped expose serious concerns about the impact of social media on our children and families. But no worker should have to choose between doing the right thing and losing their livelihood. Our bipartisan bill makes sure whistleblowers who expose wrongdoing to the FTC have the protections they deserve.”
“When something goes wrong inside a company, the workers there are often the first to know. Today, if they bring that information to the FTC, they take the risk alone,” said Congresswoman Lori Trahan. “The FTC Whistleblower Act gives them real protections and a real reason to come forward. That’s good for workers, good for families, and good for the companies doing things the right way. Frances Haugen showed what one person can do. Nobody should have to be that brave just to tell the truth.”
“The FTC Whistleblower Act would empower workers to safely report corporate misconduct without fear of retaliation. By protecting whistleblowers who report misconduct, the bill will allow the FTC to uncover violations and build strong enforcement cases,” said Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. “With increased transparency into harmful practices, the bill ensures companies can’t operate in the shadows and protects workers from retaliation.”
The FTC is the federal agency responsible for enforcing a broad range of consumer protection and antitrust laws. Unlike some other federal agencies, the FTC does not have a comprehensive whistleblower protection and award program for employees who report violations within its jurisdiction.
“This legislation is an excellent opportunity for Congress to apply cohesive rights across federal agencies, including the FTC, in accordance with their sustained leadership on whistleblower protections. The FTC’s ability to protect consumers and keep big businesses in check goes hand in hand with whistleblowers keeping Americans safe. Providing protections and best practice incentives for whistleblowers coming forward with original information to the Commission is a nonpartisan issue and essential to good governance,” said Maya Efrati, Director of Legislation & Congressional Affairs at Government Accountability Project.
“Whistleblowers are our most effective safeguard against corporate fraud and corruption. This bill strengthens essential protections and incentives so that insiders can more safely expose wrongdoing that harms American families and consumers. POGO appreciates Congresswoman Schakowsky’s leadership on this crucial bill that will enhance regulatory oversight, hold powerful corporations more accountable, and protect the public’s trust," said Joe Spielberger, Senior Policy Counsel, Project On Government Oversight.
The need for stronger protections was highlighted by Haugen’s 2021 disclosures of internal Facebook documents, which became known as the “Facebook Files.” Haugen later testified before Congress about the company’s practices and their potential impact on young people.
###
title: Schakowsky, Trahan, Kean Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect FTC Whistleblowers as The Social Reckoning Hits Theaters

McClain Delaney Leads Call with Ocasio-Cortez, Beyer, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports
Representatives demand transparency on safety testing, air traffic controller training, and oversight of the SMART system deployed at DCA, Dulles, and BWI
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (MD-06) is leading a congressional letter with co-leads Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Don Beyer, Kweisi Mfume, Suhas Subramanyam, and Sarah Elfreth urging the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to pause use of its new artificial intelligence-enabled air traffic management tool until the agency answers questions about safety testing, implementation, and oversight.
The letter to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford raises concerns about the September 21 deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) tool at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, Washington Dulles International Airport, and Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport.
“When Maryland families board a plane, they deserve to know that every system guiding their flight has been thoroughly tested and that the people keeping them safe have the training they need,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “After the devastating crash over DCA that took 67 lives, the FAA owes this region answers. I support modernizing our aviation systems, but passenger safety must come first. I’m calling on the FAA to pause this rollout, show us the safety testing, and explain who is accountable when something goes wrong.”
“Last month, the Federal Aviation Administration surprisingly launched an AI tool to help control air traffic over three major National Capital Region Airports, with plans to expand nationwide in the following 90 days. They did so without publishing a safety evaluation or sufficiently consulting air traffic controllers and safety experts. We are urging Transportation Secretary Duffy and FAA Administrator Bedford to stop the rollout until we have answers. This administration may treat Big Tech companies with impunity, but air traffic control leaves zero margin for error,” said Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
The FAA’s rush to deploy a system that could affect the lives of millions of Americans is especially concerning for residents of this region, who are still grappling with questions about air safety following last year’s fatal crash at DCA. Before deploying its AI-enabled SMART air traffic control tool, the FAA must demonstrate, through air traffic controller feedback and independently verified testing, that this technology is safe and reliable, and it must clearly communicate those findings to the public,” Congressman Don Beyer.
"Families across Baltimore count on BWI to get them where they’re going safely. Yet the Trump Administration recklessly rolled out an untested AI air traffic tool there without publishing a safety evaluation or adequately consulting the air traffic controllers who keep us safe. There is no room for error in our skies. I am proud to co-lead this letter calling for public transparency and answers from Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford on how this system was tested, who was consulted, and how it will be evaluated. Until they provide answers that ensure that this technology is safe, the FAA must pause its use," said Congressman Kweisi Mfume.
“The airspace in the DC region is incredibly complicated and demands the highest standard of safety and reliability from Air Traffic Control. We need to be extremely cautious about implementing AI tools into the systems responsible for the safety of our skies. I urge the FAA to prove that the system does not pose a risk to the public before allowing its use," said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.
“Every day, our airports and their staff ensure tens of thousands of worldwide travelers are safe and secure – including here at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport in Maryland’s Third District. While we fully recognize the need to modernize our air traffic control systems, we cannot pursue modernization at the expense of public safety, especially when it comes to implementing new technologies like AI,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “As AI safety concerns are top of mind for our neighbors, this is another instance where we cannot afford to miss the moment on regulating this technology. I also am determined to continue to work with my colleagues to ensure our hardworking air traffic controllers have every resource they need to do their jobs and ensure the safety of our passengers.”
At a time when AI safety concerns are sky high, the lawmakers warn that the FAA has not provided sufficient transparency around its decision-making process prior to deployment, nor the functioning of SMART’s underlying AI systems. Congress, and the public, deserve to know how AI systems were tested and how they will influence decisions before being deployed in safety critical systems.
The letter also raises concerns about reports that frontline aviation safety workers received only days of notice, or no notice at all, before deployment. With air traffic controllers already facing staffing pressures, the lawmakers stress that new technology must be introduced with adequate training and clear procedures for human oversight.
The lawmakers request answers in three areas:
- Safety testing: What evaluations were completed before deployment, how the system performs during severe weather or outages, and whether any safety review requirements were waived during the contracting process.
- Consultation and training: What input the FAA sought from airport authorities, air safety workers, and airlines; what training personnel received; and how the tool should influence decision-making.
- Evaluation and accountability: How the FAA will measure performance during the initial 90-day evaluation, what standards must be met before nationwide expansion, and who is responsible if a recommendation contributes to a safety incident.
The letter calls for a pause until lawmakers can better understand the FAA’s decision-making, rollout process, and evaluation plan. The co-leads emphasize that modernizing air traffic control must prioritize safety, transparency, and the expertise of the people responsible for keeping our skies safe.
title: McClain Delaney Leads Call with Ocasio-Cortez, Beyer, Mfume, Subramanyam, and Elfreth to Pause FAA’s AI Tool at Washington-Area Airports

Congresswoman Simon Introduces Legislation to Reduce Voting Barriers, Expand Voting Poll Access, and Protect Voters with Disabilities
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Last week, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12) introduced two bills to reduce voting barriers by improving accessibility for voters, especially older Americans and people with disabilities, and bolster election security. She joined Reps. Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), and Jamie Raskin (MD-08) in introducing The Accessible Voting Act; and she joined Reps. Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) and Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) in introducing The Dropbox Access Act.
The Accessible Voting Act would establish the Office of Accessibility within the Election Assistance Commission (EAC) to oversee state and local elections to ensure that voter accessibility needs are adequately met, by expanding the number of options to fairly cast ballots. The bill would also establish a website for National Voter Accessibility and fund a National Resource Center to further train election officials and poll workers on accessibility.
The Dropbox Access Act, would require states to provide in-person, secure, and clearly labeled ballot drop boxes in every county for federal elections. The bill would require counties to provide a minimum of one drop box per 20,000 voting-age residents and require that drop boxes are accessible 24 hours a day starting from 45 days before the election until polls close.
As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, Congresswoman Simon is committed to defending the civil rights of Americans with disabilities and has continuously opposed rollbacks of disability protections. She has introduced numerous pieces of legislation aimed at expanding accessibility in small businesses and public transportation, and she has pressed the Trump Administration on their failure to protect workers with disabilities.
“Our elders fought for our voting rights with blood, sweat, and tears – and yet too many people, particularly older Americans and Americans with disabilities, still face barriers to voting such as inaccessible polling locations or access to voter information. Both the Accessible Voting Act and Dropbox Access Act will improve voter accessibility for requesting mail-in ballots, accessing voter registration info, and when showing up to the ballot box,” said Rep. Simon. “As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, improving accessibility to ensure that all Americans can equally access resources and participate in society is a top priority of mine. I am proud to lead on these bills with Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon to ensure ALL individuals can equally participate in local and federal elections to make their rightful voices heard.”
“Our democracy thrives when every eligible voter is able to participate, and these bills will remove barriers that all too often make it more difficult for Americans to cast their ballots. I’ve seen how expanding accessibility and access to ballot boxes has improved voter turnout and engagement in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,” said Rep. Scanlon. “I’m proud to introduce these bills to advance more equitable and just voting policies for all Americans.”
“American democracy works best when all citizens can participate and vote, no matter where they’re from, what language they speak or whether they live with a disability,” said Rep. Raskin. “Our Accessible Voting Act strengthens access to the ballot box and addresses a wide range of systemic deficiencies, so no eligible voter is left alone to overcome barriers to casting a ballot.”
“The ability for everyone to have their voice heard is central to our American ideals—yet too often people with disabilities face unnecessary barriers in both registering to vote and casting their ballots, preventing them from fully participating in our democracy,” said Rep. Dean. “This legislation will help improve registration processes and eliminate barriers to voting, including by reauthorizing grants to improve voting accessibility for older Americans and those with disabilities. By breaking down these barriers, our communities can be better represented by every voice. I'm thankful to partner with Congresswoman Scanlon and Congressman Raskin to pass these essential bills.”
“We should be making it more accessible for Americans to vote, not harder,” said Rep. Garcia. “But the Trump administration and its Republican allies continue to attack voting rights and put up new barriers to the ballot box. That is why I am proud to once again co-lead the Dropbox Access Act, a practical bill to make sure voters have fair, accessible options to return their ballots. We should be protecting the right to vote, not suppressing it.”

HHS Recommends Science-Based Thresholds to Target Dangerous Enhanced Kratom Products
DEA takes action based on updated recommendation from HHS
WASHINGTON—OCTOBER 9, 2026—The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) provided a new recommendation to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) that establishes science-based thresholds for 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MGPI), potent opioid compounds associated with products marketed as kratom.
The Department of Justice today announced that DEA issued new Notices of Intent reflecting HHS’ updated scientific analysis and recommendations, including a new Notice of Intent for 7-OH and MGPI incorporating HHS’ recommended concentration and ratio thresholds.
Following a review of available scientific data and comments, HHS Assistant Secretary for Health Admiral Brian Christine, M.D., recommended that DEA use concentration or ratio-based thresholds to determine which products containing 7-OH and MGPI are subject to Schedule I control for purposes of temporary scheduling of these substances under the Controlled Substances Act.
The recommendation is designed to target concentrated or chemically altered products while distinguishing them from natural botanical kratom products, which may contain trace amounts of 7-OH and MGPI.
“We are drawing a clear line between natural kratom and dangerous, enhanced opioid products,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “We listened to the public, followed the science, and developed a clear recommended threshold for temporary scheduling that targets concentrated 7-OH and MGPI without sweeping natural botanical kratom into Schedule I. The Trump Administration will continue taking decisive action against dangerous products that fuel addiction while making sure our policies are grounded in rigorous science.”
Under the recommendation, 7-OH and MGPI would be controlled in Schedule I for purposes of temporary scheduling when either substance alone, or their combined amount when both are present:
- Exceeds 1 milligram per gram in solid powders, encapsulated material, or other solid forms, or exceeds 1 milligram per milliliter in liquid preparations; or
- When the mass of mitragynine present divided by the mass of 7-OH, or MGPI, or the combined amount of 7-OH and MGPI if both present, is less than 100.
The ratio-based approach reflects the alkaloid composition of natural kratom products and provides a way to identify products intentionally enhanced or concentrated with 7-OH or MGPI. Available scientific data indicate that 7-OH occurs naturally in botanical kratom at relatively low or trace levels, while some evidence reviewed by FDA suggests MGPI may also occur at trace levels in some natural or kratom-derived products.
FDA's scientific review found that 7-OH is substantially more potent than morphine in preclinical studies, with available data indicating approximately two to nine times greater potency depending on the study. FDA also identified evidence supporting a meaningful risk of opioid-like physical dependence and withdrawal from MGPI.
“Our recommendation gives DEA a scientifically supportable framework to distinguish natural botanical kratom from products that have been concentrated or manipulated to deliver dangerous levels of potent opioid compounds,” said Assistant Secretary for Health Admiral Brian Christine, M.D. “This approach allows us to focus on the products that pose the greatest threat to public health.”
In July 2025, following an FDA scientific and medical evaluation, HHS recommended that 7-OH above a specified threshold be placed in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act. In July 2026, DEA announced its intent to temporarily schedule 7-OH above a specified threshold, and HHS simultaneously sought public comment on the proposed threshold.
DEA subsequently temporarily placed MGPI and two synthetic 7-OH derivatives, MGM-15 and MGM-16, in Schedule I. Since then, questions have emerged about how scheduling could affect natural botanical kratom products potentially containing trace amounts of MGPI.
The new HHS recommendation responds to those concerns by providing DEA with a more precise threshold based on both the concentration of 7-OH and MGPI and their relationship to mitragynine, the predominant alkaloid in kratom.
HHS and FDA will continue working with DEA to protect Americans from dangerous concentrated and synthetic opioid products while ensuring federal policy is grounded in the best available science.
