99 Democratic Lawmakers Slam Department of Education for Failure to Enforce Title IX and Protect Student Survivors
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Democratic Women’s Caucus (DWC) member Maxine Dexter (OR-03), DWC member Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), DWC Chair Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) and Rep. Mark Takano (CA-41) led a letter to the Office of the Inspector General at the Department of Education. The letter urges the Acting Inspector General to open an investigation into the Department’s gutting of the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) and Title IX rollbacks and its impact on the Department’s ability to enforce Title IX protections for student survivors of sexual assault and harassment. 99 House Democrats joined the effort.
The call for the investigation comes after Jane Doe’s story from Cornell University and Kendall Francis’ story from Louisiana State University (LSU) sparked a national outcry about the high rate of sexual violence on college campuses. Additionally the survivors’ stories have renewed scrutiny of how colleges and universities respond, and how the Department of Education enforces Title IX protections for survivors.
One in four undergraduate women experience sexual assault or rape while in college. Sexual violence against women on college campuses is a public health crisis, yet significant barriers remain that block accountability and protections for students. Changes in staffing, resources, case-processing, and enforcement priorities under the Trump administration have only made that worse and have undermined the Department’s ability to properly investigate complaints and enforce Title IX protections.
As of January 2025, OCR reportedly faced a backlog of nearly 12,000 civil rights cases, while the administration reduced OCR’s workforce by nearly half. The Department has closed zero college sexual harassment or sexual violence cases. The Department also formalized weaker protections and processes for student survivors: narrowing the definition of sexual harassment, reducing school liability, and implementing intimidating investigative and hearing procedures that are retraumatizing to survivors.
Without proper federal enforcement and institutional accountability, Title IX protections become just words on a page. The Department of Education is failing student survivors. Protections for survivors are not partisan and should always be a priority, however the Department’s rollback of vital protections creates additional barriers for survivors and is leaving them to fend for themselves in their most vulnerable moments.
In their letter, the members explained how the Department’s changes will leave student survivors vulnerable and why an investigation is necessary:
“We urge the Office of Inspector General to immediately open an investigation into the Department’s failure to adequately enforce Title IX protections for survivors of sexual harassment and assault, including whether changes in staffing, resources, case-processing, and enforcement priorities have undermined the Department’s ability to protect students, investigate complaints in a timely manner, and hold institutions accountable.”
The members outlined the Department’s policies that have weakened protections for student survivors:
“At the same time that OCR’s staff and regional capacity were substantially reduced, the Department announced and pursued Title IX enforcement priorities concerning transgender students’ participation in athletics and access to sex-separated facilities, and also dismantling Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) programs. These reprioritizations do nothing to address the backlog of sexual violence cases.”
The letter also explains how reprioritizations and restructuring by the Department have decreased OCR’s capacity to investigate cases of sexual violence on campus:
“This restructuring threatens to further delay investigations, erode OCR’s institutional expertise, and create additional barriers for survivors seeking accountability. These reprioritizations, staff reductions, and the interagency agreement raise significant questions about whether OCR has sufficient capacity to investigate Title IX complaints, communicate with complainants, and fulfill its civil rights enforcement responsibilities in a timely and effective manner.”
The members also outlined what they are urging the Inspector General to investigate:
- Examining whether the Department has fulfilled its legal and administrative responsibilities to investigate and resolve Title IX complaints in a timely and effective manner.
- The causes and consequences of the absence of resolution agreements involving college sexual harassment and assault complaints since January 2025.
- Whether reductions in OCR staffing, the closure of regional offices, or changes in enforcement priorities have contributed to delays, backlogs, or failures to resolve these complaints.
- Examining whether OCR has sufficient staffing, resources, policies, and procedures to effectively enforce Title IX and protect students from sex discrimination, including sexual harassment and violence.
- Identifying how survivors have been harmed by these changes.
Lastly, the members asked the Inspector General to answer the following questions:
- How many Title IX sexual harassment and sexual violence complaints are currently pending before OCR, and how long have they been pending?
- How have processing times, case closures, investigations, and resolution agreements changed since January 2025?
- Have staffing reductions or office closures affected OCR’s ability to investigate complaints or communicate with survivors?
- Have Department officials directed, formally or informally, OCR personnel to deprioritize certain categories of Title IX complaints?
- What safeguards are currently in place to ensure Title IX complaints involving sexual violence receive timely and appropriate review?
- What corrective actions are necessary to ensure the Department is meeting its obligations to protect students under Title IX?
Read the full letter here.

Reps. Tlaib, Correa reintroduce resolution honoring Alex Odeh
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Lou Correa (CA-46) today reintroduced a resolution remembering and honoring the life and legacy of Alex Odeh. The resolution acknowledges Alex’s impact on his community and the country, and reaffirms the importance of pursuing justice against those responsible for his death.
“Alex Odeh was a teacher, a poet, and a man of peace, and he was murdered in our community simply for speaking up for civil and human rights,” said Correa. “He was a voice for peace and dignity in Orange County. Remembering him is the least we can do, and pursuing justice for his family is our obligation.”
Rep. Correa represents the district where Alex and his family lived and where the attack took place.
“Alex Odeh dedicated his life to achieving true equality and equity for all. For daring to push for a better tomorrow, Alex was assassinated by members of the Jewish Defense League, and his killers have yet to be brought to justice,” said Tlaib. “This horrific act of anti-Arab and anti-Palestinian violence was, and is not, new. But this violence will never silence us. Those who continue to fear-monger and incite hate against us will not win. Arab and Palestinian Americans are still here, loud and proud, carrying on Alex’s legacy.”
Read the bill text here.
About Alex Odeh
Alex was born in Jifna, Palestine, and lived in Orange County, California, for most of his adult life, including Santa Ana. He was a peace activist who worked to promote civil liberties for Arab-Americans in the United States. Alex Odeh was the Southern California Regional Director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC).
On October 11, 1985, Alex was killed when a pipe bomb exploded as he entered the ADC regional office in Santa Ana, California. Although the primary suspects have long been known, no one has been brought to justice. The investigation remains open.

Ranking Member Scott Calls on Watchdog to Investigate Whether or Not HHS Lied in Litigation
WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (D-VA-03) urged the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Inspector General to investigate HHS’s potential submission of inconsistent or fraudulent information in active litigation.
On February 6, 2025, Ranking Member Scott called on the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) to assess the security of HHS's information technology (IT) systems after reports that Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) accessed data from various government agencies. However, HHS has refused to comply with GAO’s requests, citing potential discrepancies between what was produced in litigation and would be provided to GAO.
Furthermore, during the Committee’s oversight hearing on April 17, 2026, Secretary Kennedy could not provide a clarification when questioned by Ranking Member Scott whether the Department is providing false or inaccurate information in litigation and failed to follow up with information on the matter.
“On May 17, 2026, I wrote to Secretary Kennedy to follow-up and request a detailed explanation about what the Department meant when it informed GAO that it could not cooperate or accommodate an observational walkthrough, artifacts, screenshots, and other documentation out of concern for discrepancies with what HHS produced in litigation and what it would provide to GAO, and whether HHS did provide false, incomplete, or inaccurate information in litigation.6 I have given the Department ample opportunity to respond to my requests and refute the assertion that it has provided misinformation to one or more courts and yet have received no response to date,” wrote Ranking Member Scott.
“Accordingly, given the serious nature of the allegation, I request the Office of Inspector General to initiate an investigation immediately of whether HHS has provided false, incomplete, or inaccurate information, materials, items, or other documentation in litigation since January 20, 2025.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05), was joined by Congressman Greg Landsman (OH-01) and Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01) to introduce the Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act, bipartisan legislation to reauthorize $1 billion in funding to help school districts across the country replace traditional school buses with electric bus alternatives. Specifically, the legislation would provide $1 billion for the Clean School Bus program at the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
Every day, 20 million children and thousands of bus drivers breathe polluted air during their commute to school, which negatively impacts student health and attendance, particularly for students with asthma and other respiratory conditions. The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act addresses this challenge by providing school districts with grants to invest in bus replacement, charging infrastructure, and workforce development.
“Since I came to Congress in 2019, I have advocated for clean school bus funding. As an educator with over a decade of classroom experience, I know how damaging diesel exhaust can be for student well-being and learning. The consequences of diesel emissions extend to our environment, exacerbating the effects of greenhouse gas emissions. The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act will help to provide cleaner and healthier air for school children in Connecticut and across the country, support clean energy jobs, and protect our environment for decades to come,” said Congresswoman Hayes.
“School buses that run on clean energy have a major impact on the environment, and they save money for our school districts. The Clean School Bus Act is an important investment in our education system that will keep our kids and our communities safe for years to come”, said Congressman Landsman.
“Getting students to and from school safely and reliably is a priority for families and school districts across Georgia. By extending the Clean School Bus Program, this legislation will give schools greater certainty as they plan for the future, replace aging buses, and make transportation decisions that best meet the needs of their communities. I’m proud to co-lead this bipartisan effort to help ensure our schools have the tools they need to keep students moving safely and reliably,’ said Congressman Carter.
The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act builds on efforts led by Congresswoman Hayes since her first time in Congress.
- In 2019, Congresswoman Hayes introduced the Clean School Bus Act to establish a grant program authorized for up to $1 billion over five years for school districts, particularly those with lower-income students, to replace diesel school buses with electric school buses.
- In 2021, Congresswoman Hayes introduced the Clean Commute for Kids Act to invest $25 billion to replace existing diesel buses with electric buses.
- Congresswoman Hayes fought for clean school bus funding in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, signed into law in 2021. This led to the inclusion of over $5 billion for the EPA to administer rebates, grants, and contracts to replace a portion of the nearly 500,000 school buses with more environmentally safe models.
- In 2023, Congresswoman Hayes joined her colleagues to urge President Biden to include at least $300 million in additional funding for clean school buses in his FY24 budget request.
- In June of 2023, The Congresswoman joined Brenda Mallory, Chair of the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) and other officials to announce the award of 25 zero-emission school buses to DATTCO Inc. to provide school transportation services for the Connecticut Technical Education and Career System (CTECS).
- In 2024, the EPA announced 67 recipients for the first Clean School Bus Program Grants Competition. The grants help awardees purchase over 2,700 clean school buses in 281 school districts across 36 states including Connecticut. The Congresswoman released the following statement.
- During Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations, Congresswoman Hayes led over 120 of her colleagues to request $300 million for the Clean School Bus program.
The Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act is endorsed by the American School Bus Industry Coalition which includes Blue Bird, First Student, Beacon Mobility, National Express, Highland, Greenpower Motor Company, National School Transportation, Student Transportation of America, and IC Bus. Additional endorsers include the American Bus Association, American Asthma and Allergy Foundation (AAFA), League of Conservation Voters, Moms Clean Air Force, Sierra Club, Union of Concerned Scientists, and World Resources Institute’s (WRI) Electric School Bus Initiative.
“Reauthorizing the Clean School Bus Program is important to American manufacturing, American workers, our nation’s school children and local communities throughout the country. As Americans, we can take pride in the fact that almost all school buses sold in the United States, including electric school buses, are also manufactured in the United States by American workers. The school bus industry has seen great enthusiasm and increased demand for alternative fuel and zero-emissions school buses from parents and school districts, and the Clean School Bus Program has significantly expanded access to these vehicles. On behalf of U.S. school bus manufacturers, and private school bus operators, the American School Bus Industry Coalition commends Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Greg Landsman and Rep. Buddy Carter for the bipartisan introduction of a five-year reauthorization bill that will positively benefit our nation’s kids.” – American School Bus Industry Coalition
Text of the Clean School Bus Reauthorization Act is available here.

ICYMI in HousingWire | HUD Action Ensures FHA Loans are for Americans Only
Following HUD Action, Homeownership Loans for Illegals and Non-Residents Drop
October 9, 2026
WASHINGTON - New data reveals Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loans for non-permanent residents and illegals fell from 6% to nearly zero after the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development revoked their eligibility in May 2025.
“President Trump promised to put Americans first, and HUD delivered,” said Secretary Turner. “We are preventing illegals and non-residents from accessing taxpayer-backed programs at the expense of American homebuyers. Today, that share is zero. Make no mistake — exploit our citizens, and HUD will act.”
Watch Secretary Turner break down what this means for Americans:
Learn more from HousingWire:
Changes to residency requirements for Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loans have sharply reduced the share of FHA purchase mortgages made to non-permanent residents, according to origination data from Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).
In March 2025, the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) issued Mortgagee Letter 2025-09 and Title I Letter 490, removing the “non-permanent resident” category from FHA’s Single Family Title I and Title II programs, effective May 25, 2025.
Before the policy changes took effect, non-permanent residents accounted for about 5.8% of FHA purchase originations and 5.6% of purchase mortgages across the broader market, according to ICE data shared with HousingWire. After the changes, their share of FHA purchase loans fell to about 0.1%, while their share of purchase mortgages across all loan types declined by 2.2 percentage points to 3.4%, the data shows.
“President Trump promised to put Americans first, and HUD delivered,” Secretary Scott Turner said in a statement. “We are preventing illegals and non-residents from accessing taxpayer-backed programs at the expense of American homebuyers. Today, that share is zero. Make no mistake — exploit our citizens, and HUD will act.”
Market-specific impacts
The changes have had a larger impact in some markets where non-permanent residents had previously represented a relatively significant share of FHA purchase activity.
ICE evaluated markets with the highest non-permanent resident alien share of purchase originations prior to the FHA policy change (measured from second-quarter 2024 through first-quarter 2025) and filtered to the 100 largest U.S. markets and 33 markets along the U.S. borders with Mexico and Canada.
Utah markets recorded some of the largest declines. In Salt Lake City, non-permanent residents accounted for 26% of FHA purchase originations before the changes, compared with 0.15% afterward (Q4 2025 to the present). In Provo, the share fell from 20% to less than 0.5%.
Florida markets also saw declines. In Orlando, the pre-policy share went from 16.1% to a post-policy share of 0.2%. Lakeland went from 13.6% to 0.16%, and both Cape Coral and Miami went from 10% to less than 1%.
Other markets also recorded significant declines. Raleigh‘s share fell from 11.1% to 0.8%, while San Jose’s fell from about 10% to 0%.
The data suggests that conventional lending has not fully offset the decline in FHA lending to non-permanent residents. ICE data shows that non-permanent resident volume across conventional prime conforming loans remained relatively stable rather than increasing by a comparable amount.
“This new policy has definitely had an impact on families that would have qualified before May 2025,” said Michael Brown, a Tennessee-based home loan specialist at Churchill Mortgage. “Many of these borrowers are doing conventional loans now because Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac permit lawful non-permanent residents to obtain financing.”
Brown said that non-QM loans are another option for non-permanent residents, but that the new policy limits affordable financing options. “Some of these non-permanent residents will end up having to put more money down, work on improving their credit scores to qualify, or simply will need to wait until they obtain permanent-resident status,” he said.
Isaac Schultz, a Michigan-based home loan specialist at Churchill Mortgage, echoed that the only options for non-permanent residents are conventional financing or “some flavor of non-qualified mortgage financing.”
“I am currently working on a loan in one such scenario, and it does make it far more difficult for the borrower to qualify. For better or for worse, that was the main desired result of the policy change,” Schultz said.
Home price declines
It is unclear whether the declines have affected affordability, but most markets in the ICE dataset recorded lower prices after the policy changes took effect, according to HousingWire Data.
In Salt Lake City, the median list price for a single-family home ranged from $619,900 to $795,000 from Q2 2024 through Q1 2025. From Q4 2025 to the present, prices ranged from $620,000 to $742,450.
In Provo, the median list price ranged from $630,000 to $877,400 from Q2 2024 through Q1 2025, compared with $589,900 to $699,950 from Q4 2025 to the present.
Prices also shifted in Florida markets. In Orlando, the median list price ranged from $490,000 to $544,950 before the policy change, then dropped to a range of $489,000 to $525,000 afterward.
The change appeared to have no impact on prices in Lakeland, where they ranged from $350,000 to $374,999 before the change, and from $357,000 to $375,000 afterward. In Cape Coral, however, prices ranged from $475,000 to $510,000 before the policy changes, compared with $420,000 to $467,450 afterward.
In Raleigh, the median list price for a single-family home ranged from $579,900 to $699,000 before the change, but later dropped to $522,000 to $624,900.
San Jose, one of the nation’s most expensive markets, saw a smaller shift. The median list price for a single-family home there ranged from $1.56 million to $1.70 million from Q2 2024 through Q1 2025. From Q4 2025 to the present, prices ranged from $1.498 million to $1.70 million.

Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

October 9, 2026

Political reconciliation talks between the interim Venezuelan government and 2015 National Assembly representatives are producing tangible reforms in civil liberties and political rights, laying the groundwork for credible elections and a democratic transition. Two rounds of talks have already taken place, producing significant results: a wholesale reform and reconstruction of an independent Venezuelan Supreme Court, the restoration of access to more than 70 previously blocked internet domains, and the reform of a key repressive law. The interim government has also released more than 1,000 political prisoners and announced the release of nearly 200 more.

The talks bring together representatives of Venezuela’s 2015 National Assembly, led by its President Dinorah Figuera, and representatives of the interim government, led by current National Assembly President Jorge Rodríguez. The 2015 National Assembly was Venezuela’s last democratically elected legislative body recognized by all Venezuelan political parties and by the international community.

The delegations held two rounds of talks in Caracas in August and September, with another round scheduled to begin October 14. The parties have decided to remain in session to maintain the momentum they have achieved.

The United States supports this Venezuelan-led process to create the conditions for a peaceful democratic transition, which is only possible because of President Trump’s bold leadership. Early accomplishments include the following:

Rebuilding an Independent Supreme Court:

Following the talks, the 2026 National Assembly published a law reforming the Supreme Court selection process, with 32 new judges to be selected by December. The Supreme Court will adjudicate any challenges to Venezuela’s future election results, underscoring the importance of a credible selection process.

The talks led to the creation of a seven-member Credentials Council, an unprecedented all-judge body that will screen candidates and send only qualified jurists to the Judicial Nominations Committee. Importantly, the 2015 National Assembly chose a majority of the Council.

The Judicial Nominations Committee, made up of 11 current National Assembly members and 12 civil society members, will choose the 32 nominees from the Credentials Council’s approved list.

This selection process increases transparency and enshrines protections to ensure the new judges will be qualified and not tied to the Maduro regime.

Expanding Freedom of Expression:

The interim government has restored or partially restored access to more than 70 previously blocked internet domains, including El Tiempo , EFE , Revista Semana , El Pitazo , Efecto Cucuyo , among others.

Reforming Repressive Laws:

The National Assembly established a commission to reform and decriminalize penalties contained in the repressive 2017 Law Against Hatred, which was notorious for its use by the Maduro regime to jail opposition leaders and those who spoke out against the regime.

The law established penalties of up to 20 years in prison for the “promotion or incitement of hatred, discrimination, or violence,” although in practice it was used to punish criticism of the regime.

Releasing Political Prisoners:

The interim government has released over 1,000 political prisoners since Operation Absolute Resolve. Since the political reconciliation talks began in August, the interim government has announced the release of an additional 177 political prisoners, an important step toward restoring fundamental political freedoms.

Prominent political prisoners released since January 3 include Juan Pablo Guanipa, advisor to Maria Corina Machado and former First Vice President of the National Assembly; Freddy Superlano, ex-gubernatorial candidate and former National Assembly member; and Enrique Márquez, ex-presidential candidate and former Vice President of the National Electoral Council.

Exiled opposition figures Claudia Macero and Omar González Moreno, who fled the threat of detention due to political motivated charges, have also returned to Venezuela.

What Comes Next

The third round of reconciliation talks is scheduled to begin October 14. The delegations will focus on finalizing the Supreme Court selection process and providing individuals and political parties participation guarantees necessary for credible elections.

Future rounds of dialogue will address reform of the National Electoral Council, repealing remaining repressive laws, and opening political space so all political parties and leaders can return and participate in political life.

We welcome the joint efforts with Venezuela’s interim government to recover the gold in the United Kingdom.

The Trump Administration will continue to support this Venezuelan-led process as it moves from dialogue to durable democratic institutions.

For media inquiries, please contact the Office of the Spokesman.

A North Hollywood man was sentenced today to 70 months in federal prison for his role in a series of fraud schemes that caused nearly $5 million in losses to federal COVID 19 relief and small business lending programs.
Sarkis Sarkisyan, a.k.a. “Samuel Shaw,” 38, of North Hollywood, was sentenced by United States District Judge Cynthia Valenzuela.
Sarkisyan pleaded guilty on April 29 to two counts of wire fraud and one count of transactional money laundering arising from his fraudulent application for a $786,457 Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan and a subsequent $25,000 laundering transaction. In addition, the government’s investigation revealed that he also orchestrated additional fraud involving Small Business Administration (SBA) Preferred Lender Program loans totaling more than $4 million, as well as attempted to obtain two Economic Injury Disaster Loans of $500,000 each.
According to court records, Sarkisyan fabricated businesses, payrolls, IRS tax forms, and financial records to obtain federally backed loans intended to support legitimate small businesses during the COVID 19 pandemic. He and his co schemers then transferred the proceeds through shell companies and associates to conceal the origin of the illicit funds.
In total, Sarkisyan and his co-schemers received $4,866,457 in fraudulently obtained loan proceeds, most of which ultimately benefited him personally.
Sarkisyan “participated in a massive scheme to defraud multiple banks and, ultimately, taxpayers, out of almost $5 million in funds from lending programs designed to benefit small businesses and those in need during the COVID-19 pandemic,” prosecutors argued in their sentencing memorandum. His scheme “involved fabricating out of whole cloth businesses to make them appear legitimate entities whose funds taxpayers would expect to be an engine for the greater economy or in need of dire assistance during the pandemic,” and by doing so, defendant “exploited the goodwill of lenders and taxpayers.”
A deferred restitution hearing is set for December 4.
SBA-OIG, IRS Criminal Investigation, and HSI are investigating this matter.
Assistant United States Attorneys Andrew M. Roach and David C. Lachman of the Major Frauds Section are prosecuting this case.
title: North Hollywood Man Sentenced to Over 5 Years in Federal Prison for COVID-19 Fraud

Department of Justice Announces Updates to Emergency Scheduling Actions for 7-OH and Related Opioid Substances
The Department of Justice today announced updated emergency scheduling actions targeting 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and three potent opioid substances related to 7-OH: mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MGPI), MGM-15, and MGM-16.
“Dangerous and addictive opioids do not belong behind convenience store counters,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Our nation’s children and communities deserve protection from harmful substances like 7-OH and other powerful synthetic drugs. The actions taken by the Department of Justice today reflect our commitment to keeping Americans safe and holding drug traffickers accountable.”
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is issuing two new Notices of Intent based on new scientific information and recommendations provided by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The updated HHS analysis supports a revised threshold approach for 7-OH and MGPI designed to distinguish products containing trace amounts of these substances from formulations that have been intentionally enhanced or concentrated.
The two Notices of Intent address:
- MGM-15 and MGM-16: DEA will reissue the Notice of Intent without changing the current scheduling approach for these substances.
- 7-OH and MGPI: DEA will issue a new Notice of Intent incorporating HHS' updated scientific recommendation for concentration and ratio thresholds applicable to both substances.
HHS recommended that 7-OH and MGPI be subject to Schedule I control when either substance alone, or their combined amount when both are present, exceeds 1 milligram per gram in solid products or 1 milligram per milliliter in liquid products, or when the ratio of mitragynine to 7-OH, MGPI, or their combined amount is less than 100 to 1. HHS recommended this approach to better distinguish products intentionally enhanced or concentrated in these opioid substances from products whose alkaloid composition is more consistent with botanical kratom.
The updated HHS analysis confirms that 7-OH occurs naturally in botanical kratom at relatively low levels and identifies additional scientific information suggesting MGPI may also occur at trace levels in some botanical or kratom-derived products. HHS noted that the science concerning the presence of MGPI continues to develop but recommended applying a threshold approach to both 7-OH and MGPI.
DEA temporarily placed MGPI, MGM-15, and MGM-16 into Schedule I on August 26, 2026. Those controls will remain in effect during the new 30-day Notice of Intent period and until DEA issues a new temporary scheduling order.
For 7-OH, DEA had not yet issued a temporary scheduling order. DEA will reissue a new Notice of Intent reflecting HHS’ updated scientific recommendation.
Press Release Number: 26-1165
title: Department of Justice Announces Updates to Emergency Scheduling Actions for 7-OH and Related Opioid Substances

Medical Supply Company Owner Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison for $30M Medicare, TRICARE, and CHAMPVA Fraud
An Oklahoma business owner and chiropractor was sentenced yesterday to 14 years in prison for his role in a years-long scheme that attempted to bilk Medicare, TRICARE, and the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA) out of over $30 million for orthotics braces, continuous glucose monitors, and other durable medical equipment (DME) that beneficiaries did not want or need.
“Yesterday's 14-year sentence shows that health care fraud does not pay,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Department of Justice's National Fraud Enforcement Division. “The Department is committed to bringing to justice those who corrupt our health care system by paying illegal kickbacks, submitting false claims, deceiving programs that serve our seniors, service members, and veterans, and treating sensitive patient information like a commodity to be bought and sold.”
“Fraud against federal health care programs is a direct attack on the public’s trust and on the vulnerable individuals these programs are meant to protect, and the jury’s verdict and sentencing of Mark Loftis demonstrate that schemes of this kind will be met with decisive action and significant consequences,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General. “HHS-OIG will not hesitate to investigate and dismantle criminal conduct wherever it threatens the integrity of federal programs, and this case reflects the unwavering commitment of our agency and our law-enforcement partners to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure that those who defraud the government are held fully accountable.”
“Healthcare fraud drains millions of dollars from federally funded programs, and we all pay the price,” said Special Agent in Charge Rodney Crawford of the FBI Tampa Field Office. “Today’s sentence underscores the FBI’s steadfast commitment to aggressively pursuing those who engage in kickback schemes and other fraudulent practices.”
“As the law enforcement arm of the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General, the Defense Criminal Investigative Service (DCIS) is committed to safeguarding the integrity of the TRICARE program,” said Acting Special Agent in Charge Nakia M. Alexander of the DCIS Southeast Field Office. “This investigation is an example of a healthcare fraud scheme that directly affected American service members and their families. I applaud the collaborative work of the investigative agencies and the Department of Justice that led to today’s sentencing.”
“Fraud schemes targeting VA programs and services compromise their integrity and divert funds from veterans who rely on these benefits,” said Inspector General Cheryl L. Mason, Department of Veterans Affairs. “The VA OIG works every day with our law enforcement partners to identify fraudsters and hold them accountable.”
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Dr. Mark Loftis, 39, of Cushing, Oklahoma, and his co-conspirators did not disclose to Medicare the ownership and management of the DME company Back Pain Home Supplies LLC dba EZ Medical Supply. Loftis and his co-conspirators hid from Medicare that unenrolled entities were billing claims through the DME company. Lofits paid over a million dollars in illegal kickbacks, including through a shell marketing company, to marketers, purported telemedicine companies, and a call center that persuaded elderly and disabled Americans to disclose their personal information and receive DME they did not need. Loftis and his co-conspirators also purchased sham doctors’ orders for orthotic braces, continuous glucose monitors, and DME that were generated by telemedicine doctors and nurse practitioners who never examined, and often never spoke to, the beneficiaries. Loftis and his co-conspirators submitted over $30 million in false and fraudulent claims and were paid over $8 million. Loftis and his co-conspirators frequently billed for multiple orthotic braces at a time, including in one example eight braces for a single beneficiary.
After a 12-day jury trial ending in July 2026, Loftis was convicted of conspiracy to commit health care fraud and wire fraud. In addition to the prison sentence, Loftis was ordered to pay over $8 million in restitution and to forfeit over $560,000.
HHS-OIG, FBI, DCIS, and VA-OIG investigated the case.
Assistant Deputy Chief Catherine Wagner and Trial Attorney Raymond Beckering III of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Health Care Fraud Section prosecuted the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. More information can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal-fraud/health-care-fraud-unit.

Op-Ed: Health care premiums continue to rise. Congress can lower them
By Rep. Joe Courtney (Published in the Day, October 9th, 2026)
Last month, Connecticut’s state insurance department officially approved an 11.3% average rate increase in 2027 for state-regulated, individual and small business health care coverage plans.
This double-digit increase, far above an already high general inflation rate, has justifiably been met with deep frustration from both individual patients and health care plan administrators, with small businesses in particular feeling the squeeze.
It is clear from the persistent high trajectory of the state insurance department rate increases that the mounting cost of health care is creating a burden that will not be sustainable over the long term. It is time for policy makers to stop this trend by digging deeper into these decisions to identify which health services are spiking in cost.
The 2026 rate decision could not be clearer. A leading driver of this year’s health care premium increase is prescription drug cost increases. According to the Connecticut Department of Insurance, 30% of a Connecticut health care premium dollar is consumed by prescription drug costs. This amount has doubled since 2010.
That trend screams out for action, not just in Hartford, but also in Washington, where over the last four years, real reductions in drug costs have been achieved because of Medicare price negotiations.
Along those lines, I am a co-sponsor of the Lowering Drug Costs for American Families Act (H.R. 6166), which would empower the Medicare program to negotiate with pharmaceutical companies for lower prescription drug costs, not just for Americans 65 and older, but for all Americans on employer-based plans and individual ACA marketplace plans (Access Health CT here in Connecticut).
This bill builds on the price negotiation success of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, which by law has saved both patients and Medicare billions. As a result of price negotiations, the diabetes drug Januvia saw its price lowered from $527 to $113, blood thinners Eliquis and Xarelto went from $521 to $231 and $517 to $197, respectively, and the Asthma and COPD drug Trelegy went from $654 to $175, to name just a few.
Expanding drug price regulation has strong public support. At least two-thirds of U.S. adults across all parties, including 68% of Republicans, say that there is not enough government regulation when it comes to the price of prescription drugs, according to 2026 polling by KFF.
Even President Trump and Congressional Republicans clearly recognize the success and popularity of drug price negotiation.
In 2025, when they cut nearly $1 trillion from the Medicaid program in their so-called “Big Beautiful Bill” (H.R. 1) and allowed Affordable Care Act marketplace (Access Health CT) premiums to skyrocket for middle-class Americans, Trump and the GOP very carefully left the Biden-era Medicare drug price negotiation in intact.
What about Trump Rx, the three-year deal with big pharma, you might ask? A close look at the Trump Rx portal that claims to provide lower drug prices in most cases recycles drug coupons for discounted prices that already exist.
In addition, Americans are only able to use Trump Rx to purchase drugs outside of their commercial health plans, meaning it does nothing to lower Connecticut premium rates. After three years, the Trump Rx deal expires, unlike the statutory permanence of the 2022 law that will expand the list of drugs subject to price reduction.
It is very clear, to lower Connecticut health care premiums, Congress should pass the Lowering Drug Costs for American Families Act into law and create cost-saving parity for working age Americans on par with Medicare. It’s simple and it will work.
title: Op-Ed: Health care premiums continue to rise. Congress can lower them

Minnesota Woman Convicted in $3.6M Scheme to Defraud Medicaid Housing Services Program
A federal jury in St. Paul convicted a Minnesota woman yesterday for executing a scheme to steal $3.6 million from the now-defunct Minnesota Medicaid Housing Stabilization Services (HSS) Program.
“The Fraud Division has arrived in Minnesota — and we are here to stay,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “The jury’s guilty verdict in this case sends a clear message that those who steal from programs meant to help our most vulnerable will be held accountable. As proven at trial, Meadows falsified records to enrich herself while preventing critical services from reaching those in need. Her fraud scheme — and others like it — forced Minnesota’s Housing Stabilization Services Program to shut down entirely after costs of the program outran estimates by four thousand percent. I commend the dedicated prosecutors, agents, and support staff who worked tirelessly to deliver justice in this case.”
“The defendant chose to defraud millions from a program meant to help vulnerable Minnesotans,” said U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota. “My office is committed to prosecuting those who steal from the American taxpayer.”
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Sharmaine Meadows, 45, of Lake Elmo, Minnesota, orchestrated a scheme to bill the HSS Program for housing services that were meant to transition the unhoused and assist them in sustaining that housing. Instead, these services were not actually provided. The HSS Program permitted providers to bill up to 150 hours for transitional services and 150 hours for sustaining services per eligible Medicaid beneficiary. Meadows routinely emphasized to her employees that they were required to maximize the billings to that 150-hour cap, even if the hours of services were never provided.
Agenda from Meadows’ company staff meeting in July 2022 at which “Maximizing of Hours” was discussed
The evidence presented at trial also proved that Meadows and her company billed the HSS Program for in-person hours supposedly provided by employees who were in other states, like Illinois, and in other countries, like the Philippines, where the defendant paid only $6.00 per hour and explicitly offered no benefits.
Employment Offer Letter from Meadows’ Company to Individual in the Philippines
She also submitted claims for services that could not have been provided because beneficiaries were in the hospital. And through data analysis, evidence showed that Meadows billed as if her employees were working more than 20 hours per day, every day, for weeks.
Summary of billing for “Impossible Days” by Meadows’ company Summaries of billing for “Impossible Days” by Meadows’ company
At the same time, Medicaid beneficiaries testified that they received little to no services from Meadows’ company. These beneficiaries testified that they were routinely told by Meadows’ employees that despite having received no assistance, they had run out of available hours in the HSS Program.
As a result of the fraud scheme, the HSS Program paid Meadows’ company over $3.6 million between 2020 and 2025 into accounts that Meadows exclusively controlled.
The jury convicted Meadows of three counts of health care fraud. She is scheduled to be sentenced at a later date and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on each count. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s Fraud Division; U.S. Attorney Daniel N. Rosen for the District of Minnesota; Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson of the FBI Minneapolis Field Office; Special Agent in Charge Thomas Ethridge of the Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG); and Special Agent in Charge Adam Jobes of the IRS Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Chicago Field Office, made the announcement
FBI, HHS-OIG, and IRS-CI investigated the case.
Trial Attorneys Brant Cook and Emily Reeder-Ricchetti of the Fraud Division’s Health Care Fraud Section, with the assistance of Health Care Fraud Section Trial Attorney Jody King and Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Murphy for the District of Minnesota, are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
The Department of Justice’s Health Care Fraud Strike Force Program, currently comprised of nine strike forces operating in federal districts across the country, has charged more than 6,200 defendants who collectively billed federal health care programs and private insurers more than $45 billion since 2007. In addition, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, working in conjunction with the Office of the Inspector General for the Department of Health and Human Services, are taking steps to hold providers accountable for their involvement in health care fraud schemes. FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
October 8, 2026
Contact: Jin.Choi@mail.house.gov
WASHINGTON — Congresswoman Nanette Barragán (CA-44) and Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, introduced a resolution recognizing October 8, 2026 as Latina Equal Pay Day and calling attention to the wage gap that shortchanges Latinas and their families. In 2025, Latinas with reported earnings were paid just 53 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic men.
“Latina Equal Pay Day is a reminder that equal work deserves equal pay,” said Rep. Barragán. “It is unacceptable that Latinas continue to face a significant wage gap compared to White, non-Hispanic men, despite decades of progress towards workplace equality. This disparity affects not only women, but American families, communities, and our economy. We must continue working to ensure every woman —regardless of her race or ethnicity— is valued fairly and paid equally for her work. Ha llegado el momento de que las latinas reciban igualdad de salarios!”
“Latinas work hard, care for our families, and keep our communities running. Yet our paychecks still do not reflect the value of our work,” said Congresswoman Leger Fernández. “When Latinas are underpaid, our families have less money for groceries, rent and child care—all things that have already been made more expensive by the Trump administration. But our contributions are not valued, and our value is not paid. Today, we recommit to closing the gender and racial wage gap. Ya basta. Latinas deserve equal pay TODAY. ”
More than six decades after the passage of the Equal Pay Act of 1963, the wage gap persists across sectors and education levels. Latinas working full time, year round were paid just 60 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic men. The gap widens to 53 cents when including workers with part-time and part-year earnings.
The resolution recognizes how the wage gap hurts women, families, and the economy and reaffirms Congress’ support for equal pay and closing the gender wage gap. It also highlights barriers that contribute to the disparity, including a lack of affordable child care and paid family and medical leave, as well as workplace harassment.
“Latinas are paid just 53 cents for every dollar paid to white, non-Hispanic men,” said Mónica Ramírez, Founder and President of Justice for Migrant Women. “We know first hand the consequences of this gap for ourselves and our families. We also recognize the work that is being done every day to change things for the better. That is why we are marking Latina Equal Pay Day this year with three words: Power. Pay. Progress. We are reflecting on the power that Latinas hold, the pay inequities that still exist, the progress that we have made in spite of this pay gap and the work that remains to ensure that Latinas are paid fully and fairly for our work.”
“Latinas face one of the largest wage gaps in the nation, earning just 53 cents for every dollar paid to their white non-Hispanic male counterparts. That should be an urgent call to action, not a statistic we simply acknowledge,” said Jessica Ramey Stender, Policy Director & Deputy Legal Director at Equal Rights Advocates. “At a time when the federal government is rolling back basic workplace protections and attacking the rights and economic security of Latinas and other women, we cannot afford to stand by as the wage gap widens. Nearly half of Latina mothers are breadwinners, meaning the wage gap doesn’t just shortchange Latina workers; it keeps many families in poverty with consequences across generations. We know what it takes to close the wage gap: stronger protections against pay discrimination, access to well-paying jobs, and policies that support working parents. We thank Rep. Leger Fernández and the Democratic Women’s Caucus for championing the rights of women and urge all lawmakers to take decisive action to close the wage gap.”
“53 cents and 11 years after the first Latina Equal Pay Day, Latinas remain among the lowest-paid workers in the country. For more than a decade, LCLAA has stood shoulder to shoulder with trabajadoras, fighting wage theft, harassment, retaliation, and pay inequity, while championing solutions like good union jobs that deliver real, tangible economic security,” said Karla Pineda, Executive Director of the Labor Council for Latin American Advancement (LCLAA). “As meaningful contributors in our homes, communities, and workplaces across every industry, we refuse to be overlooked, undervalued, and silenced. LCLAA has, is, and will continue to commit its efforts to help ensure that all workers– including working women in our comunidad– receive nothing short of what they deserve: dignity, equity, and the real opportunity to thrive rather than merely survive.”
Cosponsors include Representatives Ansari, Bonamici, Carbajal, Castor, Chu, Cisneros, Correa, Crockett, DeLauro, Espaillat, Jesús “Chuy” García, Sylvia R. Garcia, Gomez, Mejia, Menendez, Holmes Norton, Ramirez, Randall, Ruiz, Salinas, Tlaib, Vargas, Velázquez, and Wilson.
The resolution is endorsed by numerous organizations including the A Better Balance, AFL-CIO, American Association of University Women (AAUW), California National Organization for Women (CA NOW), Clearinghouse on Women’s Issues, Equal Rights Advocates, Equal Pay Today, Family Values @ Work, Feminist Majority Foundation, FL National Organization for Women, Institute for Women’s Policy Research, Justice for Migrant Women, Labor Council for Latin American Advancement (LCLAA), Legal Momentum, Minnesota Indian Women’s Resource Center, MomsRising, Montana Chapter of the National Organization for Women for Women, National Black Worker Center, National Council of Jewish Women, National Immigration Law Center, National Network to End Domestic Violence, National Organization for Women, National Partnership for Women & Families, National Women’s Law Center Action Fund, One Fair Wage, Oxfam America, Public Justice Center, Reproductive Freedom for All, Ujima, The National Center on Violence Against Women in the Black Community, Women Employed, WorkLife Law
The resolution can be found HERE.

Fact Sheet

Office of the Spokesman

October 8, 2026

The Iranian regime continues to intentionally disrupt global energy supplies, terrorize its regional neighbors, and employ violence and illegal measures to repress its own people. To sustain its destabilizing agenda, Iran depends on a shadow network of illicit shipping facilitators across multiple jurisdictions, who deliberately falsify documentation, disguise vessel identities, and evade international sanctions to smuggle Iranian oil, petroleum products, and petrochemical products to buyers in Asia.

Today under President Trump’s Operation Economic Outcast , the Department of State is further dismantling this illicit network and cutting off the Iranian regime’s ability to fund its malign activities. The Department of State is sanctioning ten entities, six individuals, and five vessels in connection with trade in Iranian-origin petroleum, petroleum products, and petrochemical products.

All Department of State targets are being designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13846 , which authorizes and reimposes certain sanctions with respect to Iran.

Sanctioning Traders of Iranian-Origin Petrochemical Products

Today’s action sanctions six entities involved in trading Iranian petrochemical products, as well as three principal executive officers tied to companies involved in this activity. These entities have channeled millions of dollars to the Iranian regime, bolstering one of its most critical revenue streams and enabling its continued illicit conduct. The U.S. government is imposing sanctions on both the buyers and sellers driving this trade in Iranian petrochemical products

NOORZAD PETROKIMYA URUNLERI NAKLIYE SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI ( NOORZAD PETROKIMYA ) is a Türkiye-based petrochemical trading company that imported and purchased approximately $3.8 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January and July 2024. SAID AHMAD NOORZAD ( NOORZAD ) is a Turkish national and the director and Chief Executive Officer of NOORZAD PETROKIMYA.

NOORZAD PETROKIMYA URUNLERI NAKLIYE SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

NOORZAD is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of NOORZAD PETROKIMYA.

ARABIANPRO MATERIALS FZCO is a United Arab Emirates-based petrochemical trading company that exported $2 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between February 2025 and July 2025.

ARABIANPRO MATERIALS FZCO is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED ( SSPL SOLUTIONS ) is an India-based petrochemical trading company that imported $2 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between February 2025 and July 2025. DHWANI NISARG VORA is an Indian national and a director of SSPL SOLUTIONS. NISARG SAMIR VORA is an Indian national and a director of SSPL SOLUTIONS.

SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

DHWANI NISARG VORA is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED.

NISARG SAMIR VORA is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SSPL SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED.

BGZ DIS TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI ( BGZ ) is a Türkiye-based petrochemical trading company that imported approximately $20 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January and September 2024, including $2 million from Iran-based PADIDEH PLASTIC POSHTIBAN COMPANY .

BGZ is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

PADIDEH PLASTIC POSHTIBAN COMPANY ( PADIDEH ) is an Iran-based petrochemical trading company that exported approximately $2 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between April and August 2024 to Türkiye-based BGZ .

PADIDEH is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

TUTER PLASTIK SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI is a Türkiye-based petrochemical trading company that imported approximately $3.5 million in Iranian-origin petrochemical products between January 2023 and August 2024.

TUTER PLASTIK SANAYI VE TICARET LIMITED SIRKETI is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

Continued Targeting of Iran’s Dark Fleet and Service Providers

The Department of State is also sanctioning one customs broker, two vessel management companies, and one registered owner for their involvement in providing Iran a maritime pathway for selling sanctioned petroleum and petrochemical products. Today’s action also blocks three principal executive officers of the customs broker which engaged in Iranian-origin petrochemical products trading. As part of this action, the Department is also identifying five vessels these companies own or manage as blocked property. These shipping companies and customs brokers operate within Iran’s larger illicit economy, helping the Iranian regime deliver its energy products to end buyers, evade sanctions, and generate revenue. The United States will not allow actors like these who enable the continued operation of the Iranian regime.

SAMUDRA MARINE SERVICES PRIVATE LIMITED ( SAMUDRA ) is an India-based customer broker that facilitated the import of multiple shipments of Iranian-origin petrochemical products to India. KETAN MANOHAR KOCHIKAR ( KOCHIKAR ) is an Indian national and a director of SAMUDURA. BHUPENDRASINGH DHALSINGH SAHU ( SAHU ) is an Indian national and a director of SAMUDRA. HARISHYAM HARIHARAN CHUNDAKATTIL ( CHUNDAKATTIL ) is an Indian national and a director of SAMUDRA.

SAMUDRA is being designated pursuant to Section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

KOCHIKAR is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or a person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SAMUDRA.

SAHU is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or a person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SAMUDRA.

CHUNDAKATTIL is being blocked pursuant to section 5(a)(vii) of E.O. 13846 as a principal executive officer, or a person performing similar functions and with similar authorities, of SAMUDRA.

ONE PLUS INTERNATIONAL CO LTD is the United Kingdom-based registered owner of YONG TAI (IMO 9231511). YONG TAI, a Gambia-flagged Oil Products tanker, loaded Iranian-origin methanol from Iran in December 2025. YONG TAI loaded Iranian-origin petrochemical products on at least twelve other occasions since 2024.

ONE PLUS INTERNATIONAL CO LTD is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(iii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petrochemical products from Iran.

YONG TAI is being identified as property in which ONE PLUS INTERNATIONAL CO LTD has an interest.

HORIZON SHIP MANAGEMENT FZE is the UAE-based commercial manager of YASHAR (IMO: 9129380), a Comoros-flagged LPG tanker that loaded Iranian-origin liquefied petroleum gas on at least three occasions between 2025 and 2026.

HORIZON SHIP MANAGEMENT FZE is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(ii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petroleum or petroleum products from Iran.

YASHAR is being identified as property in which HORIZON SHIP has an interest.

HESSONITE SHIP MANAGEMENT LLC ( HESSONITE ) is the UAE-based commercial manager of ARGO MARIS (IMO: 9041643), a Honduras-flagged Asphalt/Bitumen tanker that loaded sanctioned Iranian-origin petroleum products on at least eight occasions between January 2026 and August 2026. The other two tankers the company manages have also transported Iranian-origin petroleum products at least eight times during HESSONITE’s tenure as their commercial manager.

HESSONITE is being designated pursuant to section 3(a)(ii) of E.O. 13846 for knowingly engaging in a significant transaction for the purchase, acquisition, sale, transport, or marketing of petroleum or petroleum products from Iran.

ARGO MARIS is being identified as property in which HESSONITE has an interest.

BLACK MAYA (IMO: 9118800) is being identified as property in which HESSONITE has an interest.

ATHE NOVA (IMO: 9188116) is being identified as property in which HESSONITE has an interest.

SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS

As a result of today’s sanctions-related actions, and in accordance with E.O. 13846, all property and interests in property of the sanctioned persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.

All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt. These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov . Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro Charged with Torture
The Justice Department announced that former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro Moros and former First Lady of Venezuela Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro have been charged in a Superseding Indictment unsealed today with conspiring to commit torture, narcoterrorism, cocaine importation conspiracy, and weapons offenses.
“Since the capture and arrest of Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, the Department of Justice has been working to uncover the extent of their alleged crimes against the people of Venezuela and of the United States,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “These additional charges against the Maduros reflect the dedication of this Administration to delivering justice for the victims of torture, narcoterrorism, and organized crime.”
“As alleged in the indictment, the Maduro regime subjected American citizens to torture while held in custody of the Venezuelan government — including drugs, electric shock, sexual assault, and more,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “These charges follow the historic law enforcement-operation proudly supported by this FBI in January arresting Maduro and executing one of the most daring Foreign Transfers of Custody in United States history, returning him and his wife to the U.S. — an operation which required months of coordination, detailed planning, and seamless execution across multiple components of the federal government led by the Department of War. Today’s charges reflect the commitment from this FBI and this Department of Justice to accountability, the rule of law, and the protection of U.S. national security.”
“As alleged in today’s Superseding Indictment, for more than two decades, Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores De Maduro engaged in a conspiracy to commit torture, including the torture of United States citizens, in addition to the narcotics trafficking and weapons offenses already charged,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald for the Southern District of New York. “As described in the Superseding Indictment, the Maduros and other Venezuelan leaders abused their positions of trust to enrich themselves through narco-terrorism, cocaine trafficking, and other corruption, including by employing Venezuelan military, law enforcement, and other government entities under their control to flood the United States with illegal narcotics. Today’s indictment further alleges that the Maduros and other Venezuelan leaders conspired to repress dissent through grave violations of human rights by ordering and allowing violence, threats, and physical torture under color of law. As alleged, this included the torture of multiple United States citizens, who were subjected to unspeakable abuse. Today’s charges exemplify the tirelessness that we and our law enforcement partners will undertake to vindicate victims of crime, particularly American victims subjected to horrific treatment abroad.”
“Maduro’s regime is responsible for countless American victims of narcoterrorism and drug trafficking,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “Thanks to the leadership of President Trump, our Homeland Security Task Force partners, and strong coordination among DHS, DOJ, FBI, and DEA, we’re bringing Maduro and his wife to justice. President Trump is using all tools at his disposal to make America safe again both at home and abroad.”
“These indictments demonstrate that our work did not stop with the arrest of Nicolás Maduro, who terrorized the people of Venezuela for more than two decades,” said DEA Administrator Terry Cole. “DEA will continue to follow the evidence and pursue those who use corruption, violence, and positions of power to facilitate criminal activity and protect those who profit from it. Maduro’s arrest was an important step toward accountability, but it was not the last. We remain steadfast in our commitment to work with our partners to restore law and order across the Western Hemisphere and bring to justice any corrupt leader who thinks their political position shields them from consequences.”
For over 25 years, Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro abused their positions of public trust, enriching themselves through corruption and remaining in power through grave violations of human rights.
Through drug trafficking, the corrupt use of law enforcement and the military, the abuse of the judicial system, and the pilfering of public funds, Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other Venezuelan leaders personally benefited at the expense of the Venezuelan people. While this systemic corruption was immensely profitable for the defendants and their inner circle, it was deeply unpopular with the Venezuelan people. To undermine Venezuelan democracy and entrench themselves in power, these same leaders allegedly presided over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens. That torture included electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture, such as threats to harm and kill victims’ families.
Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro allegedly sat atop that violent power structure. They developed and facilitated the systems which they and their co-conspirators used corruptly to amass immense wealth and power, rewarding allies with ill-gotten funds and terrorizing perceived opponents through persecution and violence. These systems relied on Maduro Moros’s and Flores de Maduro’s control over Venezuela’s military, judiciary, and law enforcement agencies, and their partnerships with organized criminal groups, including terrorist organizations and groups of state-sponsored gangs known as colectivos.
In amassing such wealth and power, Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other members of their inner circle allegedly trafficked drugs under the protection of the Venezuelan military, judiciary, and law enforcement agencies. They allegedly partnered with narcotics traffickers and narco-terrorists from designated foreign terrorist organizations, including the Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia (FARC), the Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN), the Sinaloa Cartel, the Zetas, later known as the Cártel del Noreste (CDN), and Tren de Aragua (TdA), who dispatched cocaine from Venezuela to the United States via transshipment points in the Caribbean and Central America.
Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other high-ranking members of their inner circle also allegedly created and maintained a violent system of repression. Since at least 1999, thousands of Venezuelans have been harassed, threatened, arrested, prosecuted, assaulted, tortured, or killed by individuals wielding the purported authority of the Venezuelan state to ensure that Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro remained in power. Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro used military units, colectivos, and narco-terrorist groups involved in their drug trafficking to unlawfully detain and torture their victims. Such violence and repression increased around periods of political instability in which Maduro Moros’s and Flores de Maduro’s power was threatened. During these periods, Maduro Moros, Flores de Maduro, and other high-level Venezuelan officials jointly undertook efforts to stifle those who opposed, or were merely suspected of opposing, Maduro Moros or his regime. Those efforts included physical and psychological torture systematically used to terrify the populace and silence dissent.
In addition to Maduro Moros and Flores de Maduro, other high-level officials allegedly were integral to this system. One high-level Venezuelan official, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-1, ordered the murders of certain individuals who opposed Maduro Moros or his regime, oversaw torture undertaken by officials under his command, and personally threatened the murder of a prisoner’s child as a form of psychological torture. Another senior Venezuelan officer who reported directly to Maduro Moros, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-2, developed torture methods that he presented for approval to Maduro Moros, led an agency responsible for torturing scores of victims, and personally signed off on the unlawful arrest and torture of specific individuals. A third Venezuelan official, referred to in the Superseding Indictment as CC-3, personally ordered and participated in the torture of civilians and military members, including United States citizens, who were believed to pose a threat to Maduro Moros’s rule. For example, one particular United States citizen was detained in Venezuela and subjected to, among other things, deprivation of food and water, simulated drowning, repeated beatings, electric shock to his testicles, and forced injections.
The Superseding Indictment charges Maduro Moros, 63, and Flores de Maduro, 69, in Count One, with participating in a narcoterrorism conspiracy, which carries a 20-year mandatory minimum penalty and a maximum penalty of life in prison; in Count Two, with conspiring to commit torture, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; in Count Three, with conspiring to import cocaine into the United States, which carries a 10-year mandatory minimum penalty and a maximum penalty of life in prison; in Count Four, with using and carrying machine guns and destructive devices during and in relation to, and possessing machine guns and destructive devices in furtherance of, the narco-terrorism and cocaine-importation conspiracies, which carries a 30-year mandatory minimum penalty and a maximum penalty of life in prison; and in Count Five, with conspiring to use and carry machine guns and destructive devices during and in relation to, and to possess machine guns and destructive devices in furtherance of, the narco-terrorism and cocaine-importation conspiracies, which carries a maximum penalty of life in prison. The potential maximum penalties in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge.
This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by President Trump in Executive Order 14159. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders.
This case is being handled by the Office’s National Security and International Narcotics Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kaylan E. Lasky, Henry L. Ross, Kevin T. Sullivan, and Kyle A. Wirshba for the Southern District of New York are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from Trial Attorney Kevin Nunnally of the Counterterrorism Section of the National Security Division.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro Charged with Torture

Today, Congresswomen Suzan DelBene (WA-01) and Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) reintroduced the Strengthening Welfare in Marine Settings (SWIMS) Act, legislation that would end the future capture and breeding of whales for public display.
Certain cetaceans, such as orcas, beluga whales, pilot whales, and false killer whales, are cognitively, emotionally, and socially complex animals who cannot thrive in captivity, according to multiple studies. Whales held for display often exhibit signs of suffering and distress and have significantly shorter lifespans than whales in the wild. Currently, there are approximately 70 whales held in captivity in the United States.
The SWIMS Act would:
    - Prohibit the taking, importation, or exportation of these whales for public display.
- Prohibit any breeding of these whales for future public display.
- Allow exemptions for animals being transported to a sanctuary setting or released to the wild.
“Whales and dolphins are treasures to the Pacific Northwest, and they belong in the wild,” said DelBene. “Scientific evidence shows that when these majestic animals are kept in captivity, they suffer significant distress and shorter life spans. This legislation would prevent the capture and breeding of whales for public display to ensure they remain in their natural habitats and free from abuse and exploitation.”
“Whales belong in the open ocean, not behind glass,” said Dexter. “These extraordinary animals are icons of the Pacific Northwest, forming deep family bonds and playing a vital role in healthy oceans. Captivity robs them of the space, freedom, and connection they need to thrive. Their lives should be defined by the ocean’s possibilities, not the walls of a tank.” 
“Science increasingly supports the conclusion that we cannot provide conditions in a concrete enclosure that accommodate the size, wide-ranging nature, and physiological, behavioral, and social needs of these species,” said Dr. Naomi Rose, senior scientist for marine mammal biology at the Animal Welfare Institute. “The SWIMS Act recognizes that reality and offers a path forward by prohibiting breeding, trade, and capture for public display. Let this be the last generation in captivity of these ocean predators.”
The SWIMS Act is supported by the Animal Legal Defense Fund, Animal Welfare Institute, Born Free USA, Cetacean Society International, CompassionWorks International, Humane World Action Fund, Humane World for Animals, International Marine Mammal Project of Earth Island Institute, Last Chance for Animals, Oceanic Preservation Society, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine, Whale and Dolphin Conservation, Whale Sanctuary Project, and World Animal Protection.
