text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Kyriakos Mitsotakis, Greek Prime Minister

Maximos Mansion

Athens, Greece

October 7, 2026

PRIME MINISTER MITSOTAKIS: So I guess this photo may —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah.

PRIME MINISTER MITSOTAKIS: Yeah, this photo may ring some – yeah, ring some bells. (Laughter.)

SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, I – we don’t really have a site like that in America to provide so that’s about as close as it —

PRIME MINISTER MITSOTAKIS: Well, first of all, welcome, and congratulations on what was a very, very impressive speech I think that highlighted not just the historical bonds between our two countries, but also I think the debt that the rest of Europe owes to ancient Athens. And I do remember you pointed out in this photo that you were part of the welcoming committee when I had the opportunity to speak to a session of Congress and, at the time, speak about this common path between our two countries. And I’m so happy that at this point, our relationship (inaudible) are at an all-time high.

Greece is not just, I think, a pillar of stability in a turbulent region, but also a bridge between Europe, the West, the United States, the Middle East, and the Arab world, the GCC countries. And in that sense, yes, I would agree with you that we are an indispensable partner to the United States, and I’m happy that our relationship has also progressed beyond the traditional security and political partnerships that we have forged. Energy and connectivity are now so important in our bilateral relationship. So happy that Greece has invested significant resources into becoming an entry point for U.S. LNG into Europe. We are now a provider of energy security to our northern neighbors. But also the importance that we place on connectivity projects, the tremendous importance that Greek shipping plays in moving goods around. And of course, the common interest that we share in preserving the freedom of navigation, which is critical for the functioning of the world economy.

These are just some of the areas that we have in common. But I’m very happy that the strategic dialogue was able to touch upon all these issues. And again, welcome to Athens, and congratulations on a speech that I think will resonate way, way beyond the place it was delivered.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you. Firstly, thank you for the welcome. You’re okay? Thank you for your welcome and for this opportunity first to speak at such a historic setting. I never thought I’d get a chance to do that. And I thought it was important, but really, more than anything else, it builds on sort of the theme of our visit, which is the historic alliance between the United States and Greece, which is not just historic, it’s historical – it’s founded on very powerful pillars of shared culture, shared values, and it’s only grown, as you said. It’s extended beyond simply defense matters, which have always been something we’ve worked on, and even diplomatic matters, which we’ve always worked on. But now it’s extended to economics, to trade, to international maritime rights and security, to energy. And as you said, you’re – there are a lot of pillars of insecurity surrounding you in this region, but to have you here as such a strong partner of ours and to continue to build on that relationship in a way that’s mutually beneficial – I think there are things we can do on economics, on energy, on trade which are helpful to both the people of Greece and the people of the United States, and we’re always looking for those opportunities.

And the one thing I would say that defines our alliance – because sometimes the term “alliance,” it sounds like it’s just a diplomatic alliance. But one of the things that underpins our partnership – our very strong partnership – is that we agree on the same problems. We agree that we have the same problems that we’re worried about, and we more often than not agree on the right solution. So when you have partners like that – not to mention the strong historic links that are the foundation of our relationship – there’s a lot we’re excited about. And I’m happy to be here, and look forward to continue to build on this relationship.

PRIME MINISTER MITSOTAKIS: Thank you.

Congresswoman Scholten Statement on New Proposal to Narrow the Scope of the Clean Water Act
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03), Vice Ranking Member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment, released the following statement on the new proposal from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers that would narrow the scope of the Clean Water Act by redefining what qualifies as “Waters of the United States,” stripping protections from freshwater wetlands across Michigan and the country.
“Clean water should never be a partisan issue. Every family, every child, every individual deserves access to clean water – for drinking, for recreation, and for business. This unilateral move by the Trump Administration threatens to reverse decades of work and progress cleaning up our lakes, rivers, and wetlands. As Vice Ranking Member of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee, I’ve seen firsthand how the protections from the Clean Water Act keep our communities safe and have cleaned our waterways. Our children and our children’s children could be doomed to inherit polluted waterways–a problem we’ve already addressed and nearly solved. We cannot afford to go back.”
Earlier this year, Congresswoman Scholten published an article in the Harvard Law School Journal of Legislation titled “The Retreat of Cooperative Federalism: Water Rights in a Fragmented Regulatory Era.” The article argues that Congress must work with states to maintain baseline environmental protections, following decades of Supreme Court decisions — including Sackett v. EPA — that have weakened the Clean Water Act of 1972.

News Release
US Department of Labor cites Pennsylvania excavation employer for failing to provide trench protection following fatal trench cave-in
CHAMBERSBURG, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an excavation contractor for willful and serious safety violations after a young worker was fatally injured in a trench collapse.
The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an investigation into Jonas David Wagoner – doing business as J.D. Wagoner Excavating – on April 2, 2026, and found workers were installing a storm sewer system 12 feet below ground level in a trench that was not adequately protected from soil collapse. When a portion of the trench's wall failed, the unrestrained soil engulfed one worker. The agency issued a willful violation for failure to protect workers from cave-ins and two repeat violations for failing to assign a competent person to conduct daily trench inspections and removing employees from hazardous conditions.
In addition, the employer received three serious violations for failure to provide construction hazard prevention training to employees, establish a safe means for workers to exit the excavation site, keep materials at least two feet from the edge of an excavation site, and restrain side materials from becoming roll-in hazards.
OSHA proposed $254,884 in penalties.
The employer has 15 business days from receiving receipt of its citations and penalties to request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.
Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) and a group of 24 Members of Congress representing Northeastern states are pressing the Department of Energy (DOE) to take immediate action to address the rapidly rising cost of heating oil, which has surged around 60 percent since the start of President Trump’s war in Iran. In their letter—led by U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Representatives Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.) and Lori Trahan (D-Mass)—the lawmakers urged the DOE to support an immediate end to the war and prioritize lowering energy costs for the winter, warning that rising prices will force families to choose between heating their homes and paying for basic necessities.
“Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs,” wrote the lawmakers.
The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has pushed crude oil from $72 to over $100 a barrel, causing a massive increase in heating oil costs in the United States. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year. In Maine, which uses more residential heating oil per capita than any other U.S. state, the statewide average price of heating oil recently hit a record $6.02 a gallon—marking an 80% increase over last year.
In addition to jacking up the cost of heating oil, the Trump administration has made or attempted to make heating costs for the upcoming winter even higher by:
    - Attempting to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.
- Effectively increasing taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.
- Cutting more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families.  
“As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families,” the lawmakers continued.
“To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP,” the lawmakers concluded.
The lawmakers were joined by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.); and Representatives Gabe Amo (D-R.I.), Jake Auchincloss (D-Mass.), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Joe Courtney (D-Conn.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.), Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Bill Keating (D-Mass.), Seth Magaziner (D-R.I.), John Mannion (D-N.Y.), Gregory Meeks (D-N.Y.), Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Seth Moulton (D-Mass.), Richard Neal (D-Mass.), Chris Pappas (D-N.H.), Paul Tonko (D-N.Y.), and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.).
The full letter is available  here and is copied below.
+++
Secretary Wright:
We write to ask that you take immediate action to address the impact on our constituents of the rapidly rising cost of heating oil fueled by the President’s war in Iran and the administration’s failed policies. Today, the price of heating oil is around 60 percent higher than before the Iran war.1 The costs will be borne by American households struggling to heat their homes this winter while making ends meet. Instead of continuing down this path, we urge you to support an immediate end to the war and to stop blocking or restricting Department of Energy (DOE) programs that would help American families lower their energy bills.
Heating oil costs for the upcoming winter are projected to reach record levels, and families throughout the northeastern United States will likely bear the brunt of these costs. American families that rely on heating oil are projected to pay about $600 more to keep their homes warm this winter than last year. The price of heating oil has steadily risen to more than $4 a gallon, nearing record highs. Families from our states will shoulder the brunt of these prices: around one-third of New England homes rely on heating oil to heat their homes, and in some states, around half do. Families that warm their homes with heating oil are estimated to see their energy bills spike from $1,740 to around $2,300, placing immense strain on families and forcing them to make impossible decisions about whether to keep the heat on, the fridge stocked, or critical medical necessities in supply.
The President’s war in Iran has played a large part in driving up the price of heating oil. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted global trade in crude oil and impacted global supplies of heating oil and diesel, both refined products distilled from crude oil. Before the Iran war, crude was trading at $72 a barrel; now, the price for crude oil has jumped to more than $100 a barrel. Government reports indicate that national supplies of distillate fuel oil, which includes heating oil, are at their lowest levels on record. The Energy Information Administration (EIA) has assessed that constrained global supplies are “contributing to low U.S. diesel inventories and high diesel prices.”
Meanwhile, U.S. refiners and fossil fuel companies have seen banner profits while shipping heating oil abroad. As EIA notes, constraints in the global supply for heating oil have “raised domestic prices and incentivized U.S. exporters to increase distillate exports.” U.S. weekly exports of distillate products, including heating oil, hit a record high in August.
President Trump promised that high energy prices would be a “small price to pay” for a “little while” at the start of the war. In March 2026, you said that “prices have likely peaked and they’ll start going down,” stating that “[t]his is a weeks…not a months thing.” Yet, months later, energy prices have continued to surge.
Adding insult to injury, the Trump administration has made heating for the upcoming winter season even more expensive in other ways.
    - The administration has attempted to eliminate the $4 billion Low-Income Heating Assistance Program (LIHEAP) that supports families with high energy bills.
- The administration has effectively increased taxes on solutions to the heating cost crisis, by eliminating four tax credits and deductions that supported residential and commercial building energy efficiency upgrades.
- The administration has cut more than $20 billion in clean energy and grid modernization funding for hundreds of energy projects across the country that would have decreased costs for families.
As Americans face immense difficulty with keeping the heat on, the administration appears to be cutting off all avenues for meaningful relief, handing out tax cuts to billionaires, spending tens of billions of dollars on an unnecessary foreign war, and jacking up costs for struggling families.
To address these costs for American families, we urge you to reverse course on the senseless war in Iran, undo the administration’s cuts to clean energy and grid modernization programs, work with Congress to repeal the tax increases imposed on energy efficiency upgrades and other ways to lower heating costs, and end the administration’s attacks on LIHEAP.
Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04), member of the House Foreign Affairs and Appropriations Committees, released the following statement on the third anniversary of the October 7th attack:
“Three years ago today, Hamas terrorists launched a brutal, barbaric — most inhumane — attack on the people of Israel. Homes, Kibbutzim, and families were burned. Families torn apart. Unspeakable crimes committed against women, children, and seniors. More than 1,200 people were killed and 250 taken hostage, including American citizens.
The cruelty and brutality of this attack demanded universal, international condemnation and American support for our ally and friend Israel.
I have traveled to Israel several times since October 7th, to meet with grieving Israeli families and government leaders. I met twice with Prime Minister Netanyahu, urging him to pursue justice — a just war — not vengeance, to be a partner for peace.
Today, thanks to the tireless advocacy from the families and to American leadership, all the living hostages have been reunited with their loved ones. The dead have been returned to be buried with dignity. Around the world, Jewish people just celebrated their first Rosh Hashanah without any hostages held in Hamas’ custody. But the scars of October 7th run deep and are lasting. The families of those who were killed, and those who were taken, will carry that grief for the rest of their lives. We all will.
Meanwhile, the region remains in turmoil. Millions of Gazans are still displaced and vulnerable, struggling to find the food, water, medicine, and shelter they need to survive. More than 70,000 innocent Palestinian civilians have been killed and thousands more wounded, so many of them children. and Israeli violations of the ceasefire are alarmingly common. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers continue to encroach on Palestinian land, using violence to injure, kill, and drive out Palestinian families, jeopardizing any chance at peace.
We owe it to all those who died, on that day and in the devastating war since, to build a better future.
My prayer, and my work as a member of Congress, remains focused on supporting these essential pillars of peace: disarming of Hamas, a durable ceasefire to enable the mass distribution of humanitarian aid to the people of Gaza; a safe and secure future for Israel as a democratic home for the Jewish people; self-determination and dignity for the Palestinian people to rebuild their lives and create a democratic, sovereign state of their own; and a commitment by leaders around the world to these principles, that we might truly end the cycle of violence.
In this work, I am guided by the Jewish teaching of “Tikkun Olam”— the call to repair the world — and by the Scripture which tells us: blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
Today, we remember the suffering of October 7th. Tomorrow, we must continue the work, with mercy and moral clarity, each doing our part to make peace.”
Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.

title: Congresswoman Dean's Statement on Third Anniversary of October 7th Attack

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) and Congressman Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, demanded a federal investigation into former Bard College President Leon Botstein after reviewing an email in which Botstein asked Jeffrey Epstein about a young woman Epstein was trafficking: “Is [Jane Doe] for me, or are you keeping her for yourself.”
The letters — to Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel, and to Bard Board Chair Brandon Weber and Acting President Jonathan Becker — detail communications concerning a young foreign model and aspiring vocalist whom Epstein sent to Botstein in May 2014. They also question why DOJ exposed her name hundreds of times and released photographs showing her face while redacting Botstein’s email address.
“[T]his evidence, and the facts laid out in the Epstein files, surely meet and exceed the federal law enforcement standard for initiating a criminal investigation: the existence of evidence that a crime ‘may have occurred.’ These facts strongly indicate that a crime may have occurred. Yet, you have done nothing, and launched no investigation, about this incident which you and your staff must have known of for at least 18 months. In so doing, you have effectively permitted a potential co-conspirator of Jeffrey Epstein to stay in a position of power over young students, faculty and staff for an additional year at least,” the lawmakers wrote.
Emails and messages reviewed by the Committee show that Epstein groomed the young woman throughout 2014, offering advice and assistance with her education and career in the United States. After meeting Jane Doe in Paris, Epstein directed his assistant, Lesley Groff, to arrange private flights from her home country to destinations including Canada, New York, Florida, New Mexico and his island. A message to Epstein included a photograph of Jane Doe giving a woman, possibly Ghislaine Maxwell, a nude massage.
That May, Epstein sent Jane Doe to meet Botstein, ostensibly to assess her musical abilities and provide educational guidance. In an email from his Bard account, Botstein asked whether Jane Doe was “for me”. As he did with other survivors, Epstein relied on Botstein to assuage parental concerns about the sex offender, in this case by requesting orchestra tickets for the young woman’s parents to attend a Bard concert abroad. Epstein also asked Botstein to give them special treatment.
The evidence uncovered by the Committee contradicts the July 2025 DOJ–FBI memorandum and numerous follow-up claims by FBI Director Patel and Attorney General Blanche asserting that investigators found no evidence warranting an investigation of Epstein’s uncharged associates. Ranking Member Raskin demanded answers about why DOJ exposed the young woman’s identity while redacting Botstein’s email address, who directed that disparate treatment, and whom they were seeking to protect. Committee staff identified documents that still expose her name and provided the list separately to DOJ for redaction. The letters omit citations to DOJ documents to protect her identity.
Separately, more than a dozen whistleblowers have provided Committee staff information about a culture of sexual misconduct at Bard spanning decades. Multiple reports accuse Botstein of groping women and asking sexualized questions during tenure interviews. Whistleblowers described Botstein personally overseeing Title IX adjudications for the majority of his tenure as president and faculty being told that certain individuals accused of abuse were “protected by Botstein.”
In a letter to Bard’s leadership, Ranking Member Raskin sought records concerning Epstein’s use of the college to advance his trafficking activities and allegations from more than a dozen whistleblowers about sexual misconduct at Bard, including allegations that Botstein personally engaged in misconduct and intervened in Title IX proceedings to protect offenders. The Bard letter also details allegations involving a senior tenured professor who remains on campus, including that he invited a male student into his bed and supplied alcohol to the point of alcohol poisoning. That allegation appeared in a sworn federal complaint and was corroborated by whistleblower statements.
“Ultimately, we understand that your outrageous abandonment of your responsibilities is not about Leon Botstein. It is about protecting another individual who appears frequently in the Epstein files who also may have been a co-conspirator in Jeffrey Epstein’s brutal and sickening sex trafficking operation. And yet you continue to show the world that you would rather let a dozen, even 100, or 1,000 human sex traffickers go free than allow the possibility of an honest investigation of the conduct of one man,” the lawmakers concluded.
Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.

SAN BRUNO, CA –Despite bipartisan and bicameral support for preserving America’s national archives, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) gave a dismissive response to federal lawmakers who are working to protect local public access to historic records.
Before providing any justification or opportunities for the public to weigh in, NARA recently announced it would be closing its San Bruno and Chicago facilities, which are two of just 13 regional archives across America. Over one hundred community advocates, researchers, genealogists, and local families gathered at a rally and press conference Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) hosted in August to emphasize the importance of retaining culturally and historically significant records in the Bay Area.
U.S. Reps. Mullin and Judy Chu (CA-28) led a bipartisan coalition of 37 federal lawmakers in writing to NARA response letter, NARA failed to fully acknowledge concerns about the public losing physical access to local archival records, or a 2009 agreement to keep regionally-sensitive immigration files in San Bruno. NARA also did not explain how it made decisions about where to transfer non-immigration related files, and provided no insight into how the fragile 100+ year-old records would be cared for while moved across the country.
NARA didn’t definitively answer questions about the future of its local workforce, many of whom are experts in their field. While it cited an estimated $4.7 million in annual savings by shuttering the building, it didn’t justify the need to find such savings – which is less than the taxpayer funding President Trump wants to spend on renovating his living quarters at the White House this fiscal year alone.
The national archives in San Bruno house records from not only California but also Nevada, Hawaii, Pacific Island territories, and Tribes. These records hold deep value to the local community including Angel Island immigration files, Chinese Exclusion Act and Japanese Internment records, Native American and indigenous history documents, and even the notable Wong Kim Ark files, on which the recent birthright citizenship case at the Supreme Court hinged. NARA said it plans to move the immigration files to Kansas City – suggesting it expects Bay Area community members who deeply care about their ancestors’ records to travel over 1,500 miles if they want see them in person.
In August, Rep. Mullin also introduced the National Archives Protection Act, which is co-authored by Reps. Chu; Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), whose district includes the Seattle archives; and Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), whose district includes the Chicago archives. The bill would prevent NARA from closing any of its facilities including archives, records centers, and research rooms, without Congressional approval. Following the House bill, a Senate companion version was introduced on Sept. 30 by Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), along with U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Alex Padilla (D-CA), and Adam Schiff (D-CA).
After facing community pushback – and months after quietly notifying congressional offices of its plans – NARA announced it would host two virtual listening sessions for Tribal Nations on Oct. 13 and 15. Reps. Mullin and Chu encourage all Tribal members interested in joining to visit NARA’s website for instructions on signing up for a listening session at www.archives.gov/research/news. Reps. Mullin and Chu are urging NARA to conduct more public input sessions and engage with additional stakeholders who have an interest in maintaining the physical archives within the communities they represent.
“NARA’s response to federal lawmakers is extremely disappointing and dismissive toward the sincere concerns from the public about losing direct access to irreplaceable community and family records. These archives aren’t just boxes of paper — they hold the stories, memories, and history of generations of Americans. Families whose ancestors immigrated through Angel Island can track their lineage, those whose loved ones served in the Navy and were stationed in the Pacific can learn about their legacy, and Native Americans whose history is documented over generations are all able to learn more by visiting this national archive,” said Rep. Mullin. “NARA has a responsibility to ensure these tangible records are carefully preserved and accessible to the people they represent. I will continue to fight against these closures and encourage everyone – from federal lawmakers and Tribal leaders, to community advocates and researchers – to keep up the pressure and consider all legal means to protect these historic resources.”
“NARA’s response falls far short of addressing the real concerns of the communities who rely on these archives,” said Rep. Judy Chu. “For all Californians, and particularly the AANHPI community, these records are more than files and boxes. They tell the stories of families who endured the Chinese Exclusion Act and the incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II, and they are where descendants go to learn what their loved ones lived through. Moving these records across the country would force families to travel thousands of miles and spend significant time and money simply to access their own American history. NARA has offered no convincing reason to put that history out of reach, and it has a responsibility to protect these records and keep them accessible to the communities they belong to. We will keep fighting the closures of the San Francisco and San Bruno facilities, and we will not let up until these irreplaceable pieces of AANHPI history are kept with the communities whose stories they tell.”
The letter regarding the San Bruno archives was signed by U.S. Reps. Mark Amodei (NV-02), Ami Bera (CA-06), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Ed Case (HI-01), Judy Chu (CA-28), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), , Laura Friedman (CA-30), John Garamendi (CA-08), Jesús García (IL-04), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Steven Horsford (NV-04), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Susie Lee (NV-03), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Doris Matsui (CA-17), Grace Meng (NY-06), Dave Min (CA-47), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Nancy Pelosi (CA-11), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Brad Sherman (CA-32), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-29), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Dina Titus (NV-01), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Norma Torres (CA-35), Maxine Waters (CA-43); and Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam B. Known Cybersecurity Expert and Owner of Florida Ransomware Remediation Company Charged with Defrauding Clients
Zohar Pinhasi, 50, also known as “Zack Silver” and “Zack Green,” a U.S. and Israeli national, was arraigned today in the Eastern District of New York on wire fraud charges relating to Pinhasi’s false representations that he could decrypt ransomware without paying cybercriminals. Pinhasi claimed to prospective clients that his company, MonsterCloud, offered a principled alternative to paying off ransomware attackers.
“The defendant is charged with offering an alternative to ransom payments, but instead is alleged to have victimized the victim again and committed additional fraud, harming the victim again,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “This prosecution underscores the Department’s commitment to protecting ransomware victims, regardless of how these cyber ransoms occur.”
“As alleged in the indictment, by falsely claiming to decrypt ransomware without paying off the ransomers, the defendant re-victimized his clients while extracting a hefty profit for himself,” said U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella, Jr. for the Eastern District of New York. “Our Office will vigorously prosecute ransomware attackers who prey on Americans from across the world and those who cynically profit from their criminal activity.”
“As alleged, Zohar Pinhasi claimed to fix ransomware while never remediating the underlying threat. Instead, he turned the victim's crisis into his own profit center,” said Assistant Director James C. Barnacle Jr. of the FBI. “This deception is unacceptable, and the FBI is committed to ensuring accountability for those who choose to victimize the very people who trusted them for help.”
According to the indictment, Pinhasi made misrepresentations to distressed business owners who came to his company, MonsterCloud, for help after being victimized by cybercriminals. MonsterCloud’s website cautioned clients not to pay the ransom and claimed that his team specialized in helping businesses recover their data without succumbing to ransom demands. Pinhasi represented that he had access to “proprietary tools” and “advanced decryption techniques.” He allegedly had no special technology to decrypt data but instead contacted and paid the cybercriminals who had victimized MonsterCloud’s client in exchange for a decryption key that MonsterCloud employees then used in an attempt to decrypt the client’s files. Pinhasi typically charged MonsterCloud’s clients a fee that was substantially higher than the ransom that MonsterCloud secretly paid. For instance, in or around August 2023, he made a ransom payment of approximately $8,200 to a cybercriminal and charged the client approximately $150,000. Over the course of the scheme, he allegedly charged clients more than $19 million and paid more than $8 million in ransom payments.
Pinhasi is charged with two counts of wire fraud and one count of wire fraud conspiracy. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of 20 years on each count.
In joint guidance, the FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have advised that they do not recommend that ransomware victims pay ransom. Paying ransoms does not ensure that data is decrypted, that systems or data will no longer be compromised, or that data will not be leaked.
The FBI is investigating the case.
Senior Trial Attorneys Brian Mund and Vasantha Rao of the Justice Department’s Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alexander Mindlin and Lindsey Oken for the Eastern District of New York are prosecuting the case.
CCIPS investigates and prosecutes cybercrime and intellectual property (IP) crime in coordination with domestic and international law enforcement agencies, often with assistance from the private sector. Since 2020, CCIPS has secured the conviction of over 180 cyber and IP criminals, and court orders for the return of over $350 million in victim funds.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Known Cybersecurity Expert and Owner of Florida Ransomware Remediation Company Charged with Defrauding Clients

Examining Webull's China Links
A new bipartisan investigation by the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, led by Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) and Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI), finds that stock brokerage Webull Financial has not been transparent about its links to China. In addition to finding that the company’s practices exposed American investors’ data to surveillance risks in China, the investigation also documents how the company is controlled by China-linked executives and its China-based subsidiary receives subsidies and cash rewards from Chinese government authorities.
“Whether it’s this trading app or other brokerage apps, custodians of Americans’ financial data and savings should strive for transparency with the customers they serve. Webull should be forthright about its connections to the PRC, rather than seemingly seeking to minimize them,” said Ranking Member Khanna.”
"Webull’s China-based operations put American investors and their data at risk. China’s national security law compels all Chinese citizens to comply with demands for information from the CCP, and a stock brokerage storing data in China is no different,” said Chairman Moolenaar. "Using technology providers in mainland China and an opaque China-linked ownership structure, Webull exposes its data to our foremost adversary. Investors should heed this information when choosing who they do business with.”\
The report titled, Free Trades, Hidden Ties: Exposing Webull’s China Links, makes six findings:
- Webull’s data practices expose American investors to PRC legal and surveillance risk.
- Webull misrepresented where key employees worked and how they were supervised.
- Webull’s governance is dominated by PRC-linked control.
- Webull’s regulatory controls were weaker than its assurances suggested.
- Webull’s subsidiary accepted PRC government funding conditional on CCP loyalty while its affiliates expanded in China.
- Webull’s clearing and custody safeguards are concerning.
Policy Recommendations
The investigation also makes five policy recommendations as a result of its findings:
- Codify the Securities and Exchange Commission Cross-Border Task Force.
- Enact Inspectability Requirements for Broker-Dealer Operations — a Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act for Broker-Dealers.
- Create Foreign-Adversary Data Protections for Brokerage Records.
- Regulate Conflicted Clearing and Self-Custody Arrangements.
- Bring Foreign-Controlled Broker-Dealers Within Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) Jurisdiction.
Background
Webull is a stock trading platform that operates in the U.S. and purports to be an ordinary American broker-dealer; in reality, Webull's corporate and technology framework is tied directly to China, and the company has routinely distorted the facts about its personnel and operations.
In 2024, Moolenaar and then-Ranking Member Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) sent a letter to Webull regarding Webull's troubling ties to the PRC and the risks those ties may pose to the security of American user data.
In the 2024 letter, the lawmakers described that while operating in the United States, Webull has retained close ties to a network of Chinese technology companies, particularly Fumi Technology and Hunan Weibu. Webull has not only entered technology-sharing agreements with these companies, but also shares personnel with them. Additionally, Webull entities enjoy grants from the Chinese Communist Party that flow through Webull's Chinese sister company, Hunan Weibu, intended to support Webull's operations abroad. The lawmakers expressed that these entities, and related links to the Chinese Communist Party, raise concerns about Webull’s independence, the security of U.S. investor data, and its ability to comply with U.S. financial regulations.
Read the full report HERE.

Administrator Zeldin Announces EPA is Days Away from Unveiling Next Oil & Gas Proposal
WASHINGTON – While at the New Mexico Oil and Gas Association’s annual meeting in Santa Fe, New Mexico, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin announced that in the coming days the Trump EPA will be proposing the next part of the agency’s comprehensive reconsideration of the Biden Administration's 2024 oil and natural gas rules, also known as OOOOb/c. The agency’s proposal, which is part of a series of actions the Trump EPA is taking on Biden-era oil and natural gas regulations, is estimated to save $45 billion.
During his speech, Administrator Zeldin highlighted the extensive reconsideration effort the agency has undergone to address widespread concerns from American energy producers and operators that the 2024 Rule is unworkable and is holding back American energy dominance. This effort is a stark contrast to the $18 billion in regulatory costs the Biden EPA’s rule imposed without providing the environmental benefits promised.
“The Trump EPA is days not weeks away from announcing our proposal for the second part of the oil and gas reconsideration. This proposal takes on many of the problems American producers and operators have raised with us. That includes the burden on marginal wells and oil and gas operators in general, the Super Emitter Program, associated gas, and control device requirements,” said EPA Administrator Zeldin. “Americans must be able to afford to heat their homes in the winter and fill up their car and drive to work. They can’t do that when the people producing the energy are weighed down by unnecessary burdens. The Trump EPA is committed to fixing this so the U.S. can reach its full energy potential.”
Behind every barrel of oil and every cubic foot of natural gas produced in the U.S. are millions of workers, businesses, and the heartbeat of this nation’s economy; the Biden-era regulations posed a monumental threat. As a result, Americans in every state suffered from higher energy prices. The U.S. produces energy in a better and more environmentally friendly way than anywhere else in the world. The Trump EPA knows our policies must match our nation’s potential and is working to unleash the full ability of American energy by returning commonsense to regulations.
What Americans Can Expect to See in the Upcoming Proposal:
- Certain Well Sites: EPA will propose to change the approach to marginal wells by co-proposing two options that would create separate categories of well sites, each with its own standards that make sense for the circumstances of the particular type of well.
- Super Emitter Program: After hearing about serious legal concerns with the program, EPA will propose to rescind it. The agency does not think it is necessary to meet Clean Air Act requirements and is not effective.
- Covers and Closed Vent Systems: EPA will propose to split this standard into two parts, design requirements and operational requirements.
- Associated Gas: To make compliance possible all over the country and ensure a reasonable approach, EPA will propose to revisit the overall approach to regulating associated gas from oil wells.
- Control Devices: EPA will propose technical changes to give flexibility for flame monitoring data deviations, control device alerts, and visible emissions test conditions where appropriate.
Please see EPA's Actions and Notices about Oil and Natural Gas Air Pollution Standards (pdf) for a full timeline of EPA's oil and gas reconsideration.

Aurora Sentinel: Rep. Crow introduces bill to extend TPS protections for Ukrainian immigrants
AURORA | Aurora Democratic Congressperson Jason Crow is behind a House bill that would extend through 2029 temporary immigration protections for Ukrainian nationals living in the United States.
Crow’s bill would extend Temporary Protected Status, or TPS, for Ukrainians currently in the U.S. The protections are scheduled to expire Oct. 19, 2026, according to a press statement from Crow.
“Russia continues its illegal and unprovoked attacks on Ukraine,” Crow said in a statement. “America must continue to stand with the people of Ukraine.” The legislation would make the extension part of federal law rather than leaving the protections subject to presidential action, the release said.
President Donald Trump and his administration has created intense worry and consternation among immigrants living in the United States and benefiting from TPS protections.
“I think that TPS should be a part of a long overdue comprehensive immigration reform by Congress but until then, we owe it to those who are in the country under TPS to extend their status,” Aurora Mayor Mike Coffman said in a statement. “It would be heartless to force the Ukrainians back into a war zone. So I applaud Congressman Crow’s efforts to extend their status, although having been a member of Congress for 10 years, I know how difficult it will be to pass and… to have President Trump sign it into law when he already has the authority to extend it, unilaterally, without Congressional approval. “
On Sept. 9, Trump let expire TPS protections for hundreds of thousands of immigrations, primarily from Venezuela and El Salvador. The Supreme Court earlier this year ruled that, under current U.S. law, the president has authority to end TPS protections for protected groups without justification.
TPS allows nationals of designated countries experiencing armed conflict, natural disasters or other extraordinary conditions to remain temporarily in the United States and obtain work authorization. The program requires recipients to undergo screening, according to the release.
Crow introduced the bill with representatives Bill Keating, D-Mass., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa. In the Senate, the legislation was introduced by senators Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska; Chris Coons, D-Del.; and Bill Cassidy, R-La.
Crow serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the House Armed Services Committee, according to the release.
He has been a supporter of U.S. assistance to Ukraine since before Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022. Crow traveled to Kyiv in December 2021 and later advocated for U.S. military and humanitarian assistance to Ukraine, according to his office.
The legislation would apply to Ukrainian nationals already covered by TPS and extend their protections through June 2029.
The measure does not address another TPS warranty, covering immigrants from Sudan, also set to expire Oct. 19.
Colorado is home to about 17,000-18,000 Ukrainian immigrants, according to the U.S. Census records. The Aurora-Denver metro area is home to as many as about 5,000 of those immigrants, according to Census records.
Temporary legal protections for about 200,000 immigrants from El Salvador — including more than 4,000 in Aurora — was in limbo Wednesday as a deadline neared for the Trump administration to decide if they should end, as it has done for hundreds of thousands from Venezuela, Haiti and other countries.
The Temporary Protected Status designation expired in September, but the statute does not give a specific time for when that happens. If the Department of Homeland Security takes no action, protections are automatically extended for six months. This rare reprieve happened in May, when the protections were automatically extended to about 11,000 Lebanese, allowing them to stay and work in the U.S. for another 180 days.
DHS said in a statement in early September that it will announce a decision on El Salvador “at the appropriate time” and that protections would remain in place until then.
The push against Salvadoran immigrants drew a rebuke from Coffman, a Republican.
“I fully support the Trump administration’s successful effort at controlling our borders to combat illegal immigration,” Coffman said earlier this year in a social media post. “But this is not a question about illegal immigration because the Salvadorans, living in Aurora under TPS, came here legally and have had children and even grandchildren here, own homes in our city, and have not only started but expanded small businesses here.”
About 200,000 people from El Salvador have lived in the U.S. since 2001 under TPS, which allows people already in the country to remain with work permits for renewable periods of up to 18 months, if the secretary of homeland security determines conditions are unsafe for return. They are eligible for work permits.
Crow agreed with Coffman at the time that the situation of the El Salvadoran immigrants and refugees stands apart.
“Immigrants and asylum seekers who come here legally – including through Temporary Protected Status – work, pay taxes, and contribute greatly to Colorado,” Crow said. “It’s important for Coloradans to remember how we got here. President Trump and Republicans cut healthcare and food assistance to give tax breaks to billionaires and hire thousands of poorly trained ICE agents. Their aggressive immigration tactics and mass deportations have hurt our economy, terrorized our communities, and separated families. Coloradans deserve a secure border, an orderly asylum process for those fleeing violence, and a path for workers, families, and children to earn citizenship.”
During President Donald Trump’s second term, Homeland Security has ended TPS for more than 1 million people from 14 countries, including El Salvador, Venezuela, Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Afghanistan and Syria. Only about 103,000 from three countries remain protected with termination dates in October for Ukraine and Sudan, and November for Lebanon.
The Trump administration obtained a major victory when the Supreme Court ruled in June that Homeland Security acted within its authority by ending TPS for about 350,000 Haitians and 6,000 Syrians. The impact of the decision extends far beyond Haitians and Syrians, potentially affecting nearly 1.3 million people from 17 countries on TPS.
TPS was created by Congress in 1990 to prevent deportations to countries suffering from natural disasters or civil strife.
It was granted to El Salvador following two devastating 2001 earthquakes that left hundreds of thousands of people homeless. Just before leaving office, President Joe Biden extended TPS for El Salvador for 18 months to Sept. 9, 2026.
The vast majority of Salvadoran TPS holders have children born in the U.S. Many have lost their jobs and fear being detained, separated from their American family members, and deported to a country they barely know.
— The Associated Press contributed to this story.
title: Aurora Sentinel: Rep. Crow introduces bill to extend TPS protections for Ukrainian immigrants

ICYMI | Wall Street Journal: “Wells Fargo Faces Regulator Probe Over Efforts to Boost Black Homeownership”
October 7, 2026
WASHINGTON - Today, Secretary Turner launched an investigation into Wells Fargo’s initiatives to increase homeownership for Black Americans, which may be a violation of the Fair Housing Act.
“Even if Wells Fargo did not violate the law, its practice of dividing Americans based on race is immoral, unethical and un-American,” said Secretary Scott Turner. “Wells Fargo and all of its employees that engaged in race-based decision-making should be ashamed of themselves.”
“The Trump Administration will not stand for un-American and unlawful race-based mortgage lending practices from any financial institution,” said Deputy Secretary Andrew Hughes. “This investigation is another important step in the agency’s work to restore justice to fair housing enforcement.”
“The Fair Housing Act forbids racial discrimination in housing. It does not say: discriminate, so long as the discrimination is called a ‘special purpose credit program’ and justified as advancing ‘racial equity in homeownership,’” said Assistant Secretary for Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity Craig Trainor. “No matter an institution’s size, wealth, or power, if there is reasonable cause to believe it has violated Americans’ civil rights, the Trump Administration will hold it to account.”
Read the full letter here.
Read the exclusive story from the Wall Street Journal:
Trump administration housing officials are launching an investigation into Wells Fargo over programs and commitments the bank made over nearly a decade to increase homeownership among Black Americans.
The Department of Housing and Urban Development on Wednesday sent Wells Fargo Chief Executive Charlie Scharf a letter saying it would examine whether the bank violated fair-lending laws by favoring Black or other minority homeowners, according to a copy viewed by The Wall Street Journal.
Wells Fargo didn’t have an immediate comment Wednesday.
The investigation provides another example of corporate America finding itself in the crosshairs for programs that were encouraged during prior administrations, either by the government or socially conscious investors.
The Trump administration has opened investigations into companies for so-called diversity, equity and inclusion programs. It has also launched attempts to find evidence of “debanking,” where banks closed the accounts of businesses or individuals operating in politically controversial industries, from fossil fuels to firearms.
Wells Fargo’s campaign to help Black homeowners goes back years. In 2017, the bank said it was committing $60 billion in loans in an effort to help add at least 250,000 Black homeowners by 2027.
In 2022, the bank expanded the program to put the company’s own money to work refinancing minority homes. That followed criticism the bank faced over a Bloomberg report that it had rejected half of all refinancing applications by Black families in 2020.
“These efforts are an important next step and will help close the homeownership gap between white and minority families created by decades of systemic inequities,” Wells Fargo said in 2022.
In early 2023, Wells Fargo scaled down its mortgage business broadly, focusing on lending to existing customers, but again reiterated a pledge to advance racial equity in housing.
In 2024, only 24% of Black households owned the home they lived in, compared with 73% of White households, according to the Pew Research Center.
Now, Trump officials are considering whether the bank’s efforts to help Black families were a violation of the Fair Housing Act. In its letter, HUD said Wells Fargo had adopted a strategy of “sorting” homeowners and offering different products or terms based on their race.
HUD Secretary Scott Turner said that he plans a full investigation into Wells Fargo’s statements. The agency is also reviewing similar initiatives by other banks, according to a senior HUD official.
“Even if Wells Fargo did not violate the law, its practice of dividing Americans based on race is immoral, unethical and un-American,” Turner said. “Wells Fargo and all of its employees that engaged in race-based decision-making should be ashamed of themselves.”
The HUD probe follows investigations by the Justice Department examining whether government contractors violated antifraud laws by implementing what the administration has called “unlawful” DEI practices. Such programs proliferated amid social unrest in the aftermath of a wave of police violence against Black Americans, including the 2020 murder of George Floyd.
Last year, International Business Machines and Deloitte paid multimillion-dollar fines to resolve claims they defrauded the government by considering diversity when hiring and making promotion and staffing decisions.
The diversity programs and corporate initiatives responding to environmental issues became the subject of intense political backlash from conservatives. Since Trump’s election in 2024, many companies have moved away from their diversity goals, scrubbing websites and investor disclosures.
Wells Fargo achieved about 40% of its initial $60 billion lending commitment and had helped refinance about 5,100 customers—representing an average monthly payment savings of about $100—when it commissioned a racial-equity assessment in late 2023.
It has since gone silent on its racial-equity initiatives, removing the 2023 assessment from its website.
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.

Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Julia Brownley (CA-26) joined Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Chair of the California Democratic Congressional Delegation, and 40 of their California congressional colleagues in issuing the following statement regarding President Donald Trump’s inflammatory remarks at a rally in Grand Island, Nebraska:
“Upon taking office, the President swears to uphold the Constitution and to protect us from our enemies. Yesterday, President Trump, while defending his unconstitutional war against Iran, appeared, incredibly, to invite Iran to destroy two American cities. WASHINGTON — On the margins of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Trade Committee, the Office of the United States Trade Representative convened a meeting of senior officials of 14 economies to begin work to address structural excess capacity and production in key manufacturing sectors. Building on the productive discussions at the G20 Trade Ministerial in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, these fourteen economies joined the United States in signing a Joint Ministerial Statement that expresses our collective resolve to work together in new, dedicated sectoral platforms to examine and take effective actions that address structural excess capacity and production in several key sectors of concern. The Joint Ministerial Statement also calls on all countries to take steps to end the use of non-market policies and practices that distort markets and perpetuate structural excess capacity and production. The signatories include the Trade Ministers of Argentina, Australia, Canada, the European Union, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Poland, Türkiye, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
“Over the course of the U.S. G20 presidency, numerous economies raised instances of structural excess capacity and production in economies that persistently exceeded global demand and were sustained by foreign government’s non-market policies and practices,” said Ambassador Greer. “Left unchecked, these issues will continue to cripple domestic industries, displace local production, and hinder our ability to raise the standard of living for workers and their families. The Trump Administration will continue to engage with our trading partners to defend our domestic industries, workers, and economy from distortions resulting from these pervasive policies and practices.”

WASHINGTON, DC – In July 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) issued its first civil penalty under the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP). Treasury penalized Amidi, LLC (Amidi) $200,000 for failing to submit a required notification of an investment by its controlled foreign entity into a Chinese embodied artificial intelligence company. The OISP, which became effective on January 2, 2025, currently requires notification to Treasury of certain types of investments and prohibits certain other types of investments by U.S. persons into entities in or connected to the People’s Republic of China, the Special Administrative Region of Hong Kong, and the Special Administrative Region of Macau that are engaged in certain activities in the quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and semiconductor sectors. In addition, a U.S. person is required (a) to file a notification with Treasury regarding any transaction by its controlled foreign entity if the transaction would be notifiable if engaged in by a U.S. person and (b) to take all reasonable steps to prohibit and prevent transactions by its controlled foreign entity if the transaction would be prohibited if engaged in by a U.S. person.
On April 19, 2025, Amidi’s subsidiary, a Chinese fund, invested approximately $92,478 in Shanghai Qiongche Intelligent Technology Company Limited (Noematrix). Amidi is also the parent entity of the organization that does business as Plug and Play Tech Center. Noematrix is a private Chinese company that develops artificial intelligence, robotics, and embodied intelligence.
“Today’s penalty announcement under the Outbound Investment Security Program underscores Treasury’s commitment to safeguarding U.S. national security through robust investment security measures that preserve America’s technological leadership and advance President Trump’s America First Investment Policy,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.
“The Outbound Investment Security Program is an important tool aimed at addressing the advancement of key technologies by countries of concern that could pose risks to U.S. national security,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton. Pilkerton added, “We will continue to ensure that investors comply with the requirements established under the program.”
The issuance of the penalty highlights Treasury’s commitment to compliance with OISP rules. Treasury identified this transaction as part of its regular and ongoing compliance and market monitoring efforts. On December 18, 2025, Congress passed the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025 (COINS), which will expand OISP jurisdiction to include investments in additional countries and technology sectors. In assessing compliance and whether to bring an enforcement action in connection with a particular transaction, Treasury will evaluate the facts and circumstances surrounding the conduct, including the aggravating and mitigating factors described in the Outbound Investment Security Program Enforcement Overview and Guidance.
If anyone believes that a violation may have occurred, the Treasury Department encourages them to submit tips, referrals, or other relevant information to the Outbound Program tips line: Outbound.Tips@treasury.gov.
###
title: Treasury Announces Enforcement Penalty for Violation of Outbound Program

Maryland Delegation Pushes for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade
Lawmakers press for funding following reports of severe mental health concerns among service members, civilian employees at Cyber Command, including several recent deaths by suicide
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02) joined the Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation (CITI) Subcommittee of the House Armed Services Committee and the Maryland Delegation in requesting an additional $11 million in funding for mental health support at U.S. Cyber Command following reports of multiple suicides earlier this year. Olszewski joined Representatives Sarah Elfreth (D-MD-03), Don Bacon (R-NE-02), Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), Rich McCormick (R-GA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06), Herbert Conaway (D-NJ-03), Eugene Vindman (D-VA-07), and Pat Ryan (D-NY-18). On the letter from the Maryland members, Elfreth was joined by her Maryland delegation colleagues, including Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), who co-led the letter, along with Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), and Representatives Steny Hoyer (D-MD-05), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), and April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06). Both letters were directed to the heads of the House and Senate Appropriations Committees.
“We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training… Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions,” wrote the CITI members.
“As the Congressional Delegation of Maryland, we are troubled by recent public reporting describing several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. These deaths have a severe impact on the family, friends, and wider community. The concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear,” wrote the Maryland lawmakers. “Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many are effectively ‘deployed in place’ for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unit-level reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments. Because much of their work is classified, they may be unable to discuss the sources of their stress with family members or medical professionals who lack the clearances or access to secure facilities necessary for a complete conversation. These conditions can isolate personnel, delay appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness.”
“One loss of life is one too many. We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at NSA and Cyber Command has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again,” wrote the CITI members.
The full CITI letter can be accessed HERE. The full Maryland letter can be accessed HERE.
title: Maryland Delegation Pushes for Funding for Mental Health at U.S. Cyber Command at Fort Meade

OCR will determine whether the institution violated Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title VI) by allowing or failing to meaningfully respond to antisemitic harassment.

Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces $90 Million Loan to Eliminate Traffic Bottlenecks, Accident Hotspots on I-81 in Virginia
Upgrades will cut travel delays, add truck climbing lanes, replace aging bridges, and enhance freight flow along major Mid-Atlantic commerce corridor
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy today announced Virginia’s Commonwealth Transportation Board (CTB) will receive two Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (TIFIA) loans totaling up to $89.7 million from the Build America Bureau. The package funds vital capacity and safety upgrades along 325 rural miles of I-81, a key East Coast freight route carrying 43% of Virginia's interstate truck traffic.
The projects will transform I-81 by:
- Adding dedicated truck climbing lanes in Washington County and Augusta County, allowing slow-moving heavy trucks to climb steep hills without blocking passenger cars;
- Fixing dangerous merging bottlenecks by extending exit ramps in Wythe County and adding merge lanes around Wytheville to give drivers more room to speed up or slow down safely; and,
- Replacing aging bridges over Peppers Ferry Road and the I-81 northbound bridge over I-77 to guarantee long-term corridor reliability.
“President Trump understands strong roads mean strong supply chains—that’s why he is investing in big, beautiful upgrades along the I-81 corridor in Virginia,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “By upgrading the commonwealth’s transportation infrastructure, reducing dangerous bottlenecks, and separating freight and passenger traffic, Virginia families and freight will move more safely and efficiently across the entire Mid-Atlantic region.”
The package supports Virginia’s $4 billion I-81 Corridor Improvement Program, which is projected to generate $5.2 billion in economic activity, supporting regional growth and job creation. Construction on many projects is already underway, with completion slated for late 2035.
“By securing a TIFIA loan at half the standard interest rate, the Commonwealth of Virginia is delivering these critical improvements faster and more affordably,” said Build America Bureau Executive Director Morteza Farajian, Ph.D. “By cutting interest costs in half and stretching taxpayer dollars, this project serves as a national blueprint. It proves that innovative financing can help rural communities deliver vital corridor improvements faster while freeing up resources for future infrastructure needs.”
“As a vital commercial corridor not only for Virginia but the entire east coast, additional travel lanes, new bridges and interchange improvements are enhancing safety and reducing congestion on I-81,” said Virginia Transportation Secretary Nick Donohue. “The TIFIA loans will help Virginia stretch its transportation dollars and continue building the interstate corridor all travelers deserve.”
Additional Information:
The two loans, totaling up to $47.6 million and $42.1 million respectively, take advantage of low interest rates made possible by the TIFIA Rural Project Initiative and build on Secretary Duffy’s broader campaign to eliminate traffic bottlenecks across America.
###
The Build America Bureau accelerates investment in transportation infrastructure by lending federal funds to qualified public and private borrowers; clearing roadblocks for creditworthy projects; and providing technical assistance services and grants to build local and regional capacity and implement best practices and innovative solutions in project planning, funding, financing, delivery, and operations. The Bureau draws on expertise across DOT to serve as the point of coordination for states, municipalities, private partners, and other project sponsors seeking federal financing.

Reps. Davis, Bergman, Van Drew, Golden Introduce SMILE for Veterans Act
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Reps. Don Davis (NC-01), Jack Bergman (MI-01), Jeff Van Drew (NJ-02) and Jared Golden (ME-02) have introduced the SMILE for Veterans Act, bipartisan legislation which will create a Department of Veterans Affairs Pilot Program to pay for local dentists providing care to America's rural veterans.
"Too many rural veterans experience difficulty obtaining necessary dental care, and quality dental care is essential for maintaining overall health," said Rep. Don Davis. "The SMILE for Veterans Act provides community-based providers with a means to provide that care closer to home. We owe it to our veterans to maintain our promise to provide them with the best care possible.”
At this time, only approximately 15 percent of the nearly 9 million veterans receiving their healthcare through the VA are eligible for VA-funded dental care. In most cases, eligibility for dental care is based on whether a veteran has a service-connected dental issue, a 100 percent disability rating, or was a former prisoner of war.
The SMILE for Veterans Act addresses the lack of accessibility to quality dental care in rural areas by allowing local dentists already in place to be reimbursed for treating rural veterans. The legislation would allow for increased access to dental care in underserved areas using the current provider base and infrastructure, without creating additional costs or requiring the VA to develop new dental systems.
“For too many veterans in rural communities, basic dental care is either too far away or simply out of reach,”said Rep. Jack Bergman.“The SMILE for Veterans Act offers a practical solution by connecting veterans with trusted dental providers already serving their communities. Rather than building an expensive new federal system from the ground up, this legislation uses existing local providers to deliver care efficiently and closer to home.”
“I spent 30 years as a dentist, and I can tell you that putting off dental care usually only makes things worse,”said Rep. Jeff Van Drew.“For veterans living in rural communities, sometimes the hardest part is simply finding a dentist close enough to get the care they need. That should not be the case. The SMILE for Veterans Act is a practical way to connect veterans with that care closer to home. To me, that is common sense.”
“VA health care is an essential benefit for our nation’s veterans, but for too long a lack of dental coverage has been a massive gap in care. The mouth is part of the body, and our veterans shouldn’t have to jump through hoops to get basic dental care. I’m proud to work with Reps. Bergman, Davis and Van Drew on the SMILE Act, which takes a smart first step toward more comprehensive coverage by focusing on rural areas where barriers to care are the highest and community providers that can help close the gap,”said Rep. Jared Golden.
The SMILE for Veterans Act is supported by AMVETS, the National Rural Health Association, and the CareQuest Institute for Oral Health.
###
title: Reps. Davis, Bergman, Van Drew, Golden Introduce SMILE for Veterans Act

Reps. Davids (D), Crane (R) Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Eli Crane (R-AZ-02) introduced bipartisan legislation to improve how unused housing vouchers are managed and distributed. The legislation would allow Tribes to voluntarily give back vouchers they do not plan to use, so the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) can redirect assistance to Tribal communities facing a shortage.
"Native veterans hold a special place in my heart,” said Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation of Wisconsin. “My mom and grandfather both served in the Army, and as a Native person, I know how much our communities value the veterans who have served our country. Tribal Nations know best what their communities and veterans need, and respecting Tribal sovereignty means giving them the flexibility and resources to meet those needs. I'm grateful to work with Rep. Crane on this bipartisan effort to ensure more Native veterans get the housing they need after returning home.”
"The Tribal HUD-VASH program helps house Tribal veterans in need, but the current system is not as efficient as it should be,” said Representative Eli Crane (R-AZ-02). “Some Tribes have leftover vouchers they cannot use while others lack the resources to take care of our veterans. Our legislation aims to resolve this longstanding issue by getting unused vouchers into the hands of Tribes that can put them to use. This is a sensible approach that makes better use of existing support without expanding the size and scope of the federal government. As the representative for more than half of the Tribes in Arizona, I'm honored to advocate for these heroes by reforming and modernizing this process. I appreciate Rep. Davids' willingness to work across the aisle. We've made real progress together before, and I look forward to building on that success with this bill.”
Native American veterans experience some of the highest rates of homelessness in the United States. To address this, Congress created the Tribal HUD-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (Tribal HUD-VASH) demonstration program, which provides rental assistance and supportive services to Native veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
Although the program has helped many veterans secure stable housing, it lacks a clear process for Tribes to return vouchers they cannot use or to request additional ones. As a result, valuable housing support sits idle while veterans in other Tribal communities wait for help.
The new Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act directs HUD to establish a voluntary program for reallocating unused Tribal HUD-VASH vouchers to Native veterans who need them most. Under the bill, Tribes and Tribally Designated Housing Entities (TDHEs) can notify HUD via digital, phone, or mail correspondence if they have surplus vouchers or request additional assistance for their communities without impacting their future allocations.
Required to launch within 180 days of enactment, the program creates a streamlined process to strengthen Tribal HUD-VASH and expand Native veterans' access to earned housing assistance. Within that same timeframe, HUD must submit a congressional report detailing voucher usage and shortfall metrics, distribution recommendations, and an assessment of whether to increase overall program funding.
This is not the first time Davids and Crane have partnered on legislation to assist Tribal communities. Davids previously introduced the Native American Entrepreneurial Opportunity Act, which would bolster U.S. Small Business Administration outreach to Tribal entrepreneurs navigating the unique complexities of running a business on a reservation. Crane co-led the measure, and it has twice passed the House with strong bipartisan support.
title: Reps. Davids (D), Crane (R) Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Housing Access for Tribal Veterans
