Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers on FDA Move to Rewrite Vaping Approval Rules, Blasts Weakening of Scientific Standards
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, today demanded answers from Food and Drug Administration Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas over FDA’s September 28 announcement that it is considering new rulemaking to replace the 2021 regulations governing approval of new tobacco products, pressing the agency over whether the move could weaken the scientific standards manufacturers must meet.
Krishnamoorthi is also demanding to know whether FDA discussed potential changes with tobacco manufacturers, industry associations, or parties challenging the current rules before announcing its review, and is seeking communications between agency officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries and representatives, and other parties challenging the framework.
FDA announced its review less than four weeks after Altria subsidiaries NJOY and Helix Innovations sued the agency over the current Premarket Tobacco Product Application framework. FDA itself cited recent litigation challenging the framework, along with the widespread illicit tobacco market, in explaining its decision to consider replacing the rule.
“The widespread sale of illegal products is an enforcement problem,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “It should not become a justification for lowering the evidentiary requirements manufacturers must satisfy before FDA authorizes their products.”
Krishnamoorthi also raised concerns about the review in light of FDA’s recent authorization of flavored e-cigarette products. In May, the agency authorized Glas products in mango and blueberry flavors despite FDA data indicating that fruit-flavored e-cigarettes are the most popular flavor among youth. The letter notes that the FDA Center for Tobacco Products did not require the manufacturer to demonstrate that the flavors provided an added benefit to adults attempting to transition from combustible products, and that former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary reportedly resigned in part amid political interference surrounding the authorization.
FDA then authorized additional JUUL products on August 28, including a JUUL2 menthol product.
“FDA acknowledged that the menthol product carries risks ‘including youth appeal,’ but concluded that its benefits to adults who smoke outweighed those risks,” Krishnamoorthi wrote. “Exactly one month later, FDA announced that it may replace the broader framework governing applications for new tobacco products.”
Krishnamoorthi concluded:
“The FDA’s job is to protect public health, not make it easier for tobacco companies to evade rigorous scientific review. The agency should crack down on companies selling illegal products, not use their lawbreaking as a rationale for weakening safeguards governing products seeking FDA authorization.”
Krishnamoorthi requested written responses by October 20, 2026, to the following questions:
- Which specific provisions of the 2021 PMTA rule is FDA considering changing or eliminating, and what evidence supports each potential change?
- Will FDA commit that any replacement framework will not lower the scientific evidentiary bar manufacturers must meet to demonstrate that marketing their products is appropriate for the protection of public health? If not, why not?
- Did FDA discuss potential changes to the 2021 PMTA rule with any tobacco product manufacturer, industry association, or party challenging the 2021 PMTA rule before announcing its review? Please identify each such entity and provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and those entities. Please also provide all communications since January 20, 2025, between FDA officials and Altria, Reynolds American, their subsidiaries or representatives, and any other party challenging the rule concerning the PMTA framework or potential changes to it.
- How does the existence of a widespread illicit market justify changes to the regulatory requirements governing products seeking lawful authorization? What connection has FDA identified between illegal sales and the scientific evidence manufacturers should be required to provide before receiving authorization?
- What additional enforcement actions will FDA take, in coordination with the Department of Justice and U.S. Customs and Border Protection, to remove unauthorized e-cigarettes from the U.S. market?
The full letter is available here.
Congressman Krishnamoorthi has led congressional efforts to combat youth vaping and hold tobacco companies accountable. In 2019, he launched the first congressional investigation into youth vaping, exposing JUUL’s marketing tactics and pushing legislation to ban flavored e-cigarettes and close the synthetic nicotine loophole. He has since led bipartisan efforts urging federal agencies to crack down on illegal flavored vapes and launched an investigation into illicit vaping products from China advertised to children. In 2025, Krishnamoorthi and Congresswoman Celeste Maloy (R-UT), his fellow co-chair of the Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, called on FDA to strengthen enforcement as more than 6,000 flavored products remained on the market. Most recently, Krishnamoorthi helped introduce the bipartisan PROTECT Act to strengthen federal efforts to prevent and reduce youth e-cigarette use.
title: Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers on FDA Move to Rewrite Vaping Approval Rules, Blasts Weakening of Scientific Standards

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir, Icelandic Foreign Minister

Safnahúsið

Reykjavik, Iceland

October 6, 2026

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: (In Icelandic.) Thank you all for being here. I will not continue in Icelandic, my dear Marco, and thank you especially for visiting Iceland. I think that demonstrates also very well our close connections and good relationship. And it has actually been, from my point of view, a productive morning. I would say so. We started, as you know, at Hofdi House, where we first had the opportunity to hear about the historic summit back almost 40 years ago between President Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev, and I hope you enjoyed our meeting in Hofdi. I thought there’s a kind of special atmosphere there.

The Secretary and I, then we had an excellent bilateral meeting at Hofdi, and now, just now, we concluded a very good meeting with – here in Safnahusid with our prime minister here in Iceland, Kristrún Frostadóttir. I would say throughout our discussions, they have been good and it has been very clear that Iceland and U.S., the United States of America, we enjoy a very good and strong and also enduring friendship. We share a long history. The U.S. was – as we have already mentioned, the U.S. was the first country to recognize the Republic of Iceland back in 1944. We are both founding members of NATO 1949, and of course we have the valuable bilateral Defense Agreement between our two countries since 1951.

And we are working closely together every day here in Iceland, especially to safeguard the security of the High North, North Atlantic, and the Arctic. For us, being a credible and responsible ally, we take this role very seriously here in Iceland, especially when it comes to the U.S. and the whole of NATO. And this is also very much and strongly reflected in our new policy – and actually the first one – policy and defense and security. It also strongly emphasizes the very important relationship through defense and security with the U.S.

With Iceland and the U.S. both being Arctic nations, the Secretary and I, we fully agreed on the need to work together to ensure a safe and secure Arctic region. And I especially want to commend you, Marco, on how you have taken such a strong initiative to – in making the A7, Arctic 7 group, even more effective than it has been before. And that matters for us here in Iceland a lot.

And we also discussed the agreement that has been found between the U.S., Greenland, and Denmark, and that is also hugely important for the region that we got this good agreement on Greenland.

As we discussed also in both our meetings now today, there are ample opportunities to deepen our economic and investment relations even further – for instance, in geothermal energy. We discussed data centers, pharmaceuticals, as well as digital and other infrastructure. And we also talked about the challenging global context, which is on our minds as Russia full-scale invasion in Ukraine – very brutal, very relentless. And we touched on the dire situation in the Middle East and also we discussed our relations to China.

But above all, the Secretary and I, we had productive and constructive discussions, conversation, and I think the message is very clear. We are allies, we are friends, and we will continue working very closely to strengthen and deepen our good relationship.

So over to you, dear Marco.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, thank you for welcoming here – us here. This is a place that many Americans visit. I think the number that was shared with us as coming in and here today is over 700,000 Americans. Our great ambassador, who’s only been here a couple months but is already doing a great job – so he’s going to get that up to a million American visitors over the next few years, but – with direct flights from multiple cities. And now we see why people want to come here. It’s a beautiful country, a wonderful people, the most peaceful country in the world. It’s one of the safest countries in the world, a country that’s also blessed with abundance of energy that is renewable and self-sustaining.

And so you have so many good things coming and going in your direction, and we’re so happy to be a close partner of yours, as we have been for a very long time. We have tremendous respect for your – the people, and we have tremendous respect for the country and the role that it plays, and it has for a very long time. I mean, for decades this nation in Iceland has occupied a critical strategic position for our collective security, and that remains true today more than ever before.

And while the world’s focus drifted over the last 20 years, the reality is the geography is always important, and we’re seeing that come now to fruition. The location of this country between the United States and Europe and the High North means that it sits at the – Iceland sits at the center of many of the questions surrounding the security and the defense of our shared region.

And today those threats are growing, which is why this focus on the Arctic in general and Iceland in particular is so critical. Our potential adversaries and real competitors already – and the predatory industries associated with them – are already acting as – against our interests. And so it’s important that we continue to cooperate in the security realm the way we are doing and continue to do.

Obviously I think one of the unique aspects of the country – in a positive way, I think – is that you don’t have a traditional military in the traditional sense of the word, but as – but you are a NATO member and you are a contributor to collective security, and you continue to contribute that critical role in our Alliance and share the burden of defending region. And in practice, what that means and has meant for a very long time is you welcoming NATO Allies to come here and to operate jointly within Icelandic territory, and we want to continue to build upon that as a way to prevent conflict – not as a way to encourage conflict or provoke conflict, but prevent it.

History teaches us that deterrence is the best prevention of violence and the best preventer of war. And you play such – have played such a strategic role in the past and continue to play that now. So since the Second World War, Iceland has allowed the U.S. military to project power and collectively working together, using your land, your air, your sea; giving us a critical outpost for monitoring clandestine behavior and deterring our adversaries from entering your sovereign territory and the sovereign territory of our mutual allies.

This year marks the 75th anniversary of the 1951 U.S.-Iceland Defense Agreement. And I’m proud to say that our military and our Icelandic partners continue to work together to secure this land and the waters that surround it. Just last month, over 1,200 Americans participated along with our allies in the Northern Viking 2026 military exercise, something that’s occurred every year and will continue to occur.

And – but I want to talk a little bit beyond the military and security domain, because Iceland is not just an important security partner; it is a critical partner in our mutual economic interests for the foreseeable future. Your landscapes, for example, have been the training ground for American astronauts since the Appollo program and continues to host training missions for the Artemis missions. Your expertise in geothermal energy and biotechnology and marine industries, those present incredible opportunities for greater commercial and technological cooperation.

We discussed that today and our efforts to perhaps – we are going to work now on building out a group of American industries and present them to investment opportunities that exist here, and likewise identify for your companies here investment opportunities that may exist in the United States. That’s how you continue to build upon the economic bonds that lead to our shared prosperity and our mutual prosperity, so that’s important. So today we discussed concrete ideas about how we can deepen cooperation in these fields and further strengthen our robust bilateral relationship to benefit our people.

So I really look forward to – as I said, we had an opportunity to engage in Ankara earlier this year. I told you I would be coming soon, and I’m here now and I’m happy to have come. This is my first visit here in any capacity. I believe – and we discussed this earlier – it’s probably the first bilateral visit by a secretary of state in a very long time. I know Secretary Blinken had been here as part of a broader gathering earlier, but – and maybe we’ll be able to – but this, I think this is the first time a secretary of state comes in a long time in terms of a bilateral visit, and perhaps it won’t be the last one because of how much esteem we have for your country, for your government, for your people, and for the importance of this relationship.

So really, really happy to be here, really glad I came. And now I know, just in the limited things I’ve gotten to see – because obviously there’s only so much you can see through the window of a hotel and the window of a car, but you can see why people fall in love with this country and you can see why Americans are fascinated by it, and we want to build upon that both in the tourism sector, in the economic sector, and in our enduring security cooperation.

So thank you for hosting me, for hosting us, and thank you for this opportunity to interact with you.

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: Thank you, dear Marco. And actually you saw – witnessed the Northern Lights yesterday. You told me.

SECRETARY RUBIO: I did. Which, as someone from Florida —

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: Yeah. (Laughter.)

SECRETARY RUBIO: — I didn’t know if that was a UFO or what it was, but then I looked at it and I realized what it was pretty quickly. It was very special.

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: Thank you, Marco. Who is going to conduct – yes, yeah.

MODERATOR: Thank you. And we’ll take a few questions from the media now, starting with the Icelandic press. Mr. Hallgrímur Indridason from RUV, the Icelandic broadcasting service.

QUESTION: Thank you. The first question from RUV: In light of the deal that the U.S., Greenland, and Denmark made on Greenland defenses, which included buildup, like, in two more military bases in Greenland, are there any plans for the U.S. Government to have further buildup here in Iceland, whether these are its military base or more surveillance or anything of that sort? Are you increasing your presence in Iceland and —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Yeah.

QUESTION: And the second question from – on behalf of Radio Saga: Do you feel that Iceland poses a direct military threat from Russia? And if so, what makes Iceland vulnerable in that area?

And if I may add a short yes-or-no question, what is your position on NATO membership of Ukraine? Do you think Ukraine should be a member of NATO?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, just on your third point, there’s no yes-or-no answer to that other than to say that Ukraine – right now, NATO membership, as you know, is not on the table as we speak, because there’s obviously a consensus process that has to happen in order for that, a unanimity process that has to happen. Right now, we’re simply focused, when it comes to Ukraine, on the ending of this conflict if that’s possible. And it’s unfortunate the amount of loss of life. We’ve been clear that if there’s a role we can play in bringing that war to an end, we want to play a constructive role. We are obviously watching the trend lines there and seeing that’s not the direction that it’s headed right now.

On your first question which has to do – well, I forgot your first question because you guys, you’re cheating. (Laughter.) You said it was one question and then you got three, so now I gotta write these down.

QUESTION: Military buildup.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, military build – well look, we’d never do anything without cooperating with officials here about what’s available. I think there is a willingness to do more together. And what Iceland contributes really is infrastructure and technology and the ability to have surveillance and opportunity of domain awareness. And it wouldn’t be anything new. I mean, it’s already existed for a very long time. We obviously had an enduring presence here that ended in 2006, not because of anything that was going wrong but because we shifted forces to other parts of the world where we thought there was more crisis.

The reality of it is the world has changed over the last 20 years. Our focus has changed. There’s a lot of focus on the Arctic. I think Iceland plays a very critical role in the defense of NATO writ large. I think Iceland and its location plays a critical role in the defense both of Europe but also of the homeland of the United States because of geography. So we would be open to having those conversations to see what more we can do together. I know there’s interest in doing more together. And obviously, if there’s opportunities that make sense for both countries, it’s something we would pursue.

With regards to direct threats, look, at the end of the day I think we’re all concerned about what’s happening in the High North and in the Arctic region, both from irregular measures, covert measures that are happening, but also threats to undersea cables, threats to shipping lanes. We’re all aware of it, which is why so much attention is being paid to the Arctic region. And it’s something that we have to deal with collectively, not just alone unilaterally but in combination with our partners and allies, which is why we’ve been having these regular engagements with the Arctic 7 countries, and Iceland is a key component of that and a place where we’ve already had a history of cooperating on these matters in the past.

So yeah, I mean, there are direct threats, and those threats in the 21st century aren’t just military threats. They’re also economic and commercial threats that have implications on the national security of our respective countries.

MODERATOR: Thank you, Mr. Secretary. Next we will go to Richard Crowley from The New York Times .

QUESTION: Thank you. Michael Crowley with —

MODERATOR: Michael, I’m sorry.

QUESTION: No problem – with The New York Times . Thank you, Mr. Secretary. My questions were going to be similar, so just keying off of what you were just asked.

SECRETARY RUBIO: All right, good, so you don’t need your time for the same —

QUESTION: No such luck.

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Laughter.) All right, go ahead. What’s your backup question?

QUESTION: Regarding Northern Viking, although there was U.S. participation for the first time in the history of those exercises, the U.S. did not participate with ships or airplanes, which I saw was noticed in regional coverage about those exercises. Is that significant? Do you want to explain why that might have been the case?

And last month, there was a diplomatic incident when the Iceland foreign ministry summoned the ambassador over a post by the President on social media which depicted a map showing several nations in the region colored in with American stars and stripes, including Canada, Greenland, and also Iceland. I wondered if you wanted to comment on the significance of that and anything you may have said in your trip here today.

And for the prime minister —

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: Foreign.

QUESTION: — did you find the absence of American forces —

MODERATOR: Foreign minister.

QUESTION: Pardon me. Foreign Minister, do you find the absence of American forces in the Northern Viking exercises to be meaningful or worrisome at all? And do you have any comment that you want to make about the social media posting, and are you concerned that you could be facing a drama like the one that Greenland recently went through with President Trump as far as talk of American acquisition? Thank you, and my apology for misstating your title. Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: That’s an unforgivable error. I mean, I don’t even know if I should answer your question after doing that. (Laughter.)

Look, on the second point, we’re not talking about social media posts. I’m here – we’re here – meeting with a country we work very closely together on, and we do a lot of things together and everything is very positive in our relationship.

So on the first point about ships and airplanes, look, obviously there’s things going on around the world. That’s not a mystery to anyone. It requires us to allocate resources. And sometimes when you are involved, whether it’s in protecting shipping lanes like we’ve had to do in the – because of this terrorist regime in Iran targeting commercial shipping lanes, or the defense of airspace, or the need to backfill what’s happening in the Indo-Pacific as a result of this shift of forces – anytime you have active activities going on in the world, you have to move your assets to that, and sometimes they’re not available for exercises.

So it’s – I don’t think that’s an enduring decision. I think just one that, from the timing standpoint of when it happened, and it overlayed with existing operations around the world. So – but I don’t think that’s enduring. We still had people present. We’re still committed to it. And as I said, I’m visiting here today because this place matters both economically but also from a defense standpoint.

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: Yeah, actually, I have nothing to add to this. He explained – Marco explained very eloquently during our meeting why they needed the forces elsewhere. And I want to underline our really strong cooperation in terms of defense and security, and there is no change in that – what that matters.

What matters about the tweet or the posting from Mr. President, from President Trump, we discussed that, and I mean we have already dealt with that constructively. And we are actually – and yes, you are right, I summoned the ambassador. We were very open about this because we have a very good relationship with the U.S., and we want to continue to build on that relationship.

So that’s why we remain now focused on the future, on the strong and positive relationship between our two countries. And we are looking forward, not backwards.

MODERATOR: Next we’ll go to Andres Magnusson from the Icelandic Morgunbladid.

QUESTION: Yeah. And Mr. Secretary, I’m also asking on behalf of Visir. But this summer, the U.S. asked Iceland, sent actually a questionnaire, about support for U.S. foreign policy priorities. How do you view the Iceland response? And also, in light of how warmly you speak of Icelandic-U.S. relations, where do you think there is space to deepen the relationship? Where could it be strengthened? And if I might add, is the U.S. willing to explore a free trade agreement with Iceland?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, a couple points. On – about questionnaires and things like that, we’re always probing to see where we stand in comparison to what our priorities are and where that is of other countries. You’re never going to have a hundred percent on every issue, but that’s okay. But I would say our alignment with Iceland is generally very concrete. I mean, I think we share the same perspectives of the world. I think we share a lot in common. We have a shared history, which brings us to the conclusion that we identify the same things as threats and the same things as opportunities. And so that’s the way that I view that.

And so in the context of that – what was the second part of your question? Because I need to start writing these things down. These guys come with three-part questions. And – go ahead, I’m sorry.

QUESTION: Well, the second part was about – you spoke warmly of (inaudible), where do you think —

SECRETARY RUBIO: Oh, places to grow. Yeah, so I think —

QUESTION: Yeah. And the free trade agreement.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well, look – and the free trade agreement. That one I wrote. That one I did write down.

So on places where we can grow, I think I’ve highlighted some of those for you already today. Look, security is always important, right? Security underpins everything else. If you’re not secure, you can’t be prosperous. So I think there’s no doubt that – but we’re not starting from zero here. We have a history of security cooperation. What has changed is the world and the threats. What the threats looked like 20 years ago, 30 years ago are different than what they would look like today, so we have to modernize.

But we already have a baseline and a foundation of cooperation that extends all the way back for 75 years, so we’re not building something new here. We’re simply modernizing it. So there’s no doubt that on the security realm there’s very – ability to cooperate and continue to cooperate, and not just with the United States but with all of our NATO Allies, particularly those in the High North and that are involved in Arctic defense.

And – but beyond that, I think the economic opportunities are very real. You have very unique companies here that do some very unique things in the pharmaceutical realm, in biotechnology, in a variety of fields that we think there are real opportunities for them to do business in the United States. And likewise, I think there are some business opportunities potentially here that we’d like to present to American investors, which is why what we’d like to do as a follow-up, as a concrete follow-up to my visit here, is organize visits of American businesses here to identify those opportunities and see if there’s some synergy, and likewise invite companies from Iceland to come to the United States and find sectors and areas where they could also invest in our economy or find markets. So I think that’s very positive.

As far as free trade agreements are concerned, look, I think the era of free trade agreements for the foreseeable future is probably not going to be there. I mean not with Iceland but just in general writ large. Where I do think we have real opportunities is a bilateral trade agreement – bilateral trade, a reciprocal trade understanding between our countries. And it’s my understanding that meetings to try to pursue and further that are being organized as already pre-existing to my visit, and hopefully those will be very positive.

And that ties in perfectly to my previous answer to you, which is there are companies here to do very unique things that we would like to see in the United States, and there are companies in the United States that I think could find some real positive economic opportunities to invest and be a part of here. And we just want to – we want to use the government, our embassy, our presence here, your embassy in the United States, to connect and create that synergy. And we will both benefit from it. You’ll become more prosperous, we’ll become more prosperous, and I think it will only bind us together more closely.

MODERATOR: Thank you. And lastly we will go to Shannon Kingston from ABC News.

QUESTION: Thank you very much, Mr. Secretary, Madam Foreign Minister. A question on – the State Department has assessed that Russia maintains an active offensive bioweapons program. There are also reports now that the FSB is involved in a forceful response to the recent fatal suspected plague death in Siberia. My question for you is – for you both is: Do you see any reason to suspect that what we’re seeing now might be the accidental release of an intentionally modified strain of the plague that was altered by Russia? What is your level of concern?

SECRETARY RUBIO: Well look, first of all, anytime you hear that there is some disease that infected someone in a lab anywhere in the world, you’re going to be concerned about it, especially given recent events not so long ago, obviously, in 2021 and 2020 when we saw that happen.

That said, it would be irresponsible for me here to sit and speculate because we just don’t have all the information yet. I think it’s incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world. That’s what they should do. That’s what we hope they will do. And the more we can learn about what happened, then the better all of us can be in a position of responding. And maybe there’s nothing there. Maybe it’s bigger than we thought. We don’t know.

But I think it would be reckless at this moment given the limited information we still have to speculate about what this might or might not be or what this is or what this isn’t. Suffice it to say we’re watching it very closely, and I think the whole world is watching it very closely, because depending on what we learn about it, we would know how to respond. We already have measures in place to be able to address it if it’s something more serious than what so far has been acknowledged.

Suffice it to say we’re glad to be aware of it. We’re watching it very closely hour by hour. We have multiple agencies not just in the United States but internationally that are watching it. We encourage Russia to be transparent and share more information with the world so that all of us could react accordingly and appropriately, but we’ll have to make those decisions on the basis of the information that we’re learning and are being provided. And so far that’s still quite limited, but hopefully that will change in the next few hours and days.

MODERATOR: And with that we conclude this press conference. Thank you very much.

FOREIGN MINISTER GUNNARSDÓTTIR: Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: Thank you.

Tags
title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Icelandic Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir at a Joint Press Availability

WASHINGTON, DC — Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) has introduced the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act to reinstate federal funding for New York’s Essential Plan and restore health coverage for nearly 15,000 people in NY-19 and more than 450,000 New Yorkers.
New York’s Essential Plan is a lifeline for working families, providing comprehensive health coverage at affordable rates. However, H.R.1 – Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act – slashed funding for the program, forcing thousands of Upstate New Yorkers to sign up for more expensive private insurance or forgo coverage altogether.
“Upstate New Yorkers work hard, play by the rules, and deserve health care they can actually afford,” Riley said. “Washington politicians handed out massive tax breaks to the wealthy and big corporations, then paid for them by ripping health care away from working families. These cuts will drive up premiums, put more pressure on our rural hospitals, and leave thousands of Upstate New Yorkers without coverage. I’m fighting to reverse them and restore the health care our communities depend on.”
You can read the text of the Restoring Essential Plan Coverage Act HERE.
This bill builds on Riley’s ongoing push to defend healthcare in Upstate New York:
- April 2025: Supported the Protecting Options for Seniors Act (H.R. 2610) to ensure fairer reimbursement rates for rural hospitals.
- May 2025: Requested over $55 million for rural infrastructure and community health projects for Fiscal Year 2026.
- July 2025: Opposed the “One Big Beautiful Bill” (H.R. 1) that cut Medicaid and threatened hospital closures.
- August 2025: Co-sponsored the Rural Hospital Stabilization Act (H.R. 3063) to provide $500 million in emergency support for rural hospitals.
- November 2025: Sent letters to the CEOs of UnitedHealth Group, Humana, and CVS Health demanding answers for their decision to drop Medicare Advantage plans in rural communities across Upstate New York.
- December 2025: Supported CommonGround2025, a bipartisan proposal to stop premium hikes, protect families’ health coverage, and keep healthcare affordable in Upstate New York.
###
title: RILEY INTRODUCES BILL TO RESTORE HEALTH COVERAGE FOR 450,000 NEW YORKERS

Midwest Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase
October 6, 2026
Two-Story Manufactured Home by Champion Home Builders
ILLINOIS - U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) spotlighted multiple housing innovations from the Midwest region during the sixth annual Innovative Housing Showcase, held September 22-24 on the National Mall. This year’s theme, “Made in America,” highlighted American ingenuity and innovative approaches to expanding housing affordability and homeownership.
“Across the Midwest, communities are looking for ways to increase the supply of affordable housing options,” said Region V Administrator Duey Stroebel. “At the Innovative Housing Showcase, I saw firsthand how local companies are looking outside the box to increase the housing supply and make homeownership more affordable for everyday Americans.”
HUD’s “Made in America” Showcase spotlighted American builders, manufacturers and innovators’ modern technologies and creative housing solutions that are expanding housing supply, lowering construction costs, and putting affordable homeownership back in reach for hardworking Americans. The Showcase featured a variety of full-scale housing models including manufactured, 3D printed, and modular homes built by American companies from across the nation.
Examples from the Midwest
Two manufactured homes, including a two-story prototype, from Champion Home Builders (Michigan).
Guardian Structural Technologies’ (Ohio) SHIELD panels, which are energy-efficient modular panels used to frame houses and roofs.
James Hardie’s (Illinois) OneHardie exterior and outdoor living portfolio that connect durable cladding, decking, trim, and shade structures into a cohesive, resilient home solution.
Follow @SecretaryTurner on X, FB, and Instagram.
title: Midwest Housing Innovations Spotlighted at HUD’s Innovative Housing Showcase

text:
United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that Tenia A. Thompson, 51, of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was arrested and charged by indictment with 17 counts of wire fraud, two counts of bank fraud, one count of filing a false tax return, and 49 counts of aiding the filing of a false tax return, arising from a scheme to defraud the Small Business Administration (“SBA”), multiple SBA-approved lenders participating in the Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (“EIDL”) program — both established as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (“CARES”) Act, a federal law enacted in March 2020 — and the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”).
The indictment alleges that, from approximately April 2020 through June 2024, Thompson, the owner and operator of a financial services and tax preparation business called “Thompson Business and Tax Solutions” and “TBTS Taxes,” (collectively, “TBTS”) prepared false tax returns for individuals and businesses and helped them apply for and obtain COVID-19 disaster-related loans and tax benefits to which the clients were not entitled. After fraudulently obtaining these loans and tax benefits for them, Thompson charged the clients exorbitant fees.
As alleged, the defendant engaged in this fraudulent activity on behalf of more than 100 clients, generating at least $12 million in fraudulent loan proceeds, at least $5 million in fraudulent tax benefits, and at least $2.2 million in fees for herself. Moreover, Thompson fraudulently attempted to obtain tens of millions of dollars in additional tax benefits on behalf of her clients, but the IRS rejected most of these claims.
If convicted, the defendant faces a maximum possible sentence of 20 years in prison for each count of wire fraud, 30 years in prison for each count of bank fraud, and three years in prison for each tax count. In addition, she would face up to three years of supervised release, a fine of $18,750,000, and additional financial penalties.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
This case was investigated by the FBI, Amtrak Office of Inspector General, IRS Criminal Investigation, and the SBA Office of Inspector General. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Louis D. Lappen and S. Chandler Harris.
The charges and allegations contained in the indictment are merely accusations. Every defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.
title: Philadelphia Woman Indicted for Sprawling Scheme to Defraud the Government Through Bogus Pandemic Loan Applications, False Tax Returns

WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) announced more than $7 million in awards to establish nine new Regional Innovation Clusters (RICs) supporting small businesses and startups in biotechnology, defense, advanced manufacturing, and transportation. The clusters will serve as regional hubs connecting entrepreneurs with resources and opportunities—including business acceleration programs, market research, customer discovery, and government and commercial contracting assistance—to help them access funding, pursue procurement opportunities, and strengthen domestic supply chains.
“President Trump is restoring America’s industrial capacity—from defense systems and biotechnology to advanced manufacturing and transportation,” said SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler. “By expanding and modernizing our nationwide network of Regional Innovation Clusters, the SBA is supercharging production capacity in communities across the country and helping small businesses bring critical technologies from the drawing board to the factory floor. The result is a stronger industrial base, more resilient supply chains, and less dependence on foreign competitors.”
A Regional Innovation Cluster is a concentration of small businesses, suppliers, buyers, manufacturers, research institutions, and capital providers organized around a single industry in a single geographic area. The RIC Program strengthens industry through regional collaboration connecting small businesses with end customers — shortening the distance between a small business with a product and the prime contractor, manufacturer, or buyer that needs it.
With these nine new awards, there are now 12 RICs serving unique regions across the country to support small businesses in critical industries like advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical minerals, defense, and transportation.
The new RIC award recipients are as follows:
To learn more about the RIC Program, visit https://sba.gov/local-assistance/regional-innovation-clusters.
# # #
About the U.S. Small Business Administration
The U.S. Small Business Administration helps power the American dream of entrepreneurship. As the leading voice for small businesses within the federal government, the SBA empowers job creators with the resources and support they need to start, grow, and expand their businesses or recover from a declared disaster. It delivers services through an extensive network of SBA field offices and partnerships with public and private organizations. To learn more, visit www.sba.gov.
title: SBA Awards Over $7 Million Create Nine New Regional Innovation Clusters

Former Federal Employee Pleads Guilty to Defrauding the Federal Government of Approximately $194 Million
David J. Rush, 49, of Ashburn, Virginia, pleaded guilty today to executing a scheme to defraud the federal government relating to the misuse of his government position, resulting in a loss of approximately $194 million.
“Federal employees are entrusted with serving the American people, not themselves,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The Trump Administration is committed to rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse in the federal government, including by prosecuting those who foolishly defraud American taxpayers.”
“Following an internal investigation that identified potential crimes, CIA immediately referred this matter to the FBI,” said CIA Director John Ratcliffe. “David Rush abused his position and betrayed the public trust and should be held fully accountable for his actions. We appreciate our law enforcement partners in the FBI and Department of Justice for securing this outcome. The Agency is committed to ensuring that those entrusted with our Nation’s secrets are held to the absolute highest standard.”
“By his own admission, David Rush defrauded the government of hundreds of millions of dollars, and then misused those funds for extravagant purchases,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Rush betrayed his oath, his co-workers, and the American people and he will now face justice for his actions. This plea demonstrates the FBI’s commitment to protecting the public’s trust; and that no government position, security clearance, or access to government resources places anyone above the law.”
“Our Intelligence Community must have the trust of the American people to operate effectively in a Nation committed to transparency and the rule of law,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “Rush repeatedly betrayed that trust. He defrauded the United States out of approximately $194 million in real estate, jewelry, and other valuable property, including 298 gold bars. Worse, his self-serving actions threatened to erode public confidence in the intelligence services that must strive in secret to keep America safe. Thankfully, the efforts of the Department of Justice, its partners in law enforcement, and the Intelligence Community exposed Rush’s crimes. Today’s plea marks an important step in bringing Rush to justice.”
“The United States entrusted Davis Rush with the resources to protect our nation and its people, and for sheer avarice he chose to betray that trust for personal enrichment,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos for the Eastern District of Virginia. “He robbed his country, not just of its treasury, but also of its faith. This office is committed to prosecuting those who undermine the security of the United States.”
According to court documents, Rush was employed in a senior executive-level position with a federal agency and held a Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance. He reached that position, in part, by lying about his education and military experience. Rush used his position of extraordinary public trust to create fictitious government authorities – including a fabricated Special Access Program – to obtain U.S. government funds for his personal benefit. Once he received the funds, Rush acquired gold bars and directed approximately $145 million in wire transfers that he ultimately used to purchase luxury real estate, watches, and at least one car. As a result of his scheme, Rush fraudulently obtained approximately $193,590,400 in U.S. government funds.
Cash and gold bars recovered in search of Rush's residence
On May 19, 2026, the FBI searched Rush’s residence and recovered 298 gold bars, approximately $2,106,550 in cash, €104,795, and numerous luxury watches. Rush had obtained the gold bars at an approximate cost to the government of $46 million. Pursuant to the plea agreement, Rush has agreed to forfeit the gold bars and currency found at his home, the fraudulently obtained properties, 30 watches (many of which were Rolexes), and two 2026 BMW Alpina vehicles, at least one of which is valued at approximately $172,000.
Rush is scheduled to be sentenced on Jan. 28, 2027. He faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release, forfeiture, restitution, and a fine. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
The case is prosecuted by Trial Attorneys Kevin C. Hakala and Kathryn D. DeMarco of the Justice Department’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Raizza K. Ty, Gavin R. Tisdale, and Anthony T. Aminoff for the Eastern District of Virginia.
The U.S. Navy’s Naval Criminal Investigative Service also provided valuable assistance to the investigation.
The Department of Justice’s investigation is continuing. The Director of National Intelligence has requested that the Inspector General for the Intelligence Community initiate an investigation.
Related court documents and information are located on the website of the District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia or on PACER by searching for Case No. 1:26-cr-00185.
title: Former Federal Employee Pleads Guilty to Defrauding the Federal Government of Approximately $194 Million

Rep. Grijalva Statement on Border Patrol Raid Near Lochiel, Arizona
Nogales, Arizona – Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the below statement following reports of a U.S. Border Patrol raid and the toppling of a centuries-old cottonwood tree along the U.S.-Mexico border near Lochiel, Arizona. This comes after a U.S. Forest Service announcement posted on its website – without any prior public input or notification – last week closing roads and restricting public access to miles of lands along the U.S.-Mexico border as they proceed with wall construction.
“Just days after the U.S. Forest Service closed miles of public lands along the border, armed Border Patrol agents conducted a raid that injured protesters and uprooted the last of four century-old cottonwood trees. This is what the militarization of our borderlands looks like – and it’s all because DHS has more taxpayer dollars than it knows what to do with, and is wasting them on a reckless and useless second border wall. Our borderlands are home to unique ecosystems and world-class biodiversity, including some of the last remaining habitat for the Sonoran jaguar in the United States.
DHS and its private contractors have repeatedly shown they cannot be trusted to protect sensitive cultural and environmental sites. That is why public access and oversight are so critical. Instead, DHS is following the same playbook: shut out the public, evade scrutiny, and recklessly bulldoze our lands. Administrations come and go, but unfortunately the damage the Trump administration is inflicting on our irreplaceable borderlands cannot simply be undone.”
title: Rep. Grijalva Statement on Border Patrol Raid Near Lochiel, Arizona

Washington, DC – Congresswoman Julia Brownley (D-CA) joined Congressman Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and Senator Brian Schatz (D-HI) in introducing a resolution standing strong for the American freedom to read, write and learn. The lawmakers’ resolution condemns MAGA’s escalating campaign of book bans in school libraries and censorship targeting the Smithsonian Institution and other public museums, parks and facilities.
The lawmakers’ resolution specifically cites book bans issued by the Trump Administration, MAGA state legislatures, local libraries and schools across America. This year, federal officials, at the direction of President Trump, censored books and educational materials at the Smithsonian Institution and Department of Defense Education Activity schools.
More than 12,000 individual books were banned in America between July 2025 and June 2026, according to a report by PEN America. This includes books like “The Bluest Eye” by Toni Morrison and “MARCH” by former Congressman and Civil Rights Movement hero John Lewis, Andrew Aydin and Nate Powell.
PEN America’s report captures the proliferation of MAGA book bans that specifically target books written by and about outsiders and individuals from marginalized backgrounds. Books with LGBTQ+ characters or themes face a disproportionate risk of being banned.
According to PEN America, from July 2025 to June 2026, 24 States across the country limited access to certain books, including:
- Texas, where at least 8,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 45 school districts;
- Florida, where at least 3,000 books in total have been banned or restricted in 35 school districts;
- Ohio, where at least 115 books in total have been banned or restricted in one school district;
- Utah, where at least 100 books in total have been banned or restricted in five school districts; and
- Michigan, where at least 65 books in total have been banned or restricted in two school districts.
The resolution is endorsed by PEN America and the American Library Association (ALA); Authors Against Banned Books; Banned Books Week Coalition; Center for American Progress; EdTrust; EveryLibrary; Freedom to Learn Foundation; Florida Freedom to Read Project; Freedom to Read Project; Hatchette Book Group; Interfaith Alliance; JCRC of Greater Washington; Jewish Community Relations Council of Portland; Jewish Council for Public Affairs; Jewish Federation of Greater Rochester; Lee & Low Books ; Let Utah Read; Macmillan Publishing; National Coalition Against Censorship; National Council for Jewish Women; National Council of Teachers of English; National Education Association; Penguin Random House; PFLAG National; Red Wine and Blue Education Fund; Simon & Schuster; Texas Freedom to Read Project; and the Tucson Jewish Museum & Holocaust Center.
The resolution is also cosponsored in the House by Representatives Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Shontel Brown (OH-11), Andre Carson (IN-07), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Emmanuel Cleaver (MO-5), Jim Costa (CA-21), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jahana Hayes (CT-05), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Summer Lee (PA-12), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Betty McCollum (MN-04), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Grace Meng (NY-06), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Scott Peters (CA-50), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Marc Veasey (TX-33), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Nikema Williams (GA-05) and Frederica Wilson (FL-24).
The resolution is cosponsored in the Senate by Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Angus King (I-ME), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ed Markey (D-MA), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), John Fetterman (D-PA) and Ben Ray Luján (D-NM).

Rep. McBride, Senator Coons, local leaders assess coastal damage, call for more funding to rebuild Delaware’s beaches following storm
DEWEY BEACH, Del. – U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senator Chris Coons (both D-Del.), joined by the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, local elected officials, and community leaders surveyed damage on Friday morning from last week’s nor’easter that battered Delaware’s coast for four days and caused severe beach erosion, dune damage and flooding in communities all along the coast. The storm damaged homes and businesses, caused road closures, and shut down beaches. Following their assessment of the damage, Senator Coons and Representative McBride called for additional federal support to help Delaware’s coastal communities recover and replenish their beaches.
Rep. McBride and Senator Coons were joined on Friday by officials from the Army Corps of Engineers, DNREC Secretary Greg Patterson, Dewey Beach Town Manager Bill Zolper, Dewey Beach Mayor Bill Stevens, South Bethany Mayor Edie Dondero, Bethany Beach Mayor Ron Calef, State Sen. Russ Huxtable and State Rep. Claire Snyder-Hall.
“Delaware’s beaches are critical to our communities, our economy, and our way of life, and we need to make sure they have the resources they need to recover from this storm and prepare for the next one,” said Senator Coons. “I’m going to keep fighting for the funding Delaware needs to rebuild and recover. That means working with our local leaders, DNREC, the Army Corps and our entire congressional delegation to make sure we’re doing everything we can to protect our coast.”
“The damage Senator Coons and I saw is a stark reminder that investing in the resilience of our coastal communities is not optional,” said Rep. McBride. “We cannot prevent these storms from happening, but we can take action to keep people safe and help our communities withstand their impacts. That’s why I’ve been working with partners at every level of government to strengthen our coastline, combat coastal erosion, and ensure Delaware is prepared when severe weather strikes. I’m grateful to Mayor Stevens, our first responders, local leaders, and everyone who stepped up to keep our neighbors safe during the nor’easter. I’ll keep working to make sure Delaware has what it needs to recover from this storm, prepare for the next one, and protect our beaches for generations to come.”
Earlier this year, Senators Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester and Representative McBride helped secure $10 million for beach replenishment along the Delaware coast from Cape Henlopen to Fenwick Island and are working with the Army Corps of Engineers to make that funding available as quickly as possible. Senator Coons is also working with the federal delegation and DNREC to secure an additional $30 million in federal beach replenishment funding this year to help address the state’s ongoing coastal needs.
###
title: Rep. McBride, Senator Coons, local leaders assess coastal damage, call for more funding to rebuild Delaware’s beaches following storm
