text:
MATSUI, DUCKWORTH, SCHUMER LEAD BIPARTISAN CALL REQUIRING FAA TO GUARANTEE EVERY EMERGENCY MEDICAL KIT ABOARD FLIGHTS INCLUDE LIFE-SAVING EPINEPHRINE
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA-07), Co-Chair of the Congressional Food Allergy Research Caucus, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL),Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation, and U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) led a group of 20 bipartisan, bicameral lawmakers in calling on the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to guarantee that emergency medical kits (EMK) on every commercial aircraft include epinephrine, a life-saving medication to treat passengers who go into anaphylactic shock. Today is the final day for the American people to submit public comments on the FAA’s dangerous new proposed rule that would result in medications being less consistent and dependable for passengers experiencing health emergencies on commercial flights—a severely misguided proposal that prioritizes flexibility for air carriers over the safety of the flying public.
“Without proper medications that can easily be administered on board, medical emergencies happening while 35,000 feet in the air could turn deadly,” wrote the lawmakers in their official public comment to the FAA’s proposed rule. “The provisions outlined in the FAA’s proposed rule threaten the safety of airline passengers traveling with allergies and reverse previous FAA action to ensure the safety of all passengers.”
In the landmark 2024 FAA Reauthorization Law that Congresswoman Matsui supported, the FAA requires commercial airlines to have adequate emergency medical kits on board to treat conditions like anaphylaxis. And yet, the FAA’s proposed rule would not require them to carry epinephrine—the only medication that reliably treats this medical emergency—in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training.
The lawmakers continued, “If a passenger is experiencing anaphylaxis, they could have mere seconds until they are unable to breathe. Without FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed to be easily self-administered, passengers rely on the chance that there will be a good Samaritan on the flight who is a trained medical professional, or a flight attendant, in consultation with a medical professional on the ground, to quickly measure an appropriate dose of epinephrine using a vial and syringe. This is both risky and unnecessary; it is why the FAA’s working group recommended ‘pre-measured auto-delivery device’ be on the EMK contents list.”
In their letter, the lawmakers hammered the FAA’s proposed rule for ignoring expert recommendations, creating an even greater lack of transparency and consistency in EMKs for the flying public—who rely on EMKs during a medical emergency—and for needlessly putting the lives of commercial airline passengers at greater risk.
“To ensure the safety of all airline passengers, we must guarantee that U.S.-based airlines include FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed for self-administration on every flight,” the lawmakers concluded.
In light of the FAA’s misguided and dangerous proposed rule change, Matsui, Duckworth, and Schumer are calling on the FAA to heed their concerns—as well as the more than 1,500 public comments that have been submitted to express deep concern over this would-be policy failure that would place cost cutting and convenience for air carriers over the safety of the flying public.
In addition to Matsui, the letter is co-signed in the House by U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01), Maxwell Frost (D-FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-08), LaMonica McIver (D-NJ-10), Kelly Morrison (D-MN-03) and Mike Quigley (D-IL-05). In addition to Duckworth and Schumer, the letter is co-signed in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).
Full text of the letter can be found below and HERE.
Dear Administrator Bedford:
We write to provide our comments on the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) published on August 5, 2026, which would make drastic changes to how the FAA determines the composition of the emergency medical kit (EMK) carried aboard aircraft. The proposed rule is opaque and dangerous, and it threatens to undermine previous work the FAA has done to ensure the safety of the traveling public.
EMKs are supposed to enable initial treatment of a passenger experiencing moderate to severe injuries or illnesses until the aircraft can land and the passenger can be transferred to emergency medical personnel. Without proper medications that can easily be administered on board, medical emergencies happening while 35,000 feet in the air could turn deadly.
The proposed rule would make harmful steps to reverse work done at the agency to direct operators to include epinephrine in aircraft EMKs. Having multiple doses of epinephrine on every aircraft, in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training, is more urgent than ever. This is due to the on-flight presence of food items containing unlabeled allergens, a steady increase in the number of children with food allergies, the increased prevalence of a tick-borne illness that could create life-threatening allergies and the very real possibility that more than one passenger may require epinephrine during a single flight.
The provisions outlined in the FAA’s proposed rule threaten the safety of airline passengers traveling with allergies and reverse previous FAA action to ensure the safety of all passengers.
Our concerns about the proposed rule are outlined below:
Lack of Alignment with Previous Recommendations
The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 directed the FAA to assemble a panel of experts to make recommendations on EMKs and issue a proposed rule. The FAA Onboard Medical Kits Working Group included aerospace medicine experts and physicians, physiologists, psychologists, human factors specialists, cabin safety professionals and researchers. This working group submitted its report, dated May 1, 2025, to the FAA. The report stated:
“The items proposed … are intended to provide initial stabilizing Basic Life Support (BLS) care for immediately life-threatening conditions such as cardiac arrest, airway emergencies, major hemorrhage, andanaphylaxis (emphasis added), as well as to facilitate provision of limited basic first-aid interventions for minor injuries and illnesses that are known to occur in-flight.”
Importantly, the proposed EMK content list in the report includes both “pre-measured auto-delivery device” or “vial-drawn kit.” Yet, just one year later, the FAA publicly defied the recommendations in this report developed by the expert working group the FAA itself commissioned.
No Clear Requirement for Epinephrine
Through rulemaking, the Trump administration is seeking to downgrade the EMK content list, from a binding requirement to mere optional guidance. The proposed rule would allow operators to determine what components should be included in EMKs, so long as the EMK is “practical and sufficient” to address nine conditions, including anaphylaxis:
“…FAA recommends sufficient resources for anaphylaxis (sudden/acute severe allergic reaction), which may include the following signs and symptoms: hives; swelling of the mouth, throat, or tongue; difficulty breathing, rapid or weak pulse, dizziness; stomach pain; nausea or vomiting; or loss of consciousness. Treatment options could (emphasis added) include medication such as epinephrine.”
Epinephrine is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. The final rule must contain a clear directive that EMKs shall include epinephrine.
No Requirement for Epinephrine in Easily Self-Administered Forms
If a passenger is experiencing anaphylaxis, they could have mere seconds until they are unable to breathe. Without Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed to be easily self-administered, passengers rely on the chance that there will be a good Samaritan on the flight who is a trained medical professional, or a flight attendant, in consultation with a medical professional on the ground, to quickly measure an appropriate dose of epinephrine using a vial and syringe. This is both risky and unnecessary; it is why the FAA’s working group recommended “pre-measured auto-delivery device” be on the EMK contents list.
Currently, JetBlue, Southwest, Breeze and Frontier stock their EMKs with epinephrine auto-injectors, and American Airlines’ EMKs include both adult- and pediatric-dose epinephrine auto-injectors. Delta is in the process of transitioning its fleet to include auto-injectors in their EMKs by September 2027, and, this year, United Airlines and Allegiant Airlines will begin the work to include auto-injectors in EMKs. Even with tight profit margins, including epinephrine in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered, is possible. Through the rulemaking process, the FAA must direct airlines to include epinephrine in delivery methods that can be easily administered and not reverse course from its previous recommendations by abandoning the requirement to include epinephrine in EMKs in entirety.
Lack of Transparency on Compliance
The proposed rule would eliminate the exemption process, which was created to account for challenges in stocking EMKs due to drug shortages and allow airlines to substitute drugs, “without requesting an FAA exemption.” Airlines are not required to publicly or centrally report the real-time inventory and exact contents of their EMKs and have continued to operate under exemptions granted by the FAA for years. EMK suppliers and airlines can track when an EMK is opened and needs restocking, but only in instances where the kit was used. There is no means of systematically tracking incidents of allergic reactions or anaphylaxis, especially when passengers use their own epinephrine. For medical conditions that can be treated by multiple, accessible options, eliminating the need for the exemption process may make sense. However, epinephrine is the only first-line treatment for anaphylaxis. The public also deserves to know when certain items are not included in a flight’s EMK, and a rationale for the exclusion.
Conclusion
The proposed rule will reduce public safety and trust when flying by increasing ambiguity, subjectivity and opacity of EMK components. The proposed rule argues that increased flexibility is needed to keep up with advances in medicine but, without appropriate reporting and tracking, the Trump administration is significantly increasing the risk of major inconsistencies in EMKs from flight to flight. Predictability, consistency and transparency are all necessary to ensure passengers’ safety, particularly in cases of anaphylaxis, when minutes, or even seconds, matter.
To ensure the safety of all airline passengers,we must guarantee that U.S.-based airlines include FDA-approved epinephrine delivery methods designed for self-administration on every flight.
We call on the FAA to address the concerns outlined in this letter.
title: MATSUI, DUCKWORTH, SCHUMER LEAD BIPARTISAN CALL REQUIRING FAA TO GUARANTEE EVERY EMERGENCY MEDICAL KIT ABOARD FLIGHTS INCLUDE LIFE-SAVING EPINEPHRINE

Pou Demands Answers After 5,500-Gallon Data Center Diesel Spill
Record-setting leak fouled creek connected to Hackensack River
PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) is seeking answers from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) following a massive diesel fuel spill at an Equinix data center in Secaucus that contaminated local waterways in her district.
Pou called for a full accounting of the roughly 5,500-gallon spill, its environmental impact, and the safeguards being put in place to prevent another data center disaster.
“This spill in the Ninth District was the largest data center fuel spill on record in our state. The scale of this disaster demands a full accounting. We need to understand how it happened, ensure the cleanup is complete, and put protections in place to prevent another one happening again. Our residents deserve clear answers now,” Congresswoman Pou writes to New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Commissioner Ed Potosnak.
Secaucus and surrounding communities have lived with pollution for decades. Contamination from industrial sites and landfill runoff led the Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River a Superfund site in 2022. Now as a major cleanup is underway, the September 11 Equinix spill has dumped another 5,500 gallons of diesel into the local environment.
The Secaucus spill comes amid growing national concern over the environmental impact and public costs of rapidly expanding data centers. These facilities consume large amounts of electricity and can require significant water for cooling. Also, as seen in Secaucus, they can often store large quantities of diesel to power backup generators.
Data center electricity demand is rising rapidly, raising questions about energy costs and who should pay for the infrastructure needed to serve these facilities. The Secaucus spill highlights what can happen when the systems designed to keep these massive facilities running fail.
Pou concludes, “NJDEP has a vital role in protecting New Jersey’s environment and holding data centers and their owners accountable when safeguards fail. The scale of this disaster demands a full accounting. . . . Thank you for your attention to this matter.”
A copy of Congresswoman Pou’s letter is below.
Dear Commissioner Potosnak:
I write to express my concern about the recent fuel spill at the Equinix data center in Secaucus that contaminated nearby waterways. Over the last decade, several data centers have experienced large-scale fuel spills, including several in New Jersey. In 2017, roughly 600 gallons of fuel spilled into Clifton’s storm drains from the Digital Realty EWR21 Data Center. Then, in 2022, more than 1800 gallons leaked from an Equinix-owned data center in North Bergen. Now, just weeks ago, Secaucus has experienced the largest data center diesel spill on record in our state. Residents and local officials deserve to know how this happened, what damage it caused, and what safeguards will keep this from happening again.
Secaucus and the surrounding communities have a long history of dealing with pollution. Decades of contamination from manufacturing plants and landfill runoff into the Hackensack River prompted the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to designate the Lower Hackensack River as a Superfund site in 2022. The river is already undergoing a major cleanup after those years of contamination.
Against that backdrop, the September 11 spill is especially alarming. According to public reports, roughly 5,500 gallons of diesel fuel escaped the Equinix data center into a creek and tributary connected to the Hackensack River.5 The spill reportedly occurred during an automated fuel-recycling process and has been attributed to a “computer glitch.”
Three weeks later, the public still lacks a full accounting of the spill’s impact on local waterways and wildlife. The incident also raises broader questions about the environmental risks posed by data centers, including the storage and handling of large quantities of backup fuel. Those questions are particularly urgent here given the major federal cleanup underway on the Hackensack River.
I appreciate that NJDEP is working to investigate and address the spill. But NJDEP must provide a clear account of exactly what happened and what is being done to prevent another spill to ensure transparency and accountability. To that end, please provide answers to the following questions no later than October 9, 2026.
1) Please identify the best available timeline for when each of the following events occurred on September 11, 2026 and any days thereafter:
a) Equinix began its fuel recycling process.
b) The system failed, and fuel began spilling.
c) Equinix first identified the spill.
d) The flow of fuel was stopped.
e) Equinix first contacted emergency responders.
f) Equinix first notified NJDEP.
g) The emergency response team arrived on site.
h) Crews began containment efforts to prevent the diesel from spreading.
i) NJDEP first notified Secaucus officials about the spill and the response.
j) Any barges or other cleanup equipment that were removed from the site, and the basis for determining they were no longer needed.
2) Has NJDEP continued to brief Secaucus on the containment and cleanup? If so, please provide the dates of those communications. If not, please explain why.
3) Following the spill, has NJDEP required Equinix or other data centers to adopt human, on-site monitoring and other safeguards for automated fuel systems or other risks to the community? If so, please describe those requirements. If not, please explain why.
4) Has NJDEP determined whether diesel from the spill reached the Hackensack River? If so, please provide its findings and any information on remediation and cleanup.
5) When does NJDEP expect to complete its investigation and issue a final public report on the spill?
NJDEP has a vital role in protecting New Jersey’s environment and holding data centers and their owners accountable when safeguards fail. This spill in the Ninth District was the largest data center fuel spill on record in our state. The scale of this disaster demands a full accounting. We need to understand how it happened, ensure the cleanup is complete, and put protections in place to prevent another one happening again. Our residents deserve clear answers now.
Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response.
Sincerely,
Nellie Pou
Member of Congress
###
title: Pou Demands Answers After 5,500-Gallon Data Center Diesel Spill

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (D-Va.-07) joined Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.-10) and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) in a letter warning the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) about the potential consequences of the proposed merger between NextEra Energy, Inc. (“NextEra”) and Dominion Energy (“Dominion”), and urged the regulator to closely examine the deal and block it if it would increase consumers’ energy costs or otherwise fail to meet public interest requirements.
On May 18, 2026, NextEra announced a $66.8 billion deal to merge with Dominion. The proposed deal would eliminate a competitor in the energy generation market and create the largest regulated electric utility in the world. It would be the fourth largest merger of all time and would create a company worth $420 billion.
A NextEra-Dominion entity would serve about 10 million homes and businesses across Virginia, Florida, North Carolina, and South Carolina, but the effects of the merger — including higher electricity rates — could extend even further. Residential electricity prices have risen 15 percent since January 2025, and families are projected to spend an average of $110 more on electricity bills in 2026 than they did last year.
The full text of the letter can be found here.
“The merger would give the combined company control over approximately a quarter of the electricity in the New England region, leading to considerable negotiating leverage over states and the ability to demand abusive terms at the expense of households,” wrote the lawmakers. “This megamerger may consolidate competitive power markets and raise electricity rates even more for American families.”
Under the Federal Power Act, FERC shall approve a merger of public utilities only if the applicants demonstrate that the merger is in the public interest and does not pose a risk of harmful cross-subsidization, and may block a merger that is not “consistent with the public interest.”
“Our fundamental concern is that this new entity will be both a gigantic power generator and a gigantic power-providing utility,” wrote the lawmakers. “We urge you to closely scrutinize this merger and block it if the Commission determines it would increase market concentration or have an adverse effect on costs for consumers—or if the acquisition is otherwise not in the public interest.”
The lawmakers are concerned that a NextEra-Dominion merger would create an even larger vertically integrated electricity utility and electricity generator that will squash competition and raise prices. Previous utility mergers have coincided with increases in household electricity costs. Additionally, a merger increasing the market share of already vertically integrated utility companies could make it even easier for the combined entity to engage in improper “cross-subsidization,” a practice by which corporations unfairly shift onto consumers the cost of transactions between utility companies and affiliate companies, which researchers say forces households to pay higher electricity rates.
“The consequences of failing to address utility merger harms, including by imposing insufficient mitigation measures, are not theoretical: when FERC allows utility companies to gain enough power to stamp out competition in an entire region, higher prices have followed,” wrote the lawmakers.
The lawmakers also warned that large utility companies that are intertwined with generating entities have strong incentives to oppose building transmission connections to bring in cheaper power from other regions, a problem that could get worse with the creation of a giant like NextEra-Dominion. New England states have accused NextEra of using its existing power to obstruct new transmission infrastructure projects.
“We therefore urge FERC to closely examine whether this deal may decrease competition or cause electricity rates for households to climb even higher; to remain skeptical of mitigation conditions that have historically failed to blunt the negative impacts of large utility merges; and to deny the application unless the applicants demonstrate that the transaction will have no adverse effect, now or in the future, on competition, rates, or regulation and will not result in impermissible cross-subsidization or the pledge or encumbrance of utility assets,” concluded the lawmakers. “If the present record is insufficient to make those findings, the Commission should deny the application.”
Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and Representatives Chris Deluzio (Pa.-17), Maggie Goodlander (N.H.-2), Raja Krishnamoorthi (Ill.-08), and Seth Magaziner (R.I.-02) also signed the letter.
BACKGROUND
In August, Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) was the first member of the Virginia delegation to speak out against the proposed merger. He sent a letter to members of the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) urging them to reject the proposed merger between Dominion Energy and NextEra energy. In the letter, Vindman warned that the deal would put Wall Street profits ahead of Virginia families, weaken local accountability, and increase costs for consumers. You can read his letter here.
Later that month, Vindman launched a district-wide survey asking for constituents’ thoughts on the proposed merger. The results were clear: of 950 respondents, the overwhelmingly majority opposed the merger between Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy, underscoring widespread concerns about the deal’s potential impact on Virginia ratepayers.
###
title: Vindman, Subramanyam, Warren Warn Utility Merger May Increase Prices, Urge Federal Regulator to Scrutinize Deal

California Woman Arrested on Charges Alleging She Acted as Agent of China and Spied on Relatives of U.S. Based High-Ranking Taiwanese Government Official
Wanying Zhang, 34, also known as Heather Zhang, of Irvine, California, was arrested Sunday on a one count complaint charging her with acting in the United States as an unregistered agent of the government of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), including by conducting surveillance on family members of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official.
“The central allegation here — that Zhang, at the behest of the People’s Republic of China, covertly surveilled relatives of a high-ranking foreign government official in the United States — is deeply troubling,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg. “The National Security Division and U.S. Attorney’s Offices, along with the FBI and other law enforcement partners, will remain vigilant against threats like this on our soil.”
“Protecting our national security means confronting foreign governments that engage in covert operations in our nation,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli for the Central District of California. “Ms. Zhang is charged with acting at the direction of Chinese government officials to spy on the family of a senior Taiwanese official here in the United States. She violated our laws and will be held accountable in our courts. We will aggressively investigate and prosecute illegal foreign operations on American soil.”
“The complaint in this case lays bare a brazen plot directed by the Chinese government to conduct a covert surveillance mission on U.S. soil targeting close relatives of a Taiwanese government official,” said Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “Wanying Zhang’s arrest for allegedly acting as an unregistered agent of the Chinese government makes clear how far China’s authoritarian regime will go to advance its goals. However, this case also demonstrates the FBI’s unwavering commitment to defending the sovereignty of our democratic allies and combating all attempts by the Chinese government — and any foreign adversary — to conduct transnational repression within our borders.”
Zhang was arrested prior to her planned departure from Los Angeles International Airport, where she planned to board a flight to China. She is expected to make her initial appearance and be arraigned this afternoon in U.S. District Court in downtown Los Angeles.
According to the complaint, from June 2025 to September 2025, Zhang acted as an agent of the PRC without prior notification to the Attorney General of the United States, as required by federal law.
At the direction and control of PRC officials, Zhang coordinated with other individuals to promote the interests of China by, among other things, conducting surveillance on family members of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official at their residence in the United States.
In June 2025, Zhang traveled from Southern California to China, where she met with PRC officials and was tasked with conducting surveillance in the United States.
On Aug. 29, 2025, Zhang and another individual flew from John Wayne Airport in Orange County to Las Vegas. On Sept. 1, 2025, they flew from Las Vegas to the Pacific Northwest, where the victims reside. On that date, Zhang messaged a PRC official that she was “Boarding now” and sent a photograph of her boarding pass.
Upon their arrival, Zhang and the other individual traveled to the victims’ residence and conducted surveillance. Zhang sent the same PRC official the following message: “Saw him, young male, it’s the young one.” When this official asked her to join an audio call, she replied, “I am videorecording.”
Zhang also sent the same official the license plate numbers for the two vehicles parked in front of the victims’ home.
If convicted, Zhang would face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
The FBI Los Angeles Field Office is investigating the case.
Senior Counsel Scott M. Lara of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Amanda B. Elbogen and Colin S. Scott for the Central District of California are prosecuting the case.
A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: California Woman Arrested on Charges Alleging She Acted as Agent of China and Spied on Relatives of U.S. Based High-Ranking Taiwanese Government Official

text:
Ongoing Review Ensures Sanctions Remain Targeted, Effective, and Current
WASHINGTON—Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) took another major action in its sanctions modernization effort, announced by Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent in May. Today’s action removed from OFAC’s sanctions lists 125 individuals and entities, consistent with current economic, national security, and foreign policy priorities. OFAC also updated 22 list entries to facilitate and enhance compliance screening.
Those removed include deceased individuals, defunct companies, and list entries lacking sufficient information for robust compliance screening. As with any removal from its sanctions lists, and consistent with prior sanctions modernization actions, OFAC conducted interagency review to ensure that today’s removals would not harm U.S. foreign policy or national security interests.
PRIORITIZING SANCTIONS IMPACT AND SUCCESS
As Secretary Bessent has outlined, the goal of Treasury’s sanctions modernization effort is to ensure U.S. sanctions remain targeted, effective, and aligned with U.S. economic, foreign policy, and national security priorities. The Trump Administration is measuring the success of its sanctions in terms of effect, impact, and benefit—not just based on the number of names Treasury places on a list.
Today’s action is part of this broader effort to streamline sanctions for greater efficiency and effectiveness, including through the review of sanctions programs that no longer support U.S. national security priorities. For example, on September 18, OFAC removed sanctions on six individuals and entities designated pursuant to a 2021 Ethiopia-related national emergency and sanctions program, which was not renewed because the circumstances that led to the underlying national emergency have changed such that the United States no longer requires the Ethiopia sanctions program to advance U.S. interests.
Sanctions list entries without appropriate identifying information can hamper private sector screening efforts by producing false positive matches. These may require financial institutions and businesses to spend considerable time on manual review and detract from compliance investigations that are consistent with current national security priorities. Accordingly, alongside today’s delistings, OFAC’s list updates have added new identifiers and removed outdated ones; this will further reduce compliance screening burden.
MODERNIZING SANCTIONS RECONSIDERATION
The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate persons and add them to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List when appropriate and consistent with the law.
For information on the process for seeking removal from an OFAC sanctions list, including the SDN List, please refer to How to Request Removal from an OFAC Sanctions List | Office of Foreign Assets Control. The recently released Reconsideration Portal enables persons and property on an OFAC sanctions list—or their authorized representatives—to submit delisting petitions and request certain information underlying their sanctions determinations.
###
title: Treasury Announces Third Round of Sanctions Removals, Updates in Modernization Initiative

Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) announced that she is filing a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request to force the Trump administration to release unseen information on the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) program, which pays private companies to use AI to review Medicare claims.
Since the program began in January in Washington and five other states, patients have been left in severe pain and unable to access care prescribed by their doctors. In June, DelBene announced that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) ordered the company administering WISeR in Washington to submit a corrective action plan for delays in reviewing claims following an audit. Neither the audit nor the corrective action plan has been released to Congress or the public. DelBene previously requested information on the model's performance from the administration and then moved to require CMS to release these documents through an amendment during a House Ways & Means Committee markup. The majority of Ways & Means Republicans rejected the amendment by an 18-19 vote.
DelBene announced her latest move to force the release of these documents and hold the administration accountable in an op-ed in the Everett Herald.
“Washington seniors have borne the brunt of this experimental program’s malfunctions,” DelBene wrote. “From January to March, over half of the claims submitted in Washington were denied and far exceeded the 72-hour decision deadline. This triggered an internal CMS audit and corrective action plan. This shouldn’t come as a surprise because the program pays these private companies for every claim they deny, which incentivizes them to reject more care.” 
“The audit and corrective action plan have never been released, which would further help inform lawmakers, health care providers, and patients about how WISeR is failing to function,” DelBene continued. “This stonewalling must end. That’s why I am filing a new FOIA request for these specific documents in addition to the audits and corrective action plans of any other private company participating in WISeR.” 
This effort follows a bombshell report from the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EEF) on the failures of WISeR that detailed widespread delays and denials, rushed implementation, and incentives for private companies reviewing claims to deny care. EFF obtained access to the documents uncovered in the report through a FOIA request and lawsuit. The report also revealed that the administration plans to expand WISeR to cancer treatments and other types of care despite clear, documented evidence of the program’s flaws. 
DelBene introduced legislation last November to repeal WISeR and has led multiple other legislative efforts to stop the program.
Read DelBene’s op-ed here. The text of the FOIA request can be found here.
title: DelBene Moves to Force Trump Administration to Release Files on AI Medicare Experiment

Rep. Neguse Leads Colleagues in Letter to State Department Urging Additional Support for Nepal Floods Response
Washington, D.C. — Today, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse, Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Congressional Nepal Caucus, led a dozen colleagues in a letter to the United States Department of State, urging they provide additional aid to Nepal as the country recovers from devastating floods in the Trishuli River region.
In late August, a glacier collapse on the Nepal-China border, caused catastrophic flooding, destroying homes, workplaces, roads, bridges, and energy infrastructure. The floods killed 1,450 people and nearly 6,000 people are still missing, including 90 Americans.
In their letter, Neguse and his colleagues noted that the United States has been a longstanding partner in Nepal’s development and called on the State Department to provide much needed support and stability to the country as it recovers and eventually rebuilds.
Full text of the letter is available HERE and below.
It was signed by André Carson (IN-07), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), James McGovern (MA-02), Janice Schakowsky (IL-09), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Emilia Sykes (OH-13), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Marc Veasey (TX-33), and Nydia Velázquez (NY-07).
October 1, 2026
The Honorable Marco Rubio
Secretary of State
U.S. Department of State
2201 C Street NW
Washington, DC 20520
Dear Secretary Rubio,
We write to respectfully request your administration provide further assistance to aid Nepal in its recovery efforts following the devastating floods in the Trishuli River region. Given the scale of this tragedy, we implore your department to act swiftly.
As you know, this unprecedented disaster has claimed at least 1,300 lives, with an estimated 5,000 people still missing—including 90 American citizens. Further, the destruction has left many in the region without access to clean drinking water, food, shelter, and other basic services, including thousands of children. As Nepal continues to recover, the U.S. is uniquely positioned to provide critical infrastructure support and essential supplies to aid these efforts.
The U.S. has been a longstanding partner in Nepal's development, supporting improvements in public health, education, infrastructure, and industry. Continued U.S. assistance would provide much needed stability to the country and help it to rebuild at this critical time.
As such, we urge the Department of State to work to assist search and rescue efforts across Nepal and to provide additional assistance to the country to ensure a speedy recovery.
Sincerely,
###
title: Rep. Neguse Leads Colleagues in Letter to State Department Urging Additional Support for Nepal Floods Response

Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 16 Aliens for Election Crimes
Today, the Justice Department announced charges involving 16 aliens in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes across the country. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of U.S. citizenship to register or vote, and false statements on citizenship applications.
Case details are as follows:
Middle District of Florida
Two aliens were charged for illegally voting in a federal election.
- Italian national Andrea Catanese, 60, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by federal indictment with voting by an alien, attempting to procure naturalization unlawfully, and making a false statement related to naturalization. Catanese allegedly voted in the 2024 general election, falsely stated he had never voted in a federal election on an Application for Naturalization, and then made the same false statement to an immigration official who was reviewing the application.
- Bahamian national Terrance Patrick Evans, 37, a lawful permanent resident, has been charged by information with one count of voting by an alien. According to the information, Evans voted in the 2024 federal general election despite knowing that he was not a citizen of the United States.
Eastern District of Louisiana
Three aliens were indicted for illegally voting in a federal election.
- Cuban national Pedro Pablo Ruiz, 68, a lawful permanent resident, has been indicted for illegal voting in a federal election. According to the indictment, Ruiz cast a ballot in the 2024 general election.
- Mexican national Zianya Yllaly Zamorano, 34, a lawful permanent resident has been indicted for illegal voting in an election. According to the indictment, Zamorano cast a ballot in the 2024 general election.
- Nicaraguan national Dudley Francisco Zeledon, 56, a lawful permanent resident has been charged in a two-count indictment for illegal voting in an election. According to the indictment, Zeldon cast a ballot in the 2024 primary and general elections.
Eastern District of Wisconsin
North Macedonian national Sara Luma, 30, a lawful permanent resident has been charged with Unlawfully Voting as a Non-Citizen. Luma allegedly voted in the 2024 general election. The criminal complaint further alleges Luma registered to vote on the same day as the election and signed the Wisconsin Voter Registration Application form falsely certifying that she was a citizen of the United States. Luma was interviewed by a federal law enforcement agent and admitted to registering and voting on Nov. 5, 2024.
District of Minnesota
Ten aliens have been charged in Minnesota for voter fraud.
- Liberian national Bhator Konah Bryant, 61, a lawful permanent resident has been charged on one count of making a false claim of citizenship in order to vote. She is alleged to have falsely claimed United States citizenship when registering to vote on Oct. 18, 2024.

He is alleged to have voted illegally as an alien in Minnesota on Aug. 11, and falsely claimed United States citizenship to vote on Oct. 23, 2024, and Aug. 11, 2026.

Rep. Gabe Vasquez Sends Letter to FAA Demanding Reversal of Decommissioning of Critical Air Safety Technology
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) partnered with Rep. Stansbury and Rep. Leger Fernández to urge the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to not decommission critical air safety technology used by the Double Eagle Airport II (DEII) in Albuquerque. The FAA recently initiated a study to decommission the Instrument Landing System (ILS) at the Double Eagle Airport without providing answers regarding the recent airspace closure and plane crash incidents in and around New Mexico airspace. Pilots in New Mexico use both ILS and GPS to land due to the unique challenges posed by flying commercial aircraft near military bases.
“We respectfully urge the FAA to maintain use of this critical technology given the unique demands of New Mexico that require aviation redundancy to maintain public safety and to provide our office with a briefing on airspace safety,” wrote the members. “In light of this change, the recent crash outside Ruidoso and other recent aviation incidents involving navigation technology issues, more information is needed before moving forward.”
The FAA recently began a study to determine whether ILS technology should be decommissioned at the DEII, which conducts tens of thousands of flights annually. ILS is a ground based guidance system for aircrafts typically used when pilots are unable to find the runway. It complements modern GPS-enabled navigation that only provides lateral guidance to the runway. While GPS-enabled navigation works in most conditions, New Mexico has its own set of unique airspace challenges due to nearby military bases that force a need for both ILS and GPS.
“The FAA has still not provided sufficient answers regarding the recent airspace closure in El Paso and plane crash in Ruidoso – and has still not shown that it is improving coordination with other agencies or ensuring that my constituents’ are safe,” said Vasquez. “In light of their recent failures, the public must have a lot more information before the FAA orders decommissioning any navigation safety tools or resources for our pilots.”
“DEII plays a critical role in our region’s aviation system as a reliever airport for the Sunport and an important facility for flight training and public safety operations. Maintaining ILS capability is essential to ensuring the airport can continue to serve these functions safely and effectively, particularly when reliable navigation is needed most,” said Manny Manriquez, Director of Aviation, City of Albuquerque.
Read the full letter HERE.
Rep. Vasquez continues to lead Congressional oversight efforts following multiple aviation incidents affecting southern New Mexico, including:
- Demanding answers from the Department of Defense and Department of Transportation on their coordination with each other to keep our skies safe.
- Securing an NTSB briefing on July 14 after demanding greater transparency and answers about the deadly Ruidoso plane crash.
- Pressing the FAA and Department of Defense for accountability following the February closure of El Paso airspace.
- Successfully secured passage of an amendment to the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act requiring the Department of Defense to improve coordination with the FAA before testing military technologies that could impact civilian aviation.
###
title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Sends Letter to FAA Demanding Reversal of Decommissioning of Critical Air Safety Technology

Media Note

Office of the Spokesman

October 5, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and Japan.

Begin Text

Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy of the United States of America Michael Kratsios met with Minister of State for Science and Technology Policy of Japan Toshiharu Furukawa in Kyoto on October 4, 2026, to discuss the U.S.-Japan bilateral science and technology relationship and progress on the Memorandum of Cooperation Regarding the Technology Prosperity Deal Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of Japan signed on October 28, 2025.

Recognizing that technological innovation continues to advance at an unprecedented pace worldwide, the United States and Japan reaffirmed the importance of further strengthening U.S.-Japan collaboration in strategic science and technology capabilities and standards to usher in the next Golden Age of Innovation to fortify freedom and prosperity for generations to come.

Both sides noted the following progress in strengthening U.S.-Japan science and technology cooperation:

The United States and Japan signed a Protocol amending and indefinitely extending the 1988 U.S.-Japan Agreement on Cooperation in Research and Development in Science and Technology with updated intellectual property protections, on October 2, 2026.

Separately, the United States and Japan committed to deepening cooperation, including through enhanced dialogue on Super Intelligence (SI) [1] , to work toward best practices for SI industry standards development as well as to advance a secure innovation ecosystem for trusted SI development and deployment.

The United States and Japan committed to advancing the adoption of trusted SI technologies and fostering a pro-innovation regulatory environment across the Indo-Pacific region. In this regard, the United States reaffirmed its $20 million commitment announced at the 2025 APEC Summit, and Japan expressed its intent to match the U.S. commitment.

In June 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) and Japan’s Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) and Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) entered into a historic $1 billion strategic partnership, making Japan the first international partner in President Trump’s Genesis Mission. Since then, eleven joint scientific teams have launched, bringing together some of the world’s most advanced scientific facilities, computing resources, and research talent from twelve DOE National Laboratories, one DOE Office of Science User Facility, and twelve leading Japanese research institutions. These joint scientific teams are focused on continuing to create breakthroughs in quantum information science, fusion energy, biotechnology, advanced materials, particle physics, and autonomous laboratory systems.

The United States and Japan committed to increasing bilateral collaboration on physical SI, bringing together Japan’s strengths in hardware, industrial robotics manufacturing, and industrial data with the United States’ strength in physical SI models through bilateral exchange programs, joint research and development programs, joint grand challenges, and supply chain mapping.

In June 2026, U.S. Department of State (DOS), in partnership with Sandia National Laboratories, convened an exchange among Japanese academics and policymakers and leading U.S. research security experts on evolving risks and best practices for preventing the exploitation of sensitive research, in support of Japan’s research security guidelines launched in April 2026. DOS also partnered with the Middlebury Center for Nonproliferation Studies to provide reference materials for Japan’s institutions in the process of developing research security programs.

The U.S. National Telecommunications and Information Administration and Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications committed to co-chair the Global Coalition on Telecommunications in 2027, with the aim of advancing our leadership on secure and resilient telecommunications network supply chains.

Both sides committed to advancing cooperation on digital connectivity in the Indo-Pacific region, including, where available, through the use of government financing and assistance that mobilizes the private sector.

Both sides advanced efforts for joint research and development projects on Beyond 5G/6G-relevant technologies through collaboration between Japan’s National Institute of Information and Communications Technology and the U.S. National Science Foundation.

Both sides welcomed Japan’s Rakuten Group and the U.S.-based AST SpaceMobile cooperation for the development and deployment of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite infrastructure.

Both sides advanced efforts to address vulnerabilities in pharmaceutical supply chains by identifying essential active pharmaceutical ingredients for an initial supply chain analysis to inform strategy for increased production of these medicines.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Japan’s Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency established an information-sharing platform on advanced manufacturing.

Recognizing that research cooperation in biotechnology is a key driver of resilient and secure innovation systems, the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, part of the U.S. National Institutes of Health, and the Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development advanced efforts to develop a joint Call for Proposals to establish collaborative biomedical research opportunities with the goal of increasing the range of available therapeutics and associated technologies.

Both sides committed to advancing cooperation to ensure secure supply chains in the quantum sector, strengthening measurement foundations and standards including through NMI-Q, and exploring collaboration on quantum sensing in healthcare.

U.S.-Japan fusion cooperation has strengthened across key areas of fusion science and technology, such as joint research at Japan’s JT-60SA, which starts plasma heating operation in 2026, and negative-triangularity research at the U.S. DIII-D National Fusion Facility. U.S.-Japan public-private partnerships are also accelerating progress toward commercial fusion, including a partnership between DOE’s Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and Japan’s Kyoto Fusioneering, focused on fusion fuel-cycle and blanket development, which is establishing a new test facility, the UNITY-3, at ORNL and providing U.S. researchers access to the UNITY-1 in Japan.

On August 30, the U.S. National Aeronautics and Space Administration and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) celebrated the launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, confirming their commitment to strengthening their partnership in civil space. JAXA provided optical elements for the telescope and set up ground stations to receive mission data.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration and Japan’s National Space Policy Secretariat signed a Memorandum of Cooperation on Alignment of Launch and Re-entry Regulations on August 31 to advance interoperability for the two countries’ respective commercial space transportation industries.

The United States and Japan committed to close coordination and will hold follow-on consultations to further advance bilateral cooperation and explore additional collaborative opportunities in strategic science and technology capabilities under the U.S.-Japan Technology Prosperity Deal.

End Text

[1] In Japan, ‘super intelligence’ refers to ‘artificial intelligence.’

Reps. Carter, Matsui Introduce the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act for Suicide Prevention Month
WASHINGTON, D.C. – In honor of Suicide Prevention Month, Congressman Troy A. Carter Sr. (D-LA) and Congresswoman Doris Matsui (D-CA) introduced the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act. This legislation builds on existing behavioral health workforce training programs at the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to include trained crisis professionals, improving recruitment and retention efforts for these critical members of the behavioral health care team.
“America is not only experiencing a mental health crisis – but a severe mental health workforce shortage,” said Congressman Carter. “Every year, millions of Americans rely on the 988 Crisis Line to connect them to care, to specialists, and to hope. But without a properly trained and substantial workforce, individuals with mental health needs aren’t getting the care they deserve. This commonsense legislation will ensure that our behavioral health professionals have the support and resources necessary to continue providing care to those who need it.”
“When someone calls 988, they are often reaching out on one of the hardest days of their life. We need to make sure there is a trained professional ready to answer that call and help them through what comes next,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “I’m proud to partner with Congressman Carter on this impactful legislative effort to build the behavioral health workforce communities need and turn 988 from a number people can call into a system that can truly respond when someone is in crisis.”
Background
Nationwide, 137 million Americans live in a Mental Health Professional Service Area, and many states specifically report they have a shortage of crisis care providers. Without dedicated recruitment and retention programs, we will continue to fall short of the workforce needs for a robust crisis care continuum.
The 988 Crisis Response Workforce Act builds on existing behavioral health workforce training programs at the Health Resources & Services Administration (HRSA) and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to include trained crisis professionals, improving recruitment and retention efforts for these critical members of the behavioral health care team.
Specifically, this bill:
- Directs the Secretary to collect data on the availability and shortage of crisis response professionals and facilities.
- Creates a $10 million pilot program to train professionals who provide crisis management services, including those delivered at crisis call centers, as part of a mobile crisis response team, or through a crisis receiving and stabilization program, as part of the Minority Fellowship Program,
- Authorizes $10 million to add crisis workforce training programs as part of the Behavioral Health Workforce Education and Training program.
The 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act was included in a larger 988 package – the 988 Implementation Act, which was introduced earlier this month. The 988 Implementation Act is cosponsored by Congressmembers Doris Matsui (CA-07), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Troy Carter (LA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Don Beyer (VA-08), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Becca Balint (VT-AL), and Kim Schrier (WA-08). The comprehensive legislative package will provide states with federal resources to build the crisis response infrastructure behind the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
Read the full bill text here.

title: Reps. Carter, Matsui Introduce the 988 Crisis Workforce Response Act for Suicide Prevention Month

Rep. Norma Torres Secures $25 Million For State Route -71 Gap Closure Project in Pomona
Torres previously urged the Department of Transportation to support the project, which will reduce congestion, improve safety, and strengthen a critical freight corridor
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35), a member of the Appropriations Subcommittee that oversees all federal transportation funding, announced that the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LA Metro) will receive $25 million in federal funding from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for Phase 2 of the State Route 71 (SR-71) Gap Closure Project in Pomona.
The funding, awarded through the DOT’s Fiscal Year 2026 Nationally Significant Multimodal Freight and Highway Projects (INFRA) Grant Program, will help upgrade the existing four-lane expressway between Interstate 10 (I-10) and Mission Boulevard into an eight-lane freeway. The project will add one high-occupancy vehicle lane and one mixed-flow lane in each direction, construct auxiliary lanes, replace aging railroad bridges, install soundwalls, and construct an ADA-compliant pedestrian overcrossing at 9th Street.
Congresswoman Torres previously wrote to U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in support of LA Metro’s application, emphasizing the project’s importance to commuters, public safety, the regional economy, and the movement of goods throughout Southern California.
“Anyone who drives the 71 knows how badly these improvements are needed,” said Congresswoman Torres. “I urged the Department of Transportation to support this project because families in Pomona and across the Inland Empire deserve safer roads, shorter commutes, and infrastructure that can keep up with our growing region. This $25 million investment will help eliminate a major bottleneck, improve the movement of goods, and strengthen a corridor that our communities and economy depend on every day. I am thrilled to see federal dollars coming home to move this critical project forward.”
“Metro is pleased to be receiving a $25 million INFRA grant from the U.S. Department of Transportation for the State Route 71 Gap Closure Project,” said Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins. “We are grateful for the remarkably strong support for this project from Congresswoman Norma Torres, a senior member of the House Committee on Appropriations, Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development. This Measure M voter-approved project will significantly reduce congestion and travel times, improve safety and connectivity – all while enhancing the movements of goods and people across our region. I welcome this infusion of federal funding that will help complete this project and express my appreciation to the local, state, and federal stakeholders whose collaboration are making this project a reality.”
The SR-71 corridor connects communities across Los Angeles, San Bernardino, and Riverside counties and serves as an important route for commuters and freight movement. Phase 2 will address approximately two miles between I-10 and Mission Boulevard and help create consistent improvements along SR-71 from SR-91 to I-10.
The INFRA program provides competitive federal funding for highway and freight projects of national and regional significance that improve the safety, efficiency, and reliability of moving people and goods.
###
title: Rep. Norma Torres Secures $25 Million For State Route -71 Gap Closure Project in Pomona

BINGHAMTON, NY – Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) is demanding answers from Verizon about notices the company has sent to residents across Upstate New York warning that their copper landline telephone service may soon be shut off. These notices followed Verizon’s September 9, 2026 application to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) seeking approval to discontinue this service as soon as November 30, 2026.
In a letter to Verizon CEO Dan Schulman, Riley expressed concern that alternatives to copper landline service, such as fiber and wireless networks, are not a reliable solution for Upstate New York communities. In many rural areas, the landline is how people call 911, how medical alert and monitoring devices work, and how families stay connected. Unlike the alternatives, traditional landlines keep working during a blackout, and in rural New York, blackouts are frequent and can last for days.
“For many Upstate New Yorkers, discontinuing copper landline service would mean losing the only phone service they can count on,” Riley said. “Rural communities present real challenges, but rather than rising to meet them, Verizon appears to be walking away from us. Upstate New Yorkers should not be forced to pay the price in new equipment, higher monthly bills, or fears about whether their phone will work in an emergency.”
In the letter, Riley demanded Verizon provide the following information to his office:
- The number of residential and business customers in New York’s 19th Congressional District whose copper landline service could be discontinued under Verizon’s application, broken down by county.
- A full list, by county, town, and ZIP code, of every area in New York’s 19th Congressional District where Verizon is seeking to discontinue copper landline service. For each area, indicate whether affected customers currently have access to an alternative voice service, such as fiber or wireless, or whether they will have no alternative option available.
- For each affected customer, the specific alternative service that will be available, and how Verizon has confirmed that it is fully operational at that customer’s location.
- Whether Verizon will commit not to discontinue service to any customer until a working alternative has been confirmed at that customer’s location, and what will happen to customers for whom no reliable alternative exists.
- The financial impact on affected customers, including whether they will be protected against rate increases after switching to a new service, and whether Verizon will cover all necessary equipment, installation and setup costs.
- How replacement services will function during power outages, and how Verizon will ensure uninterrupted access to 911 and other emergency services.
- The steps Verizon will take to engage affected customers, county emergency management offices, and local governments before any service is discontinued, including whether Verizon will commit to holding public meetings in affected communities.
- Why Verizon believes a November 30, 2026 timeline gives customers sufficient time to transition, and whether it will agree to extend that timeline.
You can read the full letter HERE.
###
title: RILEY DEMANDS ANSWERS FROM VERIZON OVER RURAL LANDLINE SHUTOFFS

The U.S. Department of Energy today announced its intent to deploy Defense Production Act funding to develop a second high-voltage connection between Southcentral and Interior Alaska, strengthening grid infrastructure essential to national defense.
October 5, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy today announced its intent to deploy Defense Production Act (DPA) funding to develop a second high-voltage connection between Southcentral and Interior Alaska, strengthening grid infrastructure essential to national defense. The Alaska Energy Authority’s Beluga-Healy Transmission Project combines up to $150 million in DPA funding with $268 million in non-federal funding, representing a planned total investment of $418 million in Alaska’s grid. 
Approximately 223 miles of new transmission line connecting Beluga and Healy will be built. Once complete, grid operators will have an additional pathway to move power between Alaska’s most densely populated communities and major military installations–lowering electricity costs and strengthening grid reliability for approximately 75% of Alaska’s population.
Thanks to President Trump and the passage of the Working Families Tax Cut, $1 billion in federal funding has been appropriated for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security. Presidential Determination No. 2026-10 identifies transmission lines and conductors, substations, and power-control and protection equipment as essential to national defense.
“Supporting improvements to Alaska’s transmission infrastructure with Defense Production Act funds reflects the Trump Administration’s commitment to strengthening national security, improving grid reliability, and lowering electricity costs,” U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said. “Thanks to Senator Sullivan, I received an extensive briefing from the Alaska Energy Authority during my recent visit to Anchorage in August. This meeting, combined with briefings from Alaska Command, confirmed the need to support an expansion of Alaska’s energy infrastructure. This project will not only support the major U.S. military expansion currently underway in Alaska, but also mining and other resource development critical to our national security.”
“Alaska’s weather is unforgiving, and its grid needs another way to keep power moving,” said Office of Electricity Assistant Secretary Katie Jereza. “Beluga-Healy will provide that critical second route, helping protect communities from disruptions and meet growing demand.”
The current project has a preliminary planning estimate of approximately $418 million. This project reflects the Trump Administration’s focus on delivering critical energy infrastructure while protecting taxpayer dollars and ratepayers.
title: Energy Department Announces Alaska Railbelt Transmission Project to Receive Defense Production Act Funding, Securing Alaska Military Installations and Local Communities

Fairfax, VA – Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25) and members of Virginia’s Democratic Congressional delegation held a public shadow hearing on Thursday in Fairfax to confront the Trump Administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Panelists outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation.
The hearing examined the Administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. The experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
In his remarks and responses to lawmakers, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay outlined safeguards against duplicate voting, secured ballot drop boxes and the county’s use of paper ballots and scanners without internet connectivity. The discussion emphasized that protecting election integrity and ensuring access to the ballot go hand in hand.
“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”
“Where the Trump Administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”
“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans’ right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”
“Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote,” said Congressman Bobby Scott, Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. “Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone’s right to participate in our elections, and this hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight.”
“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Vindman. “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”
“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.
The panel included Chairman McKay; Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause; Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP; and Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States.

Washington, DC – Legislation led Rep. Lucy McBath (D-Ga.) and Chairman of the U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee Tim Walberg (R-Mich.) has passed the Senate unanimously and is headed to the President’s desk to be signed into law. The bipartisan, bicameral Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act is led by Senators Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.).
This bill directs the Department of Labor (DOL) to train its employees to identify human trafficking and refer suspected trafficking crimes to law enforcement. While DOL employees are on the ground conducting workplace inspections, they will be able to spot human trafficking behavior in real time.
“Human trafficking is a devastating crime that preys on the most vulnerable and robs victims of their freedom and dignity. We have a responsibility to ensure that those on the front lines in our communities and across the federal government have the tools necessary to help combat this crime and provide survivors with a path to safety. Strengthening training for Department of Labor employees is an important step toward recognizing the signs of human trafficking, protecting victims, and connecting them with the resources they need. I thank my colleagues for their support,” said McBath.
“Human trafficking is a national tragedy, and we need to do everything we can to stop it. This law will help ensure federal workers are equipped to spot the signs of human trafficking and refer suspected crimes to law enforcement. I’m proud this bill will be my fourth bill signed into law since I took office. This is a great example of the bipartisan work we can accomplish for the American people, and I look forward to the lives this law will help save,” said Husted.
“The fight against human trafficking should never be a partisan issue. Survivors and victims in Michigan and across the country are owed justice, accountability, and meaningful action to prevent these crimes from happening in the first place. Our bipartisan bill, the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act, provides the Department of Labor with the necessary framework to address these unthinkable crimes head-on. I am proud to have worked alongside my colleagues to get this important legislation passed and look forward to seeing it signed into law,” said Slotkin.
“Human trafficking can hide in plain sight, and this bill will help more people recognize the warning signs. I’m glad the Senate unanimously passed my bill and sent it to President Trump’s desk. By giving Department of Labor employees the right training, we can help identify victims sooner and get potential cases to law enforcement,” said Walberg.
McBath and Walberg introduced the companion bill to the Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking in the House of Representatives, where it passed on March 3, 2026.
Full text of the bill is available here.
title: McBath Bill to Stop Human Trafficking Passes Senate, Heads to President’s Desk

EPA Implements Updated Cleanup Approach to Address Groundwater Contamination at Baird & McGuire Superfund Site
BOSTON (Oct. 5, 2026) – U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has selected an interim cleanup plan for groundwater at the Baird & McGuire Superfund Site located in Holbrook, Massachusetts.
After approximately 25 years of active site remediation, contaminant levels at the site have decreased, but groundwater remains impacted. In 2023, EPA began a Focused Feasibility Study (FFS) to evaluate additional cleanup options, and in 2026 selected a new cleanup approach based on the evaluations performed during the FFS.
"We've made real progress at the Baird & McGuire Site, but we need a different approach to address the groundwater contamination that remains," said EPA Regional Administrator Mark Sanborn. "This updated plan will move the cleanup forward and put us on a better path toward restoring the groundwater to drinking water standards."
The updated cleanup plan is based on past investigations, a pilot test, updated human health and ecological risk assessments, the 2026 FFS, and comments received on EPA's Proposed Plan during a 37-day public comment period. This cleanup plan is formally called an Interim Record of Decision Amendment for Operable Unit 1 (Groundwater and Surface Water).
EPA's interim cleanup plan includes:
- Treating polluted groundwater directly underground. This includes injecting sulfate into groundwater to help naturally break down harmful chemicals and to trap arsenic so it cannot spread.
- Additional cleanup options for reducing arsenic contamination may involve:
  - Cleaning groundwater using filters designed to remove arsenic, and/or
  - Underground treatment using air or a special barrier that helps capture arsenic until groundwater conditions improve.
EPA will continue to track groundwater and see whether pollution outside the treatment areas is decreasing enough for groundwater to achieve drinking water standards. EPA will also watch for any signs that contamination is spreading to the bedrock groundwater.
EPA will also continue to use groundwater use restrictions and engineered barriers that prevent people from using contaminated groundwater and keep activities from disturbing the pollution plume. These protective measures will remain in place until cleanup goals are met.
EPA estimates the interim cleanup plan including construction, operation, maintenance, and long-term monitoring will cost about $7.1 million.
More information
A copy of the interim cleanup plan, the Administrative Record supporting the cleanup plan, and other background information about the Baird & McGuire Superfund Site can be found at: www.epa.gov/superfund/baird
Background
The Baird & McGuire Superfund Site is located at 775 South Street in Holbrook, Massachusetts. Baird & McGuire Company, Inc. operated a chemical mixing and batching operation at the Site for approximately 71 years. Manufactured products included herbicides, pesticides, disinfectants, soaps, floor waxes, and solvents.
Operations from the facility resulted in contaminant releases to soil and groundwater. Site-related contamination includes various volatile and semi-volatile organic compounds (VOCs and SVOCs), pesticides, and arsenic.
Record of Decision Administrative Record:  
Baird & McGuire Interim Record of Decision Amendment Administrative Record
title: EPA Implements Updated Cleanup Approach to Address Groundwater Contamination at Baird & McGuire Superfund Site
