Hartford, CT – Today, members of Connecticut’s Congressional delegation and Governor Ned Lamont announced that the State of Connecticut is being awarded a $584,250 grant from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to support its planned expansion of the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown, which will complement $294,250 in state funding that has already been allocated for the project.

This expansion, which is being overseen by the Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs (DVA), will support the creation of 1,510 additional grave sites for buried cremains on a parcel of land located contiguous to the existing cemetery at 317 Bow Lane. This property was previously used by the Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (DMHAS) for the operations of Connecticut Valley Hospital and was recently transferred to DVA to support the cemetery’s expansion.

The state’s portion of the funding will be used to support the demolition of the vacant Connecticut Valley Hospital building on the property known as Cottage 22. The federal funding will be used to provide cremains burial plots, an entry gate, fencing, landscaping, irrigation components, concrete block storage bays, site furnishings, and supporting infrastructure.

“Our veterans put their lives on the line to protect the freedoms we hold dear—we owe it to them to properly honor their service and sacrifice,” said Congressman John B. Larson. “I am pleased to announce this grant from the VA with my colleagues and Governor Lamont to expand the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown. We will continue to work together to make sure the state has the resources it needs to recognize our state’s veterans and their families, so the cemetery remains available to them for years to come.”

“This cemetery provides an invaluable resource in honoring the lives and service of our military veterans and their families, and it is important that we continue to see that this option remains available to them for decades into the future,” said Governor Lamont. “As we explore options to support these needs over the long-term, this expansion of the existing cemetery in Middletown will provide immediate support to ensure that veterans and their families have uninterrupted access to these services over the coming years.”

“The Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery is a sacred place where our nation’s heroes are laid to rest,” Senator Richard Blumenthal, ranking member of the Senate Veterans Affairs Committee, said. “I am thrilled that this $584,250 in federal funding will allow for 1,510 additional final resting places for Connecticut veterans, ensuring families have options for their loved ones for years to come.”

“Connecticut’s Second Congressional District is the proud home to over 47,000 veterans—the highest population of any of the five districts in Connecticut,” Congressman Joe Courtney said. “The expansion of the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery will mean more families are able to lay their loved ones to rest at a site that honors and remembers their service to our nation. I will continue working with my colleagues in our state’s Congressional delegation to support the Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs’ mission to honor our state’s veterans.”

“We owe it to our veterans to honor them both in life and after their passing,” Congressman Jim Himes said. “I’m heartened that the federal government will serve as a partner in expanding Connecticut’s State Veterans Cemetery and look forward to working with the delegation to provide additional resources to Connecticut veterans.”

“Those who have honorably served our nation deserve to be laid to rest with respect and dignity,” Congresswoman Jahana Hayes said. “I am pleased that federal funding will help make this a reality for more veterans and military families by expanding the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery. I look forward to the completion of this project and am committed to ensuring our veterans have the resources they need to live full, healthy lives and a safe final resting home.”

“Our Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery provides hallowed grounds for the final resting place of our Connecticut veterans,” Connecticut Veterans Affairs Commissioner Ron Welch said. “It is our privilege and honor to maintain the cemetery as a perpetual shrine to their selfless service. We look forward to the expansion of the cemetery and further to the establishment of a new cemetery in the future.”

The Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery was established in 1985 and provides a final resting place for military veterans from generations of conflicts, along with their eligible spouses and minor children. There are currently 14,718 burial plots and 3,000 columbarium niches at the cemetery.

DVA estimates that the existing cemetery will be depleted of available cremation burial plots around January 2028. With this expansion, the agency projects that cremation burial plots will remain available through at least December 2033. Importantly, this will align the estimated depletion dates of all three burial options (casket, buried cremains, and columbarium niches), enabling DVA to build all three options in its plans to develop a new cemetery that will support veterans and their families over the coming decades.
title: Connecticut Congressional Delegation and Governor Lamont Announce State and Federal Funding to Expand the Connecticut State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown

Coordinated Arrests and Charges Dismantle Hamas Terror Finance Network Raising Funds from the United States
The Justice Department announced today the unsealing of an indictment charging Saleem Alzaq, as well as the arrests of Omar Adhami, Abdel Adhami, and Raed Yousef, for their involvement in paying, soliciting and collecting funds for Hamas. In a coordinated law enforcement operation in France, three of Alzaq’s associates, Faouzi Barika, Amel Oualid, and Nordine Barika were arrested by the French General Directorate for Internal Security.
“Anyone who finances or assists terrorist organizations responsible for the deaths of American citizens should expect to be prosecuted by the Department of Justice,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “For decades, members of Hamas have raised funding to carry out brutal terrorist attacks. Under the leadership of President Trump, the Department of Justice will continue pursuing terrorists who kill Americans, dismantling terrorist finance networks, and delivering justice for the families of victims.”
"The FBI will never forget the horrific attack on Israel by Hamas on October 7, 2023 – and we will never stop our efforts to cut off funding to Hamas terrorists," said FBI Director Kash Patel. "These subjects allegedly engaged in a conspiracy that extended beyond national borders to funnel money to Hamas and fuel violent attacks, using cryptocurrency, to try to hide their criminal activity. Today's announcement shows the abilities of this FBI and our interagency partners to follow the money and shut down resources going to terrorists under the guise of charitable giving – with 4,000 Foreign Terrorist organization related disruptions and stopping 1,100 alleged terrorist actors here at home and around the world since last year. Special thanks to our FBI New York, New Orleans, and Tampa Field Offices, our Counterterrorism Division, as well as the Paris Legal Attaché's Office and French authorities for their outstanding work with us in this case.”
“Money is the lifeblood of terrorist organizations, and the arrests announced today disrupted a global financing network that was supplying Hamas with the funds needed to continue its campaign of destroying innocent lives,” said Assistant Attorney General for National Security John A. Eisenberg, “These coordinated investigations and arrests spanned multiple jurisdictions in the United States and across international borders, and demonstrate that we will use all of our capabilities to eradicate terrorism. I want to thank the FBI agents and federal prosecutors who worked together to dismantle this network, and I also want to thank Joint Task Force 10-7 for its leadership in seeking justice for the victims of the Hamas-led attack in Israel on October 7, 2023, that killed more than 1,200 men, women, and children. My thoughts are with all who are still suffering from the losses of that terrible day, and the National Security Division will never stop working to hold the perpetrators, and those who enabled them, accountable for their atrocities.”
“This Office and our law enforcement partners will root out and prosecute those who finance Hamas, no matter where they are located,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald for the Southern District of New York. “As alleged, Saleem Alzaq was the center of a Hamas financing network that operated around the globe, soliciting more than a million dollars from individual donors including here in the United States. The close cooperation of law enforcement and prosecutors’ offices to dismantle Alzaq’s alleged Hamas financing network demonstrates our commitment to depriving Hamas of the funding it relies on in Gaza and to commit terror attacks like the brutal October 7, 2023, massacre of more than a thousand innocent victims, including dozens of Americans.”
“According to the indictment and complaint filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana, Saleem Alzaq solicited financial donations on behalf of Hamas, a terrorist organization responsible for the commission of heinous attacks worldwide,” said U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle for the Eastern District of Louisiana. “Omar Adhami and Abdel Adhami are accused of providing Alzaq with resources intended to fund Hamas’ relentless reign of terror. The Department of Justice and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Louisiana are laser focused on the identification, prosecution, and eradication of terrorist networks, and the individuals who financially support these networks.”
“Providing financial assistance and support to terrorist organizations like Hamas place the safety and security of everyone, anywhere in the world, at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe for the Middle District of Florida. “The diligence and cooperation exhibited by our domestic and international law enforcement partners during this investigation demonstrates our collective resolve to relentlessly pursue, disrupt, and prosecute those who engage in these illegal activities.”
“The NYPD’s counterterrorism work knows no borders,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch. “Our intelligence analysts uncovered this international finance network and built the case that exposed more than $2 million being funneled to Hamas. Saleem Alzaq, a leader in Hamas’ military arm responsible for planning and carrying out terrorist attacks, and the other defendants allegedly solicited donations under the guise of humanitarian aid and then directed that money to Hamas. This is the kind of extraordinary counterterrorism work the NYPD does every day to disrupt threats before they reach New Yorkers, and I thank our law enforcement partners for helping us dismantle this network.”
According to the Alzaq indictment unsealed in the Southern District of New York, the Adhami complaints filed in the Eastern District of Louisiana, and the Yousef indictment filed in the Middle District of Florida:
Alzaq, 45, of Gaza, is a Hamas member in the Gaza Strip and a battalion deputy in the Izz al-Din al-Qassam Brigades (the Al-Qassam Brigades), Hamas’s armed wing responsible for planning and executing terrorist attacks. Alzaq serves in the Photography Department of the Al-Qassam Brigades’ Shujaiyya Brigade Media Office, a Hamas propaganda office. In this role, he has photographed Hamas events, including events led by senior Hamas leaders such as Ismail Haniyeh and Yahya Sinwar. He distributes these photographs and descriptions of Hamas events to others involved in the Hamas propaganda apparatus. He has also posted Hamas propaganda across multiple social media platforms, including posts glorifying deceased leaders of Hamas (such as Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, Haniyeh, and Sinwar); supporting Al-Qassam Brigades terrorists and glorifying Al-Qassam Brigades “martyrs;” and promoting and celebrating Hamas’s October 7, 2023, terrorist attacks against Southern Israel, in which more than 1,200 victims were murdered and more than 250 were taken hostage, including 46 American citizens.
Since at least about January 2020, Alzaq has operated an international Hamas fundraising network that collects donations from individuals around the world, including from individuals in the United States. Alzaq promotes this fundraising through social media campaigns purportedly providing humanitarian aid to people in Gaza, while the money is funneled to Hamas. Since January 2020, Alzaq has collected more than $1.7 million through purported charitable campaigns. Alzaq’s associates in France, Barika, Amel Oualid, and others assisted Alzaq in collecting and transferring money raised for Hamas.
Abdel Adhami, 35, and Omar Adhami, 33, both of Covington, Louisiana, donated funds to Alzaq’s Hamas financing network. Beginning in approximately February 2021, and continuing through approximately September 2026, Abdel Adhami allegedly contributed approximately $94,000 and Omar Adhami allegedly contributed approximately $11,000 to Hamas, a designated terrorist organization, knowing that the organization engaged in terrorist activities, and attempted to conceal their contributions to Hamas through wire transfers, and the use of intermediaries. Yousef, a resident of Lutz, Florida, provided almost $50,000 to Alzaq’s Hamas financing network.
Alzaq is charged with conspiring to provide material support to Hamas, a designated foreign terrorist organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiring to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiring to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; and conspiring to defraud the United States, which carries a maximum penalty of five years in prison.
Omar Adhami is charged with providing material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to provide material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to commit wire fraud, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; and conspiring to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.
Abdel Adhami is charged with providing material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to provide material support to a Foreign Terrorist Organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; conspiracy to commit wire fraud, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; and conspiring to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison.
Raed Yousef, 56, of Lutz, Florida, is charged with one count of conspiring to provide material support to a foreign terrorist organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison; five counts of attempting to provide material support to a foreign terrorist organization, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each count; one count of providing funds, goods, and services to a specially designated terrorist, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison; five counts of attempting to provide funds, goods, and services to a specially designated terrorist, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in person on each count; one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison; five counts of money laundering, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison on each count; and one count of passport fraud, which carries a maximum penalty of 5 years in federal prison.
The Alzaq case is being investigated by the FBI with the assistance of the New York Police Department (NYPD). Assistant U.S. Attorneys David A. Markewitz, Ben Arad, Sarah L. Kushner, Juliana N. Murray, and Keith Savino for the Southern District of New York are prosecuting the case, with assistance from Trial Attorneys Rob MacDonald and A.J. Dixon of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs provided significant assistance.
The Adhami case is being investigated by the FBI New Orleans Field Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Greg Kennedy for the Eastern District of Louisiana is prosecuting the case.
The Yousef case is being investigated by the FBI. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lindsey Schmidt and Michael Buchanan for the Middle District of Florida are prosecuting the case.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: Coordinated Arrests and Charges Dismantle Hamas Terror Finance Network Raising Funds from the United States

EPA Announces $272 Million WIFIA Loan to Support Drinking Water in Columbia, Tennessee
EPA Press Office (press@epa.gov)
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced a $272 million Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA) loan to the city of Columbia, Tennessee, known as “Muletown,” with a population of about 50,000. This loan will help Columbia implement expansions to its drinking water system, increasing capacity and system reliability to deliver safe drinking water throughout the city and nearby rural communities. The Trump EPA’s investments in America deliver on the agency’s “Powering the Great American Comeback” initiative, which advances public health while powering the American economy.
“Working on this WIFIA Loan with Columbia, Tennessee, has helped advance the Trump EPA’s goal of making sure water is working for Main Street USA,” said EPA Assistant Administrator for Water Jess Kramer. “Ensuring safe drinking water is critical to supporting growing populations and growing economies like in Columbia. This $272 million WIFIA loan will help us do just that and continues to prove that we can protect public health while bolstering local economies.”
“We are proud to proactively take steps to complete this necessary project to ensure the long-term viability of clean drinking water in our region,” said Jack Baxster, Interim CEO and President for Columbia Power & Water Systems. “Capitalizing on the most advantageous available financing, such as the WIFIA loan, we are locking in future savings for our ratepayers.”
The city of Columbia will use WIFIA financing for its Long Term Water Supply Program, which will expand its drinking water system to continue providing water for its growing regional population. This project includes construction of a new raw water intake structure, transmission main, and improvements to the system’s existing water treatment plant. Through these upgrades the city will increase drinking water supply reliability for its customers and provide water to rural communities within the city’s service area.
EPA’s WIFIA loan enables Columbia to meet increased demands due to population and economic growth while delivering for its communities and businesses. The program will provide Columbia flexibility through the ability to customize repayment schedules – saving the city millions over the life of the loan. Additionally, this project is expected to drive meaningful economic impact and support a substantial number of jobs during the construction process and beyond.
Since issuing its first loan in 2018, EPA’s WIFIA program has announced $24 billion in financing for water infrastructure projects that are strengthening drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater infrastructure while creating over 177,000 jobs. Through its flexible financing features and competitive interest rates, WIFIA helps communities save money, and even accelerate water infrastructure investments.
WIFIA has approximately $11 billion in flexible financing available to support additional water infrastructure projects across the country, including in small communities and rural America where WIFIA can finance up to 80% of project costs. To help small communities access WIFIA funding, the agency recently announced a commitment to waive WIFIA application and credit processing fees. Additionally, the agency’s State WIFIA program has approximately $3 billion available for loans to state infrastructure financing authorities. EPA is currently accepting letters of interest for funding through WIFIA and State WIFIA.
Learn more about EPA’s WIFIA Program and water infrastructure investments, including how to submit a letter of interest.
Background
Established by the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act of 2014, the WIFIA program is a federal loan program administered by EPA. The program aims to accelerate investment in the nation’s water infrastructure by providing long-term, low-cost supplemental credit assistance for regionally and nationally significant projects. The WIFIA program has an active pipeline of pending applications for projects that will result in billions of dollars in water infrastructure investment and thousands of jobs.
title: EPA Announces $272 Million WIFIA Loan to Support Drinking Water in Columbia, Tennessee

EPA Deputy Administrator Fotouhi Announces Over $90 million for Restoration and Clean Water in Chesapeake Bay Watershed
SMITHFIELD, Va. – During an event at the Windsor Castle Park in Smithfield, Virginia, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Deputy Administrator David Fotouhi was joined by U.S. Representative Jen Kiggans (R-VA-02) and others to announce more than $90 million for the Chesapeake Bay watershed. EPA is awarding $37 million with an additional $53 million in funding coming from other agencies to implement 83 new projects that will support critical restoration and provide long-term water quality improvements.
“Through these grants, EPA is working collaboratively with our local partners to deliver practical restoration solutions that improve water quality, restore habitat, and support the vital Chesapeake Bay watershed. These improvements will have a significant impact of the more than 1,800 local communities that depend on the watershed to support their economies,” said EPA Deputy Administrator Fotouhi. “This type of funding has a proven track record of delivering tangible environmental results and is a shining example of taxpayer dollars being put to accomplishing EPA’s core mission.”
“Preserving the health of the Chesapeake Bay is critical to the communities and native species who call Coastal Virginia home,” said Representative Kiggans. “I’m grateful to the EPA, NFWF, and James River Association for supporting commonsense conservation efforts that protect our waterways and strengthen our coastal communities. I want to thank Deputy Administrator Fotouhi for joining us in Virginia’s Second District to celebrate this investment, and I look forward to continuing to work with the Deputy Administrator and the EPA to advance practical solutions that preserve the Chesapeake Bay for generations to come.”
The projects being supported today emphasize the Trump EPA's cooperative federalism approach to engaging local communities in the planning, design, and implementation of community-level clean water projects that will improve soil quality, install physical barriers, and restore habitats. Since 1999, EPA has partnered with the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) to award over $800 million across more than 2,000 grants, resulting in the reduction of nitrogen pollution by more than 40 million pounds, the restoration of over 3,000 miles of streamside forests and 9,500 acres of wetlands, and the treatment of stormwater runoff from over 23,000 acres of impervious surfaces.
The Trump EPA is committed to safeguarding the Chesapeake Bay to both protect human health and the environment and grow the booming economies that come from it. Having clean and accessible water is essential to everyday life. This $90 million will benefit communities from farmers to homeowners, churches, businesses, and municipalities with improvements to local water quality that will also help restore the Chesapeake Bay. This investment bolsters the robust economies of the more than 1,800 communities that the Chesapeake Bay watershed supports and ensures that the families and nearly 18 million people living in the watershed continue to prosper.
Please see a complete list of the 2026 Small Watershed Grants (SWG) (pdf) recipients.
Please see a complete list of the 2026 Innovative Nutrient and Sediment Reduction (INSR) (pdf) recipients.
Background:
Today’s grants were awarded through the SWG and INSR programs, a core part of the federal-state Chesapeake Bay Program partnership administered under NFWF’s Chesapeake Bay Stewardship Fund (CBSF). CBSF is a partnership between NFWF and EPA that provides grant funding, technical assistance, and networking and information sharing in support of local, on-the-ground conservation and restoration efforts to restore the Chesapeake Bay and its tributary rivers and streams under the revised Chesapeake Bay Watershed Agreement.
title: EPA Deputy Administrator Fotouhi Announces Over $90 million for Restoration and Clean Water in Chesapeake Bay Watershed

New Jersey Woman, Colombian Lover Convicted in $13M Federal Program Fraud Scheme
Jael Watts, 45, of Alloway, New Jersey, and Luis Pino-Copete, 42, of Bogota, Colombia, were convicted by a jury of orchestrating a sweeping nationwide scheme to steal millions of dollars in federal program funds administered by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), designed to benefit elderly, disabled, and homeless Americans. This action is a part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud.
“These convictions send a clear message that those who exploit federal programs for personal gain will be held fully accountable,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Department of Justice’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “The defendants fabricated payrolls and client lists, even using the identities of deceased individuals, to siphon millions meant for the most vulnerable Americans. I commend the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York and our federal and state partners for their relentless pursuit of justice in this case.”
“These two defendants traded their Tuscan spa robes for his and hers orange jumpsuits,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney John A. Sarcone for the Northern District of New York. “I commend the hawkish work of OSC and our federal partners and thank my Assistant U.S. Attorneys for their tireless work in delivering these fraudsters justice. Had they been referred to state or local authorities for prosecution due to the irresponsible no bail laws here in NYS these two could have fled to Colombia.”
As proven at trial, Watts and Pino-Copete operated a shell company called Pearl Transit Corporation, headquartered in New Jersey, which purported to employ drivers all over the United States who gave rides to the elderly and disabled and engaged in street outreach for homeless Americans. In reality, Pearl Transit employed no such drivers and performed no such services. Rather, over the time-period of July 2019 through October 2025, Watts devised and executed a scheme to defraud numerous state and local administrators of federal pass-through funds designed to help the needy, including the Federal Transit Administration (FTA)’s Section 5310 Program and HUD’s Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG), some of which were funded during the COVID pandemic by the CARES Act, by submitting false employment and customer information using stolen identities of real people, purporting to establish that Pearl Transit had provided rides to the elderly, disabled, and homeless. Some of the individuals listed as Pearl Transit’s recipients were deceased at the times they purportedly received rides from Pearl Transit, and some of the purported drivers were individuals who did not have driver licenses and have never driven a car in their life (one had a learner’s permit at the time the defendants claimed she drove for Pearl Transit). Over the relevant period, the defendants sought reimbursement of over $13 million in federal funds through false claims and submissions. Proof at trial established that the defendants lived a lavish lifestyle off of the over $1.6 million in federal funds they fraudulently obtained as part of the scheme:
- $529,500 in CDBG funds from Gwinnett County, Georgia;
- $429,885 in Section 5310 funds from the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority;
- $283,000 in ESG funds from Kern County, California; and
- $379,149 in Section 5310 funds from the City of Raleigh, North Carolina.
Watts married Pino-Copete in Colombia in 2023, and Pino-Copete joined the fraud scheme shortly thereafter in January 2024. In January 2025, he entered the United States on a visa issued in December 2024, and his role in the crimes progressed after Watts was initially charged by complaint with wire fraud in connection with the scheme in July 2025. The defendants are pictured below conspiring to submit false documents in an effort to obtain $50,000 in federal funds from the City of San Bernadino, California while Watts was detained on the wire fraud complaint at the Albany County Correctional Facility in September 2025.
“When criminals use funds meant for our most vulnerable on lavish lifestyles, they must face the consequences,” said Assistant Secretary Ronnie Kurtz of HUD Community Planning and Development. “Fraudsters have been stealing funds from Georgia to California, but thanks to the work of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, we are standing up for taxpayer dollars and creating real accountability. At HUD, we are putting an end to the status quo to stop the fraud before it happens. If you receive even one tax dollar, we expect results.”
“Fraudsters who target federal transportation programs steal directly from the vulnerable communities these funds are meant to serve,” said Special Agent in Charge Brian C. Gallagher of the Department of Transportation Office of Inspector General, Northeastern Region. “The convictions demonstrate that together with our law enforcement and prosecutorial partners we will move swiftly and decisively to protect taxpayer dollars and hold accountable anyone who attempts to exploit these critical transportation resources.”
“Jael Watts and Luis Pino-Copete’s selfish actions diverted more than $1.5 million in federal funds to support their lavish lifestyle while depriving elderly, disabled, and homeless Americans of resources intended to benefit them. Those entrusted with overseeing HUD funds have a responsibility to protect those resources and ensure they reach the vulnerable communities they were intended to serve,” said Special Agent in Charge Shawn A. Rice of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Inspector General (OIG), Northeast Region. “This is not a victimless crime. Every dollar they stole could have been used to help vulnerable Americans. HUD OIG will continue to work with the U.S. Attorney’s Office and our law enforcement partners to hold accountable those who abuse positions of trust and jeopardize critical federal programs.”
“Watts and Pino orchestrated a nationwide scheme to defraud the public,” said New York State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli. “Thanks to the vigilance of my office and our work with our federal law enforcement partners, they will be held accountable for their crimes. I thank the United States Attorney’s and federal Department of Transportation Inspector General's office for their partnership and excellent work allowing justice be served.”
The investigation was spearheaded jointly by federal and state investigators. It began in late 2024 when Watts submitted claims for reimbursement of nearly $750,000 through the Section 5310 Program to the New York State DOT on behalf of Pearl Transit. The Office of the New York State Comptroller (“OSC”) found the invoices suspicious and initiated an audit. In response to the audit, Watts and Pino-Copete generated numerous false documents using stolen identities of real people in an effort to convince New York State that Pearl Transit had actually performed the services it sought reimbursement for. OSC quickly brought in DOT-OIG, which swiftly referred the case to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in 2025. The resulting joint federal and state investigation, joined by HUD-OIG, uncovered a multi-year nationwide scheme perpetrated by Watts to steal federal program funds perpetrated against administrators of these federal programs all over the country (including Georgia, North Carolina, California, and New York). Following Watts’ arrest in July 2025 and the search of her cell phone and computer, investigators uncovered Pino-Copete’s role in the crimes and he was initially charged for his role in the scheme in December 2025 and detained pending trial.
Searches of the defendants’ cell phones uncovered scores of communications between the defendants about creating fake documentation to respond to OSC’s audit requests. Watts declared, “one has to be committed to this type of work . . . and I am committed,” and boasted, “they are not smart . . . we are much smarter.” An exhaustive review of the defendants’ numerous bank accounts showed that the over $1.5 million they fraudulently obtained just from Georgia, North Carolina, and California was spent entirely on a lavish lifestyle, including over $100,000 spent on Porsche rentals, over $100,000 spent at Loro Piana in Manhattan (an Italian luxury clothing brand where women’s jackets can cost $9,500 and purses can cost $4,500), and a nearly year-long travel spree in 2024 that ranged from Colombia, to Aruba, and four months in Europe. Selfies the defendants took while spending fraud proceeds in Europe at a Tuscan spa and touring the BMW plant that were offered at trial are pictured below.
In another aspect of the scheme, the defendants sought CDBG reimbursements by claiming they provided free dental prostheses to homeless individuals. In reality, the defendants printed dentures at their home with an unsanitary 3-D printer and charged homeless individuals fees for scanning their mouths and fitting the dentures. Pino-Copete is pictured below showing off cash he obtained from a homeless dental client at a flea market in Maryland to Jael Watts on a video call while she was incarcerated at the Albany County Correctional Facility.
Following a multi-week jury trial in Utica, the jury found Watts and Pino-Copete guilty of all crimes charged in a third superseding indictment handed up earlier this month: Watts was convicted of one count of false statement, one count of aggravated identity theft, five counts of wire fraud; and Watts and Pino-Copete were convicted of one count of wire fraud conspiracy, one count of false document, and one count of aggravated identity theft.
At sentencing before U.S. District Judge Anthony J. Brindisi currently scheduled for January 21, 2027, Watts and Pino-Copete face a mandatory minimum of two years in prison, a maximum of twenty years in prison, fines of up to $250,000, and supervised release terms of up to three years. Watts and Pino-Copete also face a restitution order of at least $1.9 million. In addition, Pino-Copete, who is not a U.S. citizen, faces removal and deportation following completion of any term of imprisonment.
DOT-OIG, HUD-OIG, and the OSC are investigating the case.
Assistant U.S. Attorneys Benjamin S. Clark, Joshua R. Rosenthal, and Michael J. Whalen for the Northern District of New York are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, 2026, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
New Jersey Woman, Jael Watts, and Colombian Lover, Luis Pino-Copetes, spending their fraudulent earnings in hotel. Jael Watts and Luis Pino-Copete taking a photo. Colombian Lover showing off their fraudulent earnings, while New Jersey Woman is in jail. Image of Jael Watts, 45, as she is in jail and Luis Pino-Copete, 42, sitting at home.
title: New Jersey Woman, Colombian Lover Convicted in $13M Federal Program Fraud Scheme

Ryan’s bill prevents President Trump from weaponizing the military to interfere with elections; the introduction follows new reports that advisors close to the President are encouraging him to declare martial law ahead of the midterm elections

Trump has repeatedly refused to rule out declaring a national emergency on elections, has already deployed thousands of U.S. troops to Democratic-led cities, and suggested that Republicans should “take over” the voting process

The introduction comes just 33 days before the midterm election, in which Democrats are projected to massively out-perform Republicans

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan – an Iraq War combat veteran and the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress – introduced the No Troops in Our Streets Act, landmark legislation preventing the President from weaponizing the military to interfere with elections. Specifically, the bill would empower Congress to stop or reverse any domestic troop deployment ordered by the President.

The introduction follows months of threats and actions by the Trump Administration to interfere with the November midterm elections and amid new reports from the Atlantic that advisors close to the President are encouraging him to declare martial law. Trump has repeatedly refused to rule out declaring a national emergency on elections, has already deployed thousands of U.S. troops against U.S. citizens in American cities, and suggested that Republicans should “nationalize” the midterm elections and “take over” the voting process. When asked directly in a House Armed Services Committee (HASC) hearing, a senior Trump military official refused to rule out troop deployments to polling sites.

“Patriots in uniform sign up to fight for fundamental American freedoms – not against them. Trump using U.S. servicemembers as political pawns is straight-up un-American, and we’re not going to let him get away with it,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Trump and those around him are scared – they know the American people are fed up with the war in Iran and skyrocketing prices. Instead of working to lower costs, Trump and his team are cooking up ways to intimidate voters, refusing to rule out domestic troop deployments. This bill provides a necessary check on the President. If he deploys troops, Congress can and will stop him. We won’t let this chickenhawk president exploit our servicemembers just because he can’t face the fact that the American people are fed up with his failed agenda of higher costs and unprecedented corruption.”

The legislation was co-sponsored by fellow Democratic veterans Reps. Eugene Vindman, Chris Deluzio, Maggie Goodlander, Jimmy Panetta, and Chrissy Houlahan. Senator Elissa Slotkin introduced companion legislation in the Senate. The bicameral legislation also includes $1 billion in new resources for state and local law enforcement on the ground.

Congressman Ryan is a U.S. Army veteran, served two combat tours in Iraq, and is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in the U.S. House of Representatives. Amid recent threats to veterans’ benefits, national security concerns, and rising threats worldwide, Congressman Ryan led his fellow veterans in Congress to create the Democratic Veterans Caucus. He sits on the House Armed Services Committee and has led extensive legislation to deliver relief for veterans, servicemembers, and military families.

U.S. Representatives Don Beyer (D-VA) and Suzan DelBene (D-WA), Co-Chairs of the Egypt Human Rights Caucus, today urged the Egyptian government to immediately and unconditionally release the six journalists affiliated with independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash and end its escalating crackdown on independent media:

“As co-chairs of the Egypt Human Rights Caucus, we call on Egyptian authorities to immediately and unconditionally release the six journalists affiliated with the independent investigative journalism platform Matsadaash. The arrest of the outlet’s entire newsroom is a clear escalation in the government’s campaign to stifle press freedom in the country.

“Even prior to these arrests, Egypt has consistently ranked as one of the world’s most repressive regimes and has a long history of unfairly targeting independent media outlets and drastically limiting freedom of expression. Egyptian authorities regularly claim, without sufficient evidence or due process, that critics of the government are members of the Muslim Brotherhood. The recent arrests are the latest and most alarming case of this tactic on display.

“We have tried to engage constructively with the Egyptian government on our concerns about the country’s human rights situation, including its arbitrary detention of journalists and targeting of media outlets. These arrests demonstrate why Congress must strengthen its resolve, demand better from its partner, and continue to condition U.S. military aid to Egypt on demonstrable rights reforms.”
title: Egypt Human Rights Caucus Co-Chairs Urge Immediate Release of Detained Egyptian Journalists

U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA) introduced the Support for Universities and Colleges to Champion the Educational Success of Survivors (SUCCESS) Act and the Survivor Outreach and Support (SOS) Campus Act—bicameral legislation to prevent campus sexual assault and improve support for student survivors.

The SUCCESS Act would help improve academic outcomes for student survivors and ensure colleges and universities have the resources to support them. The Survivor Outreach and Support on Campus Act, or S.O.S. Campus Act, would require every college and university that receives federal funding to have an independent advocate dedicated to campus sexual assault prevention and response.

“Every student deserves to feel safe on their college campus and to know that if they experience sexual violence, they will be supported and taken seriously. The urgency to act has been put into sharp relief as we learn more about the horrific allegations coming out of Cornell,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “These bills will give colleges and universities more tools to prevent sexual violence, support survivors, and help ensure students can continue their education in a safe and supportive environment. No student should ever have to choose between their safety and their education.”

“Every student deserves to live and learn in a healthy and safe environment. We must do everything we can to prevent sexual assault on college campuses and provide comprehensive support to survivors,” said Senator Kaine.“I’m proud to introduce these bills to help ensure survivors can access medical care, counseling, and the academic support they need to heal and continue pursuing their educational and professional goals.”

Sexual violence can impact student survivors physically, psychologically, emotionally, and academically. Survivors may face difficulty learning and retaining information, lower grade point averages, and a greater risk of dropping out of school. College and university students deserve the ability to learn without fear of sexual violence, and higher education institutions have an obligation to do everything they can to provide a safe learning environment for their students. The legislation would help colleges and universities provide comprehensive guidance, resources, and support for survivors to make campuses a safer place to learn.

The S.O.S. Campus Act would require campuses to have an independent advocate to conduct public information campaigns on sexual assault prevention and ensure that survivors of sexual assault have access to:

Emergency and follow-up medical care,

Guidance on reporting assaults to law enforcement

Medical forensic or evidentiary exams,

Crisis intervention, ongoing counseling, and assistance throughout the process, and

Information on their legal rights.

The legislation would also require universities to consult with or partner with local rape crisis centers and other community-based organizations to ensure survivors can access the services they need.

The SUCCESS Act would provide funding for universities and colleges to:

Provide higher education re-entry assistance for student survivors of sexual assault and other forms of violence;

Increase training for faculty and administrators on patient-centered care and recognizing signs of trauma;

Provide patient-centered professional development training for academic advisors and counselors;

Provide academic accommodations for students experiencing trauma, such as patient-centered training for tutors or the establishment of a confidential tutoring program specifically designed to assist student survivors of sexual assault and other violence;

Increase mental health services for student survivors of sexual assault and other violence; and

Create or enhance a fund for survivors of sexual assault and other violence to use for wrap-around services like housing, health care, and mental health treatment.
title: Dingell, Kaine Introduce Legislation to Combat Campus Sexual Assault and Support Survivors

RI Delegation Announces $9.1 Million to Boost Public Safety & Support Local Law Enforcement
Washington, DC – In an effort to improve public safety, U.S. Senators Jack Reed and Sheldon Whitehouse and U.S. Representatives Seth Magaziner and Gabe Amo today announced $9,101,109 in federal funding to support police officers, law enforcement agencies, crime victims, and nonprofit organizations.
This federal funding will be used to implement a range of crime reduction strategies, criminal justice initiatives, and assistance for crime victims, and to help keep people and communities safe, including:
• Combating violence and various forms of crime with evidence-based, collaborative strategies and programs;
• Preventing domestic violence and sexual assault and assisting survivors and victims of crime through court and hospital visits;
• Upgrading critical technological infrastructure and acquisition of public safety vehicles and protective gear.
“This federal funding will improve public safety, prevent crimes, and serve justice. I am committed to ensuring our law enforcement officers are well-equipped and well-trained. This federal funding will help them take a comprehensive approach to reducing crime, supporting victims, and strengthening relationships between law enforcement and the communities they serve,” said Senator Reed.
“As a former U.S. Attorney and attorney general, I’ve seen firsthand how increasing resources for local law enforcement and community organizations can make a difference in people’s lives,” said Senator Whitehouse, a senior member of the Senate Judiciary Committee. “Our delegation has helped deliver federal funding to modernize our criminal justice system, expand behavioral and mental health services, and protect public safety.”
“Every Rhode Islander deserves to feel safe and supported in their community. This federal funding will equip our police officers with resources to protect the public, while making sure survivors of violence and abuse get the support they need,” said Magaziner. “I am proud to join my colleagues to bring home more federal funding for law enforcement officers across our state and will continue to stand up for first responders.”
“Rhode Islanders deserve to feel safe in their communities,” said Congressman Gabe Amo. “This federal funding will help support survivors, strengthen local law enforcement, and give communities the resources they need to prevent and respond to crime. I will continue to work alongside our delegation in Congress to provide the resources our communities need to remain safe and secure.”
Background
This round of federal funding, which was secured in recent appropriations laws, will be distributed to the state, as well as to local police departments, state agencies, support organizations, and nonprofits, including:
- $4,583,223 for Rhode Island’s Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) funds to provide direct services like counseling, personal advocacy, court advocacy, client transportation, and support services to victims of crimes including domestic violence, sexual violence, child abuse, and elder abuse as they move through the criminal justice system.
- $2,657,307 for the Rhode Island Department of Public Safety to provide supplemental crisis response services for victims.
- $791,279 to the Rhode Island Department of Public Safety for the Sexual Assault Services Formula Program.
- $343,065 for the Office of Violence Against Women (OVW) State and Territory Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Coalitions Program to coordinate victim services activities.
- $265,000 from the Crime Victims Fund to enhance State Victim Compensation payments to eligible crime victims.
- $197,757 for the Providence Police Marine Unit to purchase a marine enforcement operation vessel for use in and around the waterways of the Providence and Seekonk Rivers, enabling effective rapid response and public safety enforcement within these complex urban estuarine environments.
- $76,359 for the Pawtucket Police Department to support the Pawtucket Police JAG Overtime Initiative.
- $60,948 for the Woonsocket Police Department to sustain community policing programs (bicycle patrols and the Police Explorers Post) and purchase a thermal drone.
- $31,021 for the Cranston Police Department to implement a specialized Drone as First Responder initiative.
- $25,254 for the Central Falls Police Department to purchase information technology equipment and supplies.
- $19,090 for the Warwick Police Department to support the acquisition of critical underwater communication equipment for its Underwater Search & Recovery Team.
- $16,107 for Newport Police to integrate technology to increase the probability of peaceful resolutions when communicating with suspects or individuals in crisis.
- $14,118 for the City of East Providence to purchase equipment in relation to speed enforcement.
- $10,539 for the North Providence Police Department to purchase body armor gear.
- $10,042 for the Coventry Police Department to purchase Honor Guard uniforms.

Secretary Kennedy Announces 8 Communities to Receive $96 Million Through New STREETS Program
WASHINGTON, D.C. — October 2, 2026 — U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. today announced in Houston, Texas the eight communities selected to receive funding through the new Safety Through Recovery, Engagement, and Evidence-based Treatment and Support (STREETS) program. Administered by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), STREETS will provide $96 million over four years to help communities build coordinated systems of care for people who are homeless and have serious mental illness, substance use disorders, or co-occurring disorders.
“STREETS takes treatment directly to Americans living on our streets and connects them to the care and support they need to recover,” said Secretary Kennedy. “Under President Trump, we will no longer accept a system that manages human suffering instead of ending it. We are helping people reclaim their health, rebuild their lives, and achieve the dignity, purpose, and independence that come with recovery.”
Each of the eight selected communities will receive $3 million a year for four years. The selected communities are:
- Alcohol, Drug Addiction and Mental Health Services (ADAMHS) Board for Montgomery County (OH)
- Cherokee Nation (OK)
- City of Detroit, Health Department (MI)
- City of Houston, Health Department, Human Services Division (TX)
- City Of Huntington (WV)
- Miami-Dade County (FL)
- Robeson County (NC)
- Tangipahoa Parish Government (LA)
STREETS puts the Trump Administration’s Treatment First approach into action by bringing engagement and evidence-based treatment directly to people who are homeless and connecting treatment with recovery supports, housing, and other community services. Treatment is the starting point; recovery is the goal. The program emphasizes sustained engagement to improve health, promote stability and self-sufficiency, and reduce repeated homelessness and involvement with crisis systems.
“People who are homeless and struggling with serious mental illness or addiction should not have to navigate fragmented systems alone,” said SAMHSA Chief of Staff Timothy W. Westlake. “We are organizing systems around recovery instead of asking people in crisis to organize themselves around systems. STREETS brings treatment, recovery supports, housing, and community partners together to help people achieve lasting stability and greater independence.”
STREETS advances President Trump’s Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets and the Great American Recovery, co-chaired by HHS Secretary Kennedy and White House Senior Advisor for Addiction Recovery Kathryn Burgum. STREETS also supports SAMHSA’s Strategic Priorities to advance evidence-based treatment approaches that prioritize recovery, self-sufficiency, and public safety while directly combating the devastating effects of addiction, mental illness, and homelessness in America.
“The Great American Recovery is building a national culture in which recovery is expected, supported, and celebrated,” said White House Senior Advisor Kathryn Burgum. “STREETS brings that mission directly to Americans in need by connecting Treatment First with sustained recovery support, housing, and a pathway toward stability, self-sufficiency, and renewed purpose.”
STREETS places special emphasis on rapid, comprehensive, and coordinated street-based engagement, treatment, and recovery support. Grantees will bring together local government, behavioral health and health care providers, housing partners, law enforcement, courts, first responders, and other community organizations to build coordinated systems of care that help people remain engaged in treatment and recovery, achieve greater stability and independence, and reduce repeated homelessness and crisis-system involvement.
If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. To locate a treatment facility or provider, visit FindTreatment.gov.
Credentialed media outlets may send requests for comment.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.

WASHINGTON, D.C. (October 1, 2026) – Today, Congressman Adam Smith (WA-09) and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08) introduced the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act and the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act, two bills to help immigrants enter the U.S. health care workforce and address the nation's growing shortage of health care providers. A 2022 study by the Migration Policy Institute found that 2.1 million college-educated immigrants are unemployed or underemployed, even as sectors like health care face mounting workforce shortages — including a projected shortfall of up to 48,000 primary care physicians by 2034, according to the Association of American Medical Colleges.

“We have thousands of skilled nurses, doctors, and health professionals in this country whose training and expertise are going to waste because their professional expertise is not recognized and they face numerous barriers to achieve the needed licensure. At the same time, our health care system is stretched thin and patients are waiting longer for care,” said Congressman Adam Smith. “This bill package helps immigrants put their skills to work and serve their communities and will rebuild the health care system.”

“Skilled doctors, nurses, and other health professionals should have the opportunity to put their training and expertise to work caring for patients,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Our legislation would help qualified immigrants overcome unnecessary barriers to entering the health care workforce while helping communities address critical provider shortages. When we make better use of the talent already in our communities, we strengthen our health care system and expand access to care.”

Statements of Support

“Across the U.S., communities face critical health workforce shortages, yet immigrant and refugee health professionals—who possess in-demand skills—remain underemployed. Communities need this talent, and recognizing it is an essential step. By streamlining licensure and addressing unnecessary barriers, we can meet urgent labor needs and improve access to quality care. We support efforts, including at the state and federal levels, to advance policies that promote community prosperity by ensuring that immigrants can fully contribute their training and skills to their local economy.” - Kit Taintor, Head of US Policy and Practice, World Education Services (WES)

“We are proud to support these bills, which will expand opportunities for immigrant professionals while helping address critical workforce shortages in the healthcare sector," said Alice Kang, President of Upwardly Global. "With demand for healthcare workers rising nationwide, we should be creating pathways that allow qualified immigrants and refugees to contribute their expertise. This legislation will strengthen our healthcare system, bolster the economy and support safer, more resilient communities. Upwardly Global will continue to stand with Rep. Smith in moving this work forward.”

"Many members of our team hold advanced education and expertise in medicine, nursing, and behavioral health. Yet they are unable to practice here due to costly additional education requirements and complex licensing procedures. At a time when we are confronted with a significant healthcare provider shortage—and as we work to diversify the healthcare workforce—it is critical to consider policies that create pathways for these highly skilled professionals to contribute to patient care,” said Tamara Cyhan Cunitz, MN, RN, Executive Director, Nashi Immigrants Health Board. “These bills introduced by Rep. Smith would expand opportunities for immigrant healthcare professionals to serve patients in our community and region. These measures would not only strengthen our workforce with qualified providers but also enable community members to receive care from clinicians who understand their language and cultural background.”

Background

The Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act would help immigrants, regardless of previous health care experience, enter the nursing and allied health workforce by:

Creating grants for programs that provide training, licensing, certification, and case management for immigrants interested in entering the health care field; and

Opening eligibility for the National Health Service Corps (NHSC) to non-U.S.-citizen immigrants.

An estimated 200,000 nurses per year will need to be hired to meet increased demand and replace retiring nurses. This bill supports immigrants entering nursing or an allied health profession, including dental hygienists, dietitians, medical technologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech language pathologists.

A fact sheet about the Immigrants in Nursing and Allied Health Act can be found here. The bill text can be found here.

The Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act would help internationally trained physicians (ITPs) obtain a U.S. medical license by:

Incentivizing states to create temporary licensing programs allowing internationally educated immigrants with medical degrees to practice under supervision while completing the training and certification needed for a U.S. medical license;

Establishing guaranteed medical residency slots for ITPs to practice in predominantly medically underserved communities; and

Providing grants to help cover the cost of exam preparation, testing, certification, ESL classes, and case management for ITPs in need of financial assistance.

Apart from Canada, internationally trained physicians cannot immediately apply to sit for the U.S. Medical Licensing Exam (USMLE), and the cost of licensing, test preparation, and certification often puts a U.S. medical license out of reach, even for highly trained professionals. Many states have created alternative licensure pathways, but more must be done at the federal level to support these reforms nationwide to expand high-quality health care access.

A fact sheet about the Internationally Trained Physicians Assistance Act can be found here. The bill text can be found here.

Endorsements: International Medical Graduates Academy (TIMGA), Nashi Immigrants Health Board, Northwest Immigrant Rights Project, Sea Mar Community Health Center, Seattle Indian Health Board, Spring Institute for Intercultural Learning, Talent Beyond Boundaries, Upwardly Global, World Education Services (WES)

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representatives James Walkinshaw (Va.-11), Eugene Vindman (Va.-07), Bobby Scott (Va.-03), Don Beyer (Va.-08), Jennifer McClellan (Va.-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-10) released the following statement on the eighth anniversary of the murder of Jamal Khashoggi.

Eight years ago today, Virginia resident and journalist Jamal Khashoggi was brutally murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul. His murder was an unconscionable attack on a journalist and a Virginia resident, and his family and the American people deserve the full truth about what happened and what followed.

That includes transparency about President Trump’s 2019 call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Congressman Vindman reviewed the transcript of that call while serving as a lawyer on the National Security Council, and we believe the American people deserve to see it for themselves.

As members of Virginia’s congressional delegation, we will continue pressing for the transparency and accountability that this case demands. If President Trump will not release the transcript now, we will force him to do it in the next Congress when Democrats are in charge.

Eight years is far too long to wait for answers. President Trump should declassify and release the transcript and give the Khashoggi family and the American people the truth they deserve.”

BACKGROUND

Jamal Khashoggi, a Washington Post journalist and U.S. resident, was murdered inside the Saudi consulate in Istanbul in October 2018 — an assassination that drew global condemnation and raised serious questions about Saudi Arabia’s leadership and the Trump administration’s response.

In November 2025, Vindman demanded that the White House release the transcript of a “shocking” 2019 call that took place between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman following Khashoggi’s murder. Vindman reviewed this call while serving as a staff lawyer on Trump’s National Security Council.

That same month, he led 37 lawmakers in sending a letter to President Trump calling for the immediate release of the transcript. He also hosted a press conference alongside Hanan Elatr Khashoggi — Khashoggi’s wife — and U.S. Representatives Jamie Raskin (Md.-08) and Suhas Subramanyam (Va.-11) to urge President Trump to release the transcript of the call.

In October 2025, Congressman Walkinshaw and Senators Kaine and Warner introduced a bicameral resolution commemorating the seventh anniversary of Khashoggi’s murder and calling for accountability. The resolution also called for the Government of Saudi Arabia to release wrongfully detained individuals, respect the rights of Saudi citizens, and ensure the protection of the freedoms of assembly, association, and the press.

Khashoggi was a resident of Virginia’s 11th District, which was formerly represented by the late Congressman Gerry Connolly and is now represented by Walkinshaw.

MILWAUKEE – Yesterday, Ambassador Jamieson Greer released a statement following the G20 Trade Ministerial in Milwaukee, Wisconsin in his capacity as the Chair of the G20 Trade Ministerial.
“This week’s G20 Trade Ministerial in Milwaukee was a success. It is especially significant that the entire G20 was able to reach consensus on the statement on the weaponization of food through coercive trade actions,” said Ambassador Greer. “We also had constructive meetings on the sidelines regarding global diesel supplies which contributed to the anticipated release of more diesel into the global market. G20 Trade Ministers also had candid and productive discussions regarding eliminating forced labor in global supply chains, addressing structural excess capacity and production, and reforming the Most–Favored Nation principle (MFN).”
“In addition, I commend Mexico and Argentina in joining the United States in a statement on eliminating forced labor in global supply chains,” continued Ambassador Greer. “While I am disappointed that the G20 Trade Ministers did not reach consensus on this issue, I am hopeful that discussions on this topic will continue and that other economies will join us in taking increased action to combat forced labor in global supply chains. In addition, many G20 members expressed resolve to address structural excess capacity and production in key sectors of concern. I am disappointed that a handful of members rejected creating a pathway toward cooperative action. Finally, I’m encouraged that members across the development spectrum indicated that they see merit in considering how the MFN principle might be improved to address today’s global trade environment.”

Ranking Member Joe Morelle, Rep. James Walkinshaw Host Fairfax, Virginia Shadow Hearing on Election Security, Fighting Trump Administration’s Attacks on Voting
With voting underway, lawmakers and voting rights leaders gathered in Fairfax to defend mail-in voting, combat intimidation and protect election integrity
FAIRFAX, VA – Yesterday, Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25), Committee on House Administration, and Congresswoman James Walkinshaw (VA-11) hosted a public shadow hearing with members of the Virginia delegation to confront the Trump administration’s attacks on voting and detail efforts to defend every eligible American’s right to cast a ballot and have it counted.
Experts at the shadow hearing included:
- Jeff McKay, Fairfax County Board of Supervisors Chairman
- Skye Perryman, President and CEO of Democracy Forward
- Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President for Policy and Litigation Strategy at Common Cause
- Rev. Dr. Cozy Bailey, President of the Virginia State Conference NAACP
- Jessica Jones Capparell, Director of Government Affairs at the League of Women Voters of the United States
Experts outlined litigation, voter education and safeguards countering interference, intimidation and misinformation. The hearing examined the administration’s attempted overhaul of mail-ballot processing, federal demands for sensitive voter information, and concerns about armed immigration agents at polling places. Experts explained how litigation blocked the mail-voting rule and detailed ongoing efforts to protect voter privacy and prevent intimidation.
“In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle. “The election is here and we are protecting Americans right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost. Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”
“Where the Trump administration is sowing fear and confusion, we’re providing facts and defending the right to vote. We came together in Fairfax to make clear that every eligible American, no matter who they support, can cast a ballot with confidence,” said Congressman Walkinshaw (VA-11). “I’m grateful to Ranking Member Morelle for joining us and proud to stand alongside my Virginia colleagues and the voting rights leaders doing this work every day. We will keep fighting to protect every vote and ensure the American people decide who represents them.”
“Over the last two years, the Trump Administration and the Supreme Court have levied various attacks against the right to vote,” said Congressman Bobby Scott (VA-02), Ranking Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee. “Unfortunately, Congressional Republicans have been unwilling to take a stand against these actions. Democrats are fighting to defend everyone's right to participate in our elections, and yesterday's hearing demonstrates the urgency of this fight.”
“My own family struggled, fought, bled and in some cases died for the right to vote,” said Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04). “We have seen repeated efforts by the Administration to undermine the electoral process and the constitutionally protected right of millions to vote. Election integrity means protecting our election systems from foreign interference and unlawful voting, but it also means protecting every citizen’s right to vote, free of intimidation, free from discrimination. We cannot have an America that goes back to the days when propaganda, violence and voter suppression were used to keep all of the people from participating in their government.”
“Every eligible voter should be able to cast their ballot without fear, intimidation, or unnecessary barriers,” said Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). “Our democracy works when voters know their voices will be heard and their votes will be counted. I’m proud to stand with my Virginia colleagues, local election officials, and voting rights advocates to protect access to the ballot, safeguard voter privacy, and ensure every eligible Virginian can make their voice heard.”
“This Administration has threatened to cheat and exhaust every option to diminish our free and fair elections. In these unprecedented times, I am proud to stand together with my colleagues and voting rights organizations to protect the voices of all Americans. We will ensure every vote, regardless of party, gets counted this November. We will not be intimidated,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).
Ranking Member Morelle and the Committee on House Administration is charged with the oversight of federal elections, including considering proposals to amend federal election law and monitoring congressional elections across the U.S.

Santa Cruz, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) called on U.S. Postmaster General David Steiner to immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office, identify an alternative post office location in the community, and expand postal services to ensure that residents have timely and local access to their mail.

Postal services in Brookdale have been suspended since a fire severely damaged the community’s contract post office in December 2024. After residents waited nearly two years for the facility to reopen, with no apparent progress being made on repairs, the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) notified the community in September 2026 that it was conducting a feasibility study on permanently closing the location. USPS still has not proposed an alternative location or expanded service within Brookdale.

“Since the Brookdale Post Office burned down, the people of that community have waited for nearly two years in good faith while the USPS sat on its hands saying that they would reopen the facility,” said Rep. Panetta. “Then, out of the blue, the USPS made the haphazard decision to study whether it should shut down the post office without providing any postal service in Brookdale. Such an indiscriminate and arbitrary decision to shut down a local post office, without any plan to open up the existing one or attempt to provide postal services to existing Brookdale customers, is unreasonable, and we expect more out of our Postal Service. That is why I wrote this letter calling on the USPS to stop the study and start figuring out how it can provide postal services to the people of Brookdale.”

Brookdale residents do not receive home mail delivery and have historically relied on post office boxes and retail services at the local facility. Since the fire, residents have been forced to travel to neighboring communities, including Boulder Creek and Ben Lomond, to retrieve their mail and access basic postal services. In the mountain community of Brookdale, that burden is particularly significant for seniors, people with disabilities, working families, and residents without reliable transportation, especially during severe weather and other disruptions in the San Lorenzo Valley.

Rep. Panetta called on Postmaster General Steiner to:

Immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study on the proposed permanent closing of the Brookdale Post Office;

Investigate potential alternative permanent post office locations in Brookdale;

Explore home delivery service for the residents of Brookdale;

Until home delivery is available, offer cluster box units or another mail pickup solution in Brookdale; and

Schedule a meeting with Rep. Panetta to discuss next steps.

Rep. Panetta has repeatedly pressed USPS leadership to restore postal services in Brookdale. In a February 2026 letter to the Postmaster General, he called on USPS to repair and reopen the facility with a clear project timeline and provide temporary postal service within the community in the interim. After USPS missed its promised May 1 reopening date, Rep. Panetta sent a May 2026 letter requesting that the USPS Inspector General review the agency’s management, communication, and decision-making, the adequacy of interim services, and the feasibility of restoring service through a temporary or alternative facility.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Postmaster General:

I write to request your immediate action to end the discontinuance feasibility study for the Brookdale Post Office, to find a new post office location in Brookdale, California, and to expand appropriate postal services to serve this community. Since their contract post office burned down, my constituents have waited for nearly two years in good faith while the USPS deflected its responsibility to reopen the facility. The decision this month to consider discontinuing postal service in Brookdale, with no alternative services to your existing Brookdale customers, is unreasonable without any effort to find an alternative post office location or any other remedy for postal services and basic operations in the community.

In December 2024, a fire disabled service at the contract post office in Brookdale, a town I represent in California’s 19th District. Brookdale is a rural mountain community, and for nearly two years, residents waited in good faith for the USPS to restore service, traveling to other towns to receive basic postal services. This would be a burden under normal circumstances, and it is particularly challenging when residents face weather events or other impediments in the San Lorenzo Valley. For disabled, elderly, and mobility-impaired constituents, traveling out of their town presents an additional challenge, but Brookdale residents have done so patiently with the expectation that USPS would eventually restore a local post office. However, in September 2026, after years of deflections, the USPS announced a discontinuance feasibility study for the post office and took the extraordinary step of preemptively refusing to expand services in Brookdale or to consider a new post office location in the community.

Brookdale has never had home delivery, despite the fact that neighboring towns enjoy this basic service. Over time, residents have come to rely on boxes and retail services at the local post office. For years, these services were housed in a rented facility. When that facility suffered a catastrophic fire, the USPS spent years assuring residents and my office that they were waiting for the property owner to conduct necessary repairs. This rationale continued even after the property owner missed basic deadlines for the repairs. Instead of considering alternative locations for the post office, or my constituents’ requests for home delivery or cluster box units in Brookdale, the USPS took steps to discontinue service altogether.

Faced with this situation, I ask that you:

Immediately halt the discontinuance feasibility study on the proposed permanent closing for the Brookdale Post Office;

Investigate potential alternative permanent post office locations in Brookdale;

Explore home delivery service for the residents of Brookdale;

Until home delivery is available, offer cluster box units or another mail pickup solution in Brookdale;

Schedule a meeting with me to discuss next steps to ensure my constituents are being served.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. Restoring dependable postal operations is vital for my constituents, and these steps will help ensure the residents of Brookdale can rely on the United States Postal Service for years to come.

Sincerely,
title: Rep. Panetta Calls on USPS to Stop Feasibility Study to Close the Brookdale Post Office
